The finite potential Hessian is a sum of the spatial squares at the sampled times, so it adds no negative or extra zero directions. This proves the asserted clean normal Hessian.

Use any fixed product Riemannian metric on the integration variables with its group part bi-invariant and fixed in the source units. In a tubular chart about the minimum write $s$ for its circle coordinate and $y$ for a normal orthonormal coordinate. The transverse Hessian $H_s$ is obtained by differentiating (T.5i.1). The collective-coordinate factor is the induced circle volume times the density of $d\mu_J$ relative to this metric. The normalized Haar contribution in that density is the reciprocal of the product group volume. Equivalently in these coordinates the factor is $a(s,0)\,ds$ when $d\mu_J=a(s,y)\,ds\,dy$. This prescription includes the entire circle and its normal determinant. The finite leading coefficient is
$$
A_J=\int_{\rm circle} a(s,0)\,(\det H_s)^{-1/2}\,ds>0.
\tag{T.5i.2}
$$
For multiple cells take products and include every inactive cell. The classical action does not sum its fluctuation coefficients over enabled cells alone.

*Certified relative error at fixed $J$.* Let $r$ be the normal dimension. On a sufficiently small compact tube choose positive bounds $H_s\succeq m I$, $a(s,0)\ge a_0$, and numbers $C_3,C_1$ satisfying
$$
\left|S_J-S_*-\tfrac12 y^{\mathsf T}H_s y\right|\le C_3|y|^3,\qquad
|a(s,y)-a(s,0)|\le C_1|y|.
$$
A finite smooth tubular atlas can be used with a smooth partition on the circle, keeping positive density bounds on the common unpartitioned density. For a radius $\rho$ with $C_3\rho\le m/4$, the tube action excess and the comparison quadratic are both at least $m|y|^2/4$. The difference of their exponentials is bounded by $b C_3|y|^3 e^{-bm|y|^2/4}$. The density difference contributes $C_1|y|e^{-bm|y|^2/4}$. Integration and the scaling $z=\sqrt b\,y$ bound these errors by constants times $b^{-(r+1)/2}$. The omitted Gaussian exterior is bounded by an explicit Gaussian tail with exponent at least $bm\rho^2/4$. The constants are Gaussian moments and the stated tube and density bounds.

Outside the tube $S_J-S_*$ has a strictly positive infimum $\sigma$. To certify it, restrict first to a compact set and bound the continuous distance action by a finite mesh with a modulus of continuity. Then increase the compact set using the kinetic estimate on the Higgs paths. In particular the squared increments starting at the fixed $X_0$ bound a positive multiple of the sum of squared intermediate Higgs radii minus a constant, by finite Cauchy–Schwarz. The group factors are compact. Hence $\int e^{-(S_J-S_*)}\,d\mu_J<\infty$ with an effective Gaussian upper bound, and the exterior contribution for $b\ge1$ is bounded by this upper bound times $e^{-(b-1)\sigma}$. The tube constants and a positive lower bound on $A_J$ can be certified by the smooth finite matrices, the compact circle, and the positive normal eigenvalue gap. Combining the estimates proves
$$
Z_J(b)=e^{-bS_*}(2\pi/b)^{r/2}A_J\,(1+R_J(b)),\qquad
|R_J(b)|\le C_J b^{-1/2}+C'_J b^{r/2} e^{-(b-1)\sigma_J}
\tag{T.5i.3}
$$
for explicit finite positive constants, with the Gaussian exterior absorbed into the second term after decreasing $\sigma_J$. A positive lower factor can be certified from this bound at sufficiently large $b$. At the physical source strength the finite integral can also be bounded directly by finite quadrature and its effective exterior tail. Neither statement gives a regulator-uniform bound as $J$ grows. The circle measure, fluctuation determinant and error concern the marked transition integral. The renormalized order parameter, its matching to a physical Planck unit and the continuum-time remainder of Principle T.6a retain their tests. $\square$

<a id="theorem-t5j"></a>

<a id="theorem-t5j-certified-continuum-time-electroweak-transition-integral"></a>**Theorem T.5j (Certified Continuum-Time Electroweak Transition Integral).** Use the fixed bosonic configuration carrier, actual kinetic coefficients, nonnegative potential and marked boundary of Theorem T.5g. Project the quantum evolution onto the Gauss-invariant subspace by the normalized Haar boundary average used in Theorem T.5i. The exact continuum-time Euclidean transition kernel on this boundary has an effective, strictly positive enclosure from kinetic heat-kernel slices, with explicit error $O(J^{-1/2})$ at $J$ time steps. The comparison keeps all link and Higgs coordinates and integrates the whole site-gauge group, including the unbroken temporal circle. An exact positive relative factor against the free kinetic transition on the same boundary is computable without a small-fluctuation expansion. This transition factor concerns the specified quantum carrier and clock. The physical order-parameter and Planck matching entries of Principle T.6a require a separate map.

*Actual operator and the sliced estimator.* On one cell use $\mathcal M=U(2)^{\mathcal E}\times(\mathbb C^2)^{\mathcal V}$ with the metric of Theorem T.5i. Write $V=\mathcal V_{\rm EW}\ge0$ and $H=-\hbar^2\Delta_{\mathcal M}/2+V$, with its positive form realization. Its Gauss projector is the normalized group average $P_{\rm G}$ over $\mathcal G=U(2)^{\mathcal V}$. The metric and the potential are gauge invariant, so $P_{\rm G}$ commutes with the evolution. With $T=T_0$, let $p_t$ be the free kinetic heat kernel of $\hbar\Delta_{\mathcal M}/2$. Let $X_0$ and $X_*$ be the two marked configurations, as in Theorem T.5i. The interacting and free boundary kernels are
$$
K=\int_{\mathcal G}p_T(X_0,gX_*)\,
 \mathbb E_{X_0,gX_*}^{T}\exp\!\left[-\hbar^{-1}\int_0^T V(X_t)\,dt\right]dg,\qquad
K_0=\int_{\mathcal G}p_T(X_0,gX_*)\,dg .
\tag{T.5j.1}
$$
Here the expectation is for the product kinetic Brownian bridge with the indicated endpoints. The identity follows from the Feynman–Kac formula on the kinetic carrier and the orthogonal projector. One can first truncate $V$ by a bounded continuous nonnegative potential, then pass to $V$ by monotone form convergence and dominated convergence of the bridge expectations. The expression defines the continuous kernel on the marked boundary. In particular, the marked endpoints are kernel arguments. The gauge-invariant finite-width preparations used to read the kernel remain separate supplier states. See Kac (1949).

Write $\Delta=T/J$. In the first formula in (T.5j.1) replace the potential integral by $\Delta\sum_{j=0}^{J-1}V(X_{j\Delta})$, and call the result $K_J^{\rm heat}$. Its explicit finite integral uses the exact product of kinetic kernels $p_\Delta(X_j,X_{j+1})$ and the potential exponent on the intermediate positions, with $X_J=gX_*$ and the same normalized Haar endpoint integral. The initial term is zero for the marked boundary. This construction uses the kinetic heat factors with their actual densities. The distance action in (T.5i.1) gives a different finite-slice comparison.

*Uniform bridge estimate.* Identify a link with its unitary matrix entries and a Higgs variable with its real coordinates. All Higgs endpoint radii equal $v$, and every endpoint link is unitary. On any such two configurations $x,y$ the displayed polynomial source terms give a bound
$$
|V(x)-V(y)|\le C_V(1+|\phi(x)|^3+|\phi(y)|^3)
 \left(|\phi(x)-\phi(y)|+\sum_e\|W_e(x)-W_e(y)\|_{\rm HS}\right).
\tag{T.5j.2}
$$
The inequality also holds for arbitrary finite intermediate Higgs values and unitary links. Expand each polynomial difference by telescoping. The Higgs potential has degree four, the difference of the link–Higgs squares has degree at most two in Higgs variables, and the plaquette factors have norm one. Thus $C_V$ is bounded by a finite sum of the actual coefficients and the number of terms. The Higgs part of the bridge is a finite Euclidean Gaussian bridge. Its means are the segment between its endpoints, the coordinate variance is at most $\hbar T/(4I_H)$, and its centered increment variance is at most $\hbar|t-s|/I_H$ per real coordinate. The mean increment has norm at most $2v\sqrt{|\mathcal V|}|t-s|/T$. In particular all sixth moments and the square increments needed in (T.5j.2) have effective uniform bounds.

For a link bridge on $U(2)$, put $A_T=\sup_{u,w,\ t\in[T/2,T]} p_t^{\rm link}(u,w)$ and $a_T=\inf_{u,w}p_T^{\rm link}(u,w)>0$, using its own kinetic coefficients. Up to time $T/2$ the law is absolutely continuous relative to unconditioned link diffusion from its initial endpoint with density bounded by $A_T/a_T$. This is the Markov kernel bridge formula. In the second half use time reversal and the same symmetric kernel. For an unconditioned link, matrix coordinates have a bounded diffusion coefficient and a bounded drift from the explicit invariant-frame generator. Itô isometry and Cauchy–Schwarz give an increment second moment bounded by $C_{\rm link}|t-s|$ on $[0,T]$, with $C_{\rm link}$ from the fixed link metric, the matrices of an orthonormal Lie algebra basis, $\hbar$ and $T$. Therefore the bridge has the same bound with factor $A_T/a_T$ on either half. For increments straddling $T/2$, split there and use $\|a+b\|^2\le2\|a\|^2+2\|b\|^2$. These constants are effective. The Peter–Weyl expansion of $p_t^{\rm link}$ is uniform for $t\ge T/2$, since the $U(2)$ irreducible labels give polynomial dimension growth and the electric eigenvalues grow quadratically in the central and semisimple labels. Its uniformly summable tail is bounded by polynomial Gaussian sums. The same estimate for the first derivatives supplies a compact-grid modulus. Positivity of the connected group heat kernel and uniform approximation therefore give a certified positive lower bound for $a_T$ by refinement.

Cauchy–Schwarz applied to (T.5j.2) now gives $\mathbb E|V(X_t)-V(X_s)|\le C_{\rm br}\sqrt{|t-s|}$ with an explicit bound uniform in the final gauge transform. For nonnegative $u,v$ one has $|e^{-u}-e^{-v}|\le|u-v|$. Integrate the increment estimate over each slice, then sum and use (T.5j.1). This proves
$$
|K-K_J^{\rm heat}|\le K_0\,\frac{2C_{\rm br}T}{3\hbar}\sqrt{T/J}.
\tag{T.5j.3}
$$
There is no accumulated bound on a nonlinear field fluctuation around a single history. The estimate compares the full normalized bridge integral at the physical coefficient $1/\hbar$.

*Positive relative evaluation and gauge boundary.* The Gaussian Higgs moments and bounded link factors also give a uniform upper bound $V_{\rm br}$ on $\mathbb E V(X_t)$. Jensen's inequality and $V\ge0$ yield
$$
\exp[-T V_{\rm br}/\hbar]\le K/K_0\le1.
\tag{T.5j.4}
$$
At any fixed $J$ the heat integral is effectively computable. The compact group factors use the same convergent heat series at $t=\Delta$. In the Higgs intermediate coordinates use a ball and an explicit Gaussian bridge tail for its complement. All endpoint radii are fixed, and the weight is at most one, so this omitted integral is bounded by $K_0$ times the sum of the uniform Gaussian tails for the finitely many intermediate positions. Compact quadrature on the remaining domain has effective bounds from the finite polynomial, Haar densities and the heat series. Similarly $K_0$ is positive and computable by compact quadrature. For the full 759-cell transition the factors are independent and the exact ratios multiply. One can choose all per-cell absolute errors small compared with their positive lower bounds in (T.5j.4), then propagate a relative interval by finite products. This retains inactive cells as actual factors. The gauge average is the complete Gauss projection and covers every boundary gauge value, including the entire unbroken circle identified in Theorem T.5i. The resulting exact transition factor is determined by the source Hamiltonian, endpoints, time and Haar convention. It does not identify the reduced saddle determinant with the physical Higgs scale or assign a new $M_{Pl}$ normalization. $\square$

<a id="theorem-t5k"></a>

<a id="theorem-t5k-exact-radial-effective-functional-on-the-bosonic-electroweak-source"></a>**Theorem T.5k (Exact Radial Effective Functional on the Bosonic Electroweak Source).** Keep the carrier, proper clock and Gauss constraint of Theorems T.5g and T.5j. Denote the supplied squared Higgs radius by $u=v^2$. With the Higgs coordinate and its unit fixed, take the gauge-invariant squared-radius observable $R=|\mathcal V|^{-1}\sum_{x\in\mathcal V}|\phi_x|^2$ on one cell. The zero-temperature static effective functional of this observable has a unique minimum at the ground-state mean $r(u)=\langle R\rangle_u>0$. At fixed other source coefficients the equation $r(u)=u$ has only isolated solutions in $u>0$. There is a positive neighborhood of $u=0$ where $r(u)>u$. These conclusions also hold for the mean squared radius across the 759 cells, with the exact product ground state.

*Static functional and stationarity.* Let $H_u(j)=H_u+jR$, with real source $j$ and the unit of $j$ fixed so that $jR$ is energy. Define $E_u(j)=\inf\operatorname{spec}H_u(j)$ on the Gauss-invariant Hilbert space and
$$
\Gamma_u(r)=\sup_{j\in\mathbb R}\{E_u(j)-jr\}.
\tag{T.5k.1}
$$
The quartic Higgs potential bounds a positive multiple of $\sum_x|\phi_x|^4$ minus a constant locally uniformly in $(u,j)$. The link factors are compact. The form norm therefore controls a local first Sobolev norm and the quartic moment at infinity. Rellich compactness on bounded regions and the uniform tail bound give compact resolvent. The form realization has a strictly positive heat kernel by the kinetic bridge formula with this bounded-below potential. The kernel is positive because every bridge is continuous and its integral of the polynomial potential is finite almost surely. Compactness and positivity improvement give a simple strictly positive ground state on the full carrier. Gauge invariance and uniqueness then put this ground state in the Gauss-invariant subspace. The same proof applies for each real $j$.

Relative to the common quartic form domain, $R$ is infinitesimally form bounded by the quartic moment. Dependence on $u$ and $j$ is polynomial in the form coefficients, since the $u$ dependence is the quadratic-field term $-2\lambda u|\mathcal V|R$ and the constant $\lambda|\mathcal V|u^2$. Analytic form perturbation of the isolated simple eigenvalue gives local real analyticity at every real $(u,j)$, including $u=0$. Differentiation gives $\partial_j E_u(j)=\langle R\rangle_{u,j}$. The ground-state variational formula makes $E_u(j)$ concave. Its supporting line at $j=0$ proves $\Gamma_u(r(u))=E_u(0)$. Every $r\ne r(u)$ has $\Gamma_u(r)>E_u(0)$, by using a sufficiently small $j$ with the sign of $r(u)-r$. Thus the static radius readout is $\sqrt{r(u)}$ in the fixed coordinate convention. For the product cell mean the ground energy with source is $759 E_u(j/759)$, which has the same derivative at zero. See Kato (1966).

The normalized ground state at $u=0$ has $\langle R\rangle_0>0$ because $R$ vanishes only on the Lebesgue-null zero section of the Higgs carrier. Continuity proves the strict inequality for sufficiently small positive $u$. The real analytic function $r(u)-u$ is therefore nonzero as a function on the connected positive axis, so every zero there is isolated. All positive $u$ in this family are admitted source inputs. The classical saddle of Theorem T.5g has radius $\sqrt u$ and action $77/2$ throughout the family.

*Scale dependence of the transition data.* For any positive computable $b$, define the coordinate dilation $D_b(W,\phi)=(W,b\phi)$. Change the source tuple $(I_H,k_D,\lambda,u)$ to $(b^{-2}I_H,b^{-2}k_D,b^{-4}\lambda,b^2u)$, keeping the other coefficients, ruler, duration and Wilson response fixed. This family can be declared before the marked pair. The pullback of the new metric and the new potential by $D_b$ is the original metric and potential. The dilation intertwines the gauge action and takes both marked boundaries to the new boundaries. It maps Riemannian volumes exactly. The induced unitary thus intertwines the Hamiltonians, the free kinetic references and the Gauss projectors. The exact projected boundary kernels of Theorem T.5j, with respect to the stated metric volumes, and the Gaussian comparison coefficients of Theorem T.5i agree. For the fixed coordinate observable, however, $D_b^*R=b^2R$, so the new ground-state mean is $b^2r(u)$ and the new static functional at $r$ equals $\Gamma_u(r/b^2)$. The fixed radius convention can be distinguished by the bounded gauge-invariant effect $R/(R+R_*)$ for an independently fixed $R_*>0$ in the same units. Its ground-state expectation increases strictly with $b$, since $R>0$ almost everywhere. This keeps the radius readout separate from a change of field coordinate accompanied by recalibration of the meter.

The action and these boundary comparisons therefore do not select a calibrated radial scale. With a common independent unit conversion and unreduced Planck reference, the radial readout can vary with the fixed comparisons. The isolated-equality result concerns the specified static observable on the finite bosonic carrier. A scale record still requires a physical order-parameter identification, the Planck bridge and the matching of the corresponding remainder under Principle T.6a. $\square$

<a id="theorem-t5l"></a>

<a id="theorem-t5l-continuum-gaussian-reference-and-certified-transition-remainder"></a>**Theorem T.5l (Continuum Gaussian Reference and Certified Transition Remainder).** Use the bosonic source of Theorem T.5g, with the Haar boundary convention of Theorem T.5i and the exact physical-strength transition of Theorem T.5j. A continuum quadratic saddle coefficient is fixed by the kinetic heat density, the reduced boundary Hessian and the full link–Higgs potential Hessian. It is strictly positive and effectively computable. It is also the limit of the normalized quadratic coefficients of the distance-action regulators. Against this independently defined Gaussian comparison the exact quantum transition has an effectively enclosable positive relative factor at physical strength, including all inactive cells. This is a transition remainder on the marked saddle.

*Kinetic normalization.* Work on one cell, write $m=\dim\mathcal M$, $T=T_0$, and let $g$ run over the product site group $\mathcal G$. Put $F(g)=d(X_0,gX_*)^2/(2\hbar T)$ and write $s_*=1/2$ on an enabled cell and $s_*=0$ on an inactive cell. With the potential switched off, the equality argument of Theorem T.5i still gives precisely the common unbroken circle $L$ of minima. In a neighborhood of $L$ all links of the minimizing geodesic are strictly inside their cut loci. At $L$ the enabled endpoint link eigenangles are $0,1/n$, the inactive and transverse links are identity, and the Higgs geodesics are constant. The kinetic index form of Theorem T.5h gives a positive transverse Hessian $H_\partial=\operatorname{Hess}_\perp F$ on $L$. Use any fixed product group metric to write the normalized Haar density on the tubular coordinates as $a(g,y)\,d\ell\,dy$ with normal orthonormal coordinates $y$ and arc length $\ell$. Let $J_\gamma$ be the Jacobian determinant of the kinetic exponential map at the velocity of the marked cell geodesic, with geodesic parameter in $[0,1]$. It is positive. Thus the continuum kinetic quadratic coefficient at physical strength is
$$
B_{\rm kin}=(2\pi\hbar T)^{-m/2}(2\pi)^{q/2}
J_\gamma^{-1/2}\int_L a(g,0)(\det H_\partial)^{-1/2}\,d\ell,
\qquad q=\dim\mathcal G-1.
\tag{T.5l.1}
$$
This uses the kinetic heat density with generator $\hbar\Delta_{\mathcal M}/2$ relative to its metric volume. In the small-noise convention that replaces this generator by $\hbar\Delta_{\mathcal M}/(2b)$ for $b>0$, its off-cut leading density is $(b/(2\pi\hbar T))^{m/2}J_\gamma^{-1/2}e^{-bF}$. The finite endpoint Gaussian integral contributes $(2\pi/b)^{q/2}$ with the full circle volume and normalized Haar density. The same fixed convention is used at $b=1$ to specify the reference. In the product group all endpoint values at $g\in L$ coincide, so the geodesic and $J_\gamma$ are constant on $L$. The kinetic Jacobian can be obtained from the finite Jacobi equation or the differential of the group exponential (Neel and Sacchelli 2020).

*Potential determinant with endpoint variation.* Use the kinetic Cameron–Martin space $\mathcal H$ of variations of the whole cell geodesic, with zero initial variation and final variation induced by $y$. Its norm is the positive reduced kinetic Hessian. Equivalently write a variation as $\xi=\eta+J_y$, where $J_y$ is the kinetic Jacobi field with these endpoint values and $\eta$ is Dirichlet. The cross term vanishes by the Jacobi equation and the reduced norm is the Dirichlet index norm of $\eta$ plus $y^{\mathsf T}H_\partial y$. This splitting includes the boundary acceleration term in $H_\partial$. In particular, the boundary integration uses the same $q$ normal directions and the same zero circle as (T.5l.1). The spatial potential vanishes with zero derivative along the saddle, so its Hessian $U(t)$ there is positive semidefinite and contributes the form $\hbar^{-1}\int_0^T\langle\xi,U(t)\xi\rangle\,dt$. If $i:\mathcal H\to L^2$ is evaluation along the path, set $C=i i^*$ and
$$
B=B_{\rm kin}\det\bigl(1+\hbar^{-1}U^{1/2}C U^{1/2}\bigr)^{-1/2}.
\tag{T.5l.2}
$$
The determinant is the Gaussian expectation of the exponentiated negative quadratic potential. The Dirichlet covariance is trace class because the positive kinetic index form bounds a positive multiple of the fixed Dirichlet derivative norm in a parallel frame. Its inverse is bounded above by a multiple of the free Dirichlet inverse, with summable sine eigenvalues of order $k^{-2}$. The endpoint covariance is finite rank from $J_y$ and $H_\partial^{-1}$. The Hessian is the full spatial part of (T.5h.1), evaluated on these path and boundary variations. These data are effective: the positive free index bound and its effective inverse follow from Theorem T.5h with the spatial coefficients set to zero, or from the strictly nonconjugate group geodesics. The finite-dimensional boundary matrix has a computable positive lower eigenvalue by refinement. In the parallel sine basis the positive covariance tail trace beyond mode $N$ is bounded by the corresponding free inverse tail plus the effectively summable tail of the finite set of smooth Jacobi fields. For a positive trace-class covariance, the trace norm of its discarded off-diagonal blocks is bounded by twice the square root of its retained trace times its discarded trace. The finite matrix entries follow by solving the Jacobi equation and by quadrature. This gives effective trace-norm approximations to $C$, and bounded multiplication by $U^{1/2}$ preserves them. The Fredholm determinant in (T.5l.2) is therefore effectively positive with computable enclosures.

*Convergence of the time-slice quadratic coefficients.* On each uniform time slicing restrict the path variation to piecewise Jacobi fields through the intermediate slice values. Include the same final normal variations. For zero endpoint variations these subspaces are spanned, in the kinetic index inner product, by the representers of evaluation at the interior grid knots. Orthogonality to the representers is equivalent to vanishing at the knots, and integration by parts gives the piecewise Jacobi characterization. The full subspace also contains each $J_y$. The kinetic slice Hessian is the restriction of the same continuous index form, as proved in Theorem T.5i. Its Gaussian values at the knots therefore have exactly the joint law of the continuous kinetic Gaussian with covariance $C$, evaluated at those knots. This Gaussian has a continuous version: in a parallel frame the Dirichlet Green kernel is the covariance of the nonconjugate pinned kinetic Gaussian, and the kinetic norm bound gives increment variance at most a constant times $|t-s|$ by the evaluation functional bound. Gaussian fourth moments give continuity. The endpoint term is a smooth finite-rank Gaussian field. The normalized spatial determinant of the finite regulator is accordingly the expectation of the sampled potential quadratic weight under this same Gaussian. Continuous paths give Riemann-sum convergence. The sampled weights are bounded by one, so their expectations converge to the expectation in (T.5l.2).

The absolute normalization in this assertion is the product of the leading short-time kinetic densities along the saddle segments, including their volume Jacobians. For a fixed finite partition and the kinetic action, apply ordinary nondegenerate Gaussian integration to the intermediate values, at endpoints near the marked ones. The heat semigroup composition gives the same leading coefficient as the single kinetic density at time $T$. All segments and the full geodesic are off the cut locus, and the unique minimizing interpolation is the geodesic. On the complement of a small neighborhood its kinetic action is strictly greater, by the triangle and Cauchy–Schwarz inequalities and uniqueness. Thus the coefficient identity holds with the displayed normalizations. Applying the finite endpoint Gaussian integration then gives precisely (T.5l.1). This use of fixed-partition leading coefficients, followed by convergence of the quadratic comparison, requires no exchange of the large-$b$ expansion of an interacting kernel with the removal of its time regulator.

*Physical-strength interval.* For each cell fix the positive reference density $D=p_T(X_0,X_0)$ of the unprojected kinetic source at its initial endpoint. Let $D_{\rm tot}$ and $B_{\rm tot}$ be the products of $D$ and $B$ over all 759 cells, including the inactive ones, and let $K_{\rm tot}$ be the exact projected interacting kernel product. Define the dimensionless comparison $A_{\rm tr}=B_{\rm tot}/D_{\rm tot}$ using only the quadratic coefficient and the independent kinetic reference. The quantitative transition remainder is obtained from
$$
1+R_{\rm tr}=\frac{K_{\rm tot}}{B_{\rm tot}e^{-77/2}},\qquad
\frac{K_{\rm tot}}{D_{\rm tot}}=A_{\rm tr}e^{-77/2}(1+R_{\rm tr}).
\tag{T.5l.3}
$$
For any rational tolerance, compute strictly positive intervals for $K_{\rm tot}$ by (T.5j.3) and (T.5j.4), and for $B_{\rm tot}$ by (T.5l.2). With endpoints denoted by subscripts $-$ and $+$, an enclosure for $R_{\rm tr}$ is $[e^{77/2}K_-/B_+-1,\ e^{77/2}K_+/B_--1]$, using outward interval rounding. It has $1+R_{\rm tr}$ strictly positive throughout and can be refined to the requested width. This controls the full quantum deviation from the specified saddle comparison at the physical coefficient. Its size is determined by the source and need not be small. The ratio uses no Higgs-scale comparison or fitted input. The observable identification and Planck scale matching of Principle T.6a retain their independent tests. $\square$

<a id="theorem-t5m"></a>

<a id="theorem-t5m-certified-radial-response-and-range-on-the-electroweak-source"></a>**Theorem T.5m (Certified Radial Response and Range on the Electroweak Source).** Keep the finite Gauss-projected bosonic source and static squared-radius readout of Theorem T.5k. With the other coefficients fixed, the ground-state mean $r(u)$ is strictly increasing and real analytic on $u\ge0$, and its range on the admitted inputs $u>0$ is $(r(0),\infty)$. The full radial response to a constant source and the stationary radius have effective enclosures in the original field units. These enclosures give a same-source test for any proposed order-parameter interval supplied independently of the radial readout.

*Strict response and a variational range bound.* Write $N=|\mathcal V|$ and $R=N^{-1}\sum_x|\phi_x|^2$. Let $\psi$ be the positive normalized ground state of $H_u(j)$, $E=E_u(j)$, and $S$ the positive inverse of $H_u(j)-E$ on the orthogonal complement of $\psi$. Differentiation of the isolated ground-state equation in the common form domain gives
$$
\partial_j^2 E_u(j)=-2\langle(R-\langle R\rangle)\psi,S(R-\langle R\rangle)\psi\rangle<0.
\tag{T.5m.1}
$$
The quartic form bound ensures $R\psi\in L^2$. The vector on the right is nonzero because $\psi$ is positive almost everywhere and the radius varies on sets of positive volume. The reduced inverse is strictly positive in quadratic form on each nonzero vector in its domain. The same derivatives and inverse can be taken in the invariant subspace since $R$ commutes with the gauge action. The relation
$$
H_u(j)=H_0(j-2\lambda N u)+\lambda N u^2
\tag{T.5m.2}
$$
then gives $r'(u)=-2\lambda N\partial_j^2 E_u(0)>0$.

For an explicit upper energy bound at $j=0$, take constant Haar link wavefunctions and independent Higgs Gaussians at each site with mean $\sqrt u\,e_2$ and any fixed real coordinate variance $s^2>0$. Their kinetic energy is a constant in $u$, their link–Higgs expectation is affine in $u$, and their quartic expectation per site is $4s^2u+24s^4$. The last identity follows by expanding $|\sqrt u\,e_2+Z|^2-u$ for a centered four-dimensional Gaussian $Z$. The Haar plaquette expectation is independent of $u$. Thus $E_u(0)\le A_0+A_1u$ with computable constants. The trial may be evaluated on the full carrier because Theorem T.5k puts its lowest eigenstate in the Gauss sector. In the actual ground state the nonnegative potential term and Jensen's inequality yield
$$
\lambda N[r(u)-u]^2\le E_u(0)\le A_0+A_1u .
\tag{T.5m.3}
$$
This implies $r(u)\to\infty$ and gives the stated range by strict monotonicity and continuity. For any computable $r_*>r(0)$ a unique input solving $r(u)=r_*$ can be enclosed by finding pairs of rational $u$ bracketing the root with certified strict inequalities. Using a supplied target radius for this inverse operation is calibration. A forward scale record uses the direct map from independently specified coefficients.

*Effective spectral bounds.* For completeness, the radial mean is computable with the field cutoff removed. Fix computable $u,j$, and restrict the Higgs coordinate to a growing cube. On the complement the full scalar potential is bounded below by a computable quantity tending to infinity, from the quartic term minus the at-most-quadratic source. Neumann bracketing with this exterior lower bound gives a lower ground-energy bound. The Dirichlet cube ground energy gives an upper bound by zero extension. Use the compact link factors unchanged in both restrictions. These comparisons may be made in the full space since its global ground energy equals the invariant ground energy. The cube bounds converge to the global energy. For the upper sequence approximate the global ground state in form norm by compactly supported smooth functions. For the lower sequence take normalized Neumann minimizers with bounded energies. A uniform lower bound by a positive quartic moment minus a constant gives tightness of their squared norms. On every fixed smaller cube the kinetic norm is bounded. Rellich compactness, diagonal extraction and lower semicontinuity on these smaller cubes give a normalized global form-domain limit of energy at most the limit inferior. The exterior lower bound eventually exceeds the upper bound.

Both finite-volume energies have effective enclosures. Use the kinetic eigenbasis consisting of matrix coefficients on the links and tensor products of the elementary interval eigenfunctions with the corresponding boundary conditions on the real coordinates. On the cube let $M$ be a computable upper bound on the norm of the bounded multiplication potential, including $jR$. Project onto a finite kinetic space with complementary kinetic eigenvalues bounded below by $L$. The lowest eigenvalue $a$ of the compressed Hamiltonian is effectively computable by finite quadrature and interval matrix bounds. The complementary block is bounded below by $L-M$ and its cross block has norm at most $M$. When $L-M>a$, the quadratic form on the two projected norms therefore gives the lower bound $a-M^2/(L-M-a)$ by completing the square, and $a$ itself is an upper bound. Taking the kinetic cutoff to infinity yields arbitrarily sharp enclosures for each cube. The kinetic tail bound is effective by the quadratic growth of the product eigenvalues. Matrix entries use elementary interval quadrature on a compact domain, with the finite group coefficients and the polynomial field potential. Increase the cube and refine the finite spectral bounds until their certified width is below the requested tolerance. Convergence of the brackets ensures termination.

Finally, concavity bounds $\partial_j E_u(0)$ between the right and left difference quotients at $\pm h$. Use the spectral enclosures at $0,\pm h$, to error $o(h)$, and decrease positive rational $h$ until the bracket is sufficiently narrow. Analyticity guarantees termination, and strict positivity of the radial mean gives effective enclosures of its square root. The same procedure gives the mean at any supplied real source $j$. It keeps the field coordinate convention of Theorem T.5k and works on all 759 cells by the product ground-state relation. The construction bounds a physical observable of the declared carrier. Its identification with the electroweak mass scale and the independently supplied Planck unit bridge are separate requirements of Principle T.6a. $\square$

<a id="theorem-t5n"></a>

<a id="theorem-t5n-canonical-radial-spectral-sum-rule-on-the-electroweak-carrier"></a>**Theorem T.5n (Canonical Radial Spectral Sum Rule on the Electroweak Carrier).** Use the ground state of the Gauss-invariant Hamiltonian of Theorem T.5k at $j=0$ on one cell. Let $N=|\mathcal V|$, let $r=\langle R\rangle$, and write $S_R$ for the positive spectral measure of $R-r$ from this state, in the excitation energy variable $e$. Its first and inverse moments are
$$
\int e\,dS_R(e)=\frac{2\hbar^2 r}{I_HN},\qquad
\int e^{-1}\,dS_R(e)=-\frac12\partial_j^2 E_u(0)>0.
\tag{T.5n.1}
$$
Both moments are effective in the admitted source units. The canonical kinetic normalization of the radius and this pair of spectral moments is invariant under the isometric source dilation of Theorem T.5k. The fixed-coordinate radial shift under that dilation therefore does not imply a change of the canonically normalized radial scale or of an excitation energy.

*Spectral identity.* Let $A=H_u-E_u(0)$ and let $\psi$ be the normalized positive ground state. The vector $w=(R-r)\psi$ is in the gauge-invariant sector and is orthogonal to $\psi$. Write $S_R(B)=\langle w,\mathbf 1_B(A)w\rangle$ for each Borel set $B$. The inverse moment follows from (T.5m.1), since the orthogonal complement has a strictly positive spectral gap. For the first moment first take a bounded smooth radial multiplier $F$ of the Higgs coordinates with bounded gradient. The ground-state equation tested against $F^2\psi$ and the quadratic-form product rule give
$$
\langle F\psi,A F\psi\rangle_{\rm form}
=\frac{\hbar^2}{2}\int |\nabla F|^2|\psi|^2\,d\mathrm{vol}_{\mathcal M}.
\tag{T.5n.2}
$$
The multiplication potential cancels and the only term left comes from differentiating both copies of $F$. This proof takes place on the common form domain and does not require applying a double commutator to an unbounded operator product. Apply the identity to smooth truncations of $R$ with slopes bounded by one, agreeing with $R$ on successively larger radius ranges. The quartic form bound gives $R\psi\in L^2$, and $|\nabla R|^2=4R/(I_HN)$ is integrable against $|\psi|^2$. Applying (T.5n.2) also to differences of truncations shows that the truncated vectors are Cauchy in the form norm. Thus the identity passes to $R$. Subtracting $r\psi$ leaves the form value unchanged. Substitution of the gradient identity gives the first moment in (T.5n.1).

*Certified susceptibility.* For positive rational source radius $d$, use Theorem T.5m to enclose the radial means $r_j=\partial_j E_u(j)$ at $j=\pm d$. To compute the derivative of $r_j$ at zero with certified error, first bound the gap. Neumann and Dirichlet cubes and the finite kinetic compression of Theorem T.5m also enclose the second eigenvalue of the full carrier. In the compression lower bound, apply the operator inequality obtained by the same cross-block estimate, $H\ge (H_{\rm fin}-\eta I)\oplus(L-M-M^2/\eta)I$, with rational $\eta>0$, then use the min–max principle. For the Neumann cube limit take the span of the first two eigenvectors, use the same quartic tightness and local compactness, and preserve their orthonormality by the resulting strong $L^2$ convergence. Every combination in the limiting span has Rayleigh quotient at most the limit inferior of the second Neumann eigenvalue, by local lower semicontinuity applied to the corresponding combinations. This gives effective lower and upper bounds for both first eigenvalues. Their strict separation gives a certified positive gap at $j=0$.

Here is a direct error control for differentiating the response. Fix a computable positive shift $C$ with $H_u+C\ge1$. Let $B=(H_u+C)^{-1/2}R(H_u+C)^{-1/2}$. A computable norm bound follows from the explicit quartic bound and the inequality between a quadratic and a quartic polynomial in the Higgs coordinates. Choose a circular contour about the lowest eigenvalue of $H_u$ using certified eigenvalue intervals and the gap bound. The diagonal spectral theorem bounds $\|(H_u+C)^{1/2}(H_u-z)^{-1}(H_u+C)^{1/2}\|$ on it by the supremum of $(x+C)/|x-z|$ over the known spectral enclosure. For sufficiently small computable $|j|$ the Neumann series with $jB$ is uniformly convergent. It gives the analytic rank-one spectral projection and eigenvalue on the contour, with the eigenvalue bounded by the contour radius and center. Cauchy's inequalities give an effective third-derivative bound on a smaller disk. The centered first difference of $r_j$ has error bounded by this third-derivative bound for $E_u$ times $d$; the two enclosed input means add their explicit errors divided by $2d$. Refining $d$ and the means therefore encloses the second derivative. This supplies (T.5n.1) without estimating a derivative from a fixed cutoff or assuming a rate for an unqualified spectral approximation.

*Kinetic normalization and an observable energy comparison.* Fix the proper duration $T_0$ and use the dimensionless multiplier $Q=I_H R/(\hbar T_0)$ with excitation energy $\varepsilon=eT_0/\hbar$. The factor $I_H$ is the physical field inertia multiplying the Higgs kinetic form. The dilation of Theorem T.5k sends $R$ to $b^2R$ under pullback and $I_H$ to $b^{-2}I_H$, so the multiplier $Q$, its ground-state law, and its spectral measure in $\varepsilon$ agree under the unitary. In these variables the first spectral moment is $2\langle Q\rangle/N$. The inverse moment is finite and strictly positive. In particular the ratio of the first to the inverse moment is a computable positive number whose square root bounds the bottom of the active excitation spectrum from above: it is the square root of the mean of $\varepsilon^2$ under the probability measure proportional to $\varepsilon^{-1}dS_Q$. These comparisons keep the same physical duration and do not infer an active eigenvalue or pole residue from the two moments alone. They give a canonical radial response for an independently chosen observable and leave the identification with the electroweak scale, and its Planck matching, to the physical map of Principle T.6a. $\square$

<a id="theorem-t5o"></a>

<a id="theorem-t5o-certified-departure-from-a-single-radial-pole"></a>**Theorem T.5o (Certified Departure from a Single Radial Pole).** On the finite bosonic source of Theorem T.5g at any admitted positive parameters, the connected ground-state spectral response of the squared-radius multiplier $R$ has weight at at least two distinct positive excitation energies. Let $M_{-1},M_0,M_1$ denote its inverse, total and first moments, in the physical energy variable of Theorem T.5n. All three are effectively enclosable on this source and
$$
M_{-1}M_1-M_0^2>0.
\tag{T.5o.1}
$$
For any admitted computable source coefficients, a strictly positive rational lower bound in (T.5o.1) can be certified. The conclusion applies unchanged to the kinetic-normalized multiplier with its corresponding energy units. It gives a direct test of using the static radial response as a single pole.

*Why the radial excitation is not an eigenvector.* Let $N$ be the number of vertices in the cell, $d=4N$ the real Higgs dimension, and $y\in\mathbb R^d$ its real coordinates, so $R=|y|^2/N$. Write $H=H_u(0)$, $E$ for its ground energy and $\psi$ for its positive ground state. The coupled operator is elliptic with a smooth polynomial potential. Local elliptic regularity and the strictly positive heat kernel give a smooth, pointwise positive representative of $\psi$ on the full carrier. By the form argument of Theorem T.5n, $(R-r)\psi$ is a nonzero finite-energy vector, with $r=\langle R\rangle$. Suppose it were an eigenvector of $H-E$ with energy $e>0$. In the local eigenvalue equation the potential and link derivatives commute with $R$. The flat Higgs kinetic term then gives
$$
\frac{\hbar^2}{I_H N}\bigl(d\psi+2y\cdot\nabla_y\psi\bigr)
=-e\bigl(|y|^2/N-r\bigr)\psi .
\tag{T.5o.2}
$$
This computation uses the distributional equation and local smoothness, so no global product of unbounded operators is needed. Evaluate (T.5o.2) at $y=0$. Positivity there gives $er=\hbar^2d/(I_HN)$. The radial differential equation on every ray now integrates to
$$
\psi(W,y)=\psi(W,0)\exp[-e I_H|y|^2/(4\hbar^2)].
\tag{T.5o.3}
$$
Continuity at the origin fixes the integration constant for every ray at the same link configuration $W$. Divide the ground-state equation by (T.5o.3). Its link kinetic and plaquette contributions depend only on $W$. Its Higgs kinetic, link–Higgs and quadratic Higgs terms have degree at most two in $y$. The quartic part is $\lambda\sum_x|\phi_x|^4$ with $\lambda>0$. Along a ray supported at one Higgs site its coefficient of degree four is strictly positive, contradicting the constant eigenvalue. Thus the spectral measure of $(R-r)\psi$ cannot be supported at a single excitation energy. The compact resolvent and the positive gap established on this carrier ensure its weight lies in the positive discrete excitation spectrum. The argument also works for the average across the independent cells, whose connected measure is a positive constant times the one-cell measure.

*Total moment and certification.* Write $H(j_2)=H+j_2 R^2$ and $E(j_2)=\inf\operatorname{spec}H(j_2)$ for a small interval of source coefficients containing zero. The bound $N R^2\le\sum_x|\phi_x|^4$ keeps the common quartic form coercive on a computably chosen interval $|j_2|<\lambda N/2$. The ground state remains simple by positivity improvement. The effective cube and kinetic compression bounds of Theorem T.5m apply to the modified quartic polynomial, with the same tail and form arguments. Concavity and differentiability then give effective enclosures for $E'(0)=\langle R^2\rangle$ by the two one-sided secant slopes as their step tends to zero. Hence $M_0=E'(0)-r^2$ is effective, and the other two moments are effective by Theorem T.5n. Apply Cauchy–Schwarz to $e^{1/2}$ and $e^{-1/2}$ in the positive response measure. Equality would force $e$ constant almost everywhere for that measure, already excluded by (T.5o.2)–(T.5o.3). This proves (T.5o.1), and refining all moment enclosures until the lower bound is positive terminates. These moments test the complete response on the actual finite source. A physical pole assignment and the matching interval of Principle T.6a still require an independent observable and unit map. $\square$

<a id="theorem-t5p"></a>

<a id="theorem-t5p-exact-transition-level-sets-with-unbounded-canonical-radial-scale"></a>**Theorem T.5p (Exact Transition Level Sets with Unbounded Canonical Radial Scale).** Use the bosonic source, marked saddle and kinetic normalization of Theorems T.5g and T.5j–T.5n. Fix the positive bare squared radius \(u\), all kinetic coefficients, the link geometry, the clock and the action \(77/2\). Write \(K_{\rm free}>0\) for the Gauss-projected transition with all spatial potential coefficients set to zero, with the marked boundaries and kinetic density kept fixed. For every prescribed \(0<K_*<K_{\rm free}\) there is a family with all three spatial potential coefficients positive, exact interacting transition \(K_{\rm tot}=K_*\), and unbounded ground-state mean of the canonical radial multiplier \(Q=I_HR/(\hbar T_0)\). Thus the exact transition on the marked saddle and the bare radius in fixed kinetic units do not bound the stationary canonical radius. The construction uses the transition kernel as an input level and the action itself to choose the spatial coefficients.

*Exact transition level.* Let \(P(W)\), \(D(W,y)\) and \(H_u(y)\) be the unweighted sums of plaquette, Higgs link-difference and quartic terms from Theorem T.5g, with nonnegative coefficients \(p,d,\lambda\), respectively. The finite-time kernel \(K_{\rm tot}(p,d,\lambda)\) has a bridge representation after the site Haar average. Equivalently divide it by \(K_{\rm free}\) and use the probability law formed by the free bridge on each cell and the normalized endpoint measure proportional to its free density. The result is the expectation of
$$
\exp\!\left[-\hbar^{-1}\sum_{\rm cells}\int_0^{T_0}
     (pP(W_t)+dD(W_t,y_t)+\lambda H_u(y_t))\,dt\right].
\tag{T.5p.1}
$$
The finite bridge integrals are almost surely finite by continuity. The integrated plaquette sum is strictly positive almost surely. Indeed at any fixed interior time the bridge on the link group has a smooth positive density relative to product Haar. At least one plaquette uses distinct link variables, and fixing three of its links leaves at most a single value of the fourth that gives identity. The zero set of the total plaquette sum therefore has Haar measure zero. Positivity at this interior time gives a positive integral by continuity. This argument also applies to the Haar mixture over endpoints. Dominated convergence gives continuity in all nonnegative coefficients, strict decrease in \(p\) with \(d,\lambda\) fixed, and limit zero as \(p\to\infty\). At \(d=\lambda=0\) there is a unique \(p_0>0\) with transition \(K_*\). Fix two positive values \(p_-<p_0<p_+\). For all sufficiently small \(d,\lambda>0\) the transitions at \(p_-\) and \(p_+\) bracket \(K_*\). Thus there is a unique \(p(d,\lambda)\) in that interval attaining it, and \(p(d,\lambda)\to p_0\) by continuity and strict monotonicity. This uses the free reference only as a comparison. Every family member has positive coefficients and the same classical saddle, whose three spatial potential terms vanish. When \(K_*\) and the other inputs are computable, strict inequalities and the enclosures of Theorem T.5j give a terminating search for arbitrarily narrow rational brackets on the selected \(p\), by enumerating pairs of points with opposite strict inequalities.

*Decoupling estimate for the ground state.* Consider one cell at a time and let \(N\) be its number of Higgs sites. Let \(e_{\rm link}(p)\) be the ground energy of the link kinetic term plus \(pP\) on the complete compact link space. Its ground can be chosen gauge invariant by positivity improvement and simplicity, as in Theorem T.5k. The bosonic Hamiltonian is bounded below in form sense by \(e_{\rm link}(p)+T_H\), with \(T_H=-\hbar^2\Delta_y/(2I_H)\) the full flat Higgs kinetic operator. This uses the nonnegativity of the two remaining potentials. For an upper comparison use the link ground times a normalized smooth compactly supported radial Higgs wavefunction dilated to width \(L\ge1\) in the \(4N\) real Higgs coordinates. It is invariant under site gauge transformations, so is admissible on the actual Gauss sector. Its Higgs kinetic energy is \(C_0 L^{-2}\). Since the links are unitary, \(D(W,y)\le C_1 |y|^2\) uniformly, by bounding the squared difference on every link. Likewise \(H_u(y)\le C_2(1+|y|^4)\) at fixed \(u\). Therefore, for the full ground \(\psi\) at these source inputs,
$$
\langle \psi,T_H\psi\rangle
\le E_{\rm gr}(p,d,\lambda)-e_{\rm link}(p)
\le C_0 L^{-2}+C_3d L^2+C_4\lambda(1+L^4).
\tag{T.5p.2}
$$
All constants are independent of \(p,d,\lambda\). Take \(d=d_0\eta\), \(\lambda=\lambda_0\eta\) for fixed positive coefficients \(d_0,\lambda_0\) in their respective source units. In fixed Higgs coordinates use \(L=\eta^{-1/6}\) for \(0<\eta<1\). The right side is bounded by \(C\eta^{1/3}\). The estimate keeps the full link and Higgs spaces.

For any normalized vector with finite Higgs kinetic and second-position moments, integration by parts in \(y\) and Cauchy–Schwarz give \(4N\le2\|\,|y|\psi\|\,\|\nabla_y\psi\|\). The argument may first use a radial cutoff and pass to the limit by the two finite norms. Hence \(r=\langle R\rangle=\|\,|y|\psi\|^2/N\) obeys
$$
r\ \ge\ \frac{2N\hbar^2}{I_H\,\langle\psi,T_H\psi\rangle}.
\tag{T.5p.3}
$$
The denominator is positive since a nonzero \(L^2\) wavefunction cannot have zero gradient in all Higgs coordinates. Equations (T.5p.2)–(T.5p.3) give \(r\ge c\eta^{-1/3}\) with a fixed \(c>0\).

*Limiting canonical radial law.* Under the unitary dilation \(y=\eta^{-1/6}z\), subtract \(e_{\rm link}(p)\) from the one-cell Hamiltonian and divide by \(\eta^{1/3}\). The result has the exact form
$$
\eta^{-1/3}(H_{\rm link}(p)-e_{\rm link}(p))
 +H_4+\eta^{1/3}\left(d_0D(W,z)-2u\lambda_0 |z|^2\right)
 +\eta^{2/3}\lambda_0Nu^2,\qquad
H_4=-\frac{\hbar^2}{2I_H}\Delta_z+\lambda_0\sum_x|z_x|^4 .
\tag{T.5p.4}
$$
Here \(D\) is homogeneous quadratic. The operator \(H_4\) has a simple positive ground \(\varphi_4\) with energy \(e_4\), positive gap and finite fourth moment by the compactness and positivity argument of Theorem T.5k. Its ground is site-gauge invariant. The trial product of the link ground with \(\varphi_4\) bounds the scaled ground energy above by \(e_4+O(\eta^{1/3})\). The scaled form is bounded below by \(H_4-C\eta^{1/3}(1+|z|^2)\). The quartic term controls \(|z|^4\), since \(\sum_x |z_x|^4\ge |z|^4/N\). Absorbing the negative quadratic term into half of that quartic gives a uniform fourth-moment bound on the scaled ground. Applying the lower bound again, now with a uniform second moment, gives \(\langle H_4\rangle\le e_4+O(\eta^{1/3})\) in that ground. The gap of \(H_4\) then makes the squared norm outside its Higgs ground line \(O(\eta^{1/3})\), by the spectral theorem on the full link–Higgs tensor product. In particular the reduced Higgs state converges in trace norm to the rank-one projector on \(\varphi_4\). For the second moment, truncate \(|z|^2\) at a finite value, use this trace-norm convergence and then use the uniform fourth moment to remove the truncation. This proves
$$
\lim_{\eta\downarrow0}\eta^{1/3}\langle Q\rangle
=\frac{I_H}{N\hbar T_0}\langle\varphi_4,|z|^2\varphi_4\rangle>0 .
\tag{T.5p.5}
$$
The product cell mean has the same limit. The reference inertia, bare radius, geometric ruler and proper clock all stay fixed. The order-parameter map and Planck-scale matching of Principle T.6a require additional information beyond the fixed transition, bare radius and action. \(\square\)

<a id="theorem-t5q"></a>

<a id="theorem-t5q-saddle-germ-and-exact-transition-leave-the-radial-scale-unbounded"></a>**Theorem T.5q (Saddle Germ and Exact Transition Leave the Radial Scale Unbounded).** Fix the marked bosonic carrier, path family, clock, Higgs boundary radius, gauge projection and positive coefficients of Theorem T.5g. Let $K_{\mathrm{orig}}$ be its exact interacting projected boundary transition. There is a family of local, nonnegative, gauge-invariant smooth potentials on the same carrier, each quartic-confining, with the following joint equalities to the original source:

1. The potential agrees with the original potential on one fixed neighborhood of the entire saddle, including its boundary gauge orbit. The action-transport minimum, complete fluctuation operator, ghost quotient, Haar measure, kinetic reference, and the Gaussian coefficient of Theorem T.5l agree.
2. The exact projected boundary transition is $K_{\mathrm{orig}}$. Consequently the exact dimensionless comparison, normalized Gaussian coefficient and full physical-strength transition remainder in (T.5l.3) agree.

The stationary ground-state mean of the canonical radial multiplier $Q=I_HR/(\hbar T_0)$ is unbounded on this family. Thus the complete germ of the marked action, both boundary normalization data and the exact transition together fail to bound the stationary canonical radius in the declared class of local action completions. This comparison keeps the original action transport as a restriction of every completion.

*Local potentials and action transport.* Write $P(W)$, $D(W,y)$ and $H_u(y)$ for the unweighted plaquette, Higgs link-difference and quartic sums of Theorem T.5p. Write $p,d,\lambda>0$ for their original coefficients and $u>0$ for the original bare squared radius. Fix a smooth function $c:[0,\infty)\to[0,1]$ which equals one on a neighborhood of $u$ and vanishes for sufficiently large argument. Fix a second such cutoff on $[0,4]$, with value zero on a neighborhood of zero and strictly positive on a nonempty open interval. Denote it by $f$. For each plaquette with holonomy $W_\square$ put $P_\square=2-\operatorname{Re}\operatorname{Tr}W_\square$ and set $F(W)=\sum_\square f(P_\square)$. The cutoff can be chosen positive on every argument greater than some fixed threshold in $(0,2)$. With $c_x=c(|y_x|^2)$, let
$$
\begin{aligned}
V_{\eta,s}={}&pP(W)+sF(W)
+d\sum_{e=(x,z)}c_xc_z|W_e y_z-y_x|^2\\
&+\lambda\sum_x c_x(|y_x|^2-u)^2
+\eta\lambda\sum_x (1-c_x)(|y_x|^2-u)^2,
\quad 0<\eta<1,quad s\ge0.
\end{aligned}
\tag{T.5q.1}
$$
All terms are finite range and invariant under the original site gauge action. The terms containing cutoffs on $y$ are bounded. The last term gives a quartic lower bound at infinity for every $\eta>0$. The link terms and scalar kinetic operator are those of the original action. In the entire classical path family of Theorem T.5g, all plaquettes are identity and every Higgs radius equals $\sqrt u$. The displayed potential equals the original one in a fixed neighborhood of these configurations, and this property persists under all endpoint gauge transforms. In particular the minimum set, its complete local data, and the original classical transport stay fixed. For the unrestricted boundary variational problem of Theorem T.5i the unchanged kinetic action already supplies its minimum, and the nonnegative potential vanishes on the entire minimizing set. Thus these completions have the same boundary minimizing set and the same Hessian of the full action there. The Gaussian and kinetic comparisons in Theorem T.5l use precisely these data.

*Exact transition constraint.* Use the product free bridge and endpoint measure of Theorem T.5p. The transition $K(\eta,s)$ divided by $K_{\mathrm{free}}$ is the expectation of $\exp[-\hbar^{-1}\sum_{\mathrm{cells}}\int_0^{T_0} V_{\eta,s}\,dt]$. This formula also defines $K(0,s)$. The heat-slice proof of Theorem T.5j applies because these potentials are nonnegative and the norm of their derivative is bounded by a fixed multiple of $1+|y|^3$ on every bounded coefficient set. The flat Higgs bridge has finite moments of all orders, and the link factors are compact. Thus the slice error bound and effective positive enclosures hold also at $\eta=0$. Dominated convergence gives continuity for nonnegative parameters. At $\eta=s=0$ the potential is pointwise at most the original potential. The inequality is strict along bridges having a sufficiently large Higgs radius at an interior time, an event of positive probability by the positive free density. Continuity of each path makes the integrated difference strictly positive there. This yields $K(0,0)>K_{\mathrm{orig}}$.

Let $\mathcal F=\sum_{\mathrm{cells}}\int_0^{T_0}F(W_t)\,dt$. The probability that $\mathcal F>0$ is positive because the intermediate link density is strictly positive and $F>0$ on a nonempty open set. Thus $K(0,s)$ is strictly decreasing. To ensure its limit is below $K_{\mathrm{orig}}$, take a sequence of smooth cutoffs with thresholds tending to zero, each positive above twice its threshold and zero below it. For almost every bridge the total integrated unweighted plaquette action is positive by Theorem T.5p. Continuity then gives at least one positive plaquette value on a nonzero time interval, so the indicators of the events $\mathcal F=0$ converge to zero as these thresholds decrease. Dominated convergence bounds the limiting transition at $s\to\infty$ by $K_{\mathrm{free}}\Pr(\mathcal F=0)$ and gives one cutoff with limit below $K_{\mathrm{orig}}$. An effective choice enumerates such cutoffs and finite rational $s_+>0$ together with their interval precisions until the enclosures certify $K(0,s_+)<K_{\mathrm{orig}}$. The cutoff is thereafter fixed. For all sufficiently small positive $\eta$, continuity gives
$$
K(\eta,0)>K_{\mathrm{orig}}>K(\eta,s_+).
\tag{T.5q.2}
$$
Strict decrease in $s$ gives a unique $s(\eta)\in(0,s_+)$ with the required exact transition. Its effective rational brackets follow from the same strict comparisons as in Theorem T.5p. This construction uses the original transition only, independently of the stationary Higgs radius or the Planck mass.

*Canonical scale.* On a single cell let $e_{\mathrm{link}}(s)$ be the ground energy of the link Hamiltonian with potential $pP+sF$. Its ground state is unique and gauge invariant by positivity improvement on the compact link configuration space. Write $N=|\mathcal V|$ and $T_H=-\hbar^2\Delta_y/(2I_H)$. Each additional term in (T.5q.1) is nonnegative, so $H_{\eta,s}\succeq e_{\mathrm{link}}(s)+T_H$. Use the product trial state with the link ground and a product over sites of normalized smooth compactly supported radial scalar functions, each dilated by $L=\eta^{-1/6}\ge1$ in four real dimensions. The trial lies in the full Gauss sector. Its scalar kinetic energy is $O(L^{-2})$. At one site the probability of the fixed compact cutoff region is $O(L^{-4})$ by the bounded trial density. The bounded Higgs link term vanishes outside the cutoff region of its source site, and the bounded quartic cutoff term has the same probability estimate. The remaining quartic term has expectation $O(\eta(1+L^4))$ by the fourth moment of the product trial. The bounds are uniform in $s$, so the physical ground state $\psi_\eta$ obeys
$$
0<\langle T_H\rangle_{\psi_\eta}
\le E_{\mathrm{gs}}(\eta,s(\eta))-e_{\mathrm{link}}(s(\eta))
\le C\bigl(L^{-2}+L^{-4}+\eta(1+L^4)\bigr)
\le C'\eta^{1/3}.
\tag{T.5q.3}
$$
The uncertainty inequality (T.5p.3) gives $\langle Q\rangle_{\psi_\eta}\ge 2N\hbar/(T_0 C'\eta^{1/3})$. This is the minimizer of the exact static Legendre functional by the same argument as Theorem T.5k. In fact the scaling has an exact limit. Dilate $y=\eta^{-1/6}z$, subtract $e_{\mathrm{link}}(s(\eta))$ and divide the Hamiltonian by $\eta^{1/3}$. Relative to the link Hamiltonian plus the reference quartic oscillator, the additional cutoff terms are nonnegative: the two on-site terms in (T.5q.1) equal $\eta\lambda H_u+(1-\eta)\lambda\sum_x c_x(|y_x|^2-u)^2$. The reference oscillator is
$$
H_4=-\frac{\hbar^2}{2I_H}\Delta_z+\lambda\sum_x |z_x|^4 .
$$
The scaled negative quadratic term is $-2\lambda u\eta^{1/3}|z|^2$ and the residual constant is $\lambda Nu^2\eta^{2/3}$. In the product trial with the link ground and the ground of $H_4$, the scaled positive cutoff terms are $O(\eta^{1/3})$ by the same four-dimensional probability estimate as above. The one-site quartic ground density is bounded by smoothness on the compact cutoff region in the scaled coordinates. This trial gives a scaled energy upper bound $e_4+O(\eta^{1/3})$. The lower form bound by $H_4-2\lambda u\eta^{1/3}|z|^2$ controls the fourth moment uniformly, by absorbing the negative term into half the quartic. Using the bounded second moment in this lower bound then gives $\langle H_4\rangle_{\psi_\eta}\le e_4+O(\eta^{1/3})$ in the scaled variables. The spectral gap of $H_4$ and truncation of the second moment, as in Theorem T.5p, prove
$$
\lim_{\eta\downarrow0}\eta^{1/3}\langle Q\rangle_{\psi_\eta}
=\frac{I_H}{N\hbar T_0}\langle\varphi_4,|z|^2\varphi_4\rangle>0,
\tag{T.5q.4}
$$
where $\varphi_4$ is the normalized ground state of $H_4$. The product cell mean has the same limit. Every derivative of the original action along the saddle and the full transition comparison therefore coexist with arbitrarily large canonical stationary radius. A physical scale relation across these sources must use a source datum beyond those comparisons. $\square$

\in I_Ae^{-\kappa_{EW}}(1+I_R).

The specialization $I_A=\{A_{EW}\}$ and $I_R=\{0\}$ gives the leading central formula. This is a physical scale gate, not a consequence of the finite Steiner theorem or a Gaussian dimension count.

<a id="theorem-t6-electroweak-scale-on-the-full-action-transport-branch"></a>**Theorem T.6 (Electroweak Scale on the Full Action-Transport Branch).** If $\mathfrak C_{A\to\mathrm{St}}$ and $\mathfrak S_{EW}$ are accepted, then

<a id="theorem-t92a-four-family-anomaly-catalog-and-one-loop-gauge-threshold-shift"></a>**Theorem T.9.2a (Four-Family Anomaly Catalog and One-Loop Gauge Threshold Shift).** Work in the family-charge class of Definition R.8.5a.

1. On the SM15 branch with $N=4$, a primitive vector $f\in\mathbb Z^4$ satisfies (P1)--(P3) if and only if, up to permutation and overall sign,
$$
f=(x,-x,y,-y),
\qquad
x\ge1,\quad y\ge0,\quad \gcd(x,y)=1,
\tag{T.9.2a.1}
$$
and then $C_F(f)=2(x^2+y^2)$. On the SM16 branch with $N=4$, (P1)--(P3) select every primitive zero-sum vector.
2. On either branch with $N=4$, the unique minimizer of $C_F$ under (P1)--(P3) is $(1,-1,0,0)$ up to permutation and sign, and every four-family record satisfying (P1)--(P4) obeys
$$
L_b(\mathcal Q)-L_b(f_*)\ \ge\ L_{\mathrm{block}}+L_{\mathrm{mix}}(4)-L_{\mathrm{mix}}(3)\ >\ 0
$$
relative to the selected orbit $f_*=(1,-1,0)$ of Theorem R.8.5b.
3. For $N_g$ complete sequential generations on either branch and $N_H$ Higgs doublets, the one-loop GUT-normalized coefficients are
$$
b_1=\frac43N_g+\frac{N_H}{10},
\qquad
b_2=-\frac{22}{3}+\frac43N_g+\frac{N_H}{6},
\qquad
b_3=-11+\frac43N_g,
\tag{T.9.2a.2}
$$
which reproduce Definition T.15b at $(N_g,N_H)=(3,1)$. Each additional sequential generation retained on the whole running interval of Theorem T.15 raises every $b_i$ by $4/3$, leaves every difference $b_i-b_j$ unchanged, and at fixed matching data raises every $A_i(M_Z)$ of Theorem T.16 by $\frac{2}{3\pi}\ln(\mu_G/M_Z)$. For $N_H=1$, $b_3<0$ holds exactly for $N_g\le8$ and $b_2<0$ exactly for $N_g\le5$.

Every four-family survivor of the anomaly equations therefore lies in the explicit catalog (T.9.2a.1) or, on SM16, in the zero-sum hyperplane; each is PCE-demoted by at least $L_{\mathrm{block}}$, and all carry the same one-loop gauge-coefficient shift. Their heavy-generation decoupling thresholds and Yukawa and mixing entries are flavor-certificate data.

*Proof.* Item 1. Condition (P1) gives $f_4=-(f_1+f_2+f_3)$, and the identity
$$
(f_1+f_2+f_3)^3-f_1^3-f_2^3-f_3^3=3(f_1+f_2)(f_2+f_3)(f_3+f_1)
$$
turns (P2) into $(f_1+f_2)(f_2+f_3)(f_3+f_1)=0$. If $f_1+f_2=0$, then (P1) gives $f_3+f_4=0$; the other two factors give the same form after a permutation. Conversely every vector $(x,-x,y,-y)$ satisfies (P1)--(P2). Primitivity is $\gcd(|x|,|y|)=1$, and a permutation and overall sign bring $(x,y)$ into the displayed range. On SM16 no cubic equation is imposed. Item 2. A nonzero integer vector with zero sum has a positive and a negative entry, so $C_F\ge2$, with equality exactly for one entry $1$, one entry $-1$ and zeros; $(1,-1,0,0)$ also satisfies the SM15 cubic equation. The cost difference is the displayed expression plus $\lambda_F(C_F(f)-2)\ge0$, as in the proof of Theorem R.8.5b. Item 3. The one-loop coefficient of a gauge factor is $-\frac{11}{3}C_2(G)+\frac23\sum_{\mathrm{Weyl}}T(R)+\frac13\sum_{\mathrm{complex\ scalars}}T(R)$, with $T=\frac12$ for fundamentals and $T=\frac35y^2$ for the GUT-normalized abelian factor. One generation contains four $SU(2)$ doublets, three in $Q$ and one in $L$, and four color triplets or antitriplets, two in $Q$ and one each in $u^c,d^c$; this gives $\frac43$ to $b_2$ and $b_3$. Its Weyl components have $\sum y^2=6\cdot\frac1{36}+3\cdot\frac49+3\cdot\frac19+2\cdot\frac14+1=\frac{10}{3}$, giving $\frac23\cdot\frac35\cdot\frac{10}3=\frac43$ to $b_1$, and $\nu^c$ is a gauge singlet. A Higgs doublet contributes $\frac16$ to $b_2$ and $\frac13\cdot\frac35\cdot2\cdot\frac14=\frac1{10}$ to $b_1$, and the gauge terms are $-\frac{22}3$ and $-11$. Theorem T.16 contains $\frac{b_i}{2\pi}\ln(\mu_G/M_Z)$ in $A_i(M_Z)$, so a shift $\Delta b_i=\frac43$ adds $\frac2{3\pi}\ln(\mu_G/M_Z)$. Finally $-11+\frac43N_g<0$ exactly for $N_g<\frac{33}4$, and $-\frac{22}3+\frac43N_g+\frac16<0$ exactly for $N_g<\frac{43}8$. ∎

<a id="proposition-t92b-census-for-every-n-and-the-five-family-charge-chiral-minimum"></a>**Proposition T.9.2b (Census for Every $N$ and the Five-Family Charge-Chiral Minimum).** Work in the family-charge class of Definition R.8.5a on the SM15 branch.

1. For every $N\ge1$, conditions (P1)–(P2) are the equations (1) of Theorem W.14g with $n=N$. Its charts and finite point lists therefore give every nonzero rational solution of (P1)–(P2) up to a nonzero rational multiple and, after gcd normalization, every primitive integer vector satisfying (P1)–(P3).
2. Call a five-family vector charge-chiral when it has no zero entry and no two opposite entries. A nonzero five-family solution of (P1)–(P2) that is not charge-chiral is, up to permutation, $(x,-x,y,-y,0)$. In particular a five-family solution with no zero entry is charge-chiral.
3. Among primitive charge-chiral five-family vectors satisfying (P1)–(P3),
$$
\min C_F=220,
\tag{T.9.2b.1}
$$
attained exactly on the orbit of $f_{\mathrm{ch}}=(-9,-5,-1,7,8)$.
4. Every five-family record satisfying (P1)–(P4) whose charge vector is charge-chiral obeys
$$
L_b(\mathcal Q)-L_b(f_*)\ \ge\ 2L_{\mathrm{block}}+L_{\mathrm{mix}}(5)-L_{\mathrm{mix}}(3)+218\,\lambda_F,
\qquad f_*=(1,-1,0),
\tag{T.9.2b.2}
$$
with equality only on the orbit of $f_{\mathrm{ch}}$.

*Proof.* Item 1. The two equations are literally (1) of Theorem W.14g, whose statement classifies all nonzero rational solutions and all primitive integral solutions of (1) for every $n\ge1$; (P3) is primitivity.

Item 2. If a solution has a zero entry, the other four entries satisfy (P1)–(P2) with $N=4$ and are $(x,-x,y,-y)$ up to permutation by item 1 of Theorem W.14e. If it has two opposite entries, the other three are $(r,t,-r-t)$ with cube sum $-3rt(r+t)=0$, so one of them vanishes and the other two are opposite.

Item 3. Let $f$ be primitive and charge-chiral. Both signs occur because the sum vanishes and no entry is zero. One positive entry against four negative entries is impossible, since $(\sum_ix_i)^3>\sum_ix_i^3$ for positive integers $x_1,\dots,x_4$; four positive entries reduce to this case under $f\mapsto-f$. Hence, after one common sign and a permutation, $f=(-z,-y,-x,a,b)$ with $1\le x\le y\le z$, $1\le a\le b$ and
$$
S:=a+b=x+y+z .
$$
By the Cauchy–Schwarz inequality $a^2+b^2\ge S^2/2$ and $x^2+y^2+z^2\ge S^2/3$, so $C_F\ge5S^2/6$, and $C_F\le220$ forces $3\le S\le16$. With $e_2=xy+xz+yz$ and $e_3=xyz$, the identities $a^3+b^3=S^3-3abS$ and $x^3+y^3+z^3=S^3-3Se_2+3e_3$ turn (P2) into
$$
ab=e_2-\frac{e_3}{S},\qquad (a-b)^2=S^2-4e_2+\frac{4e_3}{S}=:D .
\tag{T.9.2b.3}
$$
In particular $S$ divides $xyz$. For $3\le S\le16$ the triples with $1\le x\le y\le z$, $x+y+z=S$ and $S\mid xyz$, with their values of $D$, are listed below; for $S\in\{3,4,5,7,11,13\}$ there is none.

| $S$ | $(x,y,z;\,D)$ with $S\mid xyz$ |
|:--|:--|
| $6$ | $(1,2,3;-4)$ |
| $8$ | $(2,2,4;-8)$ |
| $9$ | $(3,3,3;-15)$ |
| $10$ | $(1,4,5;-8)$, $(2,3,5;-12)$ |
| $12$ | $(1,3,8;12)$, $(2,4,6;-16)$, $(3,4,5;-24)$ |
| $14$ | $(1,6,7;-12)$, $(2,5,7;-20)$, $(3,4,7;-24)$ |
| $15$ | $(1,5,9;1)$, $(2,3,10;17)$, $(3,5,7;-31)$, $(4,5,6;-39)$ |
| $16$ | $(2,2,12;60)$, $(2,4,10;4)$, $(2,6,8;-24)$, $(4,4,8;-32)$, $(4,6,6;-44)$ |

The rows run over $x=1,\dots,\lfloor S/3\rfloor$, $y=x,\dots,\lfloor(S-x)/2\rfloor$ and $z=S-x-y$, which is the range $1\le x\le y\le z$. Integers $a\le b$ with $a+b=S$ and $(a-b)^2=D$ exist exactly when $D$ is a square of the parity of $S$; this happens only for $(1,5,9)$ with $D=1$ and for $(2,4,10)$ with $D=4$, giving $(a,b)=(7,8)$ and $(7,9)$. The resulting vectors $(-9,-5,-1,7,8)$ and $(-10,-4,-2,7,9)$ have $C_F=220$ and $C_F=250$. The first has gcd one, sum zero, cube sum zero and no opposite pair. Every primitive charge-chiral solution with $C_F\le220$ therefore lies on the orbit of $f_{\mathrm{ch}}$, which proves (T.9.2b.1).

Item 4. The proof of Theorem R.8.5b gives $L_b(\mathcal Q)-L_b(f_*)=(N-3)L_{\mathrm{block}}+L_{\mathrm{mix}}(N)-L_{\mathrm{mix}}(3)+\lambda_F(C_F(f)-2)$; with $N=5$ and $C_F(f)\ge220$, with equality only for $f_{\mathrm{ch}}$, this is (T.9.2b.2). ∎

<a id="theorem-t92c-neutral-threshold-and-mixing-catalog-for-finite-majorana-singlet-extensions"></a>**Theorem T.9.2c (Neutral Threshold and Mixing Catalog for Finite Majorana Singlet Extensions).** Fix the charged Standard Model field and its marked lepton weak frame, an ordinary Spin structure and a supplied Higgs background of nonzero amplitude \(v\). The charged-current source is used with its charged apparatus arm and its conjugate in that source's declared prepared frame. The spectral rest instrument acts on the neutral output at the declared central cut. No negative-energy excitation stock is used.

To include fully dark multiplicities, run the diagonal form of (T.9.2c.6) on all \(4(a+n)\) orthonormal real insertion coordinates of the full neutral rest factor, with their separately paid ports. Their sum is the trace of the real Majorana evolution. In the free energy basis it is \(4\sum_m k_m\cos(mt/\hbar)\), since each mass occurrence has two independent spin excitation modes and each excitation contributes a real two-plane rotation. Taking the trace uses a complete neutral reference and retains the total stock dimension, but an arbitrary enumeration of the unmarked sterile coordinates is only a passive coordinate choice. The trace at all times separates distinct nonnegative energies and their multiplicities by independence of finitely many exponentials. If the source gives an upper rest-energy bound \(E_{\rm cap}>0\), take \(0<\Delta t<\pi\hbar/E_{\rm cap}\). The symmetrized discrete spectral frequencies then lie strictly inside the Nyquist interval, where each nonnegative mass is recovered uniquely from its positive/negative phase pair. A finite Vandermonde or recurrence identity gives the finitely supported spectral measure from enough exact response-law values. Finite empirical counts supply precision and confidence bounds through the actual complete instruments. Once the support is known, the normal and conjugate amplitude laws determine their residue matrices by independence. A positive mass \(m\) gives the physical one-excitation threshold \(E=m\) at rest and the associated \(E(p)\) at each retained momentum. A parity-preserving preparation with a reference excitation keeps that reference's separate energy on its receipt.

One explicit finite instrument supplier uses \(2(a+n)\) genuine rest CAR modes, the disjoint compensation mode, two neutral binary registers for control and durable output, and one owned clock. Give the two binary registers equal degenerate one-excitation drift, with their two ready energies and four rails in the invoice. On each setting allocate one control preparation slot, four controlled slots for \(U_u,F(t),U_v,F(t)^*\) in order, one complete local control basis rotation, one copy and one paid occupation call. This is seven coherent slots and one detector slot. Each coherent slot of duration \(\tau>0\) can use the full dimension \(d_\nu=4\cdot2^{2(a+n)+1}\) including the complete CAR factor and both neutral registers. Supply \(7d_\nu^2\) real Hermitian coefficient entries for the padded implementation and the fixed \(8\tau\) total timing. Use the compensated finite even controls of Definition G.8.5j.7. For a requested endpoint choose the even principal generator \(h\) of its drift-compensated unitary, with \(\|h\|\le\pi\). The positive pulse is \(\hbar\dot s(t')F_0(t')(h+2\pi I)F_0(t')^*\), where \(F_0\) is the literal free drift and \(s\) the duration-\(\tau\) cubic ramp of Theorem G.8.6q.27. Its peak and norm action are bounded by \(9\pi\hbar/(2\tau)\) and \(3\pi\hbar\), respectively, per coherent slot. The active rest drift is bounded by \(2\sum_m k_m m\) plus the two ancillary baselines. The work allocation and actual donor/receiver records use this drift and the same pulse convention. Keep both outcome leaves and unused reserves. The instrument's labelled time \(t\) is the duration parameter of its native propagator. Any actual uncontrolled wait used to realize this propagator is charged at its own duration. A complete neutral reference is an apparatus stock. On ordinary Spin bundles the additional gauge-singlet Weyl fields have vanishing internal gauge and mixed gauge anomaly, and the purely gravitational five-dimensional ordinary-Spin bordism obstruction vanishes. Retaining the same charged sector preserves its admitted gauge and CP records.

*Separated heavy branch.* If \(n>0\), \(\sigma_{\min}(R)>2\|D\|\) suffices to tag exactly \(n\) physical thresholds as heavy. The singular values of (T.9.2c.1) differ from those of \(\operatorname{diag}(0,R)\) by at most the operator norm \(\|D\|\) of the off-diagonal perturbation. The \(a\) lower thresholds are at most \(\|D\|\), and the \(n\) upper ones are at least \(\sigma_{\min}(R)-\|D\|\). The threshold values and weak mixing are the exact Takagi and residue record above. Low-energy matching with finitely many operators and inverse-heavy-scale mass separation use other access contracts. See Broncano et al. (2002) and Grimus and Lavoura (2000).

<a id="theorem-t92d"></a>

<a id="theorem-t92d-threshold-higgs-and-weak-current-catalog-for-down-type-vectorlike-singlet-quarks"></a>**Theorem T.9.2d (Threshold, Higgs and Weak-Current Catalog for Down-Type Vectorlike Singlet Quarks).** Fix the charged Standard Model source and its marked \(a\)-dimensional up-sector weak frame, the standard global group \(S(U(3)\times U(2))\), an ordinary Spin structure, and one supplied Higgs doublet background with nonzero amplitude \(v\). Adjoin any finite number \(n\) of vectorlike quark pairs of type \((\mathbf3,\mathbf1)_{-1/3}\), with the same full right-handed gauge representation as the old down-type right-handed quarks. Assume no additional retained family charge or separately marked singlet basis. Retain the complete quadratic Dirac source, its gauge and linear Higgs responses, coherent weak-current probes in the marked frame, and the full neutral color-contracted threshold response. This class has a complete classification and realization for all \(n\), including rank loss, degeneracies and weak-current-dark heavy modes.

*Actual mass and Yukawa inputs.* The down-type left carrier splits into the \(a\) weak doublet entries and \(n\) weak singlets. Put \(d=a+n\) and let \(P:\mathbb C^d\to\mathbb C^a\) project onto the active rows. In the right-handed carrier the \(d\) entries have identical gauge type. A general admitted one-doublet mass operator in energy units is
$$
M(v)=\begin{pmatrix}vY/\sqrt2\\ B\end{pmatrix},
\qquad Y\in\mathbb C^{a\times d},\quad B\in\mathbb C^{n\times d}.
\tag{T.9.2d.1}
$$
The rows of \(B\) are the general gauge-invariant bare mass terms, including those linking the new left modes to the old right modes. The radial Higgs response is the actual derivative \(J_h=\partial_vM=P^*PM/v\) at fixed \(Y,B\). The weak doublet left inclusion, Higgs and charged-current sources use the same marked active frame. Put \(K=MM^\dagger\), let \(E_\lambda\) denote its spectral projection at \(\lambda\ge0\), and write
$$
\mathcal D=\{(\lambda,k_\lambda,H_\lambda)\},
\qquad
k_\lambda=\operatorname{rank}E_\lambda,\quad
H_\lambda=P E_\lambda P^* .
\tag{T.9.2d.2}
$$
One singular value \(\sqrt\lambda\) gives one physical rest-energy occurrence per fixed spin and color. At physical momentum \(p\) its free excitation energy is \(\sqrt{c^2|p|^2+\lambda}\). Multiplicities refer to the actual Dirac occurrences, with their prescribed spin and color factors retained separately.

*Complete response orbit and realization.* Two packets have the same \(\mathcal D\) in the marked up frame if and only if they are related by passive weak-singlet left rotations and right rotations, in the full gauge-compatible basis class. Write a unitary eigenvector matrix \(U\) of \(K\) by its blocks \(U_\lambda\). The active block \(A_\lambda=PU_\lambda\) has row Gram \(H_\lambda=A_\lambda A_\lambda^\dagger\). Equal Grams and equal \(k_\lambda\) give a block unitary on the \(k_\lambda\) columns: map the row spans isometrically and extend over their equal-dimensional complements. These changes commute with the diagonal matrix of \(\lambda\)'s, and make the two complete eigenvector matrices have identical active rows. Their relative unitary is consequently \(L=I_a\oplus L_s\), \(L_s\in U(n)\). Thus \(K'=LKL^\dagger\). If two square matrices have the same product with their adjoints, their polar partial isometries differ by a right unitary, extended over the equal-dimensional kernels. Hence \(M'=LMR\) for some \(R\in U(d)\). These are precisely the passive rotations which preserve the gauge blocks and the marked weak doublet. Moreover \(P^*P\) commutes with \(L\), so \(J_h'=LJ_hR\) with the same rotations. Conversely such rotations preserve (T.9.2d.2). The calculation includes singular \(M\).

Conversely every finite proposed packet of distinct \(\lambda\ge0\), positive multiplicities \(k_\lambda\), and Hermitian \(H_\lambda\) satisfying
$$
H_\lambda\ge0,\qquad \operatorname{rank}H_\lambda\le k_\lambda,
\qquad \sum_\lambda H_\lambda=I_a,\qquad \sum_\lambda k_\lambda=a+n
\tag{T.9.2d.3}
$$
is realized. Factor each \(H_\lambda=A_\lambda A_\lambda^\dagger\) with exactly \(k_\lambda\) columns. The concatenated matrix has orthonormal rows. Complete it to a unitary \(U\), choose \(M=U\operatorname{diag}(\sqrt\lambda)\) in an admissible right basis, and recover \(Y=\sqrt2\,PM/v\), with \(B\) the complementary rows. The equivalence proof makes this a complete reconstruction within its stated source. A new marked right-handed interaction, independent family charge or second Higgs doublet would break some of the basis freedom and would carry its own response record.

*Same-field mixing and Higgs response.* In a singular-vector basis \(M=U\widehat m V^\dagger\), put \(A=PU\). The extended charged-current mixing is \(A\), up to the simultaneous frame changes already declared. Its neutral weak isospin part on down-type left modes is \(-A^\dagger A/2\), and the charge contribution is scalar on this full charge sector. The right weak isospin vanishes. The radial Higgs matrix is
$$
U^\dagger J_h V=\frac1v A^\dagger A\,\widehat m .
\tag{T.9.2d.4}
$$
Thus the physical charged, neutral and radial matrices all come from the same source derivative and the same retained threshold eigenspaces. At a degenerate threshold their covariant blocks, not individual labelled columns of \(A\), are the invariant data. If \(H_\lambda=0\), that block is dark to the weak-doublet probe but its color/charge field and complete threshold count are retained. The quadratic kinetic and gauge responses are covariant under the same passive left/right basis rotations, including on the complementary fields and their conjugate probes. For any finite allowed instrument word transport its preparation, controls and measured effects by those rotations.
