The two instruments' full output and record distributions then agree by composition. Familiar special cases of the charged and neutral current relations occur in the vectorlike quark models of Botella et al. (2016).

*Physical phase and stock readout.* In the fixed background use the actual finite rest-mode Dirac operator on the full selected field, written for its left and right spinor insertions as the Hermitian matrix
$$
K_D=\begin{pmatrix}0&M\\M^\dagger&0\end{pmatrix}.
\tag{T.9.2d.5}
$$
In the finite native CAR representation its negative-frequency variables are re-expressed using antiparticle creation operators, with the normal-ordered drift nonnegative. Its left-left rest propagator is \(\cos(t\sqrt K/\hbar)\). The weak insertion and its conjugate yield, with the fixed spin and color response factors accounted for, the actual matrix amplitude \(\sum_\lambda\cos(t\sqrt\lambda/\hbar)H_\lambda\). In particular the equal-time response is \(I_a\) by (T.9.2d.3). Hermitian polarization in the active frame separates every matrix coefficient.

Here the physical charged probes are color- and electric-charge compensated. A declared Higgs and gauge reference supplies the weak-frame input, and the down-sector rest insertions are taken in the resulting residual gauge frame. Let \(a_{\ell,\alpha}\) be the left complex charged field insertion for normalized flavor vector \(\ell\) and color \(\alpha\). Its linear CAR evolution can involve antiparticle creation variables. Supply a separate charge-conjugate reference \(b_\alpha\), and form the invariant even arm \(S_\ell^*=(1/\sqrt3)\sum_{\alpha=1}^{3}a_{\ell,\alpha}^*b_\alpha^*\), with adjoint \(S_\ell\). Use the same stationary field state in two actual specimens. On the first prepare the \(b\) reference empty. On the second prepare it filled, together with a disjoint equally sized conjugate partner \(c\) filled. The second state is an even gauge singlet because the two determinant characters cancel. Both stocks, including the unused \(c\) modes in the first specimen, are supplied and retained. Do not drive \(c\). Retain the known common reference phase.

In the empty-\(b\) specimen the expectation of \(S_\ell(t)S_u^*\) gives the color-averaged greater contraction \(\frac13\sum_\alpha\langle a_{\ell,\alpha}(t)a_{u,\alpha}^*\rangle\), after its known reference phase. In the filled-\(b\) specimen the expectation of \(S_u^*S_\ell(t)\) gives the corresponding lesser contraction \(\frac13\sum_\alpha\langle a_{u,\alpha}^*a_{\ell,\alpha}(t)\rangle\) after the same phase correction. To check signs, \(b_\alpha a_{\ell,\alpha}a_{u,\beta}^*b_\beta^*=a_{\ell,\alpha}a_{u,\beta}^*b_\alpha b_\beta^*\), and \(a_{u,\beta}^*b_\beta^*b_\alpha a_{\ell,\alpha}=a_{u,\beta}^*a_{\ell,\alpha}b_\beta^*b_\alpha\). Summing the two actual measured contractions gives the state-independent anticommutator. This supplies actual color-contracted amplitudes.

A finite neutral controlled dilation measures each product. Use the two Hermitian contractions \((S+S^*)/C,\ i(S^*-S)/C\) at \(C=2\sqrt3\). For each contraction \(X\) the unitary with blocks \(X,\sqrt{I-X^2},\sqrt{I-X^2},-X\) has compression \(X\) at the ready work bit. Composing the two dilations on distinct fresh work bits gives the ordered product as the joint ready-block compression. Expand the complex product in these four measured products. Use the finite Heisenberg insertion formed by the actual forward and inverse native rest-propagator endpoints where needed. A neutral control selects the word or identity. A complete control \(X\) or \(Y\) readout measures the corresponding real or imaginary product with no conditioning on the work bits. Keep every work state and both outcomes.

For the full threshold count, use the corresponding complete color-contracted rest insertions on an orthonormal basis of the full left down carrier and sum their diagonal responses. It equals \(\sum_\lambda k_\lambda\cos(t\sqrt\lambda/\hbar)\) after dividing out the known common color and spin factors. The unmarked left singlet coordinates are a basis for this trace, not extra physical labels on the candidate. The full finite stock and its exact response law separate every \(\lambda,k_\lambda\), including poles with \(H_\lambda=0\). If \(E_{\rm cap}>0\) bounds the actual rest energies, use a clock grid of spacing \(0<\Delta t<\pi\hbar/E_{\rm cap}\), so the symmetrized frequencies are unaliased. A finite Vandermonde or recurrence reconstruction then determines the exact discrete frequency measure from sufficiently many exact law values. The active insertion matrix separates the \(H_\lambda\) by the same argument. Actual finite estimates retain their statistical and controller errors. The pair insertion is a local or declared central fixed-frame experiment with explicit reference carriers. No confinement, scattering, or empirical free-quark threshold claim is made.

At one periodic zero-momentum grade the source has \(12d\) independent down-type Dirac rest CAR modes, with two particle and two antiparticle spins per color. Retain the fixed old weak and Higgs supplies as their own paid ports. Each product specimen uses the six conjugate reference and partner modes, two fresh binary work registers, one neutral control and one durable binary outcome. Give the reference and partner modes degenerate native gap \(\varepsilon_r\) per mode. The filled reference specimen supplies \(6\varepsilon_r\), and the empty one supplies zero excitation energy. The four neutral binary registers are independently prepared pairs of rails with fixed positive ready gaps. Use one preparation slot, one forward and one inverse finite rest-propagator slot for the Heisenberg insertion, two controlled square-root-dilation slots, one control-basis slot, one copy slot and one complete occupation call. One product specimen therefore uses seven positive coherent slots of duration \(\tau>0\) and one detector slot of duration \(\tau\). One complete anticommutator setting can use the two reference preparations, four products of Hermitian contractions and two control quadratures, hence sixteen fresh specimens. With all active sectors retained one may allocate dimension \(2^{12d+6}\cdot2^4\) to each coherent slot. Charge its square in native Hermitian channels per slot and the positive offset and switching allocations of Definition G.8.5j.7 and Theorem G.8.6q.27. The detector, idle stocks, recorded phases and actual excitation transfers have separate same-clock receipts. The \(F(t)\) endpoint and its compensated inverse carry their prescribed physical work and timing, even when the encoded interval differs from their synthesis-slot duration.

*Admitted charge and heavy count.* The added Dirac representation descends to the actual global gauge group, since its color/hypercharge representation is the conjugate of the existing \(d^c\) module. Each pair cancels its left and conjugate local anomaly terms and its determinant-line phases on the same ordinary-Spin bundle, with a gauge-invariant vectorlike regulator. It introduces no extra weak-doublet sign. This preserves the fixed old gauge package. If an admitted task additionally requires a nonzero CP witness in the charged quark channel, retain its complete current and threshold criterion on the enlarged response; the anomaly or spectral classification alone does not guarantee that arbitrary \(Y,B\) preserve the old value. For a nonempty \(n\)-row bare block with smallest positive singular value \(b_{\min}=\sigma_n(B)>0\), put \(y=\|vY/\sqrt2\|\). From \(M^\dagger M=B^\dagger B+(v^2/2)Y^\dagger Y\), eigenvalue monotonicity gives at least \(n\) thresholds \(\ge b_{\min}\). The min–max upper bound on the \(a\)-dimensional subspace \(\ker B\) gives all \(a\) lower thresholds \(\le y\). Hence \(b_{\min}>y\) gives an exact gap and exactly \(n\) heavy occurrences. Their actual positions and charged-current weights are measured by (T.9.2d.2). This is a quadratic source threshold and its representation/mixing packet. An interacting renormalization-scheme threshold is a separate matching record.

<a id="theorem-t92e"></a>

<a id="theorem-t92e-joint-response-catalog-for-standard-type-vectorlike-quark-doublets"></a>**Theorem T.9.2e (Joint Response Catalog for Standard-Type Vectorlike Quark Doublets).** Retain the fixed one-Higgs quadratic gauge source, ordinary Spin structure and marked old left doublet frame of Theorem T.9.2d. Adjoin \(n\) vectorlike doublet pairs of type \((\mathbf3,\mathbf2)_{1/6}\), with no additional retained family charges, and retain the full up and down Dirac stocks and the actual charged and neutral weak-current probes. All gauge-invariant quadratic bare terms and Yukawa terms in this class are allowed. There is a complete finite catalog of the resulting mass, weak and linear Higgs responses, including zero modes and degeneracies. Its realization test is a pair of positive matrix and rank conditions on a single left doublet carrier. The catalog is invariant under passive rotations of the new doublets and both right singlet frames and uses the common charged current to compare the two sectors.

*One mass map for each charge and a common bare map.* Write \(L=\mathbb C^a\oplus\mathbb C^n\) for either left charge sector, identified by the charged weak generator. Let \(D=\mathbb C^n\) be the right doublet multiplicity space, also identified between the two charges by that generator. Let \(S_u,S_d\) be the two \(a\)-dimensional right singlet spaces. At the supplied \(v\ne0\) the mass maps \(S_\sigma\oplus D\to L\), \(\sigma=u,d\), are
$$
M_\sigma=[A_\sigma\ \ B],\qquad
A_\sigma=vY_\sigma/\sqrt2,\qquad
J_{h,\sigma}=[A_\sigma\ \ 0]/v .
\tag{T.9.2e.1}
$$
The common \(B:D\to L\) is the gauge-invariant bare mass and can include mixing with the old left doublets. The up Yukawa uses the conjugate Higgs doublet. The weak generator is the identity on \(L\) between the two left sectors and the identity on \(D\) between the right doublets. The right singlets have zero right weak isospin. Thus a passive left rotation must be common and fix the marked old frame. The passive right doublet rotation must also be common. Independent right singlet rotations are permitted. These statements follow by decomposing the charged generator into its doublet and singlet blocks. See Aguilar-Saavedra et al. (2013).

Set \(K_\sigma=M_\sigma M_\sigma^\dagger\) and \(H=BB^\dagger\). The admissible triples are precisely
$$
H\succeq0,\qquad \operatorname{rank}H\le n,\qquad
K_\sigma-H\succeq0,\qquad \operatorname{rank}(K_\sigma-H)\le a .
\tag{T.9.2e.2}
$$
Necessity follows from (T.9.2e.1). Conversely factor \(H\) with \(n\) columns and each \(K_\sigma-H\) with \(a\) columns, including zero columns if required. This realizes the two maps with a common \(B\). If two triples agree in the same \(L\) coordinates, the Gram factors for \(H\) differ by one right unitary on \(D\). The other two factors differ by independent right unitaries on \(S_u,S_d\). These follow by extending isometries on the row spans. If triples agree up to a left unitary fixing the old frame, first use that common left unitary and then the same factor argument. Thus the orbit of the triple is complete, and the radial derivatives transform by the same three right rotations and common left rotation. The reconstruction fixes gauge couplings, including both charged-current maps. Each added doublet is the existing left doublet gauge representation with its opposite-chirality partner. It descends to the same global group, and cancels its vectorlike perturbative and determinant-line anomalies on the same ordinary-Spin bundle. There are two added weak Weyl doublets for each fixed color and pair. A retained additional family charge or additional Higgs source changes the representation or factor problem.

*Finite separating data.* Use the alphabet \((K_u,K_d,H)\) and the isometric inclusion \(E:\mathbb C^a\to L\) of the marked old frame. All matrices are in fixed energy units. For every word \(W\) of length at most \(2(a+n)^2+1\), including the empty word, record
$$
\operatorname{Tr}_L W(K_u,K_d,H),
\qquad E^\dagger W(K_u,K_d,H) E .
\tag{T.9.2e.3}
$$
The two charge sectors use their actual common left weak frame. These data separate the orbits in (T.9.2e.2). To prove this, write \(d=a+n\), and compare two triples of that dimension. The spans of words of length at most \(d^2\) have already stabilized, since the dimension starts at one and a plateau is stable under multiplication by the generators. The Hilbert–Schmidt Gram of these words is specified by the traces in (T.9.2e.3). Equal Grams make the correspondence of words a well-defined trace-preserving linear isometry of the two generated algebras. The inner products of each \(W\) with a generator times any word of length at most \(d^2\) are also specified, by the one additional letter. Hence the isometry intertwines multiplication by the generators. Word reversal gives the adjoint, so it is a unital \(*\)-isomorphism. The trace fixes the multiplicity of each matrix block in its concrete representation, since the trace of a minimal block projection is its multiplicity. Thus the representations are unitarily equivalent.

The marked part can be aligned by first taking the span of vectors \(W E v\) in each representation. The compressed words give their Gram and hence an intertwining isometry carrying the individual marked vectors to their partners. These spans reduce the generated algebras. Subtract their block multiplicities from the trace-fixed full multiplicities to obtain equal multiplicities on the orthogonal complements, so an intertwining unitary there extends the marked isometry to \(L\). The resulting unitary fixes the marked frame after identification. This proves sufficiency of (T.9.2e.3), while its invariance is immediate from common unitary conjugation.

*Physical origin of the separating data.* Let \(\mathcal K_\sigma\) be the self-adjoint finite rest generator of (T.9.2d.5), using \(M_\sigma\) as its upper-right block and \(M_\sigma^\dagger\) as its lower-left block. Let \(P_L\) project onto the left charge block and \(P_D\) onto the right doublets. The latter is determined by the right neutral isospin in either charge block, with the electric-charge term removed. Then the compressed second moments are
$$
K_\sigma=P_L\mathcal K_\sigma^2P_L|_L,\qquad
H=P_L\mathcal K_\sigma P_D\mathcal K_\sigma P_L|_L .
\tag{T.9.2e.4}
$$
The first is read from the left rest propagation and the second from the same propagation with a right isospin insertion between two rest derivatives. For example differentiate \(P_L e^{it\mathcal K_\sigma/\hbar}P_D e^{-is\mathcal K_\sigma/\hbar}P_L\) in \(s,t\) at zero and multiply by \(\hbar^2\). The left charged generator transports the insertions between the up and down blocks. The trace in (T.9.2e.3) uses a complete left-carrier contraction, and the compressed words use the fixed old frame. The common supplied Higgs and gauge references distinguish the charge and chirality ports. Use the color- and charge-compensated rest insertions and Hermitian product dilations of Theorem T.9.2d, iterated with one fresh work register per contraction. A mixed word needs only finitely many rest and current insertions, and a finite uniform clock schedule may use difference quotients of the finite matrices. An upper bound on the rest norms bounds the derivatives of each propagator by the corresponding power of that bound divided by \(\hbar\). Thus finite difference errors can be enclosed before reading the outcomes. Trace contraction can use the uniform mixture over a full left frame with its label retained in the source; the sum is independent of the choice of its unmarked vectors. Charge-conjugate references and neutral controlled dilation are required for these complete-word readouts, as in the preceding singlet branch. All clock, reference, controller and readout costs are on this declared finite source.

The physical free rest thresholds are the singular values of each \(M_\sigma\), obtained from \(K_\sigma\) with its complete multiplicities. If \(B\) is injective and \(\sigma_n(B)>\max_\sigma\|A_\sigma\|\), each charge sector has exactly \(n\) heavy occurrences separated from the \(a\) light ones. The lower bound on the \(n\) largest eigenvalues of \(K_\sigma\) follows from \(K_\sigma\succeq H\). The bound on the \(a\) smallest follows from the min–max principle on \(\ker H\). The response invariants retain the joint weak mixing and the physical radial derivative even when degeneracies or zero singular values prevent labeling individual mass eigenvectors. The shared \(H\) distinguishes this doublet branch from independent down and up singlet additions. The catalog concerns the fixed quadratic source with the stated probes. The full extension universe, a strict family selector and interacting threshold matching lie outside it. \(\square\)

<a id="theorem-t92f"></a>

<a id="theorem-t92f-complete-one-doublet-quadratic-vectorlike-response-catalog"></a>**Theorem T.9.2f (Complete One-Doublet Quadratic Vectorlike Response Catalog).** Fix the ordinary-Spin Standard Model gauge group, the retained old chiral multiplets and frame, one Higgs doublet in its usual complex representation, and its marked nonzero neutral value $h_0=v e_0/\sqrt2$, where $\|e_0\|=1$. Adjoin any finite multiplicities of honest vectorlike Dirac representations of this same global gauge group, with conserved fermion number and without further family, interface or defect marks. Allow every gauge-invariant quadratic bare term and every fermion-number-conserving Yukawa term linear in the real Higgs coordinates. Use the retained gauge-current, chirality, neutral rest and radial Higgs insertions of the finite source, with the gauge and Higgs reference ports and complete compensated word probes of Theorems T.9.2d–T.9.2e. They are compared on one source at the given $v$ in common energy and gauge-current units. Then the complete threshold, gauge mixing, and linear Higgs response on this class is classified by a finite marked matrix-word test, with a necessary and sufficient realization test on each representation stock. This includes joint additions of singlets, standard and exotic doublets and arbitrary other honest representations, including their allowed mixed Yukawa couplings.

*Representation stocks and mass constraints.* Let $L,R$ carry the left and right unitary gauge representations $U_L,U_R$, including the prescribed old multiplets. The additional characters in the two chiralities must agree, as required for a vectorlike extension. Equivalently, enumerate nonnegative multiplicities of irreducible representations with trivial action of the central kernel on $SU(3)\times SU(2)\times U(1)$. For example, with integer abelian weight $q=6Y$, color center exponent $a\bmod 3$ and weak parity $b\bmod 2$, the descent condition is $2a+3b+q=0\bmod 6$. This uses the central generator $(e^{2\pi i/3}I,-I,e^{\pi i/3})$. No bound on a highest weight or multiplicity is required to define the catalog. Every such new pair cancels its local anomalies and its determinant-line anomaly by the conjugate opposite-chirality factor on the same Spin and gauge background. The old admission record is carried on the fixed old stock.

Let $V$ be the four-dimensional real space underlying the Higgs doublet, with real gauge action $D$. With $\mathcal H=L\oplus R$, define the fixed-background mass, rest, and radial operators by
$$
M=B+Y(h_0),\qquad
\mathcal K=\begin{pmatrix}0&M\\M^\dagger&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad
\mathcal J=\begin{pmatrix}0&J\\J^\dagger&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad
J=Y(h_0)/v .
\tag{T.9.2f.1}
$$
Here $B:R\to L$ is a complex-linear gauge intertwiner, and $Y:V\to\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb C}(R,L)$ is real-linear and equivariant. The latter convention includes use of both the Higgs and its conjugate wherever the gauge representations permit them. The action at any Higgs coordinate is recovered from $B,Y$, with radial derivative at the retained background equal to $J$. Bare mixing with old fields is allowed exactly where its intertwiner condition holds. Any prescribed matrix entries of the old source are enforced in its marked frame.

Let $t_{L,j},t_{R,j}$ be the anti-Hermitian generators on $L,R$ for a fixed basis of the gauge Lie algebra, and $d_j$ the real generators on $V$. A proposed pair $(M,J)$ passes the realization test if and only if, for $B=M-vJ$, there are four complex matrices $Y_\mu$ giving a real-linear map $Y$ in a real basis of $V$ such that
$$
t_{L,j}B=Bt_{R,j},\qquad
t_{L,j}Y(w)-Y(w)t_{R,j}=Y(d_jw),\qquad Y(h_0)=vJ .
\tag{T.9.2f.2}
$$
Use the middle equation on the four basis vectors and include any marked old matrix conditions. This is a finite real-linear feasibility problem on each stock. The conditions are necessary by differentiation of gauge invariance. Conversely they integrate to gauge equivariance because the gauge group is connected and the stock has already passed the central descent condition. They give a gauge-invariant local quadratic action with the ordinary-Spin admission just stated. The $SU(2)$ orbit of $h_0$ spans $V$ over $\mathbb R$, since it is the sphere of that nonzero radius. Equivariance therefore makes $Y(h_0)$ injective as data on the space of such maps: if two $Y$ agree at $h_0$, they agree on the orbit and hence on its real span. Thus (T.9.2f.2) gives the full angular and radial Yukawa record from the source's radial measurement and actual gauge action, including multiplicities and cases with vanishing entries.

*Response equivalence.* On $\mathcal H$ take the Hermitian alphabet consisting of $P_L$, $\mathcal K$, $\mathcal J$ and $-i(t_{L,j}\oplus t_{R,j})$ for every generator, with fixed gauge labels. Retain the isometric inclusion $E$ of the marked old frame in the indicated chiral and gauge sectors. After comparing total dimension $d=\dim\mathcal H$ and the ordered marked-frame dimension, two packets are equivalent if and only if they give the same numbers and marked matrices
$$
\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathcal H} W,qquad E^\dagger W E
\quad\text{for every alphabet word $W$ of length at most $2d^2+1$}.
\tag{T.9.2f.3}
$$
Use the empty word as well. The invariant test compares different stocks if needed: equivalence of the generators and chirality recovers the full representation on each side, because its representation of the connected group is fixed by those generators. In particular a response-active dark threshold cannot be removed by a rotation or by dropping a trace multiplicity.

For sufficiency the words of length at most $d^2$ span the generated unital algebra, since the dimension grows by at least one before the first plateau and a plateau is stable under each generator. Trace data give the Hilbert–Schmidt Gram of this span and the matrices of left multiplication by every generator. This identifies the two algebras by a trace-preserving $*$-isomorphism. Each block multiplicity equals the trace of a minimal projection in the block, so the two concrete representations are unitarily equivalent. On the span of all $WEu$, the compressed words specify the vector Gram, including the individual marked vectors. Their matching isometry intertwines all generators, since the spans are reducing and multiplication by a generator on the word span has already been identified. The complementary block multiplicities agree by subtraction from the full trace multiplicities. An intertwiner on the complement extends the marked isometry to a unitary. It is chirality-preserving and intertwines the gauge generators, rest and radial operators. It carries $B=M-vJ$ and the entire $Y$ by (T.9.2f.2). Thus it preserves all the quadratic responses and all declared marks. Conversely such a unitary gives equality of every word datum. This is a finite marked form of the trace test for systems of linear maps (Futorny et al. 2017).

*Thresholds and finite measurements.* The complete rest threshold list is the singular spectrum of $M$, with left and right zero-mode multiplicities retained by $P_L$ and $I-P_L$. Threshold projectors and joint current matrices between their spaces determine weak and other gauge mixing, including degenerate eigenspaces. One can use spectral projections of the Hermitian rest generator and the chirality compression of its square. The full response also retains $\mathcal J$ between these spaces and the angular Higgs vertices fixed by (T.9.2f.2). These records determine all fixed-background quadratic response insertions, rather than just the list of rest eigenvalues.

For each finite stock the action gives finite Hermitian rest, gauge and Higgs insertion matrices in the declared compensated source grammar. The actual radial perturbation of the rest generator is exactly linear in the supplied amplitude, with derivative $\mathcal J$. A labelled gauge rotation and the rest propagation give the current and rest insertions by derivatives at zero on the same reference ports. Chirality is a declared projection. The charge-compensated contractions of Theorem T.9.2d apply also to these finite stocks: retain conjugate references for each chosen representation and the common gauge and Higgs frames, apply the Hermitian product dilation one factor at a time, and contract with the reference at readout. A trace uses the complete normalized left-plus-right mixture and its known dimension; a marked matrix entry uses the named preparations and polarization. Each finite word uses finite work flags and clocks, all charged reference and control inputs being part of that source. Finite difference approximations converge with certified errors from the finite generator norms and the word product estimate. Thus the exact word values are response limits with a finite source of probes at each requested accuracy, even at repeated or vanishing thresholds. The catalog concerns conserved-number quadratic sources with the stated ports. Chiral sequential additions, Majorana couplings outside this class, extra marked symmetries, interacting matching and cross-class selection retain their respective tests. $\square$

<a id="theorem-t92g"></a>

<a id="theorem-t92g-one-higgs-quadratic-weyl-response-catalog"></a>**Theorem T.9.2g (One-Higgs Quadratic Weyl Response Catalog).** Fix the ordinary-Spin global gauge group $G=S(U(3)\times U(2))$, its standard charge normalization, the marked old all-left Weyl stock, and the nonzero Higgs background $h_0=v e_0/\sqrt 2$ of Theorem T.9.2f. Take any finite additional honest all-left Weyl stock, with no extra family, interface or defect action. Allow every Lorentz-invariant quadratic bare term and quadratic fermion term linear in the real Higgs coordinates. The fixed-background rest and radial responses, gauge insertions and marked Weyl frame admit a complete finite equivalence and realization test. On this class the test also gives the full gauge and Yukawa packet, the ordinary-Spin anomaly condition, and the full rest thresholds, including zero modes. It allows chiral stocks, Majorana terms, and mixing between the added and old stocks where the gauge representations permit it.

*Stocks and covariant mass forms.* Let $\mathcal F$ be the complex multiplicity space of all-left Weyl fields, including gauge indices, with unitary action $U$. Enumerate finite multisets of irreducibles of the compact covering group using their two nonnegative $SU(3)$ Dynkin labels, nonnegative $SU(2)$ highest weight, and integral abelian weight $q=6Y$. If the color center acts by $e^{2\pi i a/3}$ and the weak center by $(-1)^b$, the stock descends exactly when $2a+3b+q=0\bmod 6$ on each summand. For the full stock use the finite local anomaly test
$$
[\widehat A(T)\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal F)]_{[6]}=0
\tag{T.9.2g.1}
$$
as an invariant polynomial. Equivalently the cubic gauge tensor and the mixed gauge–gravitational linear trace vanish. These are exact representation checks at the fixed normalization. For this group $\Omega_5^{\mathrm{Spin}}(BG)=0$, so after (T.9.2g.1) the ordinary-Spin four-dimensional fermion determinant has no remaining global anomaly. This is the anomaly gate for the present source, with no inflow or additional tangential or gauge structure. See Davighi et al. (2020).

Write the mass datum as a map into the complex symmetric bilinear forms on $\mathcal F$. Symmetry follows from the antisymmetric two-component spin contraction and fermion anticommutation. On the underlying real Higgs space $V$ with action $D$, the admitted action has mass form $M(x)=B+Y(x)$, where $Y$ is real-linear and
$$
U(g)^{\mathsf T} B U(g)=B,\qquad
U(g)^{\mathsf T}Y(D(g)x)U(g)=Y(x).
\tag{T.9.2g.2}
$$
At $h_0$ set $M=M(h_0)$ and $J=Y(h_0)/v$. Here $M$ has energy units and $J$ is energy per unit Higgs amplitude. A proposed symmetric pair $(M,J)$ is realized exactly when $B=M-vJ$ and the four symmetric matrices of a real-linear $Y$ pass the finite real-linear system obtained by differentiating (T.9.2g.2) on the gauge and Higgs bases, with $Y(h_0)=vJ$. Impose any prescribed old blocks in the marked frame. Since $G$ is connected the infinitesimal equations integrate to (T.9.2g.2). The orbit of $h_0$ under $SU(2)$ spans $V$ over $\mathbb R$, so $Y$ is unique whenever it exists. In particular, the measured radial response and the actual gauge action fix the full angular Yukawa vertex. Gauge, flavor and rest records use this one source and no empirical mass or mixing value enters the test.

*Finite equivalence test.* Let $\mathcal F_{\mathbb R}$ have the real inner product $\operatorname{Re}\langle\ ,\ \rangle$ and dimension $d=2\dim_{\mathbb C}\mathcal F$. Use the real alphabet $A$ consisting of the complex structure $I_c:f\mapsto if$, all realified labelled infinitesimal gauge actions, and the two real-linear operators
$$
C_M(f)=\overline M\,\overline f,\qquad
C_J(f)=\overline J\,\overline f .
\tag{T.9.2g.3}
$$
The first operators are skew-adjoint and the last two are self-adjoint for the real inner product. The old isometry $E$ is realified with its full complex frame and fixed orientation. Fix positive common gauge and Higgs unit conversions when using the alphabet. Compare dimension, every real trace $\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathbb R}W$ and every marked compression $E^{\mathsf T}WE$ for words $W$ in the labelled alphabet and its transposes of length at most $2d^2+1$, including the empty word. Equality of these data is equivalent to a unitary identification of the full all-left source preserving the old frame, gauge action, mass form and radial form. It identifies the stock and the complete action of (T.9.2g.2), including any unmarked mixing.

For sufficiency, complexify the real tuple and frame. The word Gram and left-multiplication argument of Theorem T.9.2f gives a marked complex unitary intertwiner $T$ of the complexified tuples. Write $T=X+iY_1$ in the real coordinates. Both $X$ and $Y_1$ are real intertwiners, with $XE=E'$ and $Y_1E=0$. The real polynomial $\det(X+tY_1)$ is nonzero at $t=i$, so some real $t$ gives an invertible real intertwiner $S=X+tY_1$. Since all transposes are intertwined, $S^{\mathsf T}S$ commutes with the source alphabet. Also $SE=E'$ and $S^{\mathsf T}E'=E$ by unitarity of $T$. The real polar factor $O=S(S^{\mathsf T}S)^{-1/2}$ is therefore orthogonal, intertwines the alphabets, and carries $E$ to $E'$. Commutation with the complex structures means $O$ is the realification of a complex unitary $L$. Intertwining (T.9.2g.3) gives $M'= \overline L M L^\dagger$ and $J'=\overline L J L^\dagger$, the two required unitary congruences. The connected gauge group is reconstructed from its generators and the stock descent. Conversely a marked unitary source identification gives every listed word equality. The bound is finite because words through length $d^2$ span the generated complex algebra, as in Theorem T.9.2f.

*Rest spectrum and physical probes.* At a nonzero supplied Higgs amplitude the Lorentz-invariant two-spin rest Hamiltonian has the symmetric Weyl mass block $M$. Its positive rest thresholds are the Takagi singular values, with all zero modes and multiplicities retained. Equivalently $C_M^2=\overline M M=M^\dagger M$ in the declared complex frame. The eigenvalues of the real self-adjoint $C_M$ pair as $\pm m$ since $I_cC_M=-C_MI_c$. The marked gauge and radial matrix elements between these spectral subspaces give the charged and neutral currents and Higgs mixing, retaining phases and degeneracy blocks. No arbitrary choice of eigenframe in a degenerate block changes the word record. The all-left two-spin model realizes (T.9.2g.3) with the physical rest and radial commutator actions described below.

For the finite zero-momentum source retain both components of every Weyl spinor. In the real Majorana coordinates of $\mathcal F\oplus\mathcal F$, a rest skew generator can be taken, up to fixed spin and Majorana conventions, as
$$
K_M=\begin{pmatrix}0&C_M\\-C_M&0\end{pmatrix}.
\tag{T.9.2g.4}
$$
The rest commutator propagator therefore has physical frequencies $m/\hbar$ and its $(1,2)$ spin block at first order is $C_M/\hbar$. To obtain this form, write the spin-singlet pairing between the two spin components. Its skew complex matrix is $J_{\mathrm{sp}}\otimes\overline M$ in spin-block ordering, with $J_{\mathrm{sp}}=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}0&1\\-1&0\end{smallmatrix}\right)$. The commutator acts by this matrix on conjugate coordinates, with the common phase fixed by the Majorana and Heisenberg convention. A phase $i$ from using the creation operator convention for the pairing Hamiltonian is absorbed by a fixed common phase change of the Majorana coordinate, which commutes with the represented gauge and complex structure and applies to both $M$ and $J$. The actual radial Higgs insertion is the derivative $K_J$ of this same rest generator. The complex structure is measured by the common phase rotation of the prepared Weyl modes in their kinetic frame. This is an external phase control of the probes, and may fail to commute with the mass action. Gauge generators act complex-linearly on each spin block. The spin frame and the chosen ordered two spin blocks are common supplied references. The coefficient of a gauge-generator time or angle is calibrated at the same gauge-current port as in Theorem T.9.2f.

Here is an even finite implementation of the trace word responses. Let $m=2d$ be the real dimension of the spin-doubled one-particle coordinate, and $\gamma_a,\eta_a$ the Majorana generators of source and conjugate reference, with joint canonical CAR. Identify the reference by the real form of conjugation, so both sets of real labels transform by the same orthogonal gauge matrix. Then
$$
F=\frac{1}{m}\sum_{a=1}^{m}i\gamma_a\eta_a
$$
is gauge invariant, even, traceless and has norm at most one. Start with the normalized identity on the complete joint Fock carrier. Make the binary instrument with effects $(I\pm F)/2$ and their positive-square-root Kraus operators. Keep both outcomes, with sign $X$. After this instrument apply the source evolution while compensating the reference drift on its own paid support. If the source Majorana propagator is $R$, then a second measurement of $F$, with sign $Z$, gives $\mathbb E[XZ]=\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathbb R}R/m^2$. Indeed the unnormalized prepared difference is $F/D_{\rm F}$ for the full Fock dimension $D_{\rm F}$, and the $i\gamma_a\eta_b$ are orthonormal for the normalized real trace pairing. This is an unconditional even correlation with a finite dilation. Each binary instrument has a controlled pointer rotation with bounded angle, obtained by functional calculus of its even effect, so its finite implementation preserves parity and the compensated gauge action.

For a real matrix $A$ of marked-frame contractions use $F_A=\sum_{a,b}A_{ab}i\gamma_a\eta_b$ with a fixed norm majorant at the last instrument. The same trace identity now gives the corresponding marked matrix entry of $R$ with its known scalar factors. In particular a pair of real columns of the marked old isometry gives the required rank-one contraction. Its labels and any charged or spin-nontrivial coefficient are supplied by the retained conjugate gauge and spin frame ports of Theorem T.9.2f. The readout transforms with those physical frame inputs, while the unmarked trace above is invariant without a chosen new Weyl frame. Inserting a labelled gauge rotation or the external Higgs background uses those same frame inputs. Equivalence of the catalogue concerns their declared compensated response, including the marks and the fixed gauge labels.

Every finite skew generator $K$ has the even quadratic lift $(i\hbar/4)\sum_{a,b}K_{ab}\gamma_a\gamma_b$, with sign fixed by the chosen conjugation order. Its norm is bounded by $(\hbar/4)\sum_{a,b}|K_{ab}|$. The physical source rest control is the fixed source Hamiltonian with (T.9.2g.4) in the commutator, and the radial port varies the same $h_0$ by the stated physical amplitude. For an evolution time $t$ the difference-quotient error for a fixed generator $K$ is bounded by $|t|\|K\|^2e^{|t|\|K\|}/2$. The two specified nearby radial amplitudes give $K_J$ by difference divided by their physical amplitude difference, since the rest generator is affine in amplitude. A fixed physical spin-frame rotation $J_{\mathrm{sp}}^{-1}$ multiplied after the differentiated rest response yields $I_2\otimes C_M/\hbar$, and does the same for $C_J/\hbar$ on the radial insertion. Gauge and complex phase generators already have two identical spin blocks. Hence traces and marked compressions of the alphabet words are obtained by expanding products of those finite-difference operators and measuring the resulting finite linear combinations of propagator-word correlations. For the trace divide the two-spin real trace by two. For marked compressions use the declared marked frame on one spin block. Transposes of the alphabet are already specified by their adjoint signs. The error of each finite word follows by the telescoping product bound. This uses the full Fock sources, finite flags, reference, preparations and readouts, all at bounded Hamiltonian norm and finite clock duration for each specified accuracy. Exact word equivalence is a response-limit classification with an effective finite error bound, with finite separating precision for any fixed unequal datum.

For a concrete extension outside the conserved-number Dirac branch and the gauge-singlet type-I branch, add one left-Weyl $(\mathbf1,\mathbf3)_0$. It descends, has zero local anomaly and passes the ordinary-Spin gate (T.9.2g.1). Its real weak-triplet form admits a nonzero symmetric bare Majorana mass, and the lepton-doublet and Higgs product has a triplet component with net abelian charge zero, allowing its linear Yukawa coupling to this triplet. The declared weak-current probes see its triplet weights even when that Yukawa coefficient vanishes. This branch and its mixed stocks are included without changing the anomaly condition on the old stock. The finite probes realize the prepared external-background response. Construction of a dynamical local chiral gauge regulator is a separate requirement beyond the anomaly test. $\square$

<a id="theorem-t92h"></a>

<a id="theorem-t92h-polynomial-multi-higgs-weyl-catalog-with-marked-non-abelian-family-factors"></a>**Theorem T.9.2h (Polynomial Multi-Higgs Weyl Catalog with Marked Non-Abelian Family Factors).** Fix the ordinary-Spin product gauge group
$$
G_f=S(U(3)\times U(2))\times \prod_{a=1}^{f}SU(2)_{F,a}
$$
for any finite $f\ge0$, with the factors separately marked and no additional center identification. Fix a finite marked real orthogonal bosonic representation $V$ of this group, a supplied background $h_0\in V$, a nonnegative degree cap $p$, and the marked old Weyl frame with its prescribed representation and mass coefficients. Keep the canonical Weyl kinetic term of Theorem T.9.2g. Admit arbitrary finite honest all-left Weyl stocks and every Lorentz-invariant, derivative-free fermion-bilinear mass polynomial in $V$ of degree at most $p$. The Higgs coordinates are prepared background ports with fixed units and frame. The gauge representations, mass polynomials, physical rest thresholds, gauge and Higgs mixing and all retained compensated quadratic responses have the complete equivalence and realization tests below. This includes any finite collection of Higgs representations and all mass terms of the stated degree, including those involving distinct Higgs fields.

*Exact ordinary-Spin admission.* Enumerate the finite multisets of covering-group irreducibles by the labels of Theorem T.9.2g and the $f$ additional nonnegative family highest weights $n_a$. Each color, weak and hypercharge triple descends precisely when it passes the same modulo-six test of that theorem. There is no center quotient on the family factors. For the full stock $\mathcal F$, require the polynomial
$$
[\widehat A(T)\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal F)]_{[6]}=0
\tag{T.9.2h.1}
$$
as an invariant polynomial on the full gauge and tangent algebra. Besides the original terms this includes the mixed hypercharge and family-quadratic terms for each family factor. All other cross terms involving a single traceless generator on a simple factor have zero trace. The complete remaining anomaly tests are the $f$ mod-two equations
$$
\sum_j m_j\,\dim U_j
\left(\prod_{b\ne a}(n_{j,b}+1)\right)
\frac{n_{j,a}(n_{j,a}+1)(n_{j,a}+2)}{6}=0\pmod 2
\quad (1\le a\le f).
\tag{T.9.2h.2}
$$
Here $j$ labels the distinct irreducibles, $m_j$ is the multiplicity and $U_j$ is the electroweak-color irreducible, including its hypercharge. The fraction is the normalized instanton index of the family representation of highest weight $n_{j,a}$.

For completeness, for connected based classifying spaces $X,Y$ the stable product splitting has reduced summands $X$, $Y$, and $X\wedge Y$. It follows by splitting the inclusion of the wedge using the two projections after stabilization. Reduced $B S(U(3)\times U(2))$ starts in cell degree two since the group is connected, and reduced $BSU(2)$ has first cell in degree four, by $BSU(2)\simeq\mathbb{HP}^\infty$. Every smash summand involving a family factor and at least one other factor therefore starts in degree at least six. Connective Spin bordism gives no such summand in degree five. The pure electroweak-color summand vanishes by Theorem T.9.2g, and the point group in degree five vanishes. For each family factor its first cell is the degree-four sphere and its next cell is in degree eight, so its reduced degree-five group is $\Omega_1^{\mathrm{Spin}}=\mathbb Z/2$. A unit instanton on $S^4$ times the periodic Spin circle gives its generator. Hence $\Omega_5^{\mathrm{Spin}}(BG_f)=(\mathbb Z/2)^f$, with inclusions of the individual family factors supplying generators. Restriction of the Weyl stock to such a generator has the spectator multiplicity in (T.9.2h.2), and its sign is the four-dimensional instanton index modulo two. Thus (T.9.2h.1)–(T.9.2h.2) are necessary and sufficient for the ordinary-Spin determinant anomaly gate, on the stated product group and with no inflow. The smooth background Higgs values add no gauge anomaly, since the linear Higgs representation has an equivariant contraction to zero and the gauge representation of the fermions stays fixed. See Davighi et al. (2020) and Wang et al. (2019, §2).

*Exact polynomial realization and invisible directions at a single background.* Let $\mathcal F$ carry the full representation $U$. Symmetry of the Weyl mass form follows from the two-spin pairing as in Theorem T.9.2g. Write
$$
M(x)=\sum_{d=0}^{p}Y_d(x,\ldots,x),\qquad
Y_d\in\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb R}\!\left(\operatorname{Sym}_{\mathbb R}^d V,
\operatorname{Sym}_{\mathbb C}^2\mathcal F^*\right).
\tag{T.9.2h.3}
$$
Impose the finite real-linear system
$$
dU(\xi)^{\mathsf T}Y_d(v_1,\ldots,v_d)
+Y_d(v_1,\ldots,v_d)dU(\xi)
+\sum_{i=1}^d Y_d(v_1,\ldots,dD(\xi)v_i,\ldots,v_d)=0 ,
\tag{T.9.2h.4}
$$
on the fixed gauge and Higgs bases. Include the marked old coefficient conditions. Here $D$ is the given bosonic representation. Connectedness and polarization make these equations equivalent to $U(g)^{\mathsf T}M(D(g)x)U(g)=M(x)$ at every $x$. Thus this is an exact finite realization system, also for a proposed list of radial or mixed Higgs probes, which impose additional linear constraints on the same coefficients. There is no restriction on zero or degenerate Takagi masses and no required alignment of the Higgs directions.

More precisely, let $\mathcal P$ be the real vector space of admitted coefficient differences at fixed stock and old marking. For any prescribed sample values or derivatives, the exact invisible subspace is the kernel of the corresponding evaluation map on $\mathcal P$. For a restriction to a radial ray through $h_0$ one may use $Y_d(h_0,\ldots,h_0)$, separated by their distinct powers of the radial coordinate. Gauge covariance transports these values throughout its gauge orbit and adds no independent sample. In general the kernel is nonzero. For example, at $f=1$ take two old-neutral family-doublet left Weyl fields $\psi_1,\psi_2$, a family triplet Higgs $H$, and a family singlet $s$. Their two doublets cancel the family parity, with all other gauge charges zero. For $SU(2)$ the triplet times the alternating tensor is symmetric in two doublet indices, so the term $s\,\psi_1^{\mathsf T}(\epsilon H)\psi_2$ with the antisymmetric two-spin contraction is a degree-two mass term. The opposite block is its transpose, as in (T.9.2h.3). Choose a background with $H=0$ and $s\ne0$. The term vanishes throughout the radial ray and its gauge orbit, while a transverse triplet control with $s\ne0$ measures it. This gives inequivalent quadratic fermion sources at $p\ge2$ with the same radial and gauge response data at that background. For example the zero mass polynomial and one with just this term are distinguished by a nonzero rest threshold at a triplet sample. The example also exhibits a genuinely mixed non-Abelian family and multiple Higgs interaction.

*Finite calibration grid and marked equivalence.* Choose a labelled basis $v_1,\ldots,v_m$ of $V$ with physical unit steps $\ell_i v_i$, where $\ell_i\ne0$, and sample at the fixed grid
$$
\mathcal X=\left\{h_0+\sum_{i=1}^m j_i\ell_i v_i:\ 0\le j_i\le p\right\}.
\tag{T.9.2h.5}
$$
For $m=0$ use the single background. Each coordinate polynomial has degree at most $p$ separately in each variable. Ordinary Vandermonde interpolation in each coordinate reconstructs it from this grid. The same conclusion holds if small physical steps are chosen, since the grid remains unisolvent and its calibrated finite inverse is known. In particular there is an exact finite consistency test on proposed mass samples: interpolate, check the total-degree cap, the transpose symmetries and the covariance and old-frame system (T.9.2h.4). Conversely each passing sample list defines the unique admitted mass polynomial in that frame.

Use the real alphabet of the complex structure, all labelled realified gauge generators, and all $C_{M(x)}$ with $x\in\mathcal X$, where $C_{M(x)}(f)=\overline{M(x)}\,\overline f$. Include the realified old frame. If $d_{\mathbb R}=\dim_{\mathbb R}\mathcal F_{\mathbb R}$, compare the dimensions, unmarked real traces and all marked compressions for words in this alphabet and its transposes of length at most $2d_{\mathbb R}^2+1$. The real marked-word argument of Theorem T.9.2g applies to this finite enlarged alphabet. Thus equality is exactly an orthogonal intertwiner preserving the old frame and the complex structure. It gives a complex unitary identification of the Weyl stock, all marked gauge generators, and each symmetric sample by congruence. Congruence is real-linear in the sample, so interpolation gives the same identification of every polynomial coefficient. Conversely a marked source identification gives every word equality. The sample, gauge, and frame labels are kept throughout. With polynomial data and gauge stock fixed the rest thresholds and all quadratic responses at every other background are determined. In particular the classification does not lose a coefficient whose first derivative at $h_0$ vanishes.

*Physical threshold, current and Higgs packet.* Use the same two-spin rest generator $K_{M(x)}$ and finite even compensated CAR probes of Theorem T.9.2g for each prepared background $x$ in the grid. They act on one full spin-doubled fermion carrier, with the retained conjugate frame and both binary outcomes. All gauge, including family, controls are the labelled generators with their independent physical normalizations. The common spin-frame rotation converts the differentiated rest propagator to $C_{M(x)}/\hbar$ as in that theorem, so no separate fitted generator is used. The exact polynomial interpolation is a finite linear combination of these sampled responses. The propagated error for a reconstructed coefficient is bounded by the sum of the sample errors times the absolute interpolation coefficients. For an alphabet word the same telescoping product bound gives a specified finite error, with bounded Hamiltonian and finite retained clocks for every accuracy. This obtains each trace and marked word entry and a finite separating precision for every fixed inequivalent record.

At $h_0$ the rest thresholds are the Takagi singular values of $M(h_0)$, with all zeros, degeneracies and marked threshold subspaces. The physical Higgs insertion in direction $v$ is $K_{\partial_v M(h_0)}$ with the same rest-generator convention. Higher mixed insertions are the corresponding derivatives of (T.9.2h.3). Projecting those operators and the gauge currents to the spectral subspaces gives the Yukawa, higher Higgs and current mixing matrices in the marked kinetic frame. In a degenerate space the marked word test retains the complete joint operator data. Thus the threshold, mixing, response-equivalence and anomaly packet is populated for each admitted record in this polynomial class. The bosonic representation and controls are part of the supplied external-background source. A dynamical chiral gauge regulator, interacting higher fermion terms, other global forms and a selector between extension classes require further source tests. $\square$

<a id="theorem-t92i"></a>

<a id="theorem-t92i-weyl-response-and-anomalies-with-correlated-family-centers"></a>**Theorem T.9.2i (Weyl Response and Anomalies with Correlated Family Centers).** Let the marked covering gauge group be
$$
\widetilde G=\prod_{a=1}^{c}SU(N_a)\times\prod_{j=1}^{s}SU(2)_j\times T,
\qquad N_a\ge3,\qquad T=U(1)^t,
$$
with finite $c,s,t\ge0$. Let $G=\widetilde G/\Gamma$, where $\Gamma$ is a finite central subgroup whose projection to $T$ is injective. All such marked quotients are obtained by choosing a finite subgroup $A\subset T$ and a homomorphism from $A$ to the product of the semisimple centers, then taking its graph. Keep an independent ordinary Spin structure, the canonical Weyl kinetic term, any compatible marked old stock, and the finite marked polynomial Higgs-background and mass-polynomial grammar of Theorem T.9.2h. For every such quotient, the exact gauge admission tests, complete finite response equivalence, threshold, Higgs and mixing packets are as follows.

An irreducible stock species is specified by its covering highest weights and its marked integer torus weight. It descends precisely if its product central character is trivial on every generator of $\Gamma$. This test also applies to irreducible summands of the complexified bosonic representation. Let $\epsilon_j:\Gamma\to\{1,-1\}$ be the projection to the center of $SU(2)_j$. Then
$$
\Omega_5^{\mathrm{Spin}}(BG)\simeq\bigoplus_{j:\epsilon_j=1}\mathbb Z/2.
\tag{T.9.2i.1}
$$
The summand at $j$ is generated by the image of a unit $SU(2)_j$ instanton on $S^4$ times a periodic Spin circle, with the other covering fields trivial. For a finite honest all-left complex Weyl stock $\mathcal F$ the complete anomaly gate is
$$
[\widehat A(TX)\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal F)]_{[6]}=0,
\qquad
\sum_i m_i d_{i,\ne j}\frac{n_{ij}(n_{ij}+1)(n_{ij}+2)}6=0\pmod2
\quad\text{for all }j\text{ with }\epsilon_j=1 .
\tag{T.9.2i.2}
$$
Here $i$ runs over irreducible species, $m_i$ is its multiplicity, $n_{ij}$ is its $j$th $SU(2)$ highest weight, and $d_{i,\ne j}$ is the dimension of its tensor product of all other semisimple factors. The first equality is an invariant-polynomial identity on the entire tangent and gauge algebra, including all mixed torus terms. The admission statement concerns the ordinary-Spin fermion determinant with no compensating inflow.

*Cohomology of the actual quotient.* Set $T'=T/A$. The projection $G\to T'$ has kernel the embedded product of the simply connected simple factors, by injectivity of $\Gamma\to T$. Every character of $A$ extends to a character of $T$: the map of integer character lattices for the finite torus cover $T\to T'$ has finite cokernel, and its Smith normal form identifies the cokernel with the characters of $A$. Twist each covering fundamental by a torus character inverse to its central character on the graph. This constructs an honest unitary bundle $E_a$ for every $SU(N_a)$ and $F_j$ for every $SU(2)_j$, each restricting to the defining bundle on its own fiber factor and trivial bundles on the other fiber factors. If $x_1,\ldots,x_t$ are the degree-two integral classes from a character basis of $T'$, the bundle of $F_j$ has
$$
\ell_j=c_1(F_j)=c_1(\chi_j^2)\in\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb Z}\{x_1,\ldots,x_t\},
\tag{T.9.2i.3}
$$
where $\chi_j$ is the twisting character of $T$ and its square descends to $T'$. In particular $\ell_j=0\pmod2$ exactly when $\epsilon_j=1$. Indeed if $\chi_j^2$ has a square root in the character group of $T'$, its pullback must be $\chi_j$ by torsion-freeness of the character group of $T$. In the other direction $\epsilon_j=1$ makes $\chi_j$ itself descend. The same argument shows that changing the twist changes $\ell_j$ by an even class.

The fibration of classifying spaces over $BT'$ has trivial integral local system. Leray–Hirsch applies because monomials in the $c_k(E_a)$ for $2\le k\le N_a$ and $c_2(F_j)$ restrict to the integral polynomial monomial basis on the fiber, degree by degree. Consequently the integral and mod-two cohomology rings are polynomial in these classes and the $x_i$ with their respective coefficients. The integral homology is free in even degrees and zero in odd degrees, by the same even-degree free calculation or the integral homology spectral sequence. Write $u_a=c_2(E_a)$, $v_a=c_3(E_a)$ and $w_j=c_2(F_j)$ in mod-two cohomology.

*Degree-five Spin bordism.* The only possibly nonzero term of total degree five in the Spin Atiyah–Hirzebruch spectral sequence is $E^2_{4,1}=H_4(BG;\mathbb F_2)$. The outgoing $d_2$ is dual to $\mathrm{Sq}^2$ on $H^2$, and the incoming $d_2$ is dual to $\mathrm{Sq}^2$ on $H^4$ after mod-two reduction of integral degree-six homology. This reduction is onto. Thus the dual surviving space in this term is the kernel of $\mathrm{Sq}^2:H^4\to H^6$ modulo the image from $H^2$. All following computations are over $\mathbb F_2$:
$$
\begin{split}
\mathrm{Sq}^2x_i&=x_i^2,\
\mathrm{Sq}^2(x_ix_k)&=x_i^2x_k+x_ix_k^2\quad(i<k),\
\mathrm{Sq}^2u_a&=c_1(E_a)u_a+v_a,\
\mathrm{Sq}^2w_j&=\ell_j w_j .
\end{split}
\tag{T.9.2i.4}
$$
The last two lines are the Chern class identity $\mathrm{Sq}^2c_2=c_1c_2+c_3$, with $c_3(F_j)=0$. Each color term has its own independent $v_a$. Each nonzero $\ell_jw_j$ uses its own generator $w_j$, regardless of relations among the $\ell_j$. The distinct mixed torus monomials also have independent images. The squares $x_i^2$ are killed on passage to the quotient by the image from degree two. The remaining basis is exactly the $w_j$ for which $\epsilon_j=1$. No higher differential can enter this term. The outgoing $d_3$ has zero target, and the outgoing $d_4$ has free integral target $E^4_{0,4}$, hence vanishes on its two-torsion source. This proves (T.9.2i.1) with no extension problem, since there is one filtration degree. The indicated embedded instanton times circle pairs with its own $w_j$ and vanishes against the other basis elements by restriction to the simple factor, proving the generator assertion. The Spin spectral sequence conventions and Chern class operation agree with Davighi et al. (2020, §§3–4).

When the local polynomial vanishes, the exponentiated reduced $\eta$ invariant of the whole stock is a character on this bordism group. On each generator it is the sign of the four-dimensional instanton index. Restricting the irreducible to that factor gives the spectator dimension in (T.9.2i.2), and the index in the normalization of a fundamental doublet is $n(n+1)(n+2)/6$. This proves necessity and sufficiency of the two tests. The linear Higgs representation adds no obstruction because equivariant contraction retracts it to zero. In particular, a shared torus tying several $SU(2)$ signs removes every tied Witten summand, even if the sign characters coincide. See Wang et al. (2019, §2).

*Finite physical response catalog.* Enumerate every finite stock by the covering highest weights, integer torus charges and multiplicities, keeping the marked old frame and the honest descent and anomaly filters above. For a supplied real bosonic representation, Higgs degree bound and old polynomial coefficients, the tensors (T.9.2h.3) are exactly the real-linear solutions of (T.9.2h.4) with the Lie algebra of $G$ in those equations. Honest descent fixes the action of the quotient and connectedness makes Lie algebra covariance equivalent to group covariance. The labelled grid (T.9.2h.5) reconstructs the allowed polynomial. The marked word test of that theorem uses the realified generators of all marked simple and circle factors, the complex structure, and the symmetric mass samples on the grid. The separating intertwiners commute with the full connected group since they intertwine its Lie algebra. Every resulting catalog entry has physical rest thresholds from the Takagi singular values, complete gauge and Higgs mixing data from the corresponding spectral projections, and the marked CAR comparisons of T.9.2h on the same rest generators. This proves complete realization and equivalence on the stated polynomial source, including zero masses, degeneracies and charged sterile or vectorlike fields. A bound on the total stock dimension together with a bound on the integer charge coordinates gives a finite stock menu by the dimension formula, with continuous allowed coefficient families retained as such.

Distinct marked quotients are distinguishable if the comparison includes their allowed Wilson characters on the covering center. The annihilator of a finite subgroup in the character group of the covering center determines it. Every such character is realized as the central character of a covering irreducible, by choosing the prescribed center class of each simple-factor highest weight and the indicated torus weight. Thus any two distinct marked subgroups differ on the descent of some finite representation. This tests the global form when the corresponding line stock is registered. The local finite CAR packet above compares matter and Higgs responses at each supplied global form.

<a id="theorem-t92j"></a>

<a id="theorem-t92j-diagonal-family-center-blocks-and-their-weyl-anomalies"></a>**Theorem T.9.2j (Diagonal Family Center Blocks and Their Weyl Anomalies).** Let $H$ be any marked gauge group of Theorem T.9.2i. In addition take any finite number $b$ of marked blocks
$$
D_{m_i}=SU(2)^{m_i}/\langle(-I,\ldots,-I)\rangle,\qquad m_i\ge1,
\qquad G=H\times\prod_{i=1}^b D_{m_i}.
$$
The factors in each block are independently labelled. This includes $D_1=SO(3)$ and $D_2=SO(4)$ as well as a common diagonal sign on arbitrarily many family factors. Keep independent ordinary Spin and the finite polynomial background and Weyl source of Theorem T.9.2h. In block $i$ an irreducible with highest weights $n_{i,1},\ldots,n_{i,m_i}$ descends exactly when their sum is even. Let $a_i$ and $u_i$ be the pullbacks of $w_2,w_3$ from the first marked adjoint three-plane of that block. Then
$$
\Omega_5^{\mathrm{Spin}}(BG)\cong
\Omega_5^{\mathrm{Spin}}(BH)\oplus(\mathbb Z/2)^{\binom b2} .
\tag{T.9.2j.1}
$$
The second summand is detected by the numbers $\langle a_i u_j,[Y]_2\rangle$ for $i<j$. Every honest complex Weyl stock with vanishing local anomaly polynomial has trivial character on these mixed generators. Thus exact determinant admission requires the full local polynomial on $G$ and just the surviving Witten parity rows of $H$ in Theorem T.9.2i, with the extra block dimensions included as spectator multiplicities. This gives the complete finite threshold, Yukawa, mixing and marked response-equivalence packet on the declared background source.

*Low-degree classes of a block.* Projection to the first adjoint factor gives $D_m\to SO(3)$ with kernel the other $m-1$ copies of $SU(2)$. There is a group section sending a class in $SO(3)$ to the class of the diagonal tuple of either lift. For each $k>1$ the action $q\mapsto g_k q g_1^{-1}$ on the quaternions gives an oriented real four-plane representation $V_k$. Its Euler class $e_k$ restricts to a generator on the $k$th kernel factor and to zero on the others, since its restriction to the $k$th factor is the underlying oriented real four-plane bundle of the complex fundamental of rank two. Products of the integral Euler classes restrict to the monomial basis on the kernel classifying space. Leray–Hirsch over the simply connected base $BSO(3)$ gives the integral and mod-two cohomology as polynomial extensions of the corresponding rings of $BSO(3)$ by these classes. In particular the mod-two ring is $\mathbb F_2[a,u,\bar e_2,\ldots,\bar e_m]$, where $a=w_2$, $u=w_3$ of the first adjoint bundle and $\bar e_k$ is the reduction of $e_k$.

One has $w_2(V_k)=a$. Indeed the kernel factors have vanishing second cohomology on their classifying spaces, and on the diagonal section the action is quaternionic conjugation, a trivial real line plus the first adjoint three-plane. The Steenrod operations are
$$
\mathrm{Sq}^1a=u,\qquad \mathrm{Sq}^1u=\mathrm{Sq}^1\bar e_k=0,\qquad
\mathrm{Sq}^2u=au,\qquad \mathrm{Sq}^2\bar e_k=a\bar e_k .
\tag{T.9.2j.2}
$$
The first two identities for $a,u$ and $\mathrm{Sq}^2u$ are the rank-three oriented bundle formulas. The identity for the Euler reduction follows from the Thom identity for the top Stiefel–Whitney class of the rank-four bundle. The integral Euler lift gives the zero first square (Milnor and Stasheff 1974, §§8–9).

*Spin bordism calculation.* Work first at the prime two. The mod-two ring is the tensor product of the block polynomial rings with the one computed for $H$ in Theorem T.9.2i. Write $x_\ell$ for the integral-lift degree-two torus generators from $H$ and let $X$ denote the combined degree-two list of the $a_i$ and $x_\ell$. The degree-three list is $u_i$. The additional degree-four generators are the $\bar e_{i,k}$ and the Chern generators of $H$. Rational homology is concentrated in even degrees. All odd-local homology in this range is free even: the finite $2$-group kernel of the covering maps onto the blocks makes those maps odd-local equivalences, and the integral homology of $BH$ is free even by Theorem T.9.2i. Thus there is no odd-primary fifth bordism contribution.

For clarity, the degree-five integral reduction is the annihilator of $\mathrm{Sq}^1H^4$ and the degree-six integral reduction is the annihilator of $\mathrm{Sq}^1H^5$ in the indicated mod-two homology spaces. To prove the equalities, let $s_n$ count cyclic $2$-primary summands of $H_n(BG;\mathbb Z)$. The mod-two dimensions in degrees $2,3$ are respectively $b+t,b$, with rational ranks $t,0$ and $H_1=0$. The universal coefficient relation gives $s_2=b$ and $s_3=0$. In degree four each block contributes $m_i$ rational classes, one Pontryagin class and $m_i-1$ Euler generators. Its mod-two ring has the same count from $a_i^2$ and the Euler reductions. Thus the excess over the rational rank in degree four is $bt+\binom b2$, from cross products $a_ix_\ell$ and $a_i a_j$ with $i<j$. This gives $s_4=bt+\binom b2$. The degree-five list is exactly $u_iX$, of size $b(b+t)$, with zero rational rank, giving $s_5=b(b+1)/2$.

Now $\mathrm{Sq}^1H^4$ has independent images $x_\ell u_i$ and $a_i u_j+a_j u_i$ for $i<j$, of total dimension $s_4$. The image $\mathrm{Sq}^1H^5$ is spanned by the independent $u_i u_j$ for $i\le j$ and has this latter dimension. Reduction from integral homology annihilates these first-square images, and its mod-two codimension is $s_{n-1}$ in degree $n$, by universal coefficients. This proves the two annihilator descriptions.

On the degree-five diagonal of the Spin Atiyah–Hirzebruch spectral sequence, $E^2_{3,2}$ is killed by the differential dual to $\mathrm{Sq}^2u_i=a_i u_i$. On the term $E^2_{4,1}$ the outgoing differential is dual to $\mathrm{Sq}^2X=X^2$. The incoming differential is dual to $\mathrm{Sq}^2$ modulo the just computed degree-six annihilator complement $\operatorname{span}\{u_i u_j\}$. On a mixed product $XY$ of distinct degree-two generators its image has the independent monomials $X^2Y+XY^2$ and a possible term in the $u_i u_j$ span. On a block Euler generator its image is $a_i\bar e_{i,k}$. These monomials are independent of the images on Chern generators of $H$, which are as in (T.9.2i.4). Thus the sole survivors in $(4,1)$ are the Witten classes of $H$. The integral term $(5,0)$ injects under reduction: indeed $H_5$ is rationally zero and the first-square image in degree six has rank equal to its number of cyclic summands, so each has order two. To see the last implication, the integral Bockstein maps degree-five mod-two cohomology onto the order-two subgroup in the torsion of integral degree-six cohomology, and the reduction of this Bockstein has full rank. The order-two element of a cyclic summand of higher order would reduce to zero. In $(5,0)$ the outgoing $d_2$ imposes annihilation of the diagonal $a_i u_i$ in addition to $\mathrm{Sq}^1H^4$. The resulting dual basis is $a_i u_j$ with $i<j$. The only other possible degree-five term $(1,4)$ is zero. These calculations give an upper bound on the group order of $2^{\binom b2}|\Omega_5^{\mathrm{Spin}}(BH)|$, independent of any remaining differentials or extensions.

*Generators and actual phases.* The projection to $BH$ splits its inclusion. For each pair $i<j$ take the spin manifold $Y=\mathbb{RP}^3\times\mathbb T^2$ and the two $SO(3)$ bundles of (W.14q.11), placing them in blocks $i,j$ by the diagonal sections and leaving every other factor trivial. Equation (W.14q.12) gives characteristic number one on that pair and zero on every other pair. Such a class has order at most two because it is the image of the generator of $\Omega_5^{\mathrm{Spin}}(BSO(3)\times BSO(3)\times BU(1))=\mathbb Z/2$ in Theorem W.14q, by forgetting the circle and applying the two sections. The characteristic numbers and the split $H$ inclusion attain the upper bound and prove (T.9.2j.1) with the asserted generators. On each mixed generator every species restricts to a real coefficient representation. In fact a tensor product of $SU(2)$ highest weight modules has an equivariant antiunitary squaring to $(-1)^{\sum_k n_{i,k}}$, which is $+1$ on every descending block species. Its restriction to the section is still real. The $H$ and other factor bundles are trivial on the mixed generator. The real-coefficient five-dimensional Spin Dirac pairing in (W.14q.14) then gives reduced $\eta$ phase one, with the zero modes included. On the split $H$ generators the phase is exactly the ordinary instanton index sign with the extra spectator dimensions. After vanishing of the local polynomial the phases are bordism characters, so these tests are necessary and sufficient. The local test uses the entire Lie algebra, with every mixed torus term of $H$ and every term coupling its circles to a block quadratic invariant.

*Physical packet.* Enumerate the honest covering highest weights, torus charges and finite multiplicities with the original marks, the descent tests and the displayed anomaly gates. For each stock solve the real-linear covariance and fixed old-frame conditions of (T.9.2h.3)–(T.9.2h.4). The connected quotient makes these infinitesimal conditions equivalent to the full gauge conditions on the honest representations. Use the calibrated interpolation grid, real marked word comparison, physical rest generators and compensated probes of Theorem T.9.2h. They give the complete equivalence and realization test for every supplied finite degree, the Takagi rest thresholds with all zero and repeated modes, and the joint projected gauge and Higgs mixing maps and derivatives. The class includes correlated signs within each diagonal block and arbitrary torus-injective correlations inside $H$.

<a id="theorem-t92k"></a>

<a id="theorem-t92k-circle-twisted-diagonal-family-blocks"></a>**Theorem T.9.2k (Circle-Twisted Diagonal Family Blocks).** Keep the group $H$ of Theorem T.9.2i, independent ordinary Spin, and the finite polynomial-background Weyl source of Theorem T.9.2h. Form a product of $H$ with any finite number of independently marked family blocks. A block is either the untwisted $D_m$ of Theorem T.9.2j, $m\ge1$, or the circle-twisted block
$$
M_{p,q}=
\frac{SU(2)^{p+q}\times U(1)}
{\langle(-I_{A\cup B},1),(-I_B,-1)\rangle},
\qquad |A|=p\ge1,\quad |B|=q\ge1.
\tag{T.9.2k.1}
$$
The signs outside the named set of factors are positive. In either block the sum of all $SU(2)$ highest weights must be even. In a twisted block the sum of the highest weights in $B$ plus the integer circle charge must also be even. Together with the test for $H$, these are precisely the honest descent conditions. With $b$ the total number of blocks, twisted and untwisted, the full ordinary-Spin group is
$$
\Omega_5^{\mathrm{Spin}}(BG)\simeq\Omega_5^{\mathrm{Spin}}(BH)
\oplus(\mathbb Z/2)^{\binom b2}.
\tag{T.9.2k.2}
$$
The mixed generators are detected by the numbers $\langle a_i u_j,[Y]_2\rangle$ for $i<j$. Here $a_i,u_i$ are the Stiefel–Whitney classes of degrees two and three of a fixed first adjoint factor, chosen in $A$ for a twisted block. For every finite honest complex Weyl stock the exact ordinary-Spin admission gate is vanishing of the full local anomaly polynomial and the Witten parity rows of $H$ with the block dimensions as spectator multiplicities. The mixed stable generators have trivial phase for every such locally cancelled stock. The canonical Weyl response catalog then gives all finite threshold, Higgs, mixing and marked equivalence entries at the stated polynomial degree and background.

*Twisted block geometry.* Choose one representative from $A$ and one from $B$. Projection to them and to the original circle gives a surjection to $M_{1,1}$ with kernel the other $p+q-2$ simply connected $SU(2)$ factors. The quotient has a section that repeats each representative throughout its own sign group. For every omitted factor form the oriented quaternionic representation $w\mapsto g_k w g_*^{-1}$ using the representative of its own sign group. Both central generators act trivially on this representation. Its integral Euler class restricts to a generator on the corresponding kernel factor and to zero on every other one. Monomials in these classes give the full integral fiber basis. Leray–Hirsch therefore gives a polynomial extension of the base ring by these Euler classes, over both integral and mod-two coefficients.

The base $M_{1,1}$ is the mixed diagonal row of Theorem W.14s. Through degree six its mod-two ring is $\mathbb F_2[a,x,u]/(xu)$, with $x$ the first Chern class modulo two of the squared circle character, and $\mathrm{Sq}^1a=u$, $\mathrm{Sq}^2u=au$. The adjoint degree-two class for the representative in $B$ is $a+x$. For an extra Euler reduction $e_k$, one has $\mathrm{Sq}^1e_k=0$ and $\mathrm{Sq}^2e_k=a_* e_k$, where $a_*=a$ or $a+x$ according to its sign group. To verify the latter, the relative quaternionic four-plane is pulled back from the two factors in the same sign group through their map to $SO(4)$. In that $SO(4)$ bundle $w_2$ equals the $w_2$ of its first adjoint factor, as in the block proof of Theorem T.9.2j. The top Stiefel–Whitney formula gives the stated square. The base ring and its relation follow from the transgressions of the central extension in (W.14s.3); the relation is precisely $x u=0$ through the required degree. Repeating the same $SO(3)$ lift throughout both sign groups, with trivial circle, gives a section of the first adjoint projection. Its well-definedness uses the all-factor diagonal generator in (T.9.2k.1).

*Ordinary-Spin calculation.* Let $d$ be the number of twisted blocks and $t$ the total number of marked degree-two circle generators in the base descriptions, including the $d$ squared circle generators. Write $x_i$ for the particular generator of a twisted block $i$. In degrees through six the product mod-two ring is the tensor product of the rings just described with the untwisted block rings of Theorem T.9.2j and the ring of $H$ in Theorem T.9.2i. Its only relations in these degrees are $x_i u_i=0$ for each twisted block. A finite cover by the simple factors and circles shows that the rational ranks are given by the corresponding polynomial ring of the covers. The cover maps for the blocks have two-primary kernels. Thus at odd primes the block homology is free even, as is the integral homology of $BH$, and there is no odd-primary contribution in Spin degree five.

Let $s_n$ count the cyclic two-primary summands of integral homology in degree $n$. In degrees two and three the mod-two dimensions are $b+t$ and $b$ and the rational ranks are $t$ and zero. The universal coefficient relation gives $s_2=b$, $s_3=0$. The degree-four excess of mod-two dimension over rational rank is $bt+\binom b2-d$. Indeed, relative to the untwisted count $bt+\binom b2$ of Theorem T.9.2j, a twisted block has one fewer independent Euler generator for the same number of covering $SU(2)$ factors. The mixed monomial $a_i x_i$ was already counted in $bt$, and the circle is included in $t$. Thus $s_4=bt+\binom b2-d$. The degree-five list consists of every $u_i a_j$ and every $u_i x_\ell$ except $u_i x_i$ in a twisted block. Its dimension is $b(b+t)-d$ and its rational rank zero, giving $s_5=b(b+1)/2$.

The image of $\mathrm{Sq}^1$ from degree four to degree five has the basis $a_i u_j+a_j u_i$ for $i<j$ and the allowed $x_\ell u_i$, giving dimension $s_4$. Its image from degree five to degree six has the basis $u_i u_j$ for $i\le j$, giving dimension $s_5$. In each degree the integral homology reduction annihilates the corresponding image by the Bockstein identity. The dimensions, from the same universal coefficient sequence, show that it is the full annihilator. Also $H_5$ has exponent two: the first-square image in degree six has the same rank as the number of cyclic summands of $H_5$, whereas the order-two element in a cyclic summand of higher order in the dual integral cohomology torsion would reduce to zero. This uses the integral Bockstein onto the order-two subgroup and its reduction $\mathrm{Sq}^1$.

In the Spin Atiyah–Hirzebruch spectral sequence the only possible total-degree-five terms are $(5,0),(4,1),(3,2)$. The term $(3,2)$ is killed by the duals of $\mathrm{Sq}^2 u_i=a_i u_i$. For $(4,1)$ the outgoing dual of $\mathrm{Sq}^2$ on degree two removes the squares. Each remaining mixed degree-two product $XY$ has square $X^2Y+XY^2$ modulo the span of the $u_i u_j$. Those images have disjoint monomial supports for distinct unordered pairs. The relations $x_i u_i=0$ impose no relation on these monomials. Each block Euler generator has independent nonzero square $a_*e_k$, and the images of the Chern generators of $H$ have the independence and kernel of (T.9.2i.4). Consequently $(4,1)$ contributes at most the Witten summands of $H$. On $(5,0)$ the reduction is injective and its image is the annihilator of the first-square image. The outgoing $d_2$ additionally imposes annihilation of every $a_i u_i$. The remaining dual coordinates are exactly the mixed $a_i u_j$ for $i<j$. The resulting upper bound on the order is the right hand side of (T.9.2k.2), regardless of any later differentials or extensions. The spectral sequence inputs are those of Theorems T.9.2i–j.

*Realization and Weyl phases.* Inclusion of $BH$ splits by projection. For each pair of blocks, insert the two $SO(3)$ backgrounds of (W.14q.11) through the diagonal $SO(3)$ sections of their blocks and take the other bundles and the marked circles trivial. The sections send the chosen first adjoint bundles to the two original bundles. Their mixed number is one on the selected pair and zero on the other pairs by (W.14q.12). These are order-two classes, since each is an image of the order-two generator of Theorem W.14q after forgetting its independent circle. They attain the upper bound and prove the asserted decomposition. On each mixed representative the covering coefficient has an equivariant real structure: the all-factor diagonal condition makes the number of quaternionic highest-weight factors even within each block, and all circle and $H$ connections there are trivial. The quaternionic Spin Dirac pairing in (W.14q.14) gives phase one with zero modes included. On the split $H$ classes the $\eta$ phases are precisely the Witten index signs with the indicated spectators. Since local cancellation makes the reduced $\eta$ phase a bordism character, this proves the exact admission gate. The polynomial test is on the full Lie algebra, including all abelian cubic, linear and mixed gauge terms. In particular the torsion result does not eliminate any local condition involving the circle of a twisted block.

*Finite physical response.* For each finite honest highest-weight and charge stock passing this gate, the tensor covariance system (T.9.2h.3)–(T.9.2h.4) gives the full mass polynomial, subject to the declared degree and old-frame data. The group is connected and all coefficients use honest representations. Hence its gauge equivariance is exactly the system on the full Lie algebra. The marked grid, real marked word test and compensated CAR comparisons of Theorem T.9.2h then apply on this stock, with its actual fixed Higgs controls and canonical kinetic generators. They supply the Takagi thresholds and degeneracies, projected gauge and Higgs mixing, higher mixed Higgs derivatives and complete marked response equivalence. For example a twisted block with $p=2$, $q=1$ admits a neutral bidoublet on the two factors of $A$, and a bidoublet with one factor in each sign group at odd circle charge. A pair of opposite charges in the latter stock cancels its local anomaly. Both kinds can coexist with the ordinary electroweak source in $H$.

<a id="theorem-t92l"></a>

<a id="theorem-t92l-shared-circle-family-center-quotients"></a>**Theorem T.9.2l (Shared-Circle Family Center Quotients).** Let \(S\) be a product of finitely many \(SU(N_a)\) with \(N_a\ge3\) and finitely many additional marked \(SU(2)_j\) factors. Take a marked torus \(T\), a finite subgroup \(A\subset T\), and \(b\) independently marked diagonal family blocks \(D_{m_i}=SU(2)^{m_i}/\langle(-I,\ldots,-I)\rangle\), \(m_i\ge1\). Choose any homomorphism
$$
\kappa:A\longrightarrow Z(S)\times\prod_i Z(D_{m_i}).
$$
Divide \(S\times\prod_i D_{m_i}\times T\) by the graph of \(\kappa\), giving \(G\). Write \(T'=T/A\) and \(H=(S\times T)/\operatorname{graph}(\kappa_S)\), the quotient formed by omitting the blocks. The same torus subgroup can tie signs in arbitrarily many blocks and in \(S\). Within one block the relative signs can have any finite rank.
