A covering stock descends precisely when it is trivial on every all-factor diagonal sign and on the graph, evaluated in its covering highest-weight and torus characters. Keep independent ordinary Spin and the finite polynomial-background Weyl source of Theorem T.9.2h. Then
$$
\Omega_5^{\mathrm{Spin}}(BG)\simeq\Omega_5^{\mathrm{Spin}}(BH)\oplus(\mathbb Z/2)^{\binom b2}.
\tag{T.9.2l.1}
$$
The mixed block characters are the numbers \(\langle a_i u_j,[Y]_2\rangle\) for \(i<j\), where \(a_i,u_i\) are the second and third Stiefel–Whitney classes of a chosen first adjoint factor in block \(i\). Every locally cancelled honest complex Weyl stock has trivial phase on the mixed generators. Its exact determinant admission test is vanishing of the full local index polynomial followed by the parity rows of \(H\) in (T.9.2i.2), with the extra block dimensions included among the spectator dimensions. The finite threshold, Higgs, mixing and response-equivalence packets of Theorem T.9.2h apply to each admitted stock.

*Relative central cover.* In each \(Z(D_{m_i})\) coset, choose the unique sign tuple with positive first sign. This convention gives a homomorphic lift into the covering centers. For \(k>1\) in block \(i\), let \(\lambda_{ik}\in H^2(BT';\mathbb F_2)\) correspond to the sign on that factor of the lifted graph. Namely, extend the sign on \(A\) to a character of \(T\) and take the mod-two Chern class of its square on \(T'\), as in (T.9.2i.3). A different extension changes the integral class by twice a class. Write \(U_i=\operatorname{span}\{\lambda_{ik}:k>1\}\) and \(d_i=\dim U_i,\ d=\sum_i d_i\). Relations between forms from different blocks are allowed.

The natural map \(G\to H\times\prod_i SO(3)^{m_i}\) is a central cover with kernel the relative sign groups of ranks \(m_i-1\). The coordinate obstruction for factor \(k>1\) in block \(i\) is
$$
a_{ik}+a_i+\lambda_{ik}.
\tag{T.9.2l.2}
$$
Here \(a_{ik}\) is the second Stiefel–Whitney class of that adjoint factor, and \(\lambda_{ik}\) is pulled back from \(BT'\) through \(BH\). To check this class, both sides are determined on fundamental-group loops of the target, since its classifying space is simply connected. A loop in the first or the \(k\)th adjoint factor lifts to the nontrivial relative sign, while other adjoint loops have zero coordinate. For a loop in \(H\), lift its path to \(S\times T\) starting at identity. Its endpoint is a graph element over some \(a\in A\). With identity block paths, the endpoint in the relative deck has the \(k\)th sign of \(\kappa(a)\). On the torus lattice of \(T'\), the square of the extending character has winding parity equal to that sign. This proves the remaining term in (T.9.2l.2). Every \(D_{m_i}\) embeds in \(G\) with the torus at identity, because the graph projects injectively to \(T\). Every covering simple factor of \(S\) also embeds for the same reason.

*The required cohomology.* The mod-two Serre spectral sequence of this central cover has a degree-one fiber generator \(z_{ik}\) for each relative deck. With \(u_{ik}=\mathrm{Sq}^1a_{ik}\), its transgressions are
$$
d_2z_{ik}=a_{ik}+a_i+\lambda_{ik},\qquad
d_3z_{ik}^2=u_{ik}+u_i,\qquad
d_5z_{ik}^4=\lambda_{ik}u_i.
\tag{T.9.2l.3}
$$
Use the Steenrod transgression rule of (W.14s.3), \(\mathrm{Sq}^1\lambda_{ik}=0\), and \(\mathrm{Sq}^2u_{ik}=a_{ik}u_{ik}\) for the oriented adjoint three-plane. The first list is regular and eliminates the non-first \(a_{ik}\). After taking that homology the second list is regular and eliminates the non-first \(u_{ik}\). These two computations leave fiber degrees divisible by four on the fourth page. In total degrees through six, the base row is therefore the polynomial ring of \(BH\) with the \(a_i,u_i\) adjoined and relations \(\lambda u_i=0\) for \(\lambda\in U_i\). There is no other relation in that range, since a later incoming differential to the base row through degree six would need a nonzero fiber row of degree five. The extra total degree-four classes have leading fiber terms in the linear kernel of \(d_5\) on the \(z_{ik}^4\), of dimension \(\sum_i(m_i-1)-d\). They have no later outgoing differential by fiber degree and no incoming differential by base degree. Total degree five has only the base monomials \(u_i a_j,u_i x_\ell\), where \(x_\ell\) is the integral-lift torus basis of \(BH\), modulo the stated \(d\) independent relations. The different blocks can have overlapping \(U_i\). Their relations still use distinct \(u_i\) and hence contribute separately to this rank.

*Integral reductions and Spin differentials.* Write \(t=\dim T'\) and let \(s_n\) count the cyclic two-primary summands of integral homology in degree \(n\). The finite cover gives the rational ranks from the simple factors and circles. At an odd prime, remove the two-primary part of \(A\) and the two-primary pure diagonal deck groups by the corresponding odd-local equivalences. The remaining graph is torus-injective and has no block sign. Theorem T.9.2i applied with the covering \(SU(2)\) factors in place of the blocks gives free even homology, so there is no odd-primary fifth Spin bordism. The low-degree mod-two dimensions and rational ranks give
$$
s_2=b,\qquad s_3=0,\qquad s_4=bt+\binom b2-d,\qquad s_5=b(b+1)/2 .
\tag{T.9.2l.4}
$$
Indeed the degree-four excess over rational rank consists of \(a_i x_\ell\) and \(a_i a_j\) for \(i<j\), reduced by the \(d\) lost fiber combinations. Each \(a_i^2\) supplies the degree-four count of the first adjoint factor. The degree-five dimension is \(b(b+t)-d\) and its rational rank is zero. The first squares from degree four give \(a_i u_j+a_j u_i\) for \(i<j\) and the allowed \(x_\ell u_i\), of rank \(s_4\) already from base classes. The image cannot have larger rank because it annihilates integral homology reduction, of codimension \(s_4\) by universal coefficients. The first squares from degree five span the independent \(u_i u_j\) for \(i\le j\), of rank \(s_5\). Thus integral reduction in degrees five and six is the full annihilator of the respective first-square image. The degree-five integral homology has exponent two by the Bockstein argument of Theorem T.9.2j, since the first-square image in degree six has full rank \(s_5\).

On the degree-five Spin spectral sequence diagonal the term \((3,2)\) dies by \(\mathrm{Sq}^2u_i=a_i u_i\). In \((5,0)\) the outgoing second differential imposes annihilation of the diagonal \(a_i u_i\) in addition to the first-square image. The surviving dual coordinates are the mixed \(a_i u_j\) for \(i<j\). In \((4,1)\) the outgoing differential is dual to the squares of the degree-two generators. For the incoming differential, test \(\mathrm{Sq}^2\) modulo the span of \(u_i u_j\). Every nonzero relative Euler combination is detected after restriction to the product of the embedded untwisted \(D_{m_i}\) subgroups. By naturality of the covering spectral sequence the restriction retains its nonzero fiber coefficient, since there all \(\lambda_{ik}\) vanish and no corresponding fifth differential remains. In that product the leading Euler coefficients are independent, and their squares have independent \(a_i\bar e_{ik}\) coefficients by (T.9.2j.2). Restrictions of base classes have no such coefficients, so they cannot cancel them. Among the base classes the mixed degree-two products have independent squares \(X^2Y+XY^2\) modulo \(u_i u_j\). Every new relation contains a degree-three \(u_i\), so these monomials remain independent. The squares of the Chern generators of \(BH\) have the independence and kernel of (T.9.2i.4). Consequently \((4,1)\) has at most the Witten summands of \(H\). This proves an upper bound on the order of the full group equal to the order of the right side of (T.9.2l.1), independently of possible later differentials and extensions.

*Representatives and phases.* For each pair of blocks, insert the two \(SO(3)\) bundles of (W.14q.11) on \(\mathbb{RP}^3\times\mathbb T^2\) through the diagonal \(SO(3)\) sections of their embedded \(D_{m_i}\). All other gauge data are trivial there. Their selected mixed characteristic number is one, and the other mixed numbers are zero. Each class has order two since it is an image of the generator of Theorem W.14q after forgetting that theorem's independent circle. The independent Witten classes of \(H\) lift to \(G\) using the embedded \(SU(2)_j\) instanton times a periodic Spin circle. Their projection to \(BH\) gives its generators, and they have order two as images from \(BSU(2)_j\). They give a splitting on degree-five bordism. The mixed representatives project trivially, so these classes attain the upper bound and prove (T.9.2l.1).

A descended species restricts to a real coefficient on a mixed representative because its all-factor diagonal parity is even in each block. This makes the product of the quaternionic antiunitary squares positive. Its phase is one by the real-coefficient Dirac pairing of (W.14q.14), including zero modes. On each lifted \(H\) instanton the phase is the normalized index sign with the stated spectators. After local cancellation the phases are a bordism character, so these evaluations exhaust the global determinant gate. The local polynomial is tested on the entire algebra, including cross terms involving all shared circles. For each passing stock, the finite tensor covariance test and interpolating Higgs samples of Theorem T.9.2h, together with its marked operator words and compensated CAR probes, give the claimed equivalence and response packets on the same gauge and mass generators.

<a id="theorem-t92m"></a>

<a id="theorem-t92m-overlapping-binary-family-centers"></a>**Theorem T.9.2m (Overlapping Binary Family Centers).** Retain \(S\) and \(T\) of Theorem T.9.2l and take \(m\) additional labelled \(SU(2)\) factors. Let \(C\le\mathbb F_2^m\) be any binary subspace of their center, with every coordinate active, meaning nonzero on some element of \(C\). An inactive factor may be placed in \(S\). Put \(P=SU(2)^m/C\). Choose \(A\le T\) finite and a graph homomorphism \(\kappa:A\to Z(S)\times Z(P)\). Let \(G=(S\times P\times T)/\operatorname{graph}(\kappa)\), \(H=(S\times T)/\operatorname{graph}(\kappa_S)\), and \(r=\dim C\). Use independent ordinary Spin. Then
$$
\Omega_5^{\mathrm{Spin}}(BG)\cong
\Omega_5^{\mathrm{Spin}}(BH)\oplus(\mathbb Z/2)^{\binom r2}.
\tag{T.9.2m.1}
$$
An honest species must have its additional highest-weight parity vector in \(C^\perp\) and its full covering character trivial on the graph. There is a complete Weyl anomaly gate on the class of finite stocks for which each species has even total highest-weight parity on the \(m\) additional factors. In particular this condition holds for all honest species whenever the all-active sign \((1,\ldots,1)\) belongs to \(C\). On this class the gate consists of vanishing of the full local polynomial and the \(H\) Witten rows of (T.9.2i.2), with all additional factor dimensions included as spectators. The finite polynomial threshold, Yukawa, mixing and marked response-equivalence catalog of Theorem T.9.2h then applies. The bordism calculation (T.9.2m.1) holds for every \(C\), independently of the coefficient restriction.

*Central cover and its cohomology.* Choose information coordinates \(1,\ldots,r\) in the marked factors so that the projection \(C\to\mathbb F_2^r\) is an isomorphism. Write \(L_j\in(\mathbb F_2^r)^*\) for the \(j\)th coordinate on \(C\), \(j>r\). The remaining coordinates form a complement in the sign group, so \(\kappa_P\) lifts with all its information-coordinate signs zero. Let \(\lambda_j\) denote the mod-two degree-two form of its \(j\)th sign on \(BT'\), \(T'=T/A\), using the squared extending torus character of Theorem T.9.2l. There is a central cover \(G\to H\times SO(3)^m\) with deck \(\mathbb F_2^m/C\). In the coordinate \(j>r\) its obstruction is \(a_j+L_j(a)+\lambda_j\), where the \(a\)'s are adjoint \(w_2\)'s and \(L_j(a)=\sum_{\alpha\le r}L_{j\alpha}a_\alpha\). To check it, a loop in the adjoint factors lifts to the corresponding sign vector modulo \(C\), and a loop in \(H\) lifts to a graph endpoint with relative sign \(\lambda_j\), as in (T.9.2l.2).

In the mod-two Serre sequence let \(z_j\) be the degree-one fiber generator. The first two transgressions are \(d_2 z_j=a_j+L_j(a)+\lambda_j\), \(d_3 z_j^2=u_j+L_j(u)\), with \(u_j=\mathrm{Sq}^1a_j\). The lists are regular successively and eliminate the non-information \(a_j,u_j\). The next differential on \(z_j^4\) is
$$
f_j=(L_j(a)+\lambda_j)L_j(u)+\sum_{\alpha\le r}L_{j\alpha}a_\alpha u_\alpha .
\tag{T.9.2m.2}
$$
Indeed this is the Steenrod square of the second transgression after both eliminations, using \(\mathrm{Sq}^2u_j=a_j u_j\). In characteristic two the diagonal terms cancel in (T.9.2m.2). Thus every \(f_j\) is a linear combination of \(a_\alpha u_\beta+a_\beta u_\alpha\) for distinct indices and the \(x_\ell u_\alpha\), where \(x_\ell\) is an integral-lift torus basis of \(BH\). Let \(d\) be the rank of the list \(f_j\) in this space. Through degree six the base row has only the relations generated by the \(f_j\), and the extra total-degree-four classes have leading coefficients in the kernel of \(z_j^4\mapsto f_j\). Total degree five has only the base row. These assertions follow from the two regular stages and the fourth-page fiber degrees divisible by four. In total degree five the possible bidegree \((1,4)\) of this Serre sequence is absent because the base has no first cohomology. In degrees through six there is no further base-row differential, because it would require fiber degree five. In particular the relations do not identify any of the degree-six monomials \(u_\alpha u_\beta\).

*Spin upper bound.* Put \(t=\dim T'\). The mod-two dimensions in degrees two, three and five are \(r+t,r,r(r+t)-d\), respectively. The rational ranks there are \(t,0,0\). In degree four the mod-two excess over rational rank is \(rt+\binom r2-d\): the \(a_\alpha^2\) count the \(r\) information simple factors, the surviving fiber terms count \(m-r-d\), and the remaining additions are the mixed \(a_\alpha a_\beta\) and \(a_\alpha x_\ell\). As in Theorem T.9.2l there is no odd-primary fifth contribution, by the odd-local equivalence removing the pure two-primary code and the two-primary part of the graph. The universal coefficient sequence now gives the numbers of cyclic two-primary homology summands
$$
s_2=r,\qquad s_3=0,\qquad
s_4=rt+\binom r2-d,\qquad
s_5=r(r+1)/2.
$$
The first squares of the degree-four base classes already span a space of rank \(s_4\), since the \(d\) relations lie in precisely this first-square space. In degree five the first squares are the independent \(u_\alpha u_\beta\) for \(\alpha\le\beta\), of rank \(s_5\). By the universal coefficient and Bockstein argument of Theorem T.9.2j these give the full annihilators of integral reduction in degrees five and six, and \(H_5\) has exponent two.

In the Spin sequence \((3,2)\) dies and \((5,0)\) has at most the \(\binom r2\) mixed coordinates, by the extra constraints \(\mathrm{Sq}^2u_\alpha=a_\alpha u_\alpha\) as in Theorem T.9.2l. At \((4,1)\) the outgoing map removes the degree-two squares. To test the incoming map, use the dual of \(\mathrm{Sq}^2\) modulo the span of the \(u_\alpha u_\beta\). Every class with nonzero fiber coefficient is detected by a genuine diagonal subgroup. Here are the details of that detection. For a surviving combination with nonzero coefficient at \(z_j^4\), choose a codeword \(c\in C\) whose \(j\)th coordinate is one. The factors in its support induce a subgroup \(D_{|\operatorname{supp}c|}\to P\) by quotienting their simultaneous diagonal sign. This map need not be injective, and only its pullback on cohomology is used. Choose as its first coordinate an information index \(\alpha\) on which \(c_\alpha=1\), which exists by the information-coordinate isomorphism. On the deck group of this diagonal cover, take relative sign coordinates using representatives with that first sign zero. The relative deck character indexed by \(j>r\) pulls back, if \(j\) is in the support, to its own relative coordinate plus a linear combination of the information-index relative coordinates. If \(j\) is outside the support only the information-index terms occur. This follows directly by subtracting from a sign tuple the unique codeword with the same information coordinates. Fourth powers are additive over \(\mathbb F_2\). Therefore the pulled-back leading coefficient at the selected \(j\) remains nonzero. On the diagonal subgroup Theorem T.9.2j gives the independent Euler squares \(a\bar e_k\). Hence the pulled-back class has nonzero second square modulo \(u^2\), since the base classes have no Euler terms. This detects its square in \(BG\) modulo the \(u_\alpha u_\beta\).

For base classes, the squares of distinct degree-two mixed products have independent supports \(X^2Y+XY^2\) modulo the same \(u_\alpha u_\beta\). The relations (T.9.2m.2) and their products contain a degree-three generator and impose no relation on those supports. The Chern generators of \(BH\) have the squares of (T.9.2i.4). Consequently \((4,1)\) has at most the \(H\) Witten summands. This gives the upper bound in (T.9.2m.1), irrespective of later differentials or extensions.

*Mixed generators and Weyl phases.* For a pair \(\alpha<\beta\) use \(Y=\mathbb{RP}^3\times\mathbb T^2\) with the two adjoint bundles of (W.14q.11) on those information indices and trivial information bundles elsewhere. Their second classes are \(a,b\) with mixed number one. For each remaining adjoint factor choose a three-plane bundle with \(w_2=L_j(a_1,\ldots,a_r)\). Such a bundle exists for every class on this \(Y\). Its Pontryagin square has an integral lift, since the obstruction from \(H^4(Y;\mathbb Z/4)\) lies in the four-torsion of \(H^5(Y;\mathbb Z)\), which is zero. The degree-four Postnikov stage of \(BSO(3)\) then has the prescribed \(w_2\) and a compatible integral \(p_1\), and the next lifting obstruction has degree six, above the dimension of \(Y\) (Antieau and Williams 2012).

With torus and \(H\) data trivial the central covering obstruction vanishes, so these adjoint bundles lift to \(P\) and hence to \(G\). They have the selected mixed number one and the other mixed numbers zero. The \(H\) classes lift by its surviving instanton factors, and projection to \(BH\) splits their order-two subgroup on bordism. To rule out extensions among the mixed classes, let \(F_4\) be the degree-four Atiyah–Hirzebruch filtration subgroup. The upper bound on \((4,1)\) and the independent lifted \(H\) instantons show that \(F_4\) is exactly their subgroup. Twice each mixed class lies in \(F_4\) and projects trivially to \(BH\), hence is zero. The mixed classes and \(H\) instantons thus give (T.9.2m.1).

The additional tensor product coefficient of each species in the stated even-parity class is real. Its equivariant antiunitary is the product of the \(SU(2)\) antiunitaries and its square is \(+1\). This property holds on the actual \(P\) bundles because the species is honest. The \(H\) and torus connections are trivial on the mixed generators, so the real-coefficient five-dimensional Spin Dirac pairing (W.14q.14) gives phase one, including zero modes. On an \(H\) generator the phase is the instanton index with the spectator dimensions. The local polynomial is tested on the entire Lie algebra before applying these bordism-character evaluations. This proves the claimed determinant test. Solving the equivariant tensor system (T.9.2h.3)–(T.9.2h.4) on the resulting honest stock and applying its calibrated probes gives the full polynomial-source response packet.

<a id="theorem-t92n"></a>

<a id="theorem-t92n-pseudoreal-weyl-phases-on-overlapping-family-centers"></a>**Theorem T.9.2n (Pseudoreal Weyl Phases on Overlapping Family Centers).** Retain $S$, $T$, the $m$ additional labelled $SU(2)$ factors, the binary subspace $C\le\mathbb F_2^m$ with every coordinate active, $P=SU(2)^m/C$, the graph homomorphism $\kappa$, the groups $G$ and $H$, $r=\dim C$ and independent ordinary Spin of Theorem T.9.2m. Write elements of $C$ as zero-one vectors. Let $\mathcal F$ be a finite honest all-left complex Weyl stock. Its irreducible species $i$ has multiplicity $m_i$, additional highest weights $n_{i1},\ldots,n_{im}$, spectator dimension $D_i$ of its representation of $S$, and odd set $\nu_i=\{j:n_{ij}\text{ odd}\}$. Honesty makes $|\nu_i\cap\operatorname{supp}c|$ even for every $c\in C$. In the normalization in which the fundamental of $SU(2)$ has weights $\pm1$, the additional factor representation $V_i$ of species $i$ has the weights $\mu=(\mu_1,\ldots,\mu_m)$ with $\mu_j\in\{n_{ij},n_{ij}-2,\ldots,-n_{ij}\}$, each of multiplicity one. For $c,d\in C$ define
$$
B_i(c,d)=
\begin{cases}
0, & |\nu_i|\text{ even},\\[3pt]
\displaystyle\frac{D_i}{2}\sum_{\mu}\left|\frac{c\cdot\mu}{2}\,\frac{d\cdot\mu}{2}\right|\pmod 2, & |\nu_i|\text{ odd}.
\end{cases}
\tag{T.9.2n.1}
$$
The fractions $c\cdot\mu/2$ and $d\cdot\mu/2$ are integers, and the sum is even when $|\nu_i|$ is odd. Let $\varepsilon_i=1$ if $\nu_i$ has exactly three elements and $n_{ij}\equiv1\pmod4$ for each $j\in\nu_i$, and $\varepsilon_i=0$ otherwise. Then
$$
B_i(c,d)=\varepsilon_iD_i\,(c_ad_b+c_bd_a)\pmod 2
\tag{T.9.2n.2}
$$
for any two distinct elements $a,b$ of $\nu_i$ when $\varepsilon_i=1$. Thus each $B_i$ is an alternating bilinear form on $C$, and only species with exactly three odd additional highest weights, each congruent to one modulo four, contribute to it.

The complete ordinary-Spin determinant anomaly gate of $\mathcal F$, with no compensating inflow, consists of three conditions: vanishing of the full degree-six local index polynomial on the entire tangent and gauge algebra; the parity rows of $H$ in (T.9.2i.2), with the additional factor dimension $\prod_j(n_{ij}+1)$ of each species included in its spectator dimension; and
$$
\sum_i m_iB_i(c^{(k)},c^{(l)})=0\pmod 2\qquad(1\le k<l\le r)
\tag{T.9.2n.3}
$$
for a basis $c^{(1)},\ldots,c^{(r)}$ of $C$. By (T.9.2n.2), condition (T.9.2n.3) holds for one basis exactly when the alternating form $\sum_im_iB_i$ vanishes on $C$, hence for every basis. For each pair $k<l$ the left side of (T.9.2n.3) is the exponent of the determinant phase of $\mathcal F$ on a smooth Spin mapping torus carrying a nonliftable $P$ bundle. The finite polynomial threshold, Yukawa, mixing and marked response-equivalence catalog of Theorem T.9.2h applies to every admitted stock. For $G=P=SU(2)^3/C$ with $C$ the even-weight subspace, a single Weyl trifundamental has vanishing local polynomial, and under each covering $SU(2)$ factor it is a doublet with spectator dimension four. It fails (T.9.2n.3): its determinant phase on the mixed generator is $-1$.

*Integrality and the closed form.* For $c\in C$, $c\cdot\mu\equiv c\cdot n_i\equiv|\nu_i\cap\operatorname{supp}c|\equiv0\pmod2$, so $p_\mu=c\cdot\mu/2$ and $q_\mu=d\cdot\mu/2$ are integers. Let $|\nu_i|$ be odd. Every weight then has an odd coordinate, so $\mu\mapsto-\mu$ is a fixed-point-free involution of the weights with $|p_{-\mu}q_{-\mu}|=|p_\mu q_\mu|$. The sum in (T.9.2n.1) is therefore twice the sum over the pairs $\{\mu,-\mu\}$. A term $|p_\mu q_\mu|$ is odd exactly when $p_\mu$ and $q_\mu$ are odd, that is, when $c\cdot\mu\equiv d\cdot\mu\equiv2\pmod4$. Hence
$$
B_i(c,d)\equiv D_i\,\frac{N_i(c,d)}{2}\pmod 2,\qquad
N_i(c,d)=\#\{\mu:\ c\cdot\mu\equiv d\cdot\mu\equiv2\pmod4\}.
$$
For even $x$ the indicator of $x\equiv2\pmod4$ is $\frac14\sum_{a\in\mathbb Z/4}(-1)^a i^{ax}$. The weights form a product set, so with the $SU(2)$ characters $\chi_n(z)=\sum_{s=0}^{n}z^{n-2s}$,
$$
16\,N_i(c,d)=\sum_{a,b\in\mathbb Z/4}(-1)^{a+b}\prod_{j=1}^m\chi_{n_{ij}}\bigl(i^{ac_j+bd_j}\bigr).
$$
At elements of order dividing four, $\chi_n(1)=n+1$ and $\chi_n(-1)=(-1)^n(n+1)$, while $\chi_n(\pm i)$ is $0$ for odd $n$ and $(-1)^{n/2}$ for even $n$. Group the sixteen terms by the residues of $a,b$ modulo two. When $a,b$ are both even, every term equals $\prod_j(n_{ij}+1)$, because $c\cdot n_i$ and $d\cdot n_i$ are even. In each of the three other classes let $f\in C$ be the mod-two sum of those of $c,d$ whose coefficient is odd. A factor with $j\in\nu_i$ and $f_j=1$ vanishes, so the four terms of the class vanish unless $\operatorname{supp}f\cap\nu_i=\emptyset$. In that case the factors with $j\in\nu_i$ multiply to $\Delta_i=\prod_{j\in\nu_i}(n_{ij}+1)$ times a power of $(-1)^{|\nu_i\cap\operatorname{supp}c|}$ or of $(-1)^{|\nu_i\cap\operatorname{supp}d|}$, that is, times one. The factors with $j\notin\nu_i$ give $n_{ij}+1$ for $f_j=0$ and $(-1)^{n_{ij}/2}$ for $f_j=1$. Including the signs $(-1)^{a+b}$,
$$
4N_i(c,d)=\Delta_i\,(R_0-R_c-R_d+R_{c+d}),
$$
where $c+d$ is the mod-two sum, $R_f=0$ if $\operatorname{supp}f$ meets $\nu_i$, and otherwise $R_f=\prod_{j\notin\nu_i,\,f_j=0}(n_{ij}+1)\prod_{f_j=1}(-1)^{n_{ij}/2}$.

The set $\nu_i$ has at least three elements. Its size is odd, and $\nu_i=\{j\}$ would force $c_j=0$ for every $c\in C$, contrary to activity. Writing $\Delta_i=2^{|\nu_i|}\prod_{j\in\nu_i}\frac{n_{ij}+1}2$ gives
$$
\frac{N_i(c,d)}2=2^{|\nu_i|-3}\prod_{j\in\nu_i}\frac{n_{ij}+1}2\,(R_0-R_c-R_d+R_{c+d}),
$$
which is even when $|\nu_i|\ge5$. Let $|\nu_i|=3$. The product is odd exactly when every $n_{ij}\equiv1\pmod4$, and $R_f$ is odd exactly when $\operatorname{supp}f\cap\nu_i=\emptyset$. Write $\bar c,\bar d$ for the restrictions of $c,d$ to $\nu_i$, which lie in the two-dimensional even-weight subspace of $\mathbb F_2^{\nu_i}$. Since $R_0$ is odd, $R_0-R_c-R_d+R_{c+d}$ is odd exactly when an even number of $\bar c,\bar d,\bar c+\bar d$ vanish, that is, exactly when $\bar c,\bar d$ are linearly independent. On that subspace $c_ad_b+c_bd_a$ is an alternating bilinear form, and it takes the value one on the independent pair supported on $\{a,g\}$ and $\{b,g\}$, where $g$ is the third element of $\nu_i$. It is therefore the determinant, which equals one exactly on independent pairs. This proves (T.9.2n.2).

*Detection of the mixed summand.* Let $1,\ldots,r$ be information coordinates as in Theorem T.9.2m, and let $a_j$ and $u_j=\mathrm{Sq}^1a_j$ be the second and third Stiefel–Whitney classes of the $j$th adjoint factor. The proof of Theorem T.9.2m supplies lifted $H$ instanton classes, which project onto generators of $\Omega_5^{\mathrm{Spin}}(BH)$ and have trivial adjoint bundles. It also supplies, for each $\alpha<\beta\le r$, a class $M_{\alpha\beta}$ with trivial projection to $BH$, $\langle a_\alpha u_\beta,M_{\alpha\beta}\rangle=1$, and every other mixed number $\langle a_\gamma u_\delta,M_{\alpha\beta}\rangle$, $\gamma<\delta\le r$, zero. Hence the homomorphism
$$
\Omega_5^{\mathrm{Spin}}(BG)\longrightarrow\Omega_5^{\mathrm{Spin}}(BH)\oplus\mathbb F_2^{\binom r2},\qquad
z\longmapsto\bigl(\pi_Hz,\ (\langle a_\alpha u_\beta,z\rangle)_{\alpha<\beta}\bigr),
$$
is onto. Both sides are finite of the same order by (T.9.2i.1) and (T.9.2m.1), so it is an isomorphism. A class with trivial projection to $BH$ is therefore determined by its mixed numbers.

*Mapping-torus representatives.* Let $X=\mathbb{CP}^1\times\mathbb{CP}^1$ with the product round metric and its unique Spin structure, and let $\tau$ be complex conjugation on both factors. Conjugation reverses the orientation of each sphere, so $\tau$ is an orientation-preserving isometry. Because $X$ is simply connected, $\tau$ lifts to the Spin bundle. The square of a lift $\tilde\tau$ covers the identity and is therefore $\pm1$ on connected $X$. At a fixed point the differential of $\tau$ reverses one tangent axis in each sphere, so $\tilde\tau$ acts there by $\pm ee'$ for orthonormal tangent vectors $e,e'$, and $(ee')^2=-1$ in the Clifford algebra. Hence $\tilde\tau^2=-1$.

Let $T_P\subset P$ be the image of the diagonal maximal torus of $SU(2)^m$. For $c\in C$ the map $e^{i\theta}\mapsto(\operatorname{diag}(e^{i\theta c_j/2},e^{-i\theta c_j/2}))_j$ descends to a cocharacter $c/2$ of $T_P$, because its value at $\theta=2\pi$ is the sign vector $c\in C$. Let $h$ be the Hopf circle bundle $S^3\to\mathbb{CP}^1$ with its homogeneous connection, and let $Q_0=\operatorname{pr}_1^*h\times_X\operatorname{pr}_2^*h$, a principal $U(1)^2$ bundle. For $c,d\in C$ form $Q=Q_0\times_{U(1)^2}T_P$ through $(\lambda_1,\lambda_2)\mapsto(c/2)(\lambda_1)\,(d/2)(\lambda_2)$, and $E=Q\times_{T_P}P$. The weight-$\mu$ line of an honest representation then has degrees $\pm c\cdot\mu/2$ and $\pm d\cdot\mu/2$ on the two spheres, the common sign depending only on the orientation convention. The $j$th adjoint representation contains the line of degrees $\pm c_j$ and $\pm d_j$.

Conjugation $\sigma_0(v)=\bar v$ on $S^3\subset\mathbb C^2$ covers conjugation on $\mathbb{CP}^1$, satisfies $\sigma_0(v\lambda)=\sigma_0(v)\bar\lambda$ and $\sigma_0^2=1$, and pulls the homogeneous connection form $v^\dagger dv$ back to its negative. It therefore preserves the horizontal distribution. On $Q_0$ the product $\sigma_0\times\sigma_0$ covers $\tau$, and on $Q$ it induces $\sigma_Q[q,s]=[(\sigma_0\times\sigma_0)q,s^{-1}]$, well defined because $T_P$ is abelian. Let $W\in P$ be the image of $(w,\ldots,w)$ with $w=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}0&-1\\1&0\end{smallmatrix}\right)$. Then $WsW^{-1}=s^{-1}$ for $s\in T_P$, and $W^2=z_P$, the image of $(-I,\ldots,-I)$. The map $\Phi[q,g]=[\sigma_Qq,Wg]$ is a well-defined automorphism of the principal $P$ bundle $E$ covering $\tau$, since $[\sigma_Q(qs),Ws^{-1}g]=[(\sigma_Qq)s^{-1},sWg]$. It preserves the induced connection, and $\Phi^2$ is right multiplication by the central element $z_P$. Gluing $X\times[0,1]$ by $\tau$, its Spin bundle by $\tilde\tau$, and $E\times[0,1]$ by $\Phi$ gives a closed Spin five-manifold $Y(c,d)$ with a principal $P$ bundle and connection. The homomorphism $P\to G$ induced by the inclusion of $P$ in $S\times P\times T$ makes it a $G$ bundle, whose image in $BH$ is trivial.

*Characteristic numbers of the representatives.* Let $Z_k$ be the mapping torus of conjugation on the $k$th sphere factor of $X$. It is a closed nonorientable three-manifold whose first mod-two cohomology is spanned by the time class $\theta$, so $w_1(Z_k)=\theta$. The Wang sequence gives a class in $H^2(Z_k;\mathbb F_2)$ restricting to the generator of the sphere. By the Wu formula its first square is $\theta$ times the class, which is the nonzero top class, and its square vanishes for degree reasons. Pull these classes back to $x,y\in H^2(Y(c,d);\mathbb F_2)$ along the projections $Y(c,d)\to Z_1,Z_2$. Then $\mathrm{Sq}^1x=\theta x$, $\mathrm{Sq}^1y=\theta y$, $x^2=y^2=0$ and $\langle\theta xy,[Y(c,d)]_2\rangle=1$. Restriction $H^2(Y(c,d);\mathbb F_2)\to H^2(X;\mathbb F_2)$ is an isomorphism by the Wang sequence, since $H^1(X;\mathbb F_2)=0$ and $\tau$ acts trivially on $H^2(X;\mathbb F_2)$. On $X$ the $j$th adjoint bundle is a trivial line plus the realification of the line of degrees $\pm c_j,\pm d_j$. Hence $a_j=c_jx+d_jy$, $u_j=\theta a_j$, and
$$
\langle a_\alpha u_\beta,[Y(c,d)]_2\rangle=c_\alpha d_\beta+c_\beta d_\alpha .
$$
By the detection isomorphism, $[Y(c,d)]=\sum_{\alpha<\beta}(c_\alpha d_\beta+c_\beta d_\alpha)M_{\alpha\beta}$, and its coefficient vector is the exterior product of the information coordinates of $c$ and $d$. Projection to the information coordinates is an isomorphism $C\to\mathbb F_2^r$, and the exterior products of pairs from a basis of $\mathbb F_2^r$ form a basis of its second exterior power. Hence the classes $[Y(c^{(k)},c^{(l)})]$, $k<l$, form a basis of the kernel of the projection to $BH$, which is the summand $(\mathbb Z/2)^{\binom r2}$ of (T.9.2m.1).

*Phase of one species on a representative.* Fix a species $i$. On $Y(c,d)$ the $S$ and torus connections are trivial, so its coefficient bundle is the bundle associated with $E$ by $V_i$, tensored with a trivial $\mathbb C^{D_i}$. The tensor product $J_i$ of the quaternionic structures of the $SU(2)$ factors on $V_i$ commutes with $SU(2)^m$, and $J_i^2=(-1)^{|\nu_i|}$. Together with complex conjugation on $\mathbb C^{D_i}$ it is a parallel antiunitary structure on the coefficient bundle commuting with $\Phi$. With the operator $J$ of (W.14q.14), $J\otimes J_i$ anticommutes with the five-dimensional Dirac operator $\mathcal D_5$ and has square $-(-1)^{|\nu_i|}$. The nonzero spectrum is therefore symmetric and $\eta(\mathcal D_5)=0$. If $|\nu_i|$ is even the kernel is quaternionic and the phase is one, as in (W.14q.14). If $|\nu_i|$ is odd the phase is $(-1)^{\dim_{\mathbb C}\ker\mathcal D_5}$.

To compute this kernel, let $\mathcal D_X$ be the Dirac operator of $X$ on both chiralities with the same coefficients. On the product $X\times[0,1]$, $\mathcal D_5^2=-\partial_t^2+\mathcal D_X^2$. The gluing operator $U$ formed from $\tilde\tau$ and $\Phi$ is unitary, preserves chirality and commutes with $\mathcal D_X$. Integration by parts on the closed manifold therefore identifies $\ker\mathcal D_5$ with the $U$-invariant part of $\ker\mathcal D_X$, as in the mapping-torus mod-two index computation of Wang et al. (2019, §2). On $X$ the coefficient bundle is the sum of the weight lines of $V_i$, each tensored with $\mathbb C^{D_i}$. On a round sphere the Dirac operator coupled to the homogeneous line of degree $p$ is $\sqrt2(\bar\partial+\bar\partial^*)$ on forms of type $(0,*)$ with values in $\mathcal O(p-1)$. Its kernel is the Dolbeault cohomology, of dimensions $\max(p,0)$ and $\max(-p,0)$ in the two chiralities, hence of total dimension $|p|$. The product Dirac square is the sum of the two nonnegative sphere Dirac squares, so the weight-$\mu$ kernel $K_\mu$ has dimension $D_i|p_\mu q_\mu|$. Through $W$, $\Phi$ carries weight $\mu$ to weight $-\mu$, so $U$ interchanges $K_\mu$ and $K_{-\mu}$. Its square is $\tilde\tau^2$ times the action of $z_P$, namely $-(-1)^{|\nu_i|}=1$. An involution interchanging two spaces has invariant subspace of dimension equal to that of either space. Summing over the pairs $\{\mu,-\mu\}$ gives $\dim\ker\mathcal D_5=\frac{D_i}2\sum_\mu|p_\mu q_\mu|$, so the phase of species $i$ on $Y(c,d)$ is $(-1)^{B_i(c,d)}$. The other Spin lift $-\tilde\tau$ replaces the invariant subspace by the $-1$ eigenspace, of the same dimension.

*The gate.* Vanishing of the local polynomial on the entire algebra, including all torus and mixed terms, is necessary as in Theorem T.9.2i. After it vanishes, the exponentiated reduced $\eta$ invariant of $\mathcal F$ is a character of $\Omega_5^{\mathrm{Spin}}(BG)$. By the detection isomorphism and the basis of mixed classes, this group is generated by the lifted $H$ instanton classes and the classes $[Y(c^{(k)},c^{(l)})]$, $k<l$. On a lifted $H$ instanton the character is the sign of the instanton index with the additional factor dimensions among the spectators, which gives the rows of (T.9.2i.2). On $Y(c^{(k)},c^{(l)})$ it is $\prod_i(-1)^{m_iB_i(c^{(k)},c^{(l)})}$, which gives (T.9.2n.3). The three conditions are therefore necessary and sufficient. For an admitted stock, solving the equivariant tensor system (T.9.2h.3)–(T.9.2h.4) on the honest covering representations and applying the calibrated probes of Theorem T.9.2h gives the finite threshold, Yukawa, mixing and marked response packet on the same gauge and mass generators.

*The trifundamental.* For $m=3$ and $C=\{000,110,101,011\}$ the all-active sign is absent and $C^\perp=\{000,111\}$. The trifundamental $n=(1,1,1)$ is therefore honest, with $\nu=\{1,2,3\}$, $D=1$ and $\varepsilon=1$. It carries no torus charge, and representations of $SU(2)^3$ have no linear or cubic trace, so its local polynomial vanishes. The group $H$ is trivial. For $c=(1,0,1)$ and $d=(0,1,1)$, (T.9.2n.2) gives $B=c_1d_2+c_2d_1=1$. Directly from (T.9.2n.1), among the eight weights $(\pm1,\pm1,\pm1)$ both $c\cdot\mu/2$ and $d\cdot\mu/2$ are nonzero only for $\pm(1,1,1)$, each contributing one to the sum. A single trifundamental thus fails (T.9.2n.3), and two trifundamentals pass every condition.

## T.10 The Electroweak 5-Plane

### T.10.1 Decomposition of the Inactive Subspace

<a id="theorem-t8-complex-electroweak-carrier-on-the-ordered-full-block-branch"></a>**Theorem T.8 (Complex Electroweak Carrier on the Ordered Full-Block Branch).** On the ordered flag lift $\pi:\widetilde X=\mathrm{Flag}_{1,2,3}(Q)\to X=\mathrm{Gr}(2,8)$ of Theorem G.8.4c.0c, whose block ranks are fixed by the inactive-sector certificate of Theorem G.8.4b,
$$
\pi^*Q
\cong
\widetilde Q_C\oplus\widetilde Q_W\oplus\widetilde Q_Y,
\qquad
\operatorname{rk}_{\mathbb C}
(\widetilde Q_C,\widetilde Q_W,\widetilde Q_Y)
=(3,2,1).
$$
The electroweak normalization carrier is the complex rank-$5$ bundle
$$
W_5:=\widetilde Q_C\oplus\widetilde Q_W.
$$
It is unique up to independent $U(3)\times U(2)$ block-frame changes once the ordered full-block certificate is specified. A local unitary fiber isometry from the active rank-$2$ bundle to $\widetilde Q_W$ transports the Pauli $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ action by Theorem G.8.4c.0c; this is a local frame identification, not a real tensor factorization or a canonical global bundle isomorphism. This transport does not specify a simultaneous physical $SU(2)$ action on the active bundle. The literal-spectrum threshold specialization in Definition T.17a takes the active gauge action to be trivial; the link-labelling branch of Theorem T.18a uses its separately declared transported doublet action.

*Proof.* Theorem G.8.4b gives the unique block split $3+2+1$ of the inactive-sector certificate, and Theorem G.8.4c.0c realizes it as the displayed splitting of $\pi^*Q$ on the ordered flag lift. Its rank-$3$ and rank-$2$ summands define $W_5$. Unitary changes preserving the ordered summands form $U(3)\times U(2)$. Transport through a local unitary fiber isometry preserves commutators and the Hermitian trace pairing, so it carries the Pauli action to the weak block. ∎

**Remark T.8a (Scope: Gauge Carrier versus Row-Pair Labelling).** The gauge-module content of the $b=6$ sector is the ordered complex block decomposition above; no real $\mathbb R^6\cong\mathbb R^3\otimes\mathbb R^2$ gauge-module identification is used here. The separate real row-pair identification of Theorem T.30 remains available as a labelling of the six left-chiral links by pair index and within-pair index. Results that consume that labelling, including the link count of Theorem T.18a and the generation projectors of Theorem T.31, rest on Theorem T.30 rather than on this theorem, and the $SU(2)_L$ action they invoke is carried by the weak block $\widetilde Q_W$.

<a id="definition-t14a-electroweak-5-plane"></a>**Definition T.14a (Electroweak 5-Plane).** On this branch,
$$
W_5
=\widetilde Q_C\oplus\widetilde Q_W
\cong\mathbb C^3\oplus\mathbb C^2.
$$
The color and weak blocks carry their fundamental complex $SU(3)$ and $SU(2)$ actions. Throughout Appendix T, $Y$ denotes hypercharge in the convention $Q_{\mathrm{em}}=T_3+Y$; Appendix W uses the doubled generator $Y_W=2Y$ in $Q_{\mathrm{em}}=T_3+Y_W/2$. A block-scalar hypercharge endomorphism has the form
$$
Y=\operatorname{diag}(y_cI_3,y_wI_2).
$$

### T.10.2 Hypercharge Structure

<a id="theorem-t9"></a>**Theorem T.9** (Traceless Hypercharge). Let
$$
Y=\operatorname{diag}(y_c,y_c,y_c,y_w,y_w)
$$
be a diagonal hypercharge generator on $W_5$. Assume that $Y$ lies in the embedded $\mathfrak{su}(5)$, equivalently that $Y$ is Hilbert–Schmidt orthogonal to the identity. Then
$$
3y_c+2y_w=0.
$$

*Proof.* Since $Y\in\mathfrak{su}(5)$ is Hermitian in the physics convention, its matrix trace vanishes. Thus
$$
0=\operatorname{Tr}Y=3y_c+2y_w.
$$
The Hilbert–Schmidt condition is equivalent because $\langle I_5,Y\rangle_{\mathrm{HS}}=\operatorname{Tr}Y$. ∎

<a id="corollary-t91"></a>**Corollary T.9.1** (Hypercharge Ratio). If $y_c\ne0$, then
$$
\frac{y_w}{y_c}=-\frac32.
$$

*Proof.* Theorem T.9 gives $2y_w=-3y_c$. Division by $2y_c\ne0$ gives the displayed ratio. ∎

## T.11 Minimal Rational Hypercharge and the 5/3 Factor

### T.11.1 Uniqueness of Minimal Solution

<a id="theorem-t10"></a>**Theorem T.10** (Primitive $1/6$-Quantized Hypercharge). Assume the hypercharge generator on $W_5$ has diagonal entries $(y_c,y_c,y_c,y_w,y_w)\in\mathbb Q^5$, satisfies the tracelessness condition
$$
3y_c+2y_w=0,
$$
and is normalized so that all charges are integer multiples of $1/6$ while the pair $(6y_c,6y_w)$ is primitive in $\mathbb Z^2$. Then, up to an overall sign, the unique admissible rational solution is
$$
(y_c,y_w)=\left(-\frac13,\frac12\right).
$$
Choosing the orientation in which the weak-doublet entry is positive gives
$$
y_c = -\frac{1}{3}, \quad y_w = +\frac{1}{2}.
$$

*Proof.* Set
$$
m:=6y_c,\qquad n:=6y_w.
$$
By hypothesis, $(m,n)\in\mathbb Z^2$ is primitive and the tracelessness relation becomes
$$
3m+2n=0.
$$
Every integer solution has the form
$$
(m,n)=(-2\ell,3\ell),\qquad \ell\in\mathbb Z.
$$
Primitivity forces $|\ell|=1$, because $\gcd(2|\ell|,3|\ell|)=|\ell|$. Thus the only primitive integer solutions are
$$
(-2,3)\qquad\text{and}\qquad (2,-3).
$$
Dividing by $6$ gives the two admissible rational solutions
$$
\left(-\frac13,\frac12\right),\qquad \left(\frac13,-\frac12\right).
$$
They differ only by an overall sign. Adopting the orientation in which the weak-doublet entry is positive yields
$$
y_c=-\frac13,\qquad y_w=\frac12.
$$
This is the block assignment $\mathbf3_{-1/3}\oplus\mathbf2_{1/2}$ for the fundamental color and weak actions specified above. ∎

<a id="theorem-t111a-anomaly-only-abelian-charge-catalog-on-the-one-family-shapes"></a>**Theorem T.11.1a (Anomaly-Only Abelian Charge Catalog on the One-Family Shapes).** Fix the one-family representation shape
$$
Q=(3,2),\qquad u^c=(\bar3,1),\qquad d^c=(\bar3,1),\qquad L=(1,2),\qquad e^c=(1,1)
$$
(SM15), or this shape with one gauge-singlet Weyl fermion $\nu^c$ (SM16), and let the abelian charges $y=(y_q,y_{u^c},y_{d^c},y_\ell,y_{e^c},y_{\nu^c})$ be unrestricted real numbers, with $y_{\nu^c}:=0$ on SM15. Impose the $[SU(3)]^2U(1)$, $[SU(2)]^2U(1)$, mixed gravitational and $[U(1)]^3$ anomaly equations
$$
2y_q+y_{u^c}+y_{d^c}=0,
\qquad
3y_q+y_\ell=0,
\qquad
6y_q+3y_{u^c}+3y_{d^c}+2y_\ell+y_{e^c}+y_{\nu^c}=0,
$$
$$
6y_q^3+3y_{u^c}^3+3y_{d^c}^3+2y_\ell^3+y_{e^c}^3+y_{\nu^c}^3=0.
\tag{T.11.1a.1}
$$
The $[SU(3)]^3$ and $SU(2)$ Witten conditions hold on both shapes for every $y$, because the shape contains two color triplets against two antitriplets and four weak doublets. Then:

1. On SM15, in the coordinates $(y_q,y_{u^c},y_{d^c},y_\ell,y_{e^c})$, the solution set is the union of three lines,
$$
\mathbb R(1,-4,2,-3,6)\ \cup\ \mathbb R(1,2,-4,-3,6)\ \cup\ \mathbb R(0,1,-1,0,0);
\tag{T.11.1a.2}
$$
the second is the image of the first under the relabeling $u^c\leftrightarrow d^c$ of equal gauge representations.
2. On SM16, the three linear equations have the general solution $y_{u^c}=-y_q+s$, $y_{d^c}=-y_q-s$, $y_\ell=-3y_q$, $y_{e^c}=3y_q+r$, $y_{\nu^c}=3y_q-r$, and the cubic equation becomes
$$
18\,y_q\,(r-s)(r+s)=0.
\tag{T.11.1a.3}
$$
The solution set is therefore the union of the three planes $\Pi_0=\{y_q=0\}$, $\Pi_+=\{r=s\}$ and $\Pi_-=\{r=-s\}$, where $\Pi_-=\operatorname{span}\{(1,-4,2,-3,6,0),(1,-1,-1,-3,3,3)\}$ is spanned by six times the Standard Model hypercharge and $3(B-L)$, and $\Pi_+$ is its image under $u^c\leftrightarrow d^c$, equivalently under $e^c\leftrightarrow\nu^c$.
3. Up to these relabelings, anomaly cancellation alone leaves two classes on SM15, the Standard Model ray and the quark-only line $(0,t,-t,0,0)$, and two classes on SM16, the plane $\Pi_-$ and the plane $\Pi_0$. The Yukawa equations of Theorem G.8.1a with one Higgs doublet, which distinguish $u^c$ from $d^c$ by their Higgs couplings, retain on SM15 only the ray $\mathbb R(1,-4,2,-3,6)$.

*Proof.* The first equation of (T.11.1a.1) gives $y_{u^c}+y_{d^c}=-2y_q$, the second $y_\ell=-3y_q$, and substitution into the gravitational equation gives $y_{e^c}+y_{\nu^c}=6y_q$; this is the displayed parametrization. Using $(\alpha+\beta)^3+(\alpha-\beta)^3=2\alpha^3+6\alpha\beta^2$,
$$
3\bigl[(-y_q+s)^3+(-y_q-s)^3\bigr]=-6y_q^3-18y_qs^2,
\qquad
(3y_q+r)^3+(3y_q-r)^3=54y_q^3+18y_qr^2,
$$
so the cubic sum equals $6y_q^3-6y_q^3-18y_qs^2-54y_q^3+54y_q^3+18y_qr^2=18y_q(r^2-s^2)$, which is (T.11.1a.3). Each factor defines a plane, and the two displayed vectors satisfy $r=-s$ with $(y_q,s)=(1,-3)$ and $(1,0)$, so they span $\Pi_-$. The relabeling $u^c\leftrightarrow d^c$ sends $s\mapsto-s$ and $e^c\leftrightarrow\nu^c$ sends $r\mapsto-r$; both exchange $\Pi_+$ and $\Pi_-$ and fix $\Pi_0$. On SM15, $y_{\nu^c}=0$ forces $r=3y_q$, and (T.11.1a.3) becomes $18y_q(3y_q-s)(3y_q+s)=0$. The factor $y_q=0$ gives $r=0$ and the quark-only line, $s=-3y_q$ gives the Standard Model ray, and $s=3y_q$ gives its relabeled image, proving (T.11.1a.2). For item 3, the Yukawa equations of Theorem G.8.1a are $y_q+y_H+y_{u^c}=0$, $y_q-y_H+y_{d^c}=0$ and $y_\ell-y_H+y_{e^c}=0$. For $y=a(1,2,-4,-3,6)$ the first gives $y_H=-3a$ and the third then gives $6a=0$. For $y=(0,t,-t,0,0)$ the first gives $y_H=-t$ and the third then gives $t=0$. Every $y=a(1,-4,2,-3,6)$ satisfies all three with $y_H=3a$. ∎

<a id="theorem-t111b"></a>

<a id="theorem-t111b-global-electroweak-vacuum-census-for-singlets-and-doublets"></a>**Theorem T.11.1b (Global Electroweak Vacuum Census for Singlets and Doublets).** Retain the marked standard-family representations of Theorem G.8.5b and their primitive hypercharge convention $q=6Y$. Write $G_d=(SU(3)\times SU(2)\times U(1))/\Gamma_d$ for the four marked forms of Theorem G.8.5j.2, where $d\mid6$ and $\Gamma_d$ is generated by $(\omega_3^{6/d}I_3,(-I_2)^{6/d},e^{2\pi i/d})$. Fix any finite collection of honest complex color-singlet weak doublets $h_i$ of integer charges $q_i$ and complex color-singlet weak singlets $s_j$ of integer charges $p_j$. On each $G_d$, every value $v$ of these fields has the following exact global stabilizer and physical quadratic gauge mass map. With a supplied real-algebraic coercive invariant polynomial potential, the global vacuum orbits and the normal scalar stability tests have a terminating semialgebraic catalog.

*Stabilizer.* Keep only the nonzero singlet and doublet values in forming the following lists. Put $\mu_k=\{z\in U(1):z^k=1\}$ for $k>0$, $\mu_0=U(1)$ and $\gcd(\varnothing)=0$. In each row let $k$ be the nonnegative gcd of the active singlet charges $p_j$ together with the listed integers.

| Occupied doublet rays | Additional integers in the gcd | Allowed weak matrix $U$ for $z\in\mu_k$ |
|---|---|---|
| None | Empty list | Any $U\in SU(2)$ |
| One ray $L$ with representative charge $q_*$ | All $q_i-q_*$ | $z^{-q_*}$ on $L$ and $z^{q_*}$ on $L^\perp$ |
| Exactly two orthogonal rays with representative charges $q_*,q_{**}$ | Charge differences within each ray, and $q_*+q_{**}$ | $z^{-q_*}$ on the first ray and $z^{-q_{**}}$ on the second |
| A nonorthogonal pair of distinct rays | All $q_i-q_*$ and $2q_*$, for any representative $q_*$ | $z^{-q_*}I_2$ |

The stabilizer $H_{d,v}$ in $G_d$ is the indicated subgroup of $SU(3)\times SU(2)\times U(1)$, with the whole $SU(3)$ factor, divided by $\Gamma_d$. For $k>0$ one has $d\mid k$ and $\pi_0(H_{d,v})\simeq\mathbb Z/(k/d)$. For $k=0$ the stabilizer is connected. The orbit of each vacuum is $G_d/H_{d,v}$. With any occupied doublet it has three real broken gauge directions if $k=0$, and four if $k>0$. With only singlet values it has zero or one, respectively.

*Proof of the census.* A singlet requires $z^{p_j}=1$. An occupied doublet requires $U h_i=z^{-q_i}h_i$. On a single ray these equalities impose the indicated differences, and determinant one fixes the action on its orthogonal complement. On two orthogonal rays the eigenvalues are fixed on a basis and their product imposes the indicated sum. A unitary matrix has orthogonal eigenspaces for distinct eigenvalues. A nonorthogonal pair spanning $\mathbb C^2$ therefore forces a single eigenvalue on the whole doublet space. The determinant and every other occupied vector give the last row. Bezout's identity combines all circle equations into $z\in\mu_k$. Each weak matrix in the last three rows is a homomorphism of this circle subgroup. The descent equations for these scalars are $p_j\equiv0$ and $q_i+3\equiv0\pmod d$. They make every listed integer a multiple of $d$. All scalar representations descend, so the entire $\Gamma_d$ acts trivially on every value. Its projection to the circle is precisely $\mu_d$. The prequotient stabilizer has connected semisimple factor or factors and circle factor $\mu_k$, giving the asserted component count and dimensions.

*Physical vacuum and mass entries.* Let $V$ be the real scalar carrier with its positive invariant kinetic metric, written so that the real scalar kinetic term is $\tfrac12\langle Dv,Dv\rangle$. Use the positive gauge kinetic metric to normalize gauge fields. Include the supplied gauge couplings in the infinitesimal covariant derivative using gauge fields in their canonical kinetic coordinates. Let $A_v X=X\cdot v$ be the resulting orbit derivative. In the quadratic covariant scalar kinetic term, the squared gauge mass operator is $A_v^*A_v$. Its kernel is the Lie algebra of $H_{d,v}$ in those coordinates, since $\langle X,A_v^*A_v X\rangle=\|A_vX\|^2$. Thus the table gives the exact number of zero and nonzero weak and abelian gauge masses and the finite component group of the stabilizer, which the infinitesimal kernel cannot distinguish. For the scalar potential $P$, the normal scalar mass operator is the kinetic-metric Hessian on $(\operatorname{im}A_v)^\perp$. Invariance and criticality imply that the Hessian annihilates the gauge orbit tangent, by differentiating the covariance of the gradient along the orbit. Its strictly positive normal spectrum is the test for a positive quadratic scalar gap. If a normal eigenvalue is zero, the gap vanishes and the minimizer test still determines the global vacuum set. Any supplied invariant fermion mass polynomial evaluates at the same $v$ and obeys $R(g)^T M(v)R(g)=M(v)$ for every $g\in H_{d,v}$. With canonical positive fermion kinetic terms its singular values and mass subspaces give the rest-energy and residual representation packet, with the comparison probes and multiplicities as in Theorems T.9.2g–h.

To compute the vacuum orbits, use the real and imaginary coordinates of $v$. A value is a global minimizer exactly when $P(v)\le P(w)$ for all real $w$. Coercivity supplies a nonempty compact minimizing set. The orbit at a value is compact, and its unique lexicographic minimum exists by successively minimizing each coordinate over the previous compact level set. The algebraic equations of $SU(2)$ and $U(1)$ and the integer-charge action give a real-algebraic formula for this comparison. Negative powers of $z$ are powers of its conjugate. The center quotient has the same scalar orbit as the covering group. Real quantifier elimination therefore gives a finite semialgebraic description with one point per vacuum orbit, including continuous families when present. The ray cases are algebraic tests for vanishing vectors, proportionality and orthogonality. Quadratic mass values and the positive normal gap can be adjoined by polynomial equations for the operators, their characteristic polynomials, and the positive kinetic form on the orthogonal complement. The potential and kinetic coefficients are inputs. The effective quantifier elimination input is the one used in Theorem W.14i.

*Marked standard one-doublet component.* For $v$ of the usual doublet of $q_*=3$ and no occupied charged singlets, the table gives $k=0$. On the orbit choose $h=(0,v_0/\sqrt2)$, $v_0>0$. The global unbroken group and its representations are
$$
H_{d,v}\simeq(SU(3)\times U(1))/\langle(\omega_3^{6/d}I_3,e^{2\pi i/d})\rangle,\qquad
2a+n\equiv0\pmod d,
\tag{T.11.1b.1}
$$
where $a$ is color triality and $n$ is the circle exponent. Indeed the embedding of the prequotient stabilizer sends $(c,z)$ to $(c,\operatorname{diag}(z^3,z^{-3}),z)$. On an electroweak weight $m$ of hypercharge $q/6$ it gives $n=q+6m$, and electric charge in units of the positron charge is $n/6$. Conversely every allowed residual weight extends to an honest ultraviolet representation by taking a weak singlet of charge $q=n$ and the specified color representation. The orbit is the radius-$v_0/\sqrt2$ sphere $S^3$, since $SU(2)$ is transitive on the unit sphere of its doublet. For $P=\lambda(h^\dagger h-v_0^2/2)^2$ with $\lambda>0$, this is the entire minimum set. The canonical gauge kinetic normalization gives quadratic terms proportional to $g^2[(W^1)^2+(W^2)^2]+(gW^3-g'B)^2$ with coefficient $v_0^2/8$. The radial scalar has curvature $2\lambda v_0^2$. The physical quadratic masses are $m_W=gv_0/2$, $m_Z=v_0\sqrt{g^2+g'^2}/2$, $m_h=\sqrt{2\lambda}v_0$ and $m_\gamma=0$, with $e=gg'/\sqrt{g^2+g'^2}$.

The pure color-singlet Wilson characters of the residual group have electric charges $(d/6)\mathbb Z$. In a comparison that registers their allowed charge lattice, all four marked forms are distinct. For a fixed set of fields and local probes descending to all four forms, the covariant kinetic, potential and mass equations on a common trivialized neighborhood are identical at equal local input coefficients. Such a comparison gives equal cost whenever its objective is a function only of these local responses. A Wilson character in (T.11.1b.1) records an allowed line, with the propagating matter stock determined separately. The dependence of the Standard Model line spectrum on the quotient was computed by Tong (2017, Section 3, especially Section 3.2).

### T.11.2 Design-Preserving Inner Product

<a id="definition-t15a"></a>**Definition T.15a** (Hilbert-Schmidt Norm). For diagonal generators on $W_5$:
$$
\langle A, B \rangle_{\mathrm{HS}} = \operatorname{Tr}(A^\dagger B)
$$

<a id="theorem-t11"></a>**Theorem T.11** (Hypercharge Norm). The Hilbert--Schmidt norm of the hypercharge generator is:
$$
\lVert Y\rVert_{\mathrm{HS}}^2 = \operatorname{Tr}(Y^2) = 3\left(\frac{1}{3}\right)^2 + 2\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^2 = \frac{1}{3} + \frac{1}{2} = \frac{5}{6}
$$

*Proof.* On the primitive-$(1/6)$-quantized traceless branch of Theorem T.10,
$$
Y=\operatorname{diag}\left(-\frac13,-\frac13,-\frac13,\frac12,\frac12\right).
$$
Because $Y$ is Hermitian,
$$
\|Y\|_{\mathrm{HS}}^2=\operatorname{Tr}(Y^2)
=3\left(\frac19\right)+2\left(\frac14\right)=\frac56.
$$
∎

### T.11.3 Canonical Normalization and the 5/3 Factor

<a id="definition-t16a"></a>**Definition T.16a** ($SU(2)$ Generator Normalization). The $SU(2)_L$ generators $T_a = \sigma_a/2$ satisfy:
$$
\operatorname{Tr}(T_a T_b) = \frac{1}{2}\delta_{ab}
$$

<a id="theorem-t12"></a>**Theorem T.12** (GUT Normalization Factor). Define canonically normalized hypercharge $\hat{Y}$ by:
$$
\operatorname{Tr}(\hat{Y}^2) = \frac{1}{2} = \operatorname{Tr}(T_a^2)
$$
Then:
$$
\hat{Y} = \frac{Y}{\sqrt{5/3}}, \quad \boxed{c^2 = \frac{5}{3}}
$$

*Proof.* From $\operatorname{Tr}(Y^2) = 5/6$, requiring $\operatorname{Tr}(\hat{Y}^2) = 1/2$ gives $c^2 = (5/6)/(1/2) = 5/3$. ∎

<a id="remark-t121-origin-of-53"></a>**Remark T.12.1: Origin of 5/3.** The factor $5/3$, traditionally assumed from $SU(5)$ grand unification, emerges here on the primitive-$(1/6)$-quantized, traceless, $(3 + 2)$ hypercharge branch — the three explicit hypotheses of Theorem T.10. Under those hypotheses, the $SU(5)$ group embedding is not separately required: the same constraints (rational charges, tracelessness on the 5-plane, primitive $(1/6)$-quantization) suffice to fix $(y_c, y_w) = (-1/3, 1/2)$ and hence $\operatorname{Tr}(Y^2) = 5/6$ giving $c^2 = 5/3$. The Hypercharge $5/3$ row in the summary tables (T.19.1, T.20) inherits this branch.
