### <a id="t209-sector-prefactor-structure"></a>T.20.9 Sector Prefactor Structure ✓

<a id="theorem-t34"></a>**Theorem T.34** (Normalization-induced prefactor ratios). Let
$$
z_{\text{sector}} := \kappa_2\,C_2^{SU(2)}\,g^2 + \kappa_1\,Y^2 g^2 + \kappa_3\,C_2^{SU(3)}\,g^2 N_c
$$
denote the Bures-normalization factor for a given fermion sector (with $N_c=3$ for color triplets and $N_c=1$ for color singlets). The corresponding Yukawa prefactor is
$$
c_{\text{sector}} = \frac{Y_0}{\sqrt{z_{\text{sector}}}}.
$$

*Proof.* In the prefactor ratio computation one uses the PU-normalized gauge coefficient $g_U$ for canonical generators (Theorem T.13); the SM-canonical matching factors $Z_i$ control the gauge-boson kinetic terms but do not alter the fermion-sector prefactor ratios set by the Bures weights $\kappa_i$ (Theorem T.34). The sector normalization entering the prefactor tilt is

|Sector |$C_2(SU(2))$|$Y^2$ |$C_2(SU(3))$|$N_c$|
|--------------------------|------------|------|------------|-----|
|Lepton doublet ($\ell_L$) |$3/4$ |$1/4$ |$0$ |$1$ |
|Down quark doublet ($d_L$)|$3/4$ |$1/36$|$4/3$ |$3$ |

Therefore:
$$
z_\ell = \left(\frac{3}{4}\kappa_2 + \frac{\kappa_1}{4}\right)g_U^2,\qquad
z_d = \left(\frac{3}{4}\kappa_2 + \frac{\kappa_1}{36} + 4\kappa_3\right)g_U^2,
$$
and the prefactor ratio is
$$
\frac{c_\ell}{c_d} = \sqrt{\frac{z_d}{z_\ell}}.
$$
(Note: $c \propto 1/\sqrt{z}$, so $c_\ell/c_d = \sqrt{z_d/z_\ell}$, not $z_d/z_\ell$.)
∎

<a id="corollary-t341"></a>**Corollary T.34.1** (Normalization Constraint). Imposing the lepton-to-quark tilt normalization
$$
\frac{c_\ell}{c_d} = \frac{8}{3}
$$
is equivalent to $z_d/z_\ell = 64/9$. Writing this out:
$$
\frac{\tfrac{3}{4}\kappa_2 + \tfrac{\kappa_1}{36} + 4\kappa_3}{\tfrac{3}{4}\kappa_2 + \tfrac{\kappa_1}{4}} = \frac{64}{9}.
$$
Cross-multiplying: $9\bigl(\tfrac{3}{4}\kappa_2 + \tfrac{\kappa_1}{36} + 4\kappa_3\bigr) = 64\bigl(\tfrac{3}{4}\kappa_2 + \tfrac{\kappa_1}{4}\bigr)$, i.e.
$$
\tfrac{27}{4}\kappa_2 + \tfrac{\kappa_1}{4} + 36\kappa_3 = 48\kappa_2 + 16\kappa_1.
$$
Collecting: $36\kappa_3 = \tfrac{63}{4}\kappa_1 + \tfrac{165}{4}\kappa_2$. Multiplying by $4/3$:
$$
\boxed{21\kappa_1 + 55\kappa_2 - 48\kappa_3 = 0},
$$
equivalently $\kappa_1 = (48\kappa_3 - 55\kappa_2)/21$.

<a id="definition-t341a"></a>**Definition T.34.1a** (Bures-Weight Representation-Variance Certificate). A Bures-weight representation-variance certificate is a branch record
$$
\mathfrak B_{\kappa}
=
(\kappa_1,\kappa_2,\kappa_3,\mathcal V_{\ell d})
\tag{T.34.1a.1}
$$
with $\kappa_i>0$ and
$$
\mathcal V_{\ell d}
:=
21\kappa_1+55\kappa_2-48\kappa_3.
\tag{T.34.1a.2}
$$
The certificate is accepted when $\mathcal V_{\ell d}=0$ is derived from a PU-internal representation-variance computation before using the lepton-to-quark tilt data. A raw Casimir trace without a derivation of (T.34.1a.2)$=0$ is not an accepted certificate.

<a id="theorem-t341b"></a>**Theorem T.34.1b** (Tilt Normalization from a Bures-Weight Certificate). For positive Bures weights, the following are equivalent:
$$
\frac{c_\ell}{c_d}=\frac83,
\qquad
\frac{z_d}{z_\ell}=\frac{64}{9},
\qquad
\mathcal V_{\ell d}=0.
\tag{T.34.1b.1}
$$
Thus an accepted certificate $\mathfrak B_{\kappa}$ promotes the lepton-to-quark tilt normalization to a derived branch condition.

*Proof.* The equality $c_\ell/c_d=8/3$ is equivalent to $z_d/z_\ell=64/9$ because $c_{\mathrm{sector}}=Y_0/\sqrt{z_{\mathrm{sector}}}$ and $z_\ell,z_d>0$. Substituting
$$
z_\ell=\left(\frac34\kappa_2+\frac14\kappa_1\right)g_U^2,
\qquad
z_d=\left(\frac34\kappa_2+\frac1{36}\kappa_1+4\kappa_3\right)g_U^2
$$
and canceling $g_U^2$ gives exactly the algebra displayed in Corollary T.34.1:
$$
\frac{z_d}{z_\ell}=\frac{64}{9}
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
21\kappa_1+55\kappa_2-48\kappa_3=0.
$$
This is $\mathcal V_{\ell d}=0$. ∎

<a id="corollary-t341c"></a>**Corollary T.34.1c** (No Casimir-Only Closure of the Tilt). The value $c_\ell/c_d=8/3$ does not follow from the raw Standard Model Casimir table alone. It follows only after the Bures weights satisfy the certificate equation $\mathcal V_{\ell d}=0$.

*Proof.* The ratio is
$$
\frac{c_\ell}{c_d}
=
\sqrt{
\frac{\tfrac34\kappa_2+\tfrac1{36}\kappa_1+4\kappa_3}
{\tfrac34\kappa_2+\tfrac14\kappa_1}
}.
$$
For fixed Casimir entries, changing the positive weights $\kappa_i$ changes the ratio unless the weights are constrained. By Theorem T.34.1b, the exact value $8/3$ is equivalent to the additional weight equation $\mathcal V_{\ell d}=0$. ∎

<a id="corollary-t341d-no-mckay-only-forcing-of-the-tilt-normalization"></a>**Corollary T.34.1d (No McKay-Only Forcing of the Tilt Normalization).** A McKay quiver or Dynkin-mark computation on the lifted flag problem does not by itself force
$$
21\kappa_1+55\kappa_2-48\kappa_3=0.
\tag{T.34.1d}
$$
Indeed, if the proposed representation-theoretic identification has the form
$$
\kappa_i=C_i\chi_i,
\qquad
i=1,2,3,
$$
where $C_i$ are discrete Casimir, mark, or node-weight data and $\chi_i>0$ are sector normalization factors, then McKay data can at most fix the $C_i$ and the adjacency/mark pattern. It does not fix the continuous relative scale vector $(\chi_1,\chi_2,\chi_3)$. The normalization constraint becomes
$$
21C_1\chi_1+55C_2\chi_2-48C_3\chi_3=0,
$$
which is an additional codimension-one condition on the scale vector unless a separate PU-internal normalization certificate fixes the $\chi_i$.

Thus the definite answer to the McKay question is negative in the McKay-only sense: $c_\ell/c_d=8/3$ remains an imposed normalization branch, or else the output of a separate Bures-weight representation-variance certificate. A raw McKay quiver, even if correctly computed, is not sufficient to promote Corollary T.34.1 to an unconditional theorem.

<a id="theorem-t341e-complete-positive-weight-classification-at-fixed-total-weight"></a>**Theorem T.34.1e (Complete Positive Weight Classification at Fixed Total Weight).** In the fixed Standard Model representation and Casimir table of Theorem T.34, impose positivity and only the total-weight normalization used in Corollary T.34.2:
$$
\mathcal K_W
=
\{(\kappa_1,\kappa_2,\kappa_3)\in\mathbb R_{>0}^3:
\kappa_1+3\kappa_2+8\kappa_3=12\}.
$$
Then
$$
\mathcal K_W
=
\{(12-3s-8t,s,t):s>0,\ t>0,\ 3s+8t<12\}.
\tag{T.34.1e.1}
$$
Its exact $c_\ell/c_d=8/3$ locus is the open line segment
$$
\mathcal K_{8/3}
=
\left\{
\left(\frac{72-73s}{27},\ s,\ \frac{63-2s}{54}\right):
0<s<\frac{72}{73}
\right\}.
\tag{T.34.1e.2}
$$
Consequently positivity, the fixed Casimir table, and total-weight normalization do not force the tilt normalization. For example,
$$
(\kappa_1,\kappa_2,\kappa_3)=(1,1,1)\in\mathcal K_W,
\qquad
\mathcal V_{\ell d}=28,
\qquad
\frac{c_\ell}{c_d}=\frac{\sqrt{43}}3\ne\frac83.
\tag{T.34.1e.3}
$$

*Proof.* Put $s=\kappa_2$ and $t=\kappa_3$. The total-weight equation gives $\kappa_1=12-3s-8t$, and positivity gives exactly (T.34.1e.1). On this triangle,
$$
\mathcal V_{\ell d}
=21(12-3s-8t)+55s-48t
=252-8s-216t.
$$
Theorem T.34.1b makes $c_\ell/c_d=8/3$ equivalent to $\mathcal V_{\ell d}=0$, hence $s+27t=63/2$. Solving for $t$ and then $\kappa_1$ gives (T.34.1e.2); its three positivity inequalities reduce to $0<s<72/73$. At $(1,1,1)$, $z_\ell/g_U^2=1$ and $z_d/g_U^2=43/9$, proving (T.34.1e.3). ∎

<a id="theorem-t341f-lepton-quark-multiplet-pair-classification-of-the-tilt-ratio"></a>**Theorem T.34.1f (Lepton–Quark Multiplet-Pair Classification of the Tilt Ratio).** Extend the normalization factor of Theorem T.34 to every one-generation Standard Model multiplet $f$ by
$$
z_f=(C_f\cdot\kappa)\,g_U^2,
\qquad
C_f:=\bigl(y_f^2,\ C_2^{SU(2)}(f),\ N_c(f)\,C_2^{SU(3)}(f)\bigr),
\qquad
\kappa=(\kappa_1,\kappa_2,\kappa_3),
$$
with the hypercharges of Corollary G.8.4c.0h in the convention $Q_{\mathrm{em}}=T_3+Y$. The lepton-type vectors are $C_L=(\frac14,\frac34,0)$ and $C_{e^c}=(1,0,0)$; the quark-type vectors are $C_Q=(\frac1{36},\frac34,4)$, $C_{u^c}=(\frac49,0,4)$ and $C_{d^c}=(\frac19,0,4)$; the neutral singlet has $C_{\nu^c}=0$ and carries no prefactor. For each of the six pairs $(\ell,q)$ put
$$
\rho_{\ell q}(\kappa):=\frac{c_\ell}{c_q}=\Bigl(\frac{z_q}{z_\ell}\Bigr)^{1/2},
\qquad
m_{\ell q}:=\min\Bigl\{\frac{C_{q,i}}{C_{\ell,i}}:C_{\ell,i}>0\Bigr\}.
$$
Then, on $\mathbb R_{>0}^3$:

1. $\rho_{\ell q}(\mathbb R_{>0}^3)=(\sqrt{m_{\ell q}},\infty)$, with $m_{LQ}=\frac19$, $m_{Lu^c}=m_{Ld^c}=0$, $m_{e^cQ}=\frac1{36}$, $m_{e^cu^c}=\frac49$ and $m_{e^cd^c}=\frac19$.
2. For $\rho>\sqrt{m_{\ell q}}$ the level set $\{\rho_{\ell q}=\rho\}$ is the open two-dimensional cone $\{\kappa\in\mathbb R_{>0}^3:(C_q-\rho^2C_\ell)\cdot\kappa=0\}$, and it meets $\mathcal K_W$ of Theorem T.34.1e in a nonempty open segment.
3. Every $\rho_{\ell q}$ is nonconstant; the value $8/3$ is attained on a nonempty open segment of $\mathcal K_W$ for every pair and is forced for none.

The pair $(L,Q)$ is the table of Theorem T.34, and item 2 at $\rho=8/3$ reproduces (T.34.1e.2).

*Proof.* Each lepton vector has a positive entry and zero color entry, so $z_\ell>0$ on $\mathbb R_{>0}^3$, while each quark vector has color entry $3\cdot\frac43=4$. Splitting $C_q\cdot\kappa$ over the indices with $C_{\ell,i}>0$ and the remaining indices, which include the color index, gives
$$
C_q\cdot\kappa\ \ge\ m_{\ell q}\,C_\ell\cdot\kappa+4\kappa_3\ >\ m_{\ell q}\,C_\ell\cdot\kappa .
$$
Letting $\kappa_3\to\infty$ shows that $z_q/z_\ell$ is unbounded, and letting $\kappa_3\to0$ with the remaining weight concentrated on an index attaining $m_{\ell q}$ approaches $m_{\ell q}$. Continuity on the connected set $\mathbb R_{>0}^3$ gives item 1. For item 2, $z_q/z_\ell=\rho^2$ is the displayed linear equation. Its normal vector $C_q-\rho^2C_\ell$ has color entry $4>0$, and it has a negative entry exactly when $\rho^2>C_{q,i}/C_{\ell,i}$ for some index with $C_{\ell,i}>0$, that is, when $\rho^2>m_{\ell q}$. A plane through the origin whose normal has entries of both signs meets the open octant in a nonempty open two-dimensional cone, and each ray of that cone meets the plane $\kappa_1+3\kappa_2+8\kappa_3=12$ exactly once. Item 3 follows because $(8/3)^2=64/9$ exceeds every $m_{\ell q}$. ∎

<a id="theorem-t341g-entropy-only-weight-selection-misses-every-tilt-locus"></a>**Theorem T.34.1g (Entropy-Only Weight Selection Misses Every Tilt Locus).** On $\mathcal K_W$ the PCE objective
$$
S(\kappa)=8\kappa_3\ln\kappa_3+3\kappa_2\ln\kappa_2+\kappa_1\ln\kappa_1
$$
of Corollary T.34.2 satisfies $S\ge0$, with equality only at $\kappa=(1,1,1)$. At this unique minimizer $\mathcal V_{\ell d}=28$, and for the six pairs of Theorem T.34.1f
$$
\rho_{\ell Q}(1,1,1)=\frac{\sqrt{43}}3,
\qquad
\rho_{\ell u^c}(1,1,1)=\frac{2\sqrt{10}}3,
\qquad
\rho_{\ell d^c}(1,1,1)=\frac{\sqrt{37}}3
\qquad(\ell\in\{L,e^c\}),
\tag{T.34.1g.1}
$$
none of which equals $8/3$. Consequently the minimizer of Corollary T.34.2 on $\mathcal K_W\cap\{\mathcal V_{\ell d}=0\}$ has strictly positive objective, numerically $0.2482437938\ldots$, and the equation $\mathcal N$ enters Corollary T.34.2 as a constraint independent of the entropy objective.

*Proof.* Put $n=(1,3,8)$, so $\sum_in_i=12$ and $\mathcal W$ reads $\sum_in_i\kappa_i=12$. Jensen's inequality for the strictly convex function $x\ln x$ with probability weights $n_i/12$ gives
$$
\frac{S(\kappa)}{12}=\sum_i\frac{n_i}{12}\,\kappa_i\ln\kappa_i\ \ge\ \Bigl(\sum_i\frac{n_i\kappa_i}{12}\Bigr)\ln\Bigl(\sum_i\frac{n_i\kappa_i}{12}\Bigr)=0,
$$
with equality exactly when $\kappa_1=\kappa_2=\kappa_3$, hence $\kappa=(1,1,1)$ on $\mathcal K_W$. There $\mathcal V_{\ell d}=21+55-48=28$ and $z_q/z_\ell=\sum_iC_{q,i}/\sum_iC_{\ell,i}$. Since $\sum_iC_L=\sum_iC_{e^c}=1$, $\sum_iC_Q=\frac{43}9$, $\sum_iC_{u^c}=\frac{40}9$ and $\sum_iC_{d^c}=\frac{37}9$, this gives (T.34.1g.1). The point $(1,1,1)$ is the unique zero of $S$ on $\mathcal K_W$ and violates $\mathcal V_{\ell d}=0$, so the constrained minimum of Corollary T.34.2 is positive; its numerical value follows from the weights computed there. ∎

<a id="remark-t341h-hypercharge-weight-transport"></a>**Remark T.34.1h (Hypercharge Weight Transport).** The weight coordinates of Definition T.17a and Remark T.17a.3, written $\kappa^{\mathrm{can}}$ here, multiply the canonical generator $\hat Y=\sqrt{3/5}\,Y_{\mathrm{SM}}$; the coordinates of Theorem T.34, Theorems T.34.1e–T.34.1g and Corollary T.34.2, written $\kappa^{\mathrm{SM}}$, multiply the Standard Model hypercharge squares of the table of Theorem T.34. If both describe the same gauge-weighted quadratic operator, with unchanged nonabelian generator conventions, then
$$
\kappa_1^{\mathrm{SM}}=\frac35\kappa_1^{\mathrm{can}},\qquad
\kappa_2^{\mathrm{SM}}=\kappa_2^{\mathrm{can}},\qquad
\kappa_3^{\mathrm{SM}}=\kappa_3^{\mathrm{can}}.
\tag{T.34.1h.1}
$$
This is a condition on coordinates; the threshold interface of Definition T.17a and the matter normalization of Theorem T.34 keep their separate representation and matching requirements. For one common canonical positive triple the matter factors are
$$
\frac{z_\ell}{g_U^2}=\frac34\kappa_2^{\mathrm{can}}+\frac3{20}\kappa_1^{\mathrm{can}},\qquad
\frac{z_d}{g_U^2}=\frac34\kappa_2^{\mathrm{can}}+\frac1{60}\kappa_1^{\mathrm{can}}+4\kappa_3^{\mathrm{can}},
$$
so the $8/3$ tilt condition $9z_d=64z_\ell$ reads
$$
\frac{63}{5}\kappa_1^{\mathrm{can}}+55\kappa_2^{\mathrm{can}}-48\kappa_3^{\mathrm{can}}=0.
\tag{T.34.1h.2}
$$
For positive $\kappa_1^{\mathrm{can}}$ it cannot hold together with $21\kappa_1^{\mathrm{can}}+55\kappa_2^{\mathrm{can}}-48\kappa_3^{\mathrm{can}}=0$, the equation of Corollary T.34.1 with its numbers reused in canonical coordinates; on that plane
$$
\frac{z_d}{z_\ell}=\frac{64}{9}+\frac{14\kappa_1^{\mathrm{can}}}{3(\kappa_1^{\mathrm{can}}+5\kappa_2^{\mathrm{can}})}>\frac{64}{9}.
$$
In canonical coordinates the constraint and objective of Corollary T.34.2 read $\frac35\kappa_1^{\mathrm{can}}+3\kappa_2^{\mathrm{can}}+8\kappa_3^{\mathrm{can}}=12$ and $S=\frac35\kappa_1^{\mathrm{can}}\ln(\frac35\kappa_1^{\mathrm{can}})+3\kappa_2^{\mathrm{can}}\ln\kappa_2^{\mathrm{can}}+8\kappa_3^{\mathrm{can}}\ln\kappa_3^{\mathrm{can}}$; keeping their numbers while rescaling only the generator defines a different optimization problem. Corollary T.34.2 is stated in the Standard Model coordinates, and Remark T.17a.4 evaluates its weights in the canonical coordinates through (T.34.1h.1).

*Proof.* Substitute $\hat Y^2=\frac35Y_{\mathrm{SM}}^2$ into the matter factors of Theorem T.34. Cross-multiplying $9z_d=64z_\ell$ gives (T.34.1h.2). The two planes differ by $\frac{42}5\kappa_1^{\mathrm{can}}>0$. Substituting $\kappa_3^{\mathrm{can}}=(21\kappa_1^{\mathrm{can}}+55\kappa_2^{\mathrm{can}})/48$ gives $z_d/z_\ell=(106\kappa_1^{\mathrm{can}}+320\kappa_2^{\mathrm{can}})/(9(\kappa_1^{\mathrm{can}}+5\kappa_2^{\mathrm{can}}))$, the displayed excess. ∎

<a id="theorem-t341i-selector-tests-for-the-variance-certificate"></a>**Theorem T.34.1i (Selector Tests for the Variance Certificate).** Work in the Standard Model coordinates of Theorem T.34, in which
$$
\frac{z_\ell}{g_U^2}=\frac34\kappa_2+\frac14\kappa_1,\qquad
\frac{z_d}{g_U^2}=\frac34\kappa_2+\frac1{36}\kappa_1+4\kappa_3,\qquad
9z_d-64z_\ell=-\frac34\,g_U^2\,\mathcal V_{\ell d},
\tag{T.34.1i.1}
$$
with $\mathcal V_{\ell d}$ of Definition T.34.1a. The weights are the coefficients of the operator $\mathcal C_\kappa$ of Definition T.17a, which fixes no relation among them. A *selector* is a rule that returns one positive triple up to a common factor.

1. *Necessary condition.* On $\mathbb R_{>0}^3$, $\mathcal V_{\ell d}=0$ holds exactly when
$$
\frac{\kappa_3}{\kappa_2}=\frac{55}{48}+\frac7{16}\,\frac{\kappa_1}{\kappa_2}.
$$
Hence every variance certificate has $\kappa_3>\frac{55}{48}\kappa_2$ and $\kappa_3>\frac7{16}\kappa_1$. In the canonical coordinates of Remark T.34.1h the locus is $\kappa_3^{\mathrm{can}}/\kappa_2^{\mathrm{can}}=\frac{55}{48}+\frac{21}{80}\kappa_1^{\mathrm{can}}/\kappa_2^{\mathrm{can}}$, with the same bound.
2. *Factor-blind selectors.* If $\kappa_2=\kappa_3$ then, with $t=\kappa_1/\kappa_2$,
$$
\frac{z_d}{z_\ell}=\frac{t+171}{9(t+3)},\qquad
\frac{d}{dt}\frac{z_d}{z_\ell}=-\frac{56}{3(t+3)^2}<0,
$$
so $\frac19<z_d/z_\ell<\frac{19}3<\frac{64}9$ and $c_\ell/c_d<\sqrt{19/3}\approx2.517<\frac83$ for every $\kappa_1>0$. The bound holds in either hypercharge coordinate, which rescales $\kappa_1$ only. It covers the entropy optimum $\kappa=(1,1,1)$ of Theorem T.34.1g, where $c_\ell/c_d=\sqrt{43}/3\approx2.186$ and $\mathcal V_{\ell d}=28$; the canonical-uniform triple $\kappa^{\mathrm{can}}=(1,1,1)$, that is $\kappa=(\frac35,1,1)$, where $c_\ell/c_d=\sqrt{143/27}\approx2.301$ and $\mathcal V_{\ell d}=\frac{98}5$; and every rule that assigns equal weight to the two simple factors.
3. *Trace selectors.* (a) On the interface bundle of Remark T.17a.3 the index matrix $T_0$ has row sums $(1,1,1)$: the canonical hypercharge, $SU(2)$ and $SU(3)$ have equal total indices. (b) On one Standard Model generation with the hypercharges of Corollary G.8.4c.0h, $\operatorname{Tr}Y_{\mathrm{SM}}^2=\frac{10}3$, $\operatorname{Tr}T_a^2=2$ and $\operatorname{Tr}t_A^2=2$, so the canonical indices are $(2,2,2)$; the neutral singlet and further generations change nothing. Hence every selector $\kappa_i=F(T_i)$, with one function $F$ applied to the total index of each factor in either coordinate, has $\kappa_2=\kappa_3$ and fails by item 2; this includes weights proportional or inversely proportional to the trace. (c) The equal-variance ray $\kappa^{\mathrm{can}}\propto(1,1,1)$, equivalently $\kappa\propto(\frac35,1,1)$, which is also the minimizer of the objective of Corollary T.34.2 with its numbers written in canonical coordinates, gives for the six pairs of Theorem T.34.1f
$$
\frac{z_Q}{z_L}=\frac{143}{27},\quad \frac{z_{u^c}}{z_L}=\frac{128}{27},\quad \frac{z_{d^c}}{z_L}=\frac{122}{27},\quad
\frac{z_Q}{z_{e^c}}=\frac{143}{18},\quad \frac{z_{u^c}}{z_{e^c}}=\frac{64}{9},\quad \frac{z_{d^c}}{z_{e^c}}=\frac{61}{9};
$$
the ratio $8/3$ occurs only for the pair $(e^c,u^c)$.
4. *Single-point selectors.* None of the following triples lies on the locus:

| selector (Standard Model coordinates) | $(\kappa_1,\kappa_2,\kappa_3)$ | $\mathcal V_{\ell d}$ | $c_\ell/c_d$ |
|---|---|---|---|
| uniform (entropy optimum) | $(1,1,1)$ | $28$ | $2.186$ |
| uniform in canonical coordinates | $(\frac35,1,1)$ | $\frac{98}5$ | $2.301$ |
| gauge dimensions | $(1,3,8)$ | $-198$ | $3.703$ |
| inverse gauge dimensions | $(1,\frac13,\frac18)$ | $\frac{100}3$ | $1.247$ |
| fundamental Casimirs, $\kappa_1=1$ | $(1,\frac34,\frac43)$ | $-\frac74$ | $2.700$ |
| dual Coxeter numbers, $\kappa_1=1$ | $(1,2,3)$ | $-13$ | $2.780$ |

The locus contains simple rational points, for example $(\frac{13}{12},\frac34,\frac43)$ and $(\frac{34}{21},2,3)$, obtained by solving $\mathcal V_{\ell d}=0$ for $\kappa_1$; simplicity of a triple, or a near miss such as $2.700$, does not select it.

*Proof.* The identity in (T.34.1i.1) is direct expansion. Item 1 solves $\mathcal V_{\ell d}=0$ for $\kappa_3$; substituting $\kappa_1=\frac35\kappa_1^{\mathrm{can}}$ gives the canonical form. Item 2 substitutes $\kappa_3=\kappa_2$; the derivative is negative, the limits at $t\to0$ and $t\to\infty$ are $\frac{19}3$ and $\frac19$, and $\frac{19}3=\frac{57}9<\frac{64}9$. Item 3(a) sums the rows of $T_0$, whose rows are the three gauge factors and whose columns are the sectors $C,W,Y$. For 3(b), with $Q(\mathbf3,\mathbf2)_{1/6}$, $u^c(\bar{\mathbf3},\mathbf1)_{-2/3}$, $d^c(\bar{\mathbf3},\mathbf1)_{1/3}$, $L(\mathbf1,\mathbf2)_{-1/2}$ and $e^c(\mathbf1,\mathbf1)_1$: $\operatorname{Tr}Y_{\mathrm{SM}}^2=\frac16+\frac43+\frac13+\frac12+1=\frac{10}3$, $\operatorname{Tr}T_a^2=\frac12(3+1)=2$, $\operatorname{Tr}t_A^2=\frac12(2+1+1)=2$, and $\frac35\cdot\frac{10}3=2$. For 3(c), the vectors $C_f$ of Theorem T.34.1f give $C_L\cdot\kappa=\frac9{10}$, $C_{e^c}\cdot\kappa=\frac35$, $C_Q\cdot\kappa=\frac{143}{30}$, $C_{u^c}\cdot\kappa=\frac{64}{15}$ and $C_{d^c}\cdot\kappa=\frac{61}{15}$ at $\kappa=(\frac35,1,1)$, and Jensen's inequality, as in the proof of Theorem T.34.1g, gives the minimizer $\kappa^{\mathrm{can}}=(1,1,1)$ of $\kappa_1^{\mathrm{can}}\ln\kappa_1^{\mathrm{can}}+3\kappa_2\ln\kappa_2+8\kappa_3\ln\kappa_3$ on $\kappa_1^{\mathrm{can}}+3\kappa_2+8\kappa_3=12$. Item 4 is evaluation. ∎

<a id="corollary-t341j-fundamental-casimir-density-and-the-hypercharge-weight"></a>**Corollary T.34.1j (Fundamental Casimir Density and the Hypercharge Weight).** In the coordinates of Theorem T.34.1i, assign the two simple-factor weights by $C_2(\mathrm{fund})/\dim(\mathrm{fund})$ with common proportionality constant $k>0$ and the generator conventions of that theorem. Then $\kappa_2=3k/8$ and $\kappa_3=4k/9$. The color-to-weak ratio is $32/27>55/48$. The tilt equation requires the separate abelian weight $\kappa_1=17k/504$.

*Proof.* The fundamental Casimirs are $3/4$ and $4/3$ in dimensions $2$ and $3$. Substitution into (T.34.1i.1) gives $\mathcal V_{\ell d}=21\kappa_1-17k/24$. Thus satisfying the strict color-to-weak inequality still leaves one abelian normalization to be determined. The simple-factor prescription contains no selection rule for that normalization. ∎

<a id="theorem-t341k"></a>

<a id="theorem-t341k-the-complete-positive-variance-fiber-of-the-literal-flag-operator"></a>**Theorem T.34.1k (The Complete Positive Variance Fiber of the Literal Flag Operator).** Use the actual literal-spectrum interface branch of Definition T.17a and Remark T.17a.3, with gauge-trivial active plane and retained neutral inactive line. Hold fixed its connection, Golay involution, real mass and parity terms, boundary conditions, source-unit conventions and common finite regulator. All observations built solely from the resulting interface operator and its fixed represented gauge insertions leave a one-dimensional coefficient ambiguity, even at fixed total canonical weight. The ambiguity changes the lepton–quark variance. The positive fiber and its possible variance-zero point are classified below.

*Exact operator kernel.* Write \((x,y,z)=(\kappa_1^{\rm can},\kappa_2,\kappa_3)\) in the canonical coordinate \(\hat Y=\sqrt{3/5}\,Y_{\rm SM}\). The represented Casimir insertion on the three orthogonal charged and neutral sectors is
$$
\mathcal C_\kappa=C P_C+W P_W,\qquad
C=x/15+4z/3,\qquad W=3x/20+3y/4.
\tag{T.34.1k.1}
$$
Here \(P_C,P_W\) are the retained physical sector projections, and \(C,W>0\) are the two actual shifts. The coefficient map has rank two, with kernel
$$
v=(1,-1/5,-1/20).
\tag{T.34.1k.2}
$$
Substitute \(\kappa+tv\) in the entire displayed \(D^{\rm PCE}_{\widetilde X}\) of Definition T.17a. Both \(\mathcal C_\kappa\) and \(\eta\mathcal J_G\mathcal C_\kappa\) are unchanged exactly, as are the derivative, constant and Golay terms. Thus the whole operator, its domain, every sector and parity block used in the specified source, and every fixed-representation heat/current insertion are the same. This holds before any $\zeta$ evaluation, local subtraction or choice of spectral tail estimate. The source Hamiltonian in any common finite section is the same matrix. Actual driven histories coincide whenever their preparation, registered control couplings and readouts consume only that matrix and the fixed represented operators. A device which also reads an independently supplied weight setting is an enlarged response source.

In canonical coordinates the normalized total weight \(x+3y+8z\) is also fixed along (T.34.1k.2). In fact
$$
x+3y+8z=4W+6C.
\tag{T.34.1k.3}
$$
Thus fixing that weight in addition to all spectral data does not remove the kernel. The canonical variance functional on this same fiber is
$$
\mathcal V_{\ell d}
=\frac{63}{5}x+55y-48z
=\frac{220}{3}W-36C+4x .
\tag{T.34.1k.4}
$$
In particular the variance is not a function of the full interface operator on any open positive fiber. It cannot be obtained by evaluating more heat coefficients or more fixed gauge-current insertions on that unchanged operator.

*All positive weights and the unique possible zero.* For given \(C,W>0\), solve the two equations in (T.34.1k.1) explicitly:
$$
y=\frac43W-\frac{x}{5},\qquad
z=\frac34C-\frac{x}{20},\qquad
0<x<\min\{20W/3,15C\}.
\tag{T.34.1k.5}
$$
The variance runs strictly increasingly over the open interval obtained by substituting those two \(x\)-endpoints in (T.34.1k.4). Its sole possible zero is \(x_*=9C-\frac{55}{3}W\). Positivity of \(x_*\) requires \(C/W>55/27\). This inequality implies \(15C>20W/3\), so the upper condition reduces to \(9C<25W\). Consequently
$$
\exists\,\kappa>0:\ \mathcal C_\kappa=C P_C+W P_W,\
\mathcal V_{\ell d}=0
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\frac{55}{27}<\frac{C}{W}<\frac{25}{9}.
\tag{T.34.1k.6}
$$
At either excluded endpoint the formal solution hits a zero coefficient and is outside the positive source class. In the open interval there is exactly one such positive point, but every sufficiently small nonzero displacement along \(v\) is a positive point with the same full interface data and nonzero variance. For instance \(C=5/2,W=1\) gives
$$
\kappa_*=(25/6,\ 1/2,\ 5/3),\qquad
\kappa'=(31/6,\ 3/10,\ 97/60).
\tag{T.34.1k.7}
$$
Both triples are canonical and positive, have the same total weight \(19\) and the same operator, and their variances are respectively zero and \(4\). Multiplying both by \(12/19\) makes the canonical total weight \(12\) while preserving the zero and nonzero alternatives. These are explicit nonidentification witnesses on the interface source.

*Minimal additional measured response.* Any additional linear coefficient probe \(L(\kappa)=\ell_1x+\ell_2y+\ell_3z\) resolves the ambiguity exactly when \(L(v)\ne0\). Indeed (T.34.1k.5) gives
$$
x=\frac{L(\kappa)-(4\ell_2/3)W-(3\ell_3/4)C}
        {\ell_1-\ell_2/5-\ell_3/20}.
\tag{T.34.1k.8}
$$
For a measured interval of radius \(\epsilon_L\) at fixed exact \(C,W\), the corresponding radius in \(\mathcal V_{\ell d}\) is \(4\epsilon_L/|L(v)|\). If \(C,W\) are uncertain, their exact additional error follows by substituting their intervals into the affine reconstruction in (T.34.1k.8) and (T.34.1k.4). As an independently typed candidate, an actually retained charged-lepton singlet with \(Y_{\rm SM}=1\) and the same coefficient insertion would supply \(L(\kappa)=3x/5\). Its weak and color generators vanish, and \(L(v)=3/5\). This example identifies an operator port and its required source transfer. It does not insert such a port into the literal interface or set its independently measured value to \(3x_*/5\).

*Effect on the proposed matter normalization.* Transport \(x\) to Standard Model units by \(\kappa_1^{\rm SM}=3x/5\). On the matter transfer branch of Lemma T.34.3 with common right and Higgs kinetic data and common unnormalized cubic, the two proposed left kinetic factors obey (T.34.1i.1). Along (T.34.1k.2) their difference \(9z_d-64z_\ell\) has nonzero derivative \(-3g_U^2\) with respect to \(t\) at fixed \(g_U\). Hence the canonical three-leg map cannot turn the unchanged interface data into a unique selected tilt. This argument does not alter the actual unit fermion coefficient of the separately accepted native field source of Theorem T.78.15d. Supplying independently measured matter responses, or a PU-internal source identity that forces the special value in (T.34.1k.8), remains necessary for the positive variance certificate. \(\square\)

<a id="theorem-t341l"></a>

<a id="theorem-t341l-determinant-port-for-the-missing-flag-coefficient"></a>**Theorem T.34.1l (Determinant Port for the Missing Flag Coefficient).** Use the literal flag representation of Remark T.17a.3 and the coefficient fiber of Theorem T.34.1k. Take two weak fundamental copies with the same physical gauge link transport, and use their determinant line. A gauge-invariant closed-loop interferometer on this line gives a pure hypercharge variance probe, with exact sensitivity to the kernel direction (T.34.1k.2). It determines all three positive weights when the common transported fluctuation is independently identified with the coefficient covariance. Independent tensor copies of the literal flag operator and its fixed controls, including an exterior-power preparation on them, cannot determine that covariance coordinate.

*Physical determinant action.* Restrict the weak interface to one of its actual weak fundamental copies; equivalently the two interface copies furnished by the fixed active multiplicity can be used. The canonical hypercharge on either is $y_W I_2$, where $y_W=3/(2\sqrt{15})=\sqrt{3/5}/2$. The common weak transport is $U=e^{i y_W\theta}S$ with $S\in SU(2)$, and color is trivial there. On the one-dimensional antisymmetric line of $W\otimes W$,
$$
(\wedge^2 U)|_{\wedge^2 W}=\det U=e^{i\sqrt{3/5}\,\theta}.
\tag{T.34.1l.1}
$$
The antisymmetric line and its orthogonal complement are invariant for each common pulse. The identity applies to an ordered product of links because the determinant is multiplicative. For a closed loop the endpoint gauge transformations conjugate its holonomy, so (T.34.1l.1) is gauge invariant. Its two matter factors remain on the same total charge line in both arms of the comparison. Use a neutral control qubit prepared in $\lvert+\rangle$, one arm implementing the identity and the other the closed common transport. The control operation preserves total charge. A common eigenstate of the determinant line picks up only the phase in (T.34.1l.1); the $X$-expectation on the control is its real part. Thus the port does not require a superposition of matter charge sectors or an elementary charged-lepton singlet.

*Response and finite errors.* In the normalization of Theorem T.34.1k, let the independently prepared common link have net canonical abelian angle $\theta=\varepsilon\xi$, with $x=\mathbb E[\xi^2]$. The common traceless weak transport may be correlated with $\xi$, since its determinant is one on every word. Fix the scale $\varepsilon>0$ in the actual clock and charge coordinate before evaluating the response. The mean control observable $X_{\rm det}$ gives
$$
\left|\frac{2(1-\mathbb E X_{\rm det})}{\varepsilon^2}
-\frac35x\right|
\le \frac{(3/5)^2}{12}\varepsilon^2\mathbb E[\xi^4]
\tag{T.34.1l.2}
$$
when the fourth moment is finite. This is the fourth-order Taylor bound for the cosine. It uses the physical charge eigenvalue of (T.34.1l.1), without an arbitrary probe gain. In a two-word source with $\xi=\pm\sqrt x$, the response is exactly $\cos(\varepsilon\sqrt{3x/5})$. On an independently bounded range $0\le x\le x_{\max}$ and $0<\varepsilon\sqrt{3x_{\max}/5}\le\pi/2$, it has the exact inverse
$$
x=\frac{5}{3\varepsilon^2}\arccos^2(\mathbb E X_{\rm det}).
\tag{T.34.1l.3}
$$
The absolute derivative of this inverse is bounded by $5\pi/(3\varepsilon^2)$ on the stated expectation interval because $u/\sin u\le\pi/2$ for $0\le u\le\pi/2$. Projecting any approximate expectation onto the allowed interval preserves its absolute error bound. If $N$ independent shots of the same prepared source are used, the mean of their $\pm1$ control results has absolute error at most $\sqrt{2\log(2/\delta)/N}$ with probability at least $1-\delta$, by the bounded independent-variable exponential moment inequality. Any separately certified expectation error from the physical implementation is added before applying the inverse bound. For the general finite-fourth-moment source, (T.34.1l.2) instead supplies an additive model remainder to the scaled expectation estimate.

If the transported variance is independently identified with the kinetic coefficient $x=\kappa_1^{\rm can}$ in the same clock, gauge-generator and source units, the resulting additional linear coefficient is $L(\kappa)=3x/5$. Then $L(v)=3/5$ for the kernel vector in (T.34.1k.2), and this port and the existing $C,W$ responses reconstruct the whole triple by (T.34.1k.5). With absolute errors $\delta_x,\delta_C,\delta_W$, the corresponding variance error is at most $4\delta_x+36\delta_C+(220/3)\delta_W$. The reconstruction uses the canonical hypercharge coordinate, and Lemma T.34.3 still requires its actual matter, cubic and unit transfer. In particular the reconstructed variance vanishes exactly when $x=9C-55W/3$.

*Distinction from independent tensoring.* On independent weak interface copies the sum of their literal quadratic insertions is $2W I$, also on the determinant line. Every tensor power of the unchanged literal operators and every control that consumes only those operators and their fixed represented insertions remains identical along the fiber (T.34.1k.2). By contrast, the common fluctuation acts through $T\otimes I+I\otimes T$ for each represented generator $T$. Its squared insertion includes $2T\otimes T$. The summed weak generators vanish on the determinant line while the hypercharge adds, giving exactly the covariance coefficient $3x/5$ of that transport. A common link probe whose fluctuation law is held fixed as the kinetic weights vary gives a fixed response. Identifying the transported covariance with the actual kinetic coefficient and deriving its special value for the variance certificate require independent PU input. $\square$

<a id="theorem-t341m"></a>

<a id="theorem-t341m-electric-link-calibration-of-the-flag-coefficients"></a>**Theorem T.34.1m (Electric-Link Calibration of the Flag Coefficients).** Take the actual flag gauge group $G=S(U(3)\times U(2))$ of Theorem G.8.4h.5, its defining color and weak representations $C,W$, and the determinant line $D=\Lambda^2W$ of Theorem T.34.1l. On the declared compact electric-link source below, the charged flag response and the gauge-invariant determinant rotor read the same three coefficients, in one physical clock and charge coordinate. On a finite spatial cycle their three vacuum insertion spectra determine the entire positive triple. Holding the two flag shifts fixed leaves the complete open coefficient interval (T.34.1k.5) as genuine positive dynamical sources. In particular the shared canonical electric action, Gauss law, determinant charge and kinetic calibration do not force the zero-variance point.

*Group and action.* In the covering group $SU(3)\times SU(2)\times U(1)$, use the map $(A,B,u)\mapsto(u^{-2}A,u^3B)$ of Proposition G.8.4h.4. The color, weak and determinant actions are $u^{-2}A$, $u^3B$, and $u^6$, respectively. Each is trivial on the stated central kernel, and the determinant exponent six is primitive for a character trivial on both simple factors: the central kernel requires an abelian exponent divisible by six. Thus the line $D$ has primitive Standard Model hypercharge $1$, and canonical charge $q_D=\sqrt{3/5}$, with $\hat Y=\sqrt{3/5}\,Y_{\rm SM}$. In the same normalization $C,W$ have charges $-1/\sqrt{15}$ and $3/(2\sqrt{15})$. Normalize the simple generators by $\operatorname{Tr}(t_at_b)=\delta_{ab}/2$ in their defining modules.

Fix a common physical energy unit $E_0>0$, set $\tau_0=\hbar/E_0$, and take a marked connected finite graph with oriented edges. On each edge put $L^2(G)$ with normalized Haar measure. Let $\widehat Q_e$ be the self-adjoint generator of canonical hypercharge translation and $\mathcal C_{2,e},\mathcal C_{3,e}$ the positive quadratic Casimirs in these normalizations. Use the gauge-invariant positive electric Hamiltonian
$$
H_E=\frac{E_0}{2}\sum_e\bigl(x\widehat Q_e^{\,2}+y\mathcal C_{2,e}+z\mathcal C_{3,e}\bigr),
\qquad x,y,z>0 .
\tag{T.34.1m.1}
$$
The coefficients, graph, fixed energy unit and absence of extra link dynamics in the cycle experiment are inputs of this enlarged source. At a vertex the actual gauge group acts by left or right multiplication on its adjacent links; the physical subspace is invariant under all these transformations. The operators in (T.34.1m.1) commute with the gauge action. Their finite coefficient-matrix functions of compact-group representations form a common dense invariant domain. Peter–Weyl decomposition diagonalizes the electric terms in irreducible representations, giving their nonnegative self-adjoint closure and the complete gauge-invariant electric spectrum by restriction. For a coefficient function in an actual fundamental $C$ or $W$ on one link, the dimensionless operator $2H_{E,e}/E_0$ gives, respectively,
$$
C=x/15+4z/3,\qquad W=3x/20+3y/4 .
\tag{T.34.1m.2}
$$
The gauge-covariant matrix-coefficient embedding is a linear isometry after its Haar normalization, and acts on the same represented generators as the flag matter factors. Thus its electric response has precisely the two Casimir shifts of (T.34.1k.1), with the source gain fixed by the action. This identifies the coefficient comparison on the enlarged electric source. It does not assert equality of its whole Hamiltonian to the original clamped flag operator.

*Closed-cycle spectra and readouts.* Use a single spatial cycle of $\ell\ge3$ edges and no extra potential. Integrate over the vertex group to impose the Gauss constraints. Fixing a spanning path, every invariant function of the link coordinates is a class function of the remaining cycle holonomy $U$: vertex transformations remove the path links, and the residual transformation conjugates $U$. The product Haar measure pushes forward to normalized Haar on the cycle holonomy by successive Haar integrations. Hence this identification is unitary onto $L^2(G)^G$. The irreducible characters $\chi_R(U)$ are an orthonormal basis, and their link representation labels are $R$ on every forward edge, with dual labels on any reversed edges. Thus they are eigenvectors with energies
$$
E_R=\frac{\ell E_0}{2}\bigl(xq_R^2+y c_2(R)+z c_3(R)\bigr).
\tag{T.34.1m.3}
$$
The constant function is the unique ground state because the three positive Casimirs jointly vanish only on the trivial representation. Multiplication by the Wilson character $\chi_R$ sends this ground state to $\chi_R$ with norm one. In particular the determinant insertion is the gauge-invariant unitary multiplication by the line character $D(U)$.

For each $R\in\{C,W,D\}$ the normalized two-time vacuum response of that insertion and its adjoint is exactly
$$
\langle 1,\ \chi_R^\dagger(t)\chi_R(0)\,1\rangle
=e^{-i E_R t/\hbar}.
\tag{T.34.1m.4}
$$
It determines the three dimensionless quantities $2E_C/(\ell E_0)=C$, $2E_W/(\ell E_0)=W$, and $2E_D/(\ell E_0)=(3/5)x$, with no classical angle-noise amplitude. For the determinant line one may implement a neutral controlled loop operation, as in Theorem T.34.1l, and read its complex interference. For the general character, use the conjugate contraction of the marked representation tensor along the loop to supply the Wilson insertion, or use its normalized vacuum-to-character preparation in the retained subspace. The response (T.34.1m.4) uses only the vacuum and its one indicated character. Projection onto their span keeps its exact matrix element and the subsequent time evolution. A finite control experiment on these registered subspaces has no spectral truncation error in these specified vacuum responses. It does not compare arbitrary ordered products of Wilson insertions on the full rotor Hilbert space.

For example bound the energy independently by $E_R\le E_{\max}$ in the finite comparison menu and take $0<t<\pi\hbar/(2E_{\max})$. If the measured complex response has absolute error at most $\epsilon<1$, its phase changes by at most $\arcsin\epsilon$ by the tangent bound for the disk of radius $\epsilon$ about a unit complex number. Use the continuous determination of phase on the chosen arc, or unwrap in that independently chosen interval. The resulting energy radius is $(\hbar/t)\arcsin\epsilon$. Applying the three known gains in (T.34.1m.3) and the affine inverse (T.34.1k.5) gives finite radii in the kinetic weights and then the variance radius of Theorem T.34.1l.

*Determinant first-moment calibration with an interaction.* Keep (T.34.1m.1) on a finite graph and add a bounded real gauge-invariant multiplication potential $V$. Let $D_\Gamma$ multiply by the determinant character of the holonomy around a simple oriented loop of $\ell$ edges. This is a gauge-invariant unitary, and it commutes with $V$. The canonical abelian derivative on each loop edge obeys $D_\Gamma^\dagger\widehat Q_e D_\Gamma=\widehat Q_e+\epsilon_e q_D$, with $\epsilon_e=\pm1$ the edge orientation. The simple Casimirs commute with $D_\Gamma$. Thus, on the common electric form domain, for $H=H_E+V$,
$$
D_\Gamma^\dagger H D_\Gamma+D_\Gamma H D_\Gamma^\dagger-2H
=\ell E_0 xq_D^2 I .
\tag{T.34.1m.5}
$$
Multiplication by these smooth characters preserves the electric domain. For any normalized physical ground state $\Omega$ of $H$, let $\mu_\pm$ be the unit positive spectral measures of $H-E_{\rm gs}$ on $D_\Gamma^{\pm1}\Omega$. Equation (T.34.1m.5) says their summed first energy moments are exactly $\ell E_0(3/5)x$. This still fixes the same $x$ when an interaction spreads the two spectra. For a finite energy cutoff $T>0$, each omitted first moment is at most $M_{2,\pm}/T$ when $M_{2,\pm}=\|(H-E_{\rm gs})D_\Gamma^{\pm1}\Omega\|^2$. The commutator formula gives the bound
$$
M_{2,\pm}^{1/2}\le E_0 x q_D
\sqrt{\frac{2\ell\langle H_E\rangle_\Omega}{E_0x}}
+\frac{\ell E_0 xq_D^2}{2}.
$$
Indeed its linear term is $E_0xq_D\sum_{e\in\Gamma}\epsilon_e\widehat Q_e$, and the squared norm of that sum is bounded by $\ell\sum_{e\in\Gamma}\langle\widehat Q_e^2\rangle$. This tail bound is for the determinant first moment; the exact $C,W$ line frequencies in (T.34.1m.4) use the pure cycle experiment.

*Surviving dynamical alternatives.* For any fixed $C,W>0$ and any $x$ in (T.34.1k.5), use $y=4W/3-x/5$ and $z=3C/4-x/20$ in the same electric action with the same $E_0$, graph, group, vacuum and gauge charges. Every member is a positive self-adjoint gauge-invariant source. It has the same two covariant flag shifts and the same $C,W$ vacuum response spectra, and its determinant frequency varies strictly with $x$. Thus the two alternatives in (T.34.1k.7) are physically distinct enlarged sources with identical original two shifts and distinct variances. The dynamical determinant port measures which coefficient is present. An independent rule selecting $x=9C-55W/3$ and a physical transfer to the native matter kinetic and cubic data of Lemma T.34.3 retain their tests. See Kogut and Susskind (1975). $\square$

<a id="theorem-t341n"></a>

<a id="theorem-t341n-interacting-wilson-first-moment-calibration"></a>**Theorem T.34.1n (Interacting Wilson First-Moment Calibration).** On the electric-link source (T.34.1m.1), take any simple loop of length $\ell$ on a finite graph. Add any bounded self-adjoint gauge-equivariant multiplication potential $V$. A finite-dimensional unitary matter carrier at the vertices is permitted, with the electric terms acting trivially on its indices and the physical space defined by the joint Gauss constraint. Assume this space is nonzero. For every normalized physical ground state, the equal-time Wilson norms and the first energy moments of the real and imaginary Wilson quadratures in the three actual representations $C,W,D$ determine $(x,y,z)$ in the same physical units as Theorem T.34.1m. The inversion has strictly positive denominators and finite spectral-tail bounds.

*Energy identity.* Let $U_\Gamma$ be the loop holonomy and $\chi_R=\operatorname{Tr}R(U_\Gamma)$ for $R=C,W,D$. Write $f_R=\operatorname{Re}\chi_R$, $g_R=\operatorname{Im}\chi_R$ and $M_R=\langle\Omega,|\chi_R|^2\Omega\rangle$ for the equal-time norm. Denote the positive spectral measure of $H-E_{\rm gs}$ on $u\Omega$ by $\mu_u$ for either real quadrature $u$. Put
$$
J_R=\frac{2}{\ell E_0}\int_0^\infty \lambda\,d(\mu_{f_R}+\mu_{g_R})(\lambda).
\tag{T.34.1n.1}
$$
These are observables on the joint Gauss space because the loop traces are gauge invariant. Compactness of $G^E$ and positivity of the coefficients give an elliptic electric operator with compact resolvent on $L^2(G^E)$ with finite-dimensional fibers. The Gauss projector commutes with it and with $V$, so the nonzero physical space has a ground state. Boundedness of $V$ preserves the electric operator domain, which is stable under smooth scalar multiplication.

Write $D_\beta$ for the real translation derivations on the edges, and $w_\beta$ for their respective weights $x,y,z$. Then $H_E=-(E_0/2)\sum_\beta w_\beta D_\beta^2$. The product rule on the electric domain and commutation with $V$ give
$$
2\int_0^\infty \lambda\,d\mu_u(\lambda)
=\langle\Omega,[u,[H,u]]\Omega\rangle
= E_0\sum_\beta w_\beta\langle\Omega,|D_\beta u|^2\Omega\rangle .
\tag{T.34.1n.2}
$$
The first equality follows by expanding the commutators and using $H\Omega=E_{\rm gs}\Omega$. The sum over both real quadratures is $|D_\beta\chi_R|^2$ on the right. A loop edge differentiated in the abelian direction contributes $q_R^2|\chi_R|^2$. In a simple-factor direction the insertion in the loop trace is $i t_a$ transported by a unitary, with the orientation sign when the edge is reversed. The transport rotates the normalized generator basis orthogonally. For the defining $n$-dimensional representation the sum over its simple-factor directions is
$$
\sum_a |\operatorname{Tr}(t_a R(U_\Gamma))|^2
=\frac12\left(n-\frac{|\chi_R|^2}{n}\right).
\tag{T.34.1n.3}
$$
Indeed $\{I/\sqrt n,\sqrt2 t_a\}$ is an orthonormal basis of the complex matrix space for the Hilbert–Schmidt inner product, and $\operatorname{Tr}(R(U_\Gamma)^*R(U_\Gamma))=n$. The other simple factor acts trivially. For $D$ both simple factors act trivially and $|\chi_D|=1$. Each of the $\ell$ distinct loop edges contributes the same formula. Therefore
$$
J_D=xq_D^2,\qquad
J_C=xq_C^2M_C+\tfrac z2(3-M_C/3),\qquad
J_W=xq_W^2M_W+\tfrac y2(2-M_W/2).
\tag{T.34.1n.4}
$$

*Inversion and finite error.* The squared trace of a unitary of size $n$ equals $n^2$ only when it is scalar. Product Haar measure on the link coordinates pushes forward to Haar measure on $G$ under the simple loop holonomy. Each defining projection from $G$ onto $U(n)$ is surjective, since the other factor can supply the inverse determinant. The scalar subgroup is Haar null for $n=2,3$. The ground-state probability $\|\Omega\|^2$ times product Haar measure is absolutely continuous. Hence $M_C<9$ and $M_W<4$, and (T.34.1n.4) first determines $x=J_D/q_D^2$, then $z$ and $y$ by subtraction and division. The inverse gives the shifts in (T.34.1m.2) in the declared canonical hypercharge coordinate.

For an energy cutoff $\Lambda>0$, the omitted first moment is at most $\|[H,u]\Omega\|^2/\Lambda$. One explicit bound for its numerator follows from
$$
\|[H,u]\Omega\|
\le \frac{E_0}{2}\left\|\sum_\beta w_\beta D_\beta^2u\right\|_\infty
+E_0\left\|\sum_\beta w_\beta |D_\beta u|^2\right\|_\infty^{1/2}
\left(\frac{2\langle H_E\rangle_\Omega}{E_0}\right)^{1/2}.
\tag{T.34.1n.5}
$$
The bound is the product rule followed by pointwise Cauchy–Schwarz and the electric form identity. The factor $\langle H_E\rangle_\Omega$ is at most $E_{\rm gs}+\|V\|$ and can also be bounded by a trial-state energy plus $\|V\|$. On a declared bounded coefficient region these bounds give computable tail radii. Combining them with measurement intervals in (T.34.1n.4) gives finite coefficient intervals as soon as the upper endpoints for $M_C$ and $M_W$ lie below $9$ and $4$. The exact strict bounds ensure such endpoints at sufficient precision for each fixed source. Independent selection of zero variance and the transfer of the electric coefficients to the native kinetic and cubic matter data of Lemma T.34.3 retain their tests. $\square$

<a id="theorem-t341o"></a>

<a id="theorem-t341o-unified-fundamental-trace-kinetic-forms-and-the-variance-test"></a>**Theorem T.34.1o (Unified Fundamental-Trace Kinetic Forms and the Variance Test).** Let $G=S(U(3)\times U(2))\subset SU(5)$ act on its defining color and weak blocks as in Theorem T.34.1m. Fix a Hermitian adjoint background with two distinct eigenvalues of multiplicities three and two, so its stabilizer is precisely $G$. For quadratic terms in one fundamental trace with arbitrary insertions of functions of that background, the direct electric coefficient convention and the inverse metric convention give respectively the complete positive families
$$
x=\frac{2z+3y}{5},\qquad\text{or}\qquad
\frac1x=\frac15\left(\frac2z+\frac3y\right),
\quad y,z>0 .
\tag{T.34.1o.1}
$$
Here $(x,y,z)=(\kappa_1^{\rm can},\kappa_2,\kappa_3)$ are the actual coefficients of the electric-link Hamiltonian in the canonical coordinate and common clock of Theorem T.34.1m. On either family the two full flag shifts already determine all three coefficients. The two families yield different zero-variance tests. They give distinct physical electric responses at fixed original flag shifts except on their common equal-weight ray. A separate product of two fundamental traces supplies the independent center coefficient and restores the full positive three-parameter family.

*The restricted kinetic forms.* Use Hermitian generators with the fundamental form $2\operatorname{Tr}(XY)$. The normalized hypercharge generator is
$$
Y_0=\sqrt{\frac35}\,
\operatorname{diag}\!\left(-\frac13 I_3,\frac12 I_2\right).
$$
It has norm one for this form. A background $\Phi$ as above is scalar on each block, with spectral projectors $P_C,P_W$. Each single-trace quadratic word with two Lie algebra arguments $X,Y\in\mathfrak g$ and arbitrary insertions of functions of $\Phi$ has block coefficients $a_C,a_W$: all the insertions commute with $X,Y$, so the word restricts to a linear combination of the two block traces. This holds for the full real symmetric linear span, with the positive restriction exactly when $a_C,a_W>0$. Conversely any such pair occurs from $2\operatorname{Tr}[(a_C P_C+a_W P_W)XY]$. The relative $Y_0$ squared norms of the two blocks are $2/5$ and $3/5$, while the weak and color simple generators live in their respective blocks. There are no cross terms by tracelessness of the simple generators. The same argument applies to analytic functions on a neighborhood of the two fixed eigenvalues. The linear insertion is the usual adjoint-dependent trace kinetic term in $SU(5)$ (Hall and Sarid 1993).

In the direct convention the form gives the electric quadratic symbol itself, with $z=a_C$, $y=a_W$. In the inverse convention it gives the configuration-space kinetic metric, with $z=a_C^{-1}$, $y=a_W^{-1}$. The inverse in this statement is taken after restriction to the retained group $G$, so its inverse on the center is the inverse of the weighted sum. The two calculations give (T.34.1o.1). Both define actual sources on $L^2(G^E)$ with the joint Gauss constraint and the physical energy factor $E_0/2$ in Theorem T.34.1m. The direct form gives the positive central quadratic electric generator by the invariant generators on the retained group. For the inverse metric, the Legendre transform gives that same type of generator with the inverse coefficients. The Haar normalization of the retained group is the common normalized measure for both sources. These are sources with a fixed background and retained link group. They consume no dynamics of the broken $SU(5)$ directions.

*Complete determination at fixed flag shifts.* Keep the measured shifts $C,W$ of (T.34.1k.1) and their original represented current. On their positive coefficient interval the other weights are
$$
y(x)=\frac43W-\frac x5,\qquad
z(x)=\frac34C-\frac x{20},\qquad
0<x<\min\{20W/3,15C\}.
\tag{T.34.1o.2}
$$
Substitution into the direct family gives its only possible value
$$
x_{\rm direct}=\frac{15C+40W}{57}.
\tag{T.34.1o.3}
$$
This is in the interval (T.34.1o.2) exactly when $1/21<C/W<68/3$. In the inverse metric family, $x^{-1}$ decreases strictly on that interval, while $(2z(x)^{-1}+3y(x)^{-1})/5$ increases strictly. Their difference tends to $+\infty$ at zero and to $-\infty$ at the upper endpoint, so there is exactly one admissible value $x_{\rm inverse}$ for all $C,W>0$. Equivalently it is the unique root in the positive interval of $5y(x)z(x)=x(2y(x)+3z(x))$. Both reductions use a source restriction fixed before applying any variance condition.

When both sources exist at fixed shifts, their coefficients coincide exactly when $C/W=14/9$. Indeed arithmetic and harmonic means coincide precisely when $y=z$, which then gives $x=y=z$ and $C/W=14/9$ by (T.34.1k.1). Conversely that equal-weight triple is a solution of both restrictions at that shift ratio, and both solutions are unique. Away from this ratio, the arithmetic mean of the positive simple-factor coefficients at $x_{\rm inverse}$ is strictly larger than $x_{\rm inverse}$. The direct equation has strictly increasing left-minus-right difference along (T.34.1o.2), hence $x_{\rm direct}>x_{\rm inverse}$. The determinant first moment $J_D=q_D^2 x$ of Theorem T.34.1n distinguishes the two actual sources, even with the allowed interactions of that theorem. Since the first moments have finite cutoff errors there, any fixed strict difference can be certified at finite precision by disjoint intervals.

*Exact variance classification and the center extension.* Write $r=z/y$. In the direct family,
$$
\frac{\mathcal V_{\ell d}}{y}=\frac{2(782-537r)}{25}.
$$
In the inverse metric family,
$$
\frac{\mathcal V_{\ell d}}{y}
=\frac{-2(72r^2-66r-55)}{2+3r}.
\tag{T.34.1o.4}
$$
The unique positive zero ratios are $782/537$ and $(11+\sqrt{561})/24$, respectively. Each exceeds $55/48$. In terms of the two original measured flag shifts, the respective zero conditions are
$$
\frac{C}{W}=\frac{1085}{498},\qquad
\frac{C}{W}=\frac{275-5\sqrt{561}}{72}.
\tag{T.34.1o.5}
$$
These follow by substituting the corresponding $r$ and $x/y$ into (T.34.1k.1). The positive simple-factor ratios range over $(0,\infty)$ in both sources, and the variance takes both signs. The fixed equal-form source $a_C=a_W$ gives the common nonzero variance $98y/5$. The background pattern and the fundamental trace therefore determine the missing direction relative to the two shifts on either declared family. Variance zero additionally requires the physical shift ratio in (T.34.1o.5).

The fixed positive shifts $C=2$ and $W=1$ provide an explicit common-input comparison chosen independently of (T.34.1o.5). Both families are positive at these shifts. The inverse metric equation becomes $3x^2-45x+50=0$ after substituting (T.34.1o.2) and clearing the positive denominators. The two sources therefore have
$$
x_{\rm direct}=\frac{70}{57},
\qquad
x_{\rm inverse}=\frac{45-5\sqrt{57}}6 .
$$
Their full original flag operators and canonical total weight coincide by Theorem T.34.1k. Their additional determinant responses differ by the strict arithmetic versus harmonic inequality already proved.

For the product of traces use the background $\Phi$ with its distinct block values. The functional $\operatorname{Tr}(\Phi X)$ vanishes on both simple summands and is nonzero on $Y_0$. Therefore a real coefficient multiplying $\operatorname{Tr}(\Phi X)\operatorname{Tr}(\Phi Y)$ changes only the center form. With the complete restricted form required positive, it gives every positive center coefficient at fixed positive simple coefficients. This holds in the direct and inverse conventions and realizes every positive electric triple on the retained compact-link Gauss source. The condition of positivity here is on the physical retained link group. The current readout and finite coefficient tests of Theorem T.34.1n apply to all these sources.

These results classify the tested kinetic-source branches without using the lepton–quark tilt, masses, mixing or the entropy objective to set their coefficients. They give explicit zero-variance tests for a further independently selected source. Native matter and cubic transport still require the common field and unit identifications of Lemma T.34.3. $\square$

<a id="theorem-t341p"></a>

<a id="theorem-t341p-endpoint-wilson-first-moments-and-the-multiplet-kinetic-obstruction"></a>**Theorem T.34.1p (Endpoint Wilson First Moments and the Multiplet Kinetic Obstruction).** Use the electric action (T.34.1m.1) with the actual group $G=S(U(3)\times U(2))$ on a finite graph with a simple path of $m\ge1$ edges and distinct endpoints. Keep the confining scalar and finite CAR fields of Construction G.8.6p.1 on the same carrier, using representations that descend to $G$ and the joint Gauss projection. The Hamiltonian has the stated positive electric coefficients, scalar Laplacian, positive on-site quartic, finite-range gauge-covariant hops and gauge-invariant multiplication interactions of that construction. Fix one physical energy unit $E_0$ and a normalized physical ground state $\Omega$. For any irreducible unitary representation $R$ of $G$, an open Wilson insertion with two charged endpoint registers determines
$$
K_R=xq_R^2+y c_2(R)+z c_3(R)
\tag{T.34.1p.1}
$$
from an exact conjugate pair of unit-mass energy responses, with an explicit finite spectral-tail bound. The insertions for $C,W,D$ of Theorem T.34.1m give the exact positive-triple inverse on the interacting source using fixed, state-independent gains. For the lepton and quark doublets of Theorem T.34, this readout has the color Casimir $4/3$ on the normalized quark multiplet. On every positive variance-zero branch of Definition T.34.1a the induced doublet prefactor ratio from a common one-leg kinetic transfer satisfies
$$
\sqrt{\frac{22}{9}}<\sqrt{\frac{K_Q}{K_L}}<\sqrt{\frac{82}{27}}<\frac83.
\tag{T.34.1p.2}
$$

*Carrier and invariant insertions.* The groups, confinement and bounded hopping and linear scalar–CAR coefficients give the form estimate $H\ge H_E-C_0 I$ on the unconstrained Hilbert space for an explicit $C_0$. Indeed the quartic absorbs the on-site quadratic and the linear scalar–CAR bound, and the magnetic and scalar-neighbor forms are nonnegative. The compact gauge configuration space and confining on-site potential give a compact resolvent by the argument of Construction G.8.6p.1. An empty-CAR, Haar-constant gauge and radial scalar trial state is Gauss invariant. Its trial energy $E_{\rm tr}$ bounds the physical ground energy $E_{\rm gs}$ above and satisfies $\langle H_E\rangle_\Omega\le E_{\rm tr}+C_0$. The same realization works on the quotient group because its compact link form, normalized Haar measure and the descended representations preserve these domain and symmetry arguments.

At the first endpoint use an extra register with a neutral ready line and charged summands $R,\overline R$. At the second use a neutral ready line and the paired summands $\overline R,R$. Take the orthogonal sum of these charged pairs for the entire probe menu on the same two registers and keep one common ready line at each endpoint. Distinct labels distinguish the summands even for equivalent representations. Let the occupied summands at each endpoint have a common independently fixed energy $\Delta>E_{\rm tr}+C_0$ above the ready line, with no coupling of these registers in the drift. The enlarged Hamiltonian is $H$ plus the two occupation gaps, with the Gauss projection acting on all charges. The ready state tensored with $\Omega$ has energy $E_{\rm gs}$. Every nonready sector has energy at least $-C_0+\Delta>E_{\rm gs}$, so the ready state is still a physical ground state.

Orient the path $\Gamma$ so that its ordered product $U_\Gamma$ transforms as $h_x U_\Gamma h_y^{-1}$. With $d_R=\dim R$, the charged register vectors are
$$
v_R(U)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{d_R}}\sum_{i,j} R(U_\Gamma)_{ij}\,|i\rangle_x\otimes|\bar j\rangle_y,
\qquad
v_{\overline R}(U)=\overline{v_R(U)}
\tag{T.34.1p.3}
$$
in the stated summands. Their pointwise norm is one by unitarity. Each is equivariant under the two endpoint actions. The vertex gauge action on the simple path is transitive on its link configurations, with stabilizer the diagonal $G$ at the identity links. Any equivariant vector built only from the path and the specified endpoint representations is thus determined by a vector in $(R\otimes\overline R)^G$. Schur's lemma makes this line one-dimensional, so normalization fixes the insertion up to a constant phase. Multiplication by either vector maps the ready sector isometrically to the corresponding joint Gauss sector and retains all color and weak components. This insertion is the ready-to-charged block of the bounded operator $|v_R(U)\rangle\langle 0,0|$ and has a direct invariant unitary implementation by interchanging the orthogonal ready and $v_R(U)$ lines and acting identically on their complement. The same construction applies to the conjugate label. These operators depend on the gauge links alone and act trivially on the original scalar and CAR indices.

*Exact energy calibration.* Write $D_\beta$ for the real link derivations, with positive weights $w_\beta$ as in Theorem T.34.1n. On an edge of $\Gamma$, $D_\beta$ inserts the corresponding Hermitian Lie algebra generator multiplied by $i$, up to a sign and unitary conjugation. The derivation vanishes off the path. Hilbert–Schmidt invariance and the Casimir identity in $R$ give, for $v=v_R$ and separately for its conjugate,
$$
\sum_\beta w_\beta\|D_\beta v\|^2=m K_R,qquad
\sum_\beta w_\beta D_\beta^2v=-m K_R v.
\tag{T.34.1p.4}
$$
For example, on one edge the sum in a simple factor is $d_R^{-1}\operatorname{Tr}\sum_a T_a^2=c_i(R)$, and the abelian part is $q_R^2$. The direct formula is invariant under edge reversal because the generator sign cancels in each square. The derivative $\langle v,D_\beta v\rangle$ is imaginary, and it changes sign for the conjugate vector. The electric form on $\Omega v$ expands into the form on $\Omega$, the known derivative square (T.34.1p.4), and a cross term linear in $\langle v,D_\beta v\rangle$. Conjugate averaging cancels that term for every ground state, including a state carrying electric current. The other terms of $H$ commute through the multiplier: scalar derivatives act on distinct coordinates, and the magnetic, Higgs and hopping interactions are link multiplication operators acting on the original scalar or CAR factors.

Let $\mu_+,\mu_-$ be the energy measures of $H_{\rm ext}-E_{\rm gs}$ on the two prepared states $\Omega v_R$ and $\Omega v_{\overline R}$. Each is positive, supported on $[0,\infty)$ and has total mass one. The form calculation proves
$$
\frac12\int_0^\infty \lambda\,d(\mu_++\mu_-)(\lambda)
=2\Delta+\frac{m E_0}{2}K_R .
\tag{T.34.1p.5}
$$
This first moment uses the physical charged endpoint response. Subtracting $2\Delta$ removes the two known register energies in the same clock. The color, weak and determinant coefficients have gains $K_C=x/15+4z/3$, $K_W=3x/20+3y/4$ and $K_D=(3/5)x$. Their inverse has constant denominators, with $x=5K_D/3$, $y=4(K_W-3x/20)/3$ and $z=3(K_C-x/15)/4$. The path and endpoint charge factors stay the same across the comparison.

*Finite errors.* The link-multiplication vectors are smooth and bounded, with bounded first and second link derivatives, so multiplication preserves the common form domain. On that domain integration by parts and (T.34.1p.4) give the weak identity
$$
(H_{\rm ext}-E_{\rm gs})(\Omega v)
=\left(2\Delta+\frac{mE_0K_R}{2}\right)\Omega v
-E_0\sum_\beta w_\beta(D_\beta\Omega)\otimes(D_\beta v).
\tag{T.34.1p.6}
$$
The right side lies in $L^2$ by Cauchy–Schwarz in the weighted derivative sum. The operator-domain characterization by the closed form gives (T.34.1p.6) in $L^2$. Therefore each of the two second moments is bounded above by
$$
\left(2\Delta+\frac{m E_0K_R}{2}
+\sqrt{2E_0m K_R(E_{\rm tr}+C_0)}\right)^2.
\tag{T.34.1p.7}
$$
The tail of each first moment beyond $\Lambda>0$ is at most (T.34.1p.7) divided by $\Lambda$. An independently supplied upper bound on $K_R$ in a specified coefficient menu makes this a finite error radius before measuring the insertion. The affine coefficient inverse propagates the radii of the three responses without a lower-margin requirement on any ground-state Wilson norm.

*Doublet transfer.* The lepton doublet $L$ is the dual of the weak fundamental and the quark doublet $Q$ is the tensor product of the color and weak fundamentals. Their Standard Model hypercharges are $-1/2$ and $1/6$. The coordinate relation of Remark T.34.1h gives $\kappa_1=(3/5)x$, $\kappa_2=y$, $\kappa_3=z$, so
$$
K_L=\tfrac34\kappa_2+\tfrac14\kappa_1,qquad
K_Q=\tfrac34\kappa_2+\tfrac1{36}\kappa_1+\tfrac43\kappa_3.
\tag{T.34.1p.8}
$$
Using an unnormalized endpoint insertion would multiply both its first moment and its mass by $d_R$. Dividing by that mass recovers (T.34.1p.8). On the positive variance-zero locus, put $t=\kappa_1/\kappa_2>0$ and substitute $48\kappa_3=55\kappa_2+21\kappa_1$. This gives $K_Q/K_L=(82+22t)/(27+9t)$, strictly decreasing from $82/27$ to $22/9$. By Lemma T.34.3 a one-leg kinetic transfer that identifies the two physical forms with these normalized responses in a common gain has prefactor ratio $\sqrt{K_Q/K_L}$. The difference $9K_Q-64K_L$ equals $-\tfrac34(21\kappa_1+55\kappa_2-16\kappa_3)$. It vanishes at ratio $8/3$ and equals $-24\kappa_3$ on the positive variance-zero locus. This gives a finite exclusion whenever the propagated cutoff error in the difference is smaller than $24\kappa_3$. A source that uses a different matter response or a separately proved conversion must derive the corresponding kinetic and cubic maps. $\square$

<a id="theorem-t341q"></a>

<a id="theorem-t341q-complete-endpoint-calibrated-fermion-leg-transfer-test"></a>**Theorem T.34.1q (Complete Endpoint-Calibrated Fermion-Leg Transfer Test).** Use the common electroweak source and primitive hypercharge coordinate of Theorem T.34.1p. Compare the charged-lepton and down-quark cubic couplings with one common scalar Higgs normalization and the same unnormalized cubic prefactor. On each of the two fermion legs, use either a common scalar kinetic form in the two sectors, or a scalar form proportional by a common positive gain to that leg's normalized endpoint Wilson coefficient. On the full positive variance-zero locus of Theorem T.34.1i, the left-only transfer cannot give $c_\ell/c_d=8/3$. The right-only and the two-leg transfers each give that value at exactly one positive ray, and the two rays are distinct. The physical flag shifts already test these compatibility conditions without a cubic-response measurement. This classifies the transfer tests under the stated identification of the fermion kinetic forms; the electric calibration alone does not impose that identification or select either ray.

*Kinetic coefficients on the variance locus.* Write $(x,y,z)=(\kappa_1^{\rm can},\kappa_2,\kappa_3)$, $t=x/y>0$, and impose the theoretical variance equation $z/y=55/48+21t/80$. Use the actual multiplets $L,Q,e_R,d_R$ with Standard Model hypercharges $-1/2,1/6,-1,-1/3$. A conjugate representation gives the same Wilson first moment. In (T.34.1p.1) the respective weak Casimirs are $3/4,3/4,0,0$, and the color Casimirs are $0,4/3,0,4/3$. Therefore the normalized endpoint coefficient for each multiplet is
\[
\frac{K_L}{y}=\frac{3t}{20}+\frac34,qquad
\frac{K_Q}{y}=\frac{11t}{30}+\frac{41}{18},\qquad
\frac{K_e}{y}=\frac{3t}{5},\qquad
\frac{K_d}{y}=\frac{5t}{12}+\frac{55}{36}.
\tag{T.34.1q.1}
\]
The normalizations are by the dimensions of the full endpoint multiplets as in (T.34.1p.3). In particular the color coefficient is $4/3$ both for $Q$ and for $d_R$. The available flags of Theorem T.34.1k read $W=K_L$ and $C=K_d$. These identifications use their charges and Casimirs alone.

*Classification of the scalar transfers.* Lemma T.34.3 gives the squared prefactor ratio by multiplying the kinetic ratios on the legs where the endpoint identification is made. The common positive gains and the single Higgs factor cancel. The cases of a common form on both legs, left only, right only, and both legs give, respectively,
\[
1,\qquad
R_L(t)=\frac{2(33t+205)}{27(t+5)},\qquad
R_R(t)=\frac{75t+275}{108t},\qquad
R_{LR}(t)=\frac{25(3t+11)(33t+205)}{1458t(t+5)} .
\tag{T.34.1q.2}
\]
The left ratio decreases from $82/27$ to $22/9$ and is always below $64/9$. The right ratio decreases from infinity to $25/36$, so $R_R=64/9$ occurs exactly at $t_R=25/63$. Direct differentiation of the last ratio gives
\[
R_{LR}'(t)=-\frac{25(483t^2+4510t+11275)}{1458t^2(t+5)^2}<0 .
\tag{T.34.1q.3}
\]
It decreases from infinity to $275/162$, so $R_{LR}=64/9$ has exactly one positive solution $t_{LR}$. Clearing the strictly positive denominator yields $7893t_{LR}^2+27390t_{LR}-56375=0$. It lies strictly between $1451/1000$ and $1452/1000$ by the signs of that polynomial and its positive derivative there. In particular it differs from $t_R$. Multiplying the left ratio by the right ratio cannot give the same calibration as the right-only transfer at $t_R$, since $R_L(t_R)>1$. Each equation here is a compatibility test on an already specified kinetic prescription.

*Testing both prescriptions on the same electric source.* On the variance locus the independently determined flag-shift ratio is
\[
\frac{C}{W}=\frac{25(3t+11)}{27(t+5)},\qquad
\frac{d}{dt}\frac{C}{W}=\frac{100}{27(t+5)^2}>0 .
\tag{T.34.1q.4}
\]
Thus $C/W=320/153$ is necessary and sufficient for the right-only compatibility test on that locus. The two-leg test requires the distinct value in (T.34.1q.4) at $t_{LR}$. The latter value has rational brackets from the polynomial signs and monotonicity, and those brackets are disjoint from the former. The flag and endpoint current bounds of Theorems T.34.1n and T.34.1p give finite enclosing intervals for $C,W$ and for all four $K$ values. Dividing by positive lower bounds for the needed denominators and multiplying the resulting ratio intervals propagates the error in (T.34.1q.2). Since all quantities are strictly positive at a named point, sufficiently fine enclosures eventually certify a strict mismatch whenever the appropriate equality fails. Exact equality requires the corresponding analytic source relation. This test consumes neither a measured lepton-to-quark prefactor nor an entropy optimum. A source rule giving a variance-zero triple and identifying its actual fermion kinetic forms is needed to infer the prefactor from the physical source. $\square$

<a id="corollary-t342"></a>**Corollary T.34.2** (PCE-Optimal Bures Weights on the $c_\ell/c_d = 8/3$ Normalization Branch). On the lepton-to-quark tilt normalization branch $c_\ell/c_d = 8/3$ (Corollary T.34.1), equivalently on a branch carrying the Bures-weight certificate of Theorem T.34.1b, minimize the strictly convex PCE objective
$$
S(\kappa)=8\kappa_3\ln\kappa_3 + 3\kappa_2\ln\kappa_2 + \kappa_1\ln\kappa_1
$$
subject to the two linear constraints
$$
\mathcal{W}\colon\; 8\kappa_3 + 3\kappa_2 + \kappa_1 = 12,\qquad \mathcal{N}\colon\; 21\kappa_1 + 55\kappa_2 - 48\kappa_3 = 0.
$$
$\mathcal{W}$ enforces that the weighted sum of Bures weights equals the gauge algebra dimension $n_G = 12$; $\mathcal{N}$ is the normalization constraint from Corollary T.34.1.

*Derivation.* Introduce Lagrange multipliers $\mu$ for $\mathcal{W}$ and $\nu$ for $\mathcal{N}$. The stationarity conditions are
$$
n_i(1+\ln\kappa_i) = \mu\,n_i + \nu\,c_i, \qquad i\in\{1,2,3\},
$$
where $(n_1,n_2,n_3)=(1,3,8)$ are the multiplicities and $(c_1,c_2,c_3)=(21,55,-48)$ are the $\mathcal{N}$ coefficients. Thus
$$
1+\ln\kappa_1 = \mu + 21\nu,\quad 1+\ln\kappa_2 = \mu + \tfrac{55}{3}\nu,\quad 1+\ln\kappa_3 = \mu - 6\nu.
$$
Define $y := e^{-\nu/3}$. Then the ratios of the $\kappa_i$ are
$$
\ln(\kappa_1/\kappa_3) = 27\nu ;\Longrightarrow; \kappa_1/\kappa_3 = y^{-81},
$$
$$
\ln(\kappa_2/\kappa_3) = \tfrac{73}{3}\nu ;\Longrightarrow; \kappa_2/\kappa_3 = y^{-73}.
$$
(Here the exponents arise from $27/(1/3)=81$ and $(73/3)/(1/3)=73$ after expressing everything in terms of $y = e^{-\nu/3}$.)

Substituting into $\mathcal{N}$: $21\kappa_3 y^{-81} + 55\kappa_3 y^{-73} = 48\kappa_3$, which simplifies to
$$
21y^{-81} + 55y^{-73} = 48.
$$
Equivalently, multiplying through by $y^{81}$:
$$
21 + 55y^{8} = 48y^{81},
$$
which has a unique positive solution $y^*>1$. Equivalently, in the form
$$
21y^{-81}+55y^{-73}=48,
$$
the left side is strictly decreasing on $(0,\infty)$, tends to $\infty$ as $y\downarrow0$, and tends to $0$ as $y\to\infty$.

Substituting into $\mathcal{W}$ determines $\kappa_3$:
$$
\kappa_3 = \frac{12}{8 + 3y^{-73} + y^{-81}}.
$$
Numerically, $y^* \approx 1.00613$, giving
$$
\boxed{\kappa_1^*\approx 0.695,\quad \kappa_2^*\approx 0.729,\quad \kappa_3^*\approx 1.140.}
$$
Verification with the displayed three-decimal weights gives $8(1.140)+3(0.729)+0.695=12.002$ and $21(0.695)+55(0.729)-48(1.140)=-0.030$. These small residuals result from rounding the exact positive solution. That solution is the unique minimizer: it satisfies the two linear constraints and the stationarity equations, while strict convexity of $x\ln x$ on $x>0$ makes the objective strictly convex on their feasible one-parameter segment.

<a id="remark-t341-conditional-interpretation"></a>**Remark T.34.1: Conditional Interpretation.** On the imposed normalization branch, or after an accepted $\mathcal V_{\ell d}=0$ certificate fixes the required Bures weights, the color and hypercharge Casimir entries evaluate the stated lepton--quark tilt. Quarks and leptons have different color data, but that difference alone does not derive the numerical factor $8/3$; Theorem T.34.1b gives the exact additional certificate equation.

<a id="lemma-t343-canonical-three-leg-yukawa-transfer"></a>**Lemma T.34.3 (Canonical Three-Leg Yukawa Transfer).** Let the field-coordinate action of a fermion sector contain
$$
\mathcal L_2=i\bar\psi_LZ_L\not{D}\psi_L+i\bar\psi_RZ_R\not{D}\psi_R+(DH)^\dagger Z_H(DH),\qquad
\mathcal L_3=-\sum_A\bar\psi_LC_A\psi_RH^A+\mathrm{h.c.},
$$
with constant positive Hermitian kinetic matrices $Z_L,Z_R,Z_H$ commuting with their respective gauge actions. The fields $\psi_L=Z_L^{-1/2}\psi_L^{\rm can}$, $\psi_R=Z_R^{-1/2}\psi_R^{\rm can}$, $H^A=\sum_b(Z_H^{-1/2})^A{}_bH_{\rm can}^b$ have unit kinetic forms, and the canonical Yukawa matrices are
$$
Y_b=\sum_AZ_L^{-1/2}C_AZ_R^{-1/2}(Z_H^{-1/2})^A{}_b .
$$
Hence the prefactor map $c_{\rm sector}\propto z_{\rm sector}^{-1/2}$ of Theorem T.34 holds when one fermion kinetic form of the sector equals $z_{\rm sector}I$ while the other fermion form, $Z_H$ and the unnormalized cubic $C$ are common to the compared sectors; when both fermion forms equal $z_{\rm sector}I$ the factor is $z_{\rm sector}^{-1}$. A single Higgs doublet has one kinetic form, so $Z_H$ carries no sector-dependent factor. On the selected native source of Theorem T.78.15d ($\kappa=4$, $c=4$, spacing $a=1$, unit fermion time coefficient) the scalar form is $Z_H=c/(2\kappa)=\tfrac12$ and the transfer is $Y_f=K_f/(2\sqrt2)$ for all four species $f=u,d,e,\nu$: it carries no sector factor.

*Proof.* Because $Z_L^{-1/2}$ is constant and Hermitian, $\bar\psi_LZ_L\not{D}\psi_L=\bar\psi_L^{\rm can}Z_L^{-1/2}Z_LZ_L^{-1/2}\not{D}\psi_L^{\rm can}=\bar\psi_L^{\rm can}\not{D}\psi_L^{\rm can}$, and likewise for $\psi_R$ and $H$. Substituting the same fields into $\mathcal L_3$ gives $-\sum_b\bar\psi_L^{\rm can}Y_b\psi_R^{\rm can}H_{\rm can}^b$ with $Y_b$ as displayed; no commutation of $C_A$ with the kinetic matrices is used. If $Z_L=z_{\rm sector}I$ and the remaining data are common, $Y=z_{\rm sector}^{-1/2}Y'$ with $Y'$ common to the sectors; if also $Z_R=z_{\rm sector}I$, a second factor $z_{\rm sector}^{-1/2}$ appears. On the native source each real scalar coordinate has Hamiltonian term $\kappa p^2$, hence Lagrangian time term $\dot q^2/(4\kappa)$. In $x^0=ct$ and with $H=(q_1+iq_2,q_3+iq_4)^T/\sqrt2$ this is $\tfrac{c}{2\kappa}|\partial_0H|^2$, so $Z_H=c/(2\kappa)=\tfrac12$. The fermion time term $i\psi^\dagger\partial_t\psi$ has unit coefficient in $x^0$, and the Hamiltonian Yukawa coefficient $K_f$ becomes $C_f=K_f/c$. Therefore $Y_f=K_f/(c\sqrt{Z_H})=K_f/(2\sqrt2)$. ∎

\lambda_{\mathrm{PU}}(\mathfrak{A}_{PU};\gamma) &= (\gamma^2-1)/36 \quad \text{(zero only with the accepted }\gamma=1\text{ datum, Theorems T.22b and T.25)}\\

Flavor observables retain their separate normalization and profile ledgers.
