The counts sum to 4,196,640; no cutoff is used. Their coverage proof is Theorem T.42.1b, whose root-neighbour counts produce these cardinalities. They are also checked directly by the integer-scaled root decoder of A.4.a: enumerate all triples, retain exactly the displayed validity predicate, and tabulate the exact distance tuples; equivalently, fix $r_3$ and multiply by 240, by Weyl transitivity on roots.

The complete physical maximizer set is the union of **two** Weyl orbits, $q=(2,4,4)$ and $q=(4,6,4)$, each with 967680 ordered representatives. Its response probability is 1/8. Every other candidate has success probability at most 1/12, giving an exact gap 1/24. The predeclared tie rule, which returns the lexicographically smallest maximizing tuple, gives

$$
q_*=(q_{32},q_{31},q_{21})=(2,4,4).
$$

The two maximizing orbits have equal utility, and no individual root vector is preferred. The deterministic tie rule fixes the output; the complete maximizing set is retained.

**A.4. Complete common source and resource objective.**

So that no candidate-dependent preparation cost is appended after the comparison, the service source executes one fixed batch in **every** candidate comparison:

1. One three-register root preparation and binary test for every $t\in\mathcal T$, in lexicographic order of the integer-scaled root words. Store every pointer outcome and every source state; do not postselect or reset. All 4,196,640 tests occur regardless of the nominated report candidate.
2. Prepare/execute the entire finite all-thirteen real field/source batch of Construction T.79.5b.9 at the same registered accuracy, physical clock/holding windows and source-aware controller rules. Retain every source and provider complement, coefficient/input interval, actual execution trace and readout archive. The selected tag identifies one of these source blocks as the exported flavor block; the other blocks remain paid source and test auxiliaries.
3. Compute and retain the complete root validity, distance, determinant, orbit and tie tables using the displayed finite arithmetic, before reporting any utility. Compute the complete physical label table of all thirteen sources. Candidate nomination changes only which already owned tagged test and field block is designated for the requested output. The complete output archive remains available; no unmeasured hidden block is deleted from the source.

The construction is a complete finite witness; its size is not minimized, and its resource account is stated for the fixed finite task.

**A.4.a. Explicit root-batch account.**

The root batch owns $N=4{,}196{,}640$ disjoint blocks, each with three eight-level registers and one pointer (ten qubits). Thus it owns exactly 41,966,400 qubits before auxiliary ROM/controller/field resources. It executes exactly $3N=12{,}589{,}920$ root Householder pulses and $N=4{,}196{,}640$ projector-meter pulses; one serial schedule has duration $4N\tau$. Its root/meter integrated added norm bound is $4N\pi\hbar$; the sum of pulse total-variation bounds is $16N\pi\hbar/\tau$. Every block has the stated positive baseline through its actual live/holding interval. Stored roots may be encoded in eight signed three-bit coordinates for $2r$; a literal 240-word root ROM therefore uses 5760 bits. A direct table stores each triple's three eight-bit root indices, three four-bit distances, one three-bit determinant, one four-bit orbit index and one retained pointer bit, at most $44N$ bits. Its redundant values are checked by the explicit integer formulas; this upper allocation counts actual initialized cells even if some are unused. Program counters and fixed arithmetic scratch are additional, with the explicit finite decoder below.

The root ROM can instead be generated by loops over pairs of coordinate indices and signs, then over eight sign bits of even parity. The full candidate decoder loops over $240^3$ index triples, rejects repetitions and $q_{31}\le q_{32}$, and assigns the remaining indices sequentially. All loops have literal finite endpoints; arithmetic operates on the bounded signed integers $2r$. It computes squared distances by eight subtractions/squares/sums and division by four, then $D$ by the displayed small-integer polynomial. Rank/table comparison is over thirteen stored triples. A reversible implementation retains its entire finite instruction and old-register trace. This prescription specifies every logical operation and a terminating full trace; its memory requirement can be bounded by the total number of loop iterations times the fixed maximum arithmetic word size. Invalid triples have their explicit failure bit and are not admitted competitors.

for the **full** resource objective. The nonmaximizer gap is $\eta/24$, the two exact orbit ties remain, and the declared tie rule then selects $q_*$. **A.4.c. Fixed finite field/query profile and expected-cost typing.**

The following profile fixes the parameterized field compiler to one finite mathematical protocol, with the execution meaning stated at the beginning of Part A.

**Source settings.** Use a periodic box of side $c\hbar/Q$ and momentum set $\{0\}$. The zero mode is exactly invariant under the homogeneous sources. Use all thirteen literal 128-bit $h_b$ programs printed above; all repeated edge values share one stored mantissa. Retain the full heavy, reference and complement source, source energy $Q$, clock $t_c=\hbar/Q$, scalar calibration record and canonical kinetic coefficients. The normalized current's formal exact eigensystem and current identities use these **dyadic** $a,b$, not ideal heat entries. Any finite approximation of the remaining source-owned scalar constants is carried as a separately certified generator or pole error.

For each field source, compute a rational coefficient-sum norm bound for its full native source, loading providers, detector and spin-one reference, including all their positive baseline terms. Use the same ceiling

$$
B=\max\!\left(1,\left\lceil\frac{\text{maximum full native/provider bound}}Q\right\rceil\right).
$$

over every active block in all thirteen source programs, and let $K$ be the integer ceiling, at least one, of the maximum full current/reference coefficient-sum norm used by any query. These are deterministic finite sums from the explicit source matrices, not norms of a reduced visible $3\times3$ matrix. $B$ bounds the known active **native drift**. It excludes the intentionally applied fast pulse or clock-drive Hamiltonian, which is part of the prescribed control and has its own charged peak/action/derivative ledger, not a Duhamel error term. Any genuinely noncommuting static native clock term is included; isolated commuting clock/program phases are retained exactly. Archived spectator blocks are isolated tensor factors with their native evolution and baseline phases retained exactly; they are not subtracted from the resource account. The local approximation norm is unchanged on tensoring those untouched evolutions.

Set

$$
\omega=Q/16,\qquad\epsilon=\frac{2^{-30}}{(1+K)^3},\qquad
T=\frac{t_c}{16(1+B)},\qquad\eta_p=2^{-30}\epsilon^2,\qquad
n=\left\lceil\frac{64}{\eta_p^2}\right\rceil.
$$

Use the complete spin-one reference and its pulse envelope $f_T(t)=2\sin^2(\pi t/T)/T$, with the actual kinetic-action current. Since every relevant energy difference is at most $2BQ+Q/16$, the source Fourier factor obeys $|F_\Delta-1|<1/8$, hence $|F_\Delta|>7/8$. These constants are fixed from source norms before reading an outcome.

**Literal query list.** For a d-dimensional same-charge input port list define

$$
\operatorname{Prep}(d)=\{e_i:1\le i\le d\}\cup\{(e_i+e_j)/\sqrt2,\ (e_i+\mathrm i e_j)/\sqrt2:i<j\}.
$$

It has $d^2$ members. For quarks, query both current orientations, each of the two rest spins and three colors, all nine members of $\operatorname{Prep}(3)$, and all three exclusive output generation ports: $2\cdot2\cdot3\cdot9\cdot3=324$ binary tests. For leptons query $e\to(\text{light}+\text{heavy neutrino})$ on both spins, $\operatorname{Prep}(3)$ and all six outputs ($2\cdot9\cdot6=108$ tests); and the reverse current on both spins, $\operatorname{Prep}(6)$ and three charged-lepton outputs ($2\cdot36\cdot3=216$ tests). Include the charge-conjugate protocol of each test, even where a Majorana conjugate duplicates a case. Thus there are exactly **1296 fixed binary current tests per source**, and **16848** over thirteen sources. Every exclusive success effect has its complete failure complement; all other spin/color/occupation/heavy/source/reference outcomes remain in it. No response-nullity inference rests on omitting an untested complement. Exact spin/color and conjugate relations also follow from the full canonical action.

Each query is repeated n times with freshly prepared source/provider/reference/record stocks. The complete physical field batch therefore contains all $16848n$ nominated fresh preparations plus all their retained complements and archives. It does not prepare only the favorable member or stop on success. Every actual ground-loading operation, parity/charge provider, pointer, calibration, coefficient routine and decoder is counted on each run at its actual reuse/fresh-stock boundary.

**Finite compilation inputs.** Supply each query's actual source matrix, desired state/effect error $\eta_p/64$, desired normalized Fourier/calibration arithmetic error $2^{-40}$, and the fixed window $T$ to the terminating finite source-aware compiler of Construction T.79.5b.9 and the field-current instrument of Proposition T.79.5a.3. For each emitted finite list of $G$ preparation/readout gates, use common positive durations no greater than

$$
\tau_{\mathrm{gate}}=\frac{\eta_pt_c}{512G(1+B)},
$$

and require integrated generator approximation error at most $\eta_p/(512G)$ per gate. Here $B$ is recomputed from the complete, fixed active source/provider inventory before choosing the gate durations; pulse controls themselves are separately counted by their actual peak/action/derivative bounds. The source-native Duhamel estimate of Construction T.79.5b.9 makes the total drift error at most $\eta_p/512$, and the same bound holds for the summed coefficient error. Refine all scalar/matrix-function evaluation until its interval proof certifies these input error budgets and the actual Riesz-projector error below $\eta_p/64$. The all-thirteen dyadic spectral margin of Part C and the explicit signed/neutral gaps make these finite stopping tests terminate. All iteration counts, emitted coefficients, bits, force/control/support reservations and positive durations are retained.

Execute the exact lexicographic source/query/repetition schedule. Hold every source/provider/output archive until that deterministic schedule's computed final time plus one $t_c$. Consequently the holding window is an explicit sum of the finitely generated gate durations and $16848n$ windows $T$, plus the registered root-test schedule and one final $t_c$. The algorithm computes this number and its storage before the designated report is chosen.

**Response error and unequal-energy coherent queries.** The full-source Dyson remainder of Proposition T.79.5a.3 satisfies $\rho\le\epsilon^2K^2$ since $\epsilon K\le2^{-30}$. Each probability remainder is at most $3\epsilon^3K^3$. For a **basis-input intensity**, division by its actual factor $\epsilon^2|F_i|^2/8$ multiplies this by at most $512/(49\epsilon^2)$, so its systematic normalized intensity error is at most $33\epsilon K^3<33\cdot2^{-30}<2^{-24}$.

A coherent superposition does not have a single common Fourier factor when its input energies differ. For the two pair preparations Proposition T.79.5a.3 instead gives

$$
\begin{aligned}
p_+-\frac{p_i+p_j}{2}&=\frac{\epsilon^2}{8}\operatorname{Re}\!\left[F_iV_{bi}\overline{F_jV_{bj}}\right]+\text{error},\\
p_{\mathrm{iPhase}}-\frac{p_i+p_j}{2}&=\frac{\epsilon^2}{8}\operatorname{Im}\!\left[F_iV_{bi}\overline{F_jV_{bj}}\right]+\text{error}.
\end{aligned}
$$

Each subtraction has absolute coefficient sum 2, so its probability error is at most $6\epsilon^3K^3$. Reconstruct the complex pair and divide by the actual **complex** $F_i\overline{F_j}$, whose modulus exceeds $49/64$. The Euclidean complex-product error is at most

$$
\frac{3072\sqrt2}{49}\epsilon K^3<89\cdot2^{-30}<2^{-23}.
$$

This covers, in particular, the reverse lepton queries coherently mixing light and heavy inputs. Each input keeps its own $F_i$; absolute row phases are conventional and are not reconstructed. Preparation/effect/coefficient errors are allocated above at the probability scale $\eta_p$, not a raw larger current scale. The source compiler is required to make their combined probability contribution at most $\eta_p/8$ per test; tighten any individual allocation if the emitted trace requires it. Under the same paired-subtraction and complex-division rule their response contribution is bounded explicitly. A sampling error $\eta_p$ per probability contributes less than $30\cdot2^{-30}$ to a complex pair; the hardware $\eta_p/8$ contributes less than $4\cdot2^{-30}$, and the normalized Fourier arithmetic has its separate $2^{-40}$ budget. Thus the combined error is less than **$2^{-21}$** for every basis intensity and within-row complex product on the joint successful sampling event. The actual Hermitian current and full failure effects are used throughout.

Hoeffding's inequality for the n fresh Bernoulli runs gives probability-estimation error at most $\eta_p$ except on probability $2e^{-2n\eta_p^2}\le2e^{-128}$ per test. A union bound over 16848 tests is below $2^{-20}$, because $2\cdot16848<2^{16}$ and $e>2$. These statistical errors concern a run of the specified source. ## T.21.6 Hierarchy Invariant and Phenomenology

<a id="corollary-t422"></a>**Corollary T.42.2** (Leading-order hierarchy diagnostic).
On the selected $(d_{31}^2,d_{32}^2)=(6,2)$ branch, assume Theorem T.39's full-matrix certificate verifies $\log(m_3/m_2)\ne0$, a common leading coefficient and residuals satisfying
$$
\frac{\mathcal R_{31}}{d_{31}^2}
=
\frac{\mathcal R_{32}}{d_{32}^2}
$$
(in particular, both residuals may vanish),
$$
\mathcal R_{\mathrm{LO}}
=\frac{\log(m_3/m_1)}{\log(m_3/m_2)}
=\frac{d_{31}^2}{d_{32}^2}
=3.
$$
Without that realization certificate, the final value is the discrete model diagnostic selected in Theorem T.42.1, not a mass theorem.

Experimentally, using charged-lepton masses,

## T.21.7 UV to IR Evolution

### T.21.7.1 Decomposition of the Effective Exponent

The unit-radius branch value $\alpha_{\mathrm{UV}}=3/2$ and the empirical
extraction $\alpha_{\mathrm{IR}}^{\mathrm{obs}}=1.411$ differ by about six
percent. A source-exhaustive decomposition of that difference into geometric
and renormalization-group terms requires a separately computed common-scheme
ledger with controlled thresholds, remainders, and covariance. The registered
value $1.41804458\ldots$ is the distinct coefficient prescription of Theorem
T.24.2.1.

### T.21.7.2 RG Contribution

Let $t=\ln\mu$. On a supplied unbroken Standard Model one-loop record with diagonal positive charged-lepton Yukawas, no neutrino Yukawa terms and no threshold inside the interval, write
$$
16\pi^2\,\frac{d\ln y_i}{dt}
=C(t)+\frac32y_i(t)^2,
$$
where $C(t)$ contains the common trace and gauge terms. They cancel in the ratio, giving
$$
\frac{d}{dt}\ln(y_3/y_i)
=\frac{3}{32\pi^2}\bigl(y_3^2-y_i^2\bigr).
$$
For a registered squared distance $q_{3i}>0$, the corresponding coefficient change between two scales on that interval obeys
$$
\delta_{\mathrm{RG}}:=\left|\frac{\Delta\ln(y_3/y_i)}{q_{3i}}\right|
\le\frac{3}{32\pi^2q_{3i}}
\int_{\min(t_a,t_b)}^{\max(t_a,t_b)}
|y_3(t)^2-y_i(t)^2|\,dt.
$$
Evolution through electroweak or other thresholds requires a declared matched-running record with its finite matching terms; the unbroken equation alone cannot be continued to $m_\tau$ as a physical bound. The displayed allowance for $\delta_{\mathrm{RG}}$ below is a separate acceptance test on that complete integration, not a bound established by the self-term alone.

$$
\delta_{\mathrm{RG}} \lesssim 0.01\,\alpha_{\mathrm{UV}}.
$$

### T.21.7.3 Conditional Geometric Correction

The sinc transport and Grassmannian Van Vleck terms are geometric ingredients on their stated branch. The piecewise values $D_{\mathrm{eff}}(2)=3/8$ and $D_{\mathrm{eff}}(4)=13/6$ are separate phenomenological inputs of Theorem T.42.5.

Numerical agreement obtained after adopting those values validates that model branch only; it does not turn the assignment into a first-principles derivation. The hierarchy formula below must therefore carry forward-calibration status and compare preregistered alternatives.

Theorem T.24.2.1 registers the prescription
$$
\alpha_{\mathrm{IR}}:=\alpha_{\mathrm{UV}}\operatorname{sinc}(1/\sqrt3)=1.41804458\ldots .
$$
Because coherent averaging acts on amplitudes and does not by itself rescale a Gaussian exponent, this is a calibrated IR-coefficient branch. Its proximity to the empirical extraction $1.411$ is a diagnostic, not a causal derivation of running.

The complete fourth-order hierarchy formula is the certificate-gated
common-kernel re-expansion of Theorem T.42.6. Its base coefficient is the
common fourth-derivative output of the charged-lepton packet/VVM certificate
of Theorem T.42.2.

The effective geodesic dimension $D_{\mathrm{eff}}(d^2)$ uses two declared phenomenological assignments at $d^2_{\mathrm{th}}=4$:

On the marked calibration branch of Lemma T.42.4, the two registered charged-lepton pairs satisfy $h_{ij}=2d_{ij}^2$, so the pair with $d^2=4$ is assigned $h=8=d_{\min}$. ### T.21.8.1 Normalized Overlap-Certificate Requirement

### T.21.8.2 Packet/VVM Fourth-Order Coefficient Status

<a id="lemma-t421a"></a>**Lemma T.42.1a** (Conditional Packet-Overlap Expansion). Let
$d_{\max}>0$, let
$\alpha_{\mathrm{UV}},\alpha_{\mathrm{IR}},\beta\in\mathbb R$, let $D>0$,
and let $G\in C^6([0,d_{\max}])$. Assume
$$
G(0)=0,
\qquad
G^{(1)}(0)=G^{(3)}(0)=G^{(5)}(0)=0,
$$
$$
G^{(2)}(0)=2(\alpha_{\mathrm{UV}}-\alpha_{\mathrm{IR}}),
\qquad
G^{(4)}(0)=24\beta D,
$$
and assume that a verified constant $B_6\ge0$ satisfies
$$
\sup_{0\le d\le d_{\max}}|G^{(6)}(d)|\le720B_6.
$$
Define the normalized positive kernel
$$
\mathcal I(d):=\exp\!\left[-\alpha_{\mathrm{UV}}d^2+G(d)\right].
$$
Then
$$
-\log\mathcal I(d)
=\alpha_{\mathrm{IR}}d^2-\beta Dd^4+\mathcal R_6(d),
\qquad |\mathcal R_6(d)|\le B_6d^6
\tag{T.42.1a.1}
$$
for every $d\in[0,d_{\max}]$.

*Proof.* Taylor's theorem through order five gives
$$
G(d)=(\alpha_{\mathrm{UV}}-\alpha_{\mathrm{IR}})d^2
+\beta Dd^4+E_6(d),
\qquad |E_6(d)|\le B_6d^6.
$$
Therefore
$$
-\log\mathcal I(d)
=\alpha_{\mathrm{UV}}d^2-G(d)
=\alpha_{\mathrm{IR}}d^2-\beta Dd^4-E_6(d).
$$
Setting $\mathcal R_6(d):=-E_6(d)$ proves (T.42.1a.1). ∎

<a id="remark-t4211-scope-of-the-112-coefficient"></a>**Remark T.42.1.1: Scope of the $1/12$ Coefficient.** *A numerical factor
$1/12$ occurs in several local tensor expansions, including the cited

T.42.2.*

### T.21.8.2a Common Packet/VVM Certificate and Its Fourth-Order Coefficient

<a id="theorem-t422"></a>**Theorem T.42.2** (Conditional Packet/VVM Fourth-Order Coefficient). Put
$$
\mathcal E_\ell:=\{p_{\tau\mu},p_{\mu e}\},
\qquad d_{\tau\mu}:=\sqrt2,
\qquad d_{\mu e}:=2,
\qquad D_p:=D_{\mathrm{eff}}(d_p^2).
$$
A common charged-lepton packet/VVM certificate is the finite record
$$
\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{pkt/VVM}}^\ell
=\left(
g_B,\mu,\Lambda_{\mathrm{fl}},\mathcal D_{\mathrm{op}},\tau_*,
\{\gamma_p,A_p,\Delta_p,\epsilon_p,\mathcal T_p,
\mathcal Q_p,B_p\}_{p\in\mathcal E_\ell},
\alpha_{\mathrm{UV}},\alpha_{\mathrm{IR}},
\chi_{\mathrm{src}},\chi_{\mathrm{pre}}
\right),
$$
with the following types and acceptance tests.

1. $\Lambda_{\mathrm{fl}}$ is the same positive self-adjoint Schur--heat
   operator used by Theorem T.39, with declared domain
   $\mathcal D_{\mathrm{op}}\subset L^2(\mathrm{Gr}(2,8),\mu)$ and
   $\tau_*=\sigma_B^2/2$.

2. For each $p\in\mathcal E_\ell$,
   $\gamma_p:[0,d_p]\to\mathrm{Gr}(2,8)$ is a minimizing geodesic in the same

   d_{g_B}(\gamma_p(0),\gamma_p(s))=\frac{s}{\sqrt8}.
   $$
   Writing
   $$
   K_p^{\mathrm{mag}}(s)
   :=\mathcal N_\ell

   e^{-\tau_*\Lambda_{\mathrm{fl}}}
   \middle|\gamma_p(0)\right\rangle,

   the certificate supplies
   $\Delta_p,\mathcal T_p\in C^6([0,d_p];\mathbb R_{>0})$ and
   $\epsilon_p\in C^6([0,d_p];(-1,\infty))$, with
   $\mathcal T_p(0)=1$, and verifies the exact normalized Theorem-T.39 identity
   $$
   \widehat{\mathcal I}^{\mathrm{UV}}_p(s)
   :=\frac{K_p^{\mathrm{mag}}(s)}{A_p}
   =e^{-\alpha_{\mathrm{UV}}s^2}
   \left(\frac{\Delta_p(s)}{\Delta_p(0)}\right)^{1/2}
   \frac{1+\epsilon_p(s)}{1+\epsilon_p(0)}.
   \tag{T.42.2.1}
   $$

3. The independently registered infrared packet kernel is
   $$
   \mathcal I_p(s):=\mathcal T_p(s)
   \widehat{\mathcal I}^{\mathrm{UV}}_p(s),
   $$
   where $\chi_{\mathrm{pre}}$ verifies that
   $\Lambda_{\mathrm{fl}}$, the paths, normalizations, and transport functions
   were specified independently of the charged-lepton masses being evaluated.

4. Define the complete non-Gaussian logarithmic correction
   $$
   G_p(s):=\log\mathcal T_p(s)
   +\frac12\log\frac{\Delta_p(s)}{\Delta_p(0)}
   +\log\frac{1+\epsilon_p(s)}{1+\epsilon_p(0)}.
   $$
   Exact arithmetic or outward-rounded singleton intervals must verify
   $$
   G_p(0)=0,
   \qquad G_p^{(1)}(0)=G_p^{(3)}(0)=G_p^{(5)}(0)=0,
   $$
   $$
   G_p^{(2)}(0)=2(\alpha_{\mathrm{UV}}-\alpha_{\mathrm{IR}}).
   $$
   Define
   $$
   \beta_p:=\frac{G_p^{(4)}(0)}{24D_p}.

   The certificate is common only if it verifies
   $\beta_{\tau\mu}=\beta_{\mu e}$; denote this common value by
   $\beta_{\mathrm{pkt}}$.

5. $\mathcal Q_p$ is a finite cover of $[0,d_p]$ by intervals with rational endpoints, carrying enclosures on each interval's intersection with $[0,d_p]$ that verify positivity of every
   outward-rounded interval enclosures that verify positivity of every
   logarithm argument and
   $$
   |G_p^{(6)}(s)|\le720B_p
   \qquad(0\le s\le d_p).
   $$

6. The signed source ledger $\chi_{\mathrm{src}}$ assigns
   $\log\mathcal T_p$, $\frac12\log(\Delta_p/\Delta_p(0))$, and
   $\log((1+\epsilon_p)/(1+\epsilon_p(0)))$ exactly once. No VVM, heat,

On an accepted certificate, Lemma T.42.1a gives
$$
-\log\mathcal I_p(s)
=\alpha_{\mathrm{IR}}s^2
-\beta_{\mathrm{pkt}}D_ps^4+\mathcal R_{6,p}(s),
\qquad |\mathcal R_{6,p}(s)|\le B_ps^6.

Consequently,
$$
|\mathcal R_{6,\tau\mu}(\sqrt2)|\le8B_{\tau\mu},
\qquad
|\mathcal R_{6,\mu e}(2)|\le64B_{\mu e}.

If the exact fourth-derivative output satisfies

G_p^{(4)}(0)=\frac{D_p}{6}
\qquad\text{for both }p\in\mathcal E_\ell,

then
$$
\boxed{\beta_{\mathrm{pkt}}=\frac1{144}=\frac1C}
\tag{T.42.2.2}

because Theorem Z.13a independently gives $C=bM=144$.

*Proof.* Items 1--3 give
$\mathcal I_p(s)=\exp[-\alpha_{\mathrm{UV}}s^2+G_p(s)]$ with
$\mathcal I_p(0)=1$. Items 4--5 satisfy Lemma T.42.1a for each path and give
the displayed remainder bounds. Equality of the two fourth-derivative
quotients establishes one common coefficient. If
$G_p^{(4)}(0)=D_p/6$, then
$$
\beta_{\mathrm{pkt}}=\frac{D_p/6}{24D_p}=\frac1{144}.
$$
The equality with $1/C$ is arithmetic. Item 6 proves that the two
representations use one source ledger rather than two multiplied correction

<a id="theorem-t422c-exact-van-vleck-morette-coefficients-on-the-bures-grassmannian"></a>**Theorem T.42.2c (Exact Van Vleck–Morette Coefficients on the Bures Grassmannian).** Let $\gamma$ be a unit-speed geodesic of $\mathrm{Gr}(2,8)$ in the Bures metric of Theorem T.39a, whose initial tangent $X\in\operatorname{Hom}(\mathbb C^2,\mathbb C^6)$ has singular values $\sigma_1,\sigma_2$ with $\frac12(\sigma_1^2+\sigma_2^2)=1$. Put $a^2:=\sigma_1^2/2$, $b^2:=\sigma_2^2/2$ and $\tau:=a^2b^2\in[0,\frac14]$, so that $\tau=0$ is the rank-one Schubert direction and $\tau=\frac14$ the equal-singular-value direction.

1. The Jacobi operator $Y\mapsto R(Y,X)X$ has eigenvalues
$$
8a^2,\quad 8b^2,\quad 2(a+b)^2\ (\times2),\quad 2(a-b)^2\ (\times2),\quad 2a^2\ (\times8),\quad 2b^2\ (\times8),\quad 0\ (\times2),
\tag{T.42.2c.1}
$$
with trace $32$ and squared sum $112-128\tau$.
2. With $s:=\sqrt8\,d_{g_B}$ as in Theorem T.42.2 and $s\max(a,b)<\pi$, the Van Vleck–Morette determinant along $\gamma$ is $\Delta(s)=\prod_\kappa\frac{\sqrt\kappa\,s/\sqrt8}{\sin(\sqrt\kappa\,s/\sqrt8)}$, the product running over the nonzero eigenvalues in (T.42.2c.1), and
$$
\frac12\log\frac{\Delta(s)}{\Delta(0)}=\frac{s^2}{3}+\frac{7-8\tau}{1440}\,s^4+O(s^6).
\tag{T.42.2c.2}
$$
Its contributions to $G_p$ of Theorem T.42.2 are therefore $G^{(2)}(0)=2/3$ and $G^{(4)}(0)=(7-8\tau)/60\in[\frac1{12},\frac7{60}]$ for every geodesic type.
3. Consider a certificate of Theorem T.42.2 in which $\Delta_p$ is the Van Vleck–Morette determinant of item 2 along $\gamma_p$, and write $E_p:=\log\mathcal T_p+\log\frac{1+\epsilon_p}{1+\epsilon_p(0)}$ for its transport and heat-remainder terms.
   (a) If $E_p''(0)=0$, item 4 of Theorem T.42.2 forces $\alpha_{\mathrm{UV}}-\alpha_{\mathrm{IR}}=1/3$, whereas the registered values $\alpha_{\mathrm{UV}}=3/2$ of Corollary T.41.3 and $\alpha_{\mathrm{IR}}=(3/2)\operatorname{sinc}(1/\sqrt3)$ of Section T.21.6.2 give $0.0819554165\ldots$.
   (b) If $E_p^{(4)}(0)=0$, which holds on the Van Vleck reading of Remark T.42.2.1, the exact-output condition $G_p^{(4)}(0)=D_p/6$ of (T.42.2.2) forces $D_p=(7-8\tau_p)/10\in[\frac12,\frac7{10}]$, which excludes both registered assignments $D_{\mathrm{eff}}(2)=3/8$ and $D_{\mathrm{eff}}(4)=13/6$ of Theorem T.42.5.
   (c) On the reading of (b) with the registered assignments, the common-coefficient condition $\beta_{\tau\mu}=\beta_{\mu e}$ fails for every pair of geodesic types, because $(7-8\tau)/D_{\mathrm{eff}}(2)\in[\frac{40}{3},\frac{56}{3}]$ while $(7-8\tau)/D_{\mathrm{eff}}(4)\in[\frac{30}{13},\frac{42}{13}]$.

The registered values of $\alpha_{\mathrm{UV}}$ and $\alpha_{\mathrm{IR}}$ therefore require nonzero second-order content, and the registered effective dimensions, in the common coefficient and in the exact subbranch $\beta_{\mathrm{pkt}}=1/144$, require nonzero fourth-order content, from the infrared transport $\mathcal T_p$ or the heat remainder $\epsilon_p$.

*Proof.* Item 1. For the symmetric space $U(8)/(U(2)\times U(6))$ with tangent vectors embedded as $P(X)=\begin{pmatrix}0&-X^\dagger\\X&0\end{pmatrix}$, the curvature of every invariant metric is $R(Y,X)X=-[[P(Y),P(X)],P(X)]$. Computing the off-diagonal block gives
$$
R(Y,X)X=XX^\dagger Y+YX^\dagger X-2XY^\dagger X.
$$
By $U(2)\times U(6)$ equivariance take $X=\sigma_1E_{11}+\sigma_2E_{22}$. For $Y=cE_{ij}$ with $c\in\mathbb C$: if $i\ge3$, then $R(Y,X)X=\sigma_j^2Y$, giving $2a^2$ and $2b^2$ on $4$ complex rows each; if $i=j\le2$, then real $c$ gives $0$ and imaginary $c$ gives $4\sigma_i^2$, that is $8a^2$ and $8b^2$; if $\{i,j\}=\{1,2\}$, then $R(cE_{12},X)X=(\sigma_1^2+\sigma_2^2)cE_{12}-2\sigma_1\sigma_2\bar cE_{21}$ and symmetrically, so the four real combinations $E_{12}\pm E_{21}$ and $i(E_{12}\pm E_{21})$ have eigenvalues $(\sigma_1\pm\sigma_2)^2=2(a\pm b)^2$, each twice. The listed eigenvalues fill all $24$ real dimensions. With $a^2+b^2=1$, the trace is $32$ and the squared sum is $112(a^4+b^4)+96a^2b^2=112-128\tau$. At $\tau=0$ the holomorphic sectional curvature is $8$, as in Theorem T.39a.

Item 2. The curvature of a symmetric space is parallel, so in a parallel orthonormal eigenframe along $\gamma$ the Jacobi field with $J(0)=0$ and $J'(0)=e_\kappa$ is $\kappa^{-1/2}\sin(\sqrt\kappa\,r)\,e_\kappa(r)$, where $r=d_{g_B}$. The Van Vleck–Morette determinant is the reciprocal normalized Jacobian of the exponential map, hence the displayed product for $r$ below the first conjugate distance $\pi/\sqrt{8\max(a^2,b^2)}$. Using $\log(x/\sin x)=x^2/6+x^4/180+O(x^6)$ with $x^2=\kappa s^2/8$ gives
$$
\frac12\log\frac{\Delta(s)}{\Delta(0)}=\frac{s^2}{96}\sum\kappa+\frac{s^4}{23040}\sum\kappa^2+O(s^6),
$$
and item 1 gives (T.42.2c.2). Differentiation yields $G^{(2)}(0)=2/3$ and $G^{(4)}(0)=24(7-8\tau)/1440$.

Item 3. Under the stated vanishing, $G_p^{(2)}(0)$, respectively $G_p^{(4)}(0)$, equals the value of item 2. Item 4 of Theorem T.42.2 then reads $2/3=2(\alpha_{\mathrm{UV}}-\alpha_{\mathrm{IR}})$, and $\frac32-\frac32\operatorname{sinc}(1/\sqrt3)=0.0819554165\ldots$. The condition $G_p^{(4)}(0)=D_p/6$ gives $D_p=(7-8\tau_p)/10$, and $3/8<1/2$ and $13/6>7/10$. Finally $\beta_p=(7-8\tau_p)/(1440D_p)$, so equality of the two quotients requires equal values of $(7-8\tau)/D_p$; the two displayed ranges are disjoint because $42/13<40/3$. ∎

<a id="theorem-t422d-complete-forward-schur-heat-and-physical-matrix-computation"></a>**Theorem T.42.2d (Complete Forward Schur-Heat and Physical-Matrix Computation).** The actual predictive source and finite marked coherent paths of Theorem T.79.5b populate the original heat, transport/remainder and complete physical-matrix computation on the specified finite externally controlled regular-network and free-field branch. The following existing proof components give the remaining operator-domain, normalized finite comparison, full neutral/provider/current, matching and error statements.

**Domain strengthening**

<a id="definition-t422b"></a>**Definition T.42.2b** ($E_8$ Generation Triangle). *The three charged-lepton generations occupy $E_8$ root positions $r_\tau, r_\mu, r_e$ with squared distances:*
$$
(d^2_{\tau\mu}, d^2_{\mu e}, d^2_{\tau e}) = (2, 4, 6)
$$

*The corresponding $E_8$ inner products are $\langle r_\tau, r_\mu \rangle = 1$, $\langle r_\mu, r_e \rangle = 0$, $\langle r_\tau, r_e \rangle = -1$, via the relation $d^2 = 4 - 2\langle r_i, r_j \rangle$ for roots of squared norm $2$.*

<a id="theorem-t422a"></a>**Theorem T.42.2a** (Path Composition of Model Suppression Factors). *Let $\ell_{\tau\mu},\ell_{\mu e}\in\mathbb R$ be any two supplied adjacent-edge model exponents. Define*
$$
S_{\tau\mu}:=e^{-\ell_{\tau\mu}},
\qquad
S_{\mu e}:=e^{-\ell_{\mu e}}.
$$
*On the dominant-path composition branch, define the long-transition model factor by $S_{\tau e}:=S_{\tau\mu}S_{\mu e}$. Then*
$$
-\log S_{\tau e}=\ell_{\tau\mu}+\ell_{\mu e}.
\tag{T.42.2a.1}
$$
*No independent direct value at $d^2_{\tau e}=6$ is introduced.*

A physical mass-ratio conclusion additionally requires an anchored realization certificate with declared anchor data that verifies
$$
S_{\tau\mu}=\frac{m_\mu}{m_\tau},
\qquad
S_{\mu e}=\frac{m_e}{m_\mu}
\tag{T.42.2a.2}
$$
for consistently defined masses and one common $m_\mu$. On that certificate,
$$
S_{\tau e}=\frac{m_e}{m_\tau},
\qquad
\log\!\left(\frac{m_\tau}{m_e}\right)
=
\log\!\left(\frac{m_\tau}{m_\mu}\right)
+
\log\!\left(\frac{m_\mu}{m_e}\right).
$$

*Proof.* Positivity of the two model factors permits taking $-\log$ of their defining product, which gives (T.42.2a.1). Under (T.42.2a.2), cancellation of the common positive mass $m_\mu$ gives the long factor and the displayed logarithmic identity. The algebraic identity does not itself verify the realization certificate. ∎

<a id="remark-t4221a-consistency-check"></a>**Remark T.42.2.1a: Consistency Check.** *Path additivity ensures internal consistency: the $\tau/e$ model factor is uniquely determined by the adjacent-edge model factors, with no additional parameters or choices required for the longest-range ratio.*

## T.21.9 Quark Sector and Sector Prefactors

The same geometric hierarchy applies to quarks, with generation-independent sector prefactors determined by gauge/Bures normalization at the attractor.

### T.21.9.1 Explicit $E_8$ Triads for Quark Sectors

The displayed quark triads were chosen using the observed hierarchy and are therefore calibration candidates. An independent mass prediction requires a selector and score whose inputs exclude the evaluated masses. An independently tested calibrated model retains its calibration inputs.

**Down-type quarks** ($\mathcal{R} \approx 2$; minimal $(d^2_{32}, d^2_{31}) = (2, 4)$):

$$
\begin{aligned}
r_3 &= (1, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0),\\
r_2 &= (1, 0, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0) \quad\Rightarrow\quad d^2_{32} = 2,\\
r_1 &= (-1, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0) \quad\Rightarrow\quad d^2_{31} = 4.
\end{aligned}
$$

**Up-type quarks** (stronger suppression; $(d^2_{32}, d^2_{31}) = (4, 8)$):

$$
\begin{aligned}
r_3 &= (1, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0),\\
r_2 &= (-1, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0) \quad\Rightarrow\quad d^2_{32} = 4,\\
r_1 &= (-1, -1, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0) \quad\Rightarrow\quad d^2_{31} = 8.
\end{aligned}
$$

Each triple comprises valid $E_8$ roots of type $(\pm 1, \pm 1, 0, \ldots, 0)$, and the listed pairwise distances are verified directly.

### T.21.9.2 Sector Prefactors

<a id="theorem-t44"></a>**Theorem T.44** (Sector Prefactors on the Registered Normalization Branch). Let $c_\ell,c_d,c_u$ denote the charged-lepton, down-quark, and up-quark sector prefactors at $\mu_G$. Assume either the imposed normalization branch $c_\ell/c_d=8/3$ or an independently accepted Bures-weight representation-variance certificate $\mathcal V_{\ell d}=0$ of Theorem T.34.1b, and take the corresponding positive weights from Corollary T.34.2. Then
$$
\frac{c_\ell}{c_d}=\frac83,
\qquad
\frac{c_d}{c_u}=1.024667673462575\ldots
$$
under Theorem T.38's declared right-handed hypercharge convention. The first ratio is not a consequence of raw Casimir or McKay data, and the second is a prefactor ratio, not a stiffness ratio.

*Proof.* In the prefactor ratio computation one uses the PU-normalized gauge coefficient $g_U$ for canonical generators (Theorem T.13); the SM-canonical matching factors $Z_i$ control the gauge-boson kinetic terms but do not alter the fermion-sector prefactor ratios set by the Bures weights $\kappa_i$ (Theorem T.34). The sector normalization entering the prefactor tilt is

$$
z_{\mathrm{sector}}
=
\left(
\kappa_2\,C_2^{SU(2)}
+
\kappa_1\,Y^2
+
\kappa_3\,C_2^{SU(3)}\,N_c
\right)g_U^2,
$$

where $C_2$ are quadratic Casimirs and $Y$ is the hypercharge.

**Left-chiral doublets:**

- Lepton $L$: $C_2(\mathrm{SU}(2)) = 3/4$, $C_2(\mathrm{SU}(3)) = 0$, $Y^2 = 1/4$, $N_c=1$
- Quark $Q$: $C_2(\mathrm{SU}(2)) = 3/4$, $C_2(\mathrm{SU}(3)) = 4/3$, $Y^2 = 1/36$, $N_c=3$

Therefore:
$$
z_\ell=\left(\frac{3}{4}\kappa_2+\frac{1}{4}\kappa_1\right)g_U^2,
\qquad
z_d=\left(\frac{3}{4}\kappa_2+\frac{1}{36}\kappa_1+4\kappa_3\right)g_U^2,
$$
where $4\kappa_3$ comes from $C_2^{SU(3)}=4/3$ and $N_c=3$. The normalization constraint (Corollary T.34.1) imposes $z_d/z_\ell=64/9$, hence
$$
\frac{c_\ell}{c_d} = \sqrt{\frac{z_d}{z_\ell}} = \frac{8}{3}.
$$

**Right-chiral singlets (Theorem T.38):**

For up- and down-type singlets ($C_2(\mathrm{SU}(3))=4/3$, $N_c=3$, giving $4\kappa_3$):

$$
z_{u_R} = \left(4\kappa_3 + \frac{4}{9}\kappa_1\right)g_U^2, \qquad z_{d_R} = \left(4\kappa_3 + \frac{1}{9}\kappa_1\right)g_U^2,
$$

and the prefactor ratio is

$$
\frac{c_d}{c_u} = \sqrt{\frac{z_{u_R}}{z_{d_R}}} = \sqrt{\frac{4\kappa_3 + \frac{4}{9}\kappa_1}{4\kappa_3 + \frac{1}{9}\kappa_1}}.
$$

Using $(\kappa_1,\kappa_2,\kappa_3)=(0.695,0.729,1.140)$ (Corollary T.34.2) gives $c_d/c_u\approx 1.025\approx 1.02$. ∎

These prefactors and the selected $E_8$ triads define quark-sector model inputs. Reproduction of physical hierarchies requires Theorem T.39's accepted common-scale full-matrix realization, labels, threshold matching, renormalization evolution and residual certificate. The source-normalized value $y_t^{\mathrm{PU}}(\mathfrak{A}_{PU})=1$ is a PU model anchor; transferring it to a physical up-sector normalization requires that same accepted matching record.

\mathcal{N}_{PU} = \frac{1}{N_g} \cdot \frac{1}{M} \cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{n_G}} = \frac{1}{3 \cdot 24 \cdot \sqrt{12}} = \frac{1}{72\sqrt{12}} \approx 0.00401
$$
The model assigns these three factors to a democratic generation fraction $1/N_g=1/3$, a per-mode fraction $1/M=1/24$, and an isotropic amplitude factor $1/\sqrt{n_G}=1/\sqrt{12}$. Their product is the declared normalization input; capacity saturation and isotropy alone do not derive its absolute Yukawa normalization. The sector prefactor using the PCE-optimal weights $(\kappa_1^*,\kappa_2^*,\kappa_3^*) \approx (0.695,0.729,1.140)$ from Corollary T.34.2 and $g_U^2 = \pi/6$ (Theorem T.39a) is as follows.

**Normalization convention.** To avoid collision with other uses of the symbol $Y_0$ in the manuscript, we distinguish:
- $Y_0^{\rm src}$: the discrete-action source normalization (a separate constant; e.g. $Y_0^{\rm src}=2$ where defined), and
- $Y_0^{\rm sec}$: the sector-prefactor normalization entering $c_{\rm sector}=Y_0^{\rm sec}/\sqrt{z_{\rm sector}}$.

In this appendix we fix
$$
Y_0^{\rm sec} \equiv g_U,
$$
so the lepton sector prefactor is
$$
c_\ell = \frac{Y_0^{\rm sec}}{\sqrt{z_\ell}} = \frac{g_U}{\sqrt{z_\ell}}, \qquad
z_\ell = \left(\tfrac{3}{4}\kappa_2^* + \tfrac{1}{4}\kappa_1^*\right)g_U^2
\approx 0.7205 \times 0.5236 = 0.3773,
$$
and therefore $c_\ell \approx 1.178$.

The leading-order Yukawa coupling at matching is therefore
$$
y_\tau^{(0)}(\mu_G) = \mathcal{N}_{\rm PU}\,c_\ell
= \frac{1}{72\sqrt{12}}\cdot\frac{g_U}{\sqrt{z_\ell}}
\approx 0.00401 \times 1.178 \approx 0.00472.
$$
In the 2-loop SM-running scheme defined in Lemma T.45.1a, the running factor is $\eta_\tau \approx 1.11$ (scheme-defined; do not over-interpret sub-percent digits without a full EFT threshold treatment), hence the leading-order absolute mass anchor is
$$
\boxed{
m_\tau^{(0)} = \frac{v_{\rm PU}}{\sqrt{2}}\,\eta_\tau\,y_\tau^{(0)}(\mu_G)
\approx 178.2 \times 1.113 \times 0.00472 \approx 0.94\ \text{GeV},
}
$$
a factor $\approx 1.9$ below the historical central input $m_\tau^{\rm obs}=1776.86\ \text{MeV}$ chosen from Workman et al. (2022, lepton summary, pp. 1–2) for this diagnostic, using $v_{\rm PU}=252\ \text{GeV}$ (Theorem T.6; Theorem T.29).

<a id="remark-t451-leading-order-normalization-gap"></a>**Remark T.45.1 (Leading-order normalization gap).** The leading absolute normalization misses the observed $\tau$ mass by an order-one factor. The displayed ratio values are conditional outputs of Theorem T.42.6 after its distance, coefficient, effective-dimension, and calibration entries are fixed; their common-prefactor cancellation does not supply the missing overlap or remainder certificates. Until both the absolute-normalization ledger and the ratio-model certificates close, neither layer is a parameter-free prediction.

<a id="lemma-t451a-two-loop-sm-rge-correction-to-absolute-lepton-masses"></a>**Lemma T.45.1a (Two-loop SM RGE correction to absolute lepton masses).** *Let $y_\tau(\mu_G)$ be the $\tau$ Yukawa coupling at the matching scale*
$$
\mu_G = M_{\rm Pl}e^{-\kappa_R}\approx 1.51\times 10^{15}\ \text{GeV}.
$$
*In this appendix we adopt the matching convention $\mu_G\equiv M_R$ (the seesaw threshold and Yukawa matching scale coincide), so the effective theory below $\mu_G$ is the SM. The leading-order PU framework estimate is*
$$
 y_\tau^{(0)}(\mu_G)=\mathcal{N}_{\rm PU}\,c_\ell
 =\frac{1}{72\sqrt{12}}\cdot\frac{g_U}{\sqrt{z_\ell}}\approx 0.00472,
$$
*with $\mathcal{N}_{\rm PU}=1/(72\sqrt{12})\approx 0.00401$ and $c_\ell=g_U/\sqrt{z_\ell}\approx 1.178$ (Section T.21.11; Corollary T.34.2; Theorem T.39a).* 

*Define the SM running factor*
$$
\eta_\tau := \frac{y_\tau(m_\tau)}{y_\tau(\mu_G)}.
$$
*Then the absolute lepton masses obey*
$$
\boxed{
 m_\tau = \frac{v_{\rm PU}}{\sqrt{2}}\,\eta_\tau\,y_\tau(\mu_G),\qquad
 m_\mu = m_\tau\,e^{-\ln(m_\tau/m_\mu)},\qquad
 m_e = m_\tau\,e^{-\ln(m_\tau/m_e)}.
}
$$
*Here Theorem T.42.6's zero-remainder model exponents are
$L_{\tau\mu}^{(0)}=2.8256725003\ldots$ and
$L_{\tau e}^{(0)}=8.2571100936\ldots$.  They become logarithmic physical mass
ratios only if Theorem T.39's full-matrix realization certificate is accepted;
$v_{\rm PU}=252\ \text{GeV}$ is itself branch-conditional under Theorems T.6
and T.29.*

*Proof.* **Step 1 (RGE setup).** Using GUT-normalized $g_1^2=\tfrac{5}{3}g_Y^2$, the two-loop $\overline{\rm MS}$ $\beta$ functions for the coupled set $\{g_1^2,g_2^2,g_3^2,y_t^2,\lambda,y_\tau^2\}$ are given in Buttazzo et al. (2013), Appendix B, eqs. (96)–(103) (with $y_b$ set to $0$ here). At one loop the $\tau$ Yukawa satisfies
$$
16\pi^2\,\frac{d y_\tau}{d\ln\mu}
= y_\tau\!\left[
3y_t^2 + \frac{5}{2}y_\tau^2 - \frac{9}{4}g_2^2 - \frac{9}{4}g_1^2
\right],
$$
and we include the full two-loop contributions in the numerical integration below. Neglecting $y_b$ and lighter Yukawas (numerically irrelevant for $\eta_\tau$ at the stated precision), the gauge part of the matching-scale boundary is
$g_i^2(\mu_G)=g_U^2/Z_i$ with $g_U^2=\pi/6$ (Theorem T.39a) and $Z_i=1+\Delta_i/24$ from the lifted spectral threshold data (Definition T.17a). The displayed external integration uses the external threshold tuple of Remark T.26.2, separately inserts $y_t(\mu_G)=0.392$, and uses the external SM trajectory input $\lambda_{\mathrm{SM}}(\mu_G)=0$. On the literal-spectrum, gauge-trivial-active-plane specialization of Definition T.17a, Proposition T.17a.5 excludes this threshold tuple from $T_0F$, so the computed $\eta_\tau$ and all masses using it remain diagnostics of that external run, not predictions of that specialization. The assignments of $y_t(\mu_G)$ and $\lambda_{\mathrm{SM}}(\mu_G)$ are not consequences of the threshold triplet alone; a predictive Higgs boundary would require the matching and criticality records of Definition T.25.2 and Theorem T.26.

**Step 2 (Two-loop integration with explicit electroweak matching).** The symmetric-phase SM RGEs are matched onto the low-energy effective description at an electroweak scale $\mu_{\rm EW}$ as a scheme choice: evolve with full SM RGEs for $\mu\in[\mu_G,\mu_{\rm EW}]$, and for $\mu<\mu_{\rm EW}$ decouple the top Yukawa by setting $y_t(\mu)=0$ in the $\beta$ functions while continuing to evolve $\{g_1^2,g_2^2,g_3^2,\lambda,y_\tau^2\}$ down to $\mu=m_\tau$.

For the displayed polynomial system, initial data and stipulated top-decoupling rule, numerical integration at the two declared matching scales gives
$$
\eta_\tau(\mu_{\rm EW}=173\ \text{GeV})=1.10960018\ldots,\qquad
\eta_\tau(\mu_{\rm EW}=252\ \text{GeV})=1.11625006\ldots .
$$
Their midpoint and half-range are
$$
\boxed{\eta_\tau=1.11292512\ldots\ \pm\ 0.00332494\ldots .}
$$
This half-range is the endpoint matching-scale variation of the stipulated scheme proxy, not a statistical uncertainty or a complete effective-field-theory threshold interval. Numerical changes under a $\pm5\%$ variation of the displayed $y_\tau(\mu_G)$ input are about $5\times10^{-6}$ at either endpoint. These are finite numerical diagnostics of the stated equations; they do not authenticate the imported $\beta$ functions or supply a rigorous interval enclosure.

**Supplemental note (reproducible two-loop integration code).** The following Python implements the *two-loop* SM RGE integration used in Step 2 (with $y_b$ neglected) and reproduces the quoted $\eta_\tau$ band. It integrates the equations in Buttazzo et al. (2013), Appendix B, eqs. (96)–(99), (101), (103), which are written as derivatives with respect to $\ln\bar\mu^2$, so the integration variable is $u=\ln\mu^2$.

~~~python
# Reproduce Lemma T.45.1a: eta_tau = y_tau(m_tau)/y_tau(mu_G)
#
# Two-loop SM RGEs in terms of g_i^2, y_t^2, lambda, y_tau^2:
#   Buttazzo et al. (2013), Appendix B, eqs. (96)–(99), (101), (103).
#
# Note: Buttazzo et al. write d/d ln(mu_bar^2); we therefore integrate in
#       u = ln(mu^2), so the beta functions can be used directly without
#       extra factors of 2.
#
# Requirements: numpy, scipy  (tested with solve_ivp + DOP853).
#
import math
import numpy as np
from scipy.integrate import solve_ivp

def betas_two_loop(u, X, yt_decouple=False):
    # State vector X = [g1sq, g2sq, g3sq, yt2, lam, ytau2]
    # where g1 is GUT-normalized: g1^2 = 5/3 g_Y^2.
    g1, g2, g3, yt2, lam, ytau2 = X
    yt2_eff = 0.0 if yt_decouple else yt2  # scheme: decouple top Yukawa below mu_EW

    fourpi = 4.0 * math.pi
    k1 = 1.0 / (fourpi**2)   # 1/(4π)^2
    k2 = 1.0 / (fourpi**4)   # 1/(4π)^4

    # --- Gauge couplings: eqs. (96)–(98), truncated at two loops; y_b set to 0.
    dg1 = (g1**2) * (k1 * (41.0/10.0)
                     + k2 * ((44.0/5.0)*g3 + (27.0/10.0)*g2 + (199.0/50.0)*g1
                             - (17.0/10.0)*yt2_eff - (3.0/2.0)*ytau2))

    dg2 = (g2**2) * (k1 * (-19.0/6.0)
                     + k2 * (12.0*g3 + (35.0/6.0)*g2 + (9.0/10.0)*g1
                             - (3.0/2.0)*yt2_eff - (1.0/2.0)*ytau2))

    dg3 = (g3**2) * (k1 * (-7.0)
                     + k2 * (-26.0*g3 + (9.0/2.0)*g2 + (11.0/10.0)*g1
                             - 2.0*yt2_eff))

    # --- Higgs quartic: eq. (99), truncated at two loops; y_b set to 0.
    beta_lam_1 = (
        lam*(12.0*lam + 6.0*yt2_eff + 2.0*ytau2 - (9.0/2.0)*g2 - (9.0/10.0)*g1)
        - 3.0*(yt2_eff**2) - (ytau2**2)
        + (9.0/16.0)*(g2**2) + (27.0/400.0)*(g1**2) + (9.0/40.0)*g2*g1
    )
    beta_lam_2 = (
        lam**2 * (-156.0*lam - 72.0*yt2_eff - 24.0*ytau2 + 54.0*g2 + (54.0/5.0)*g1)
        + lam*yt2_eff * (-(3.0/2.0)*yt2_eff + 40.0*g3 + (45.0/4.0)*g2 + (17.0/4.0)*g1)
        + lam*ytau2 * (-(1.0/2.0)*ytau2 + (15.0/4.0)*g2 + (15.0/4.0)*g1)
        + lam * (-(73.0/16.0)*(g2**2) + (1887.0/400.0)*(g1**2) + (117.0/40.0)*g2*g1)
        + (yt2_eff**2) * (15.0*yt2_eff - 16.0*g3 - (4.0/5.0)*g1)
        + yt2_eff * (-(9.0/8.0)*(g2**2) - (171.0/200.0)*(g1**2) + (63.0/20.0)*g2*g1)
        + (ytau2**2) * (5.0*ytau2 - (6.0/5.0)*g1)
        + ytau2 * (-(3.0/8.0)*(g2**2) - (9.0/8.0)*(g1**2) + (33.0/20.0)*g2*g1)
        + (305.0/32.0)*(g2**3) - (3411.0/4000.0)*(g1**3)
        - (289.0/160.0)*(g2**2)*g1 - (1677.0/800.0)*g2*(g1**2)
    )
    dlam = k1*beta_lam_1 + k2*beta_lam_2

    # --- Top Yukawa: eq. (101), truncated at two loops; y_b set to 0.
    if yt_decouple:
        dyt2 = 0.0
    else:
        beta_yt2_1 = yt2 * ((9.0/2.0)*yt2 + ytau2 - 8.0*g3 - (9.0/4.0)*g2 - (17.0/20.0)*g1)
        beta_yt2_2 = yt2 * (
            yt2 * (-12.0*yt2 - (9.0/4.0)*ytau2 - 12.0*lam + 36.0*g3 + (225.0/16.0)*g2 + (393.0/80.0)*g1)
            + ytau2 * (-(9.0/4.0)*ytau2 + (15.0/8.0)*g2 + (15.0/8.0)*g1)
            + 6.0*lam**2 - 108.0*(g3**2) - (23.0/4.0)*(g2**2) + (1187.0/600.0)*(g1**2)
            + 9.0*g3*g2 + (19.0/15.0)*g3*g1 - (9.0/20.0)*g2*g1
        )
        dyt2 = k1*beta_yt2_1 + k2*beta_yt2_2

    # --- Tau Yukawa: eq. (103), truncated at two loops; y_b set to 0.
    beta_ytau2_1 = ytau2 * (3.0*yt2_eff + (5.0/2.0)*ytau2 - (9.0/4.0)*g2 - (9.0/4.0)*g1)
    beta_ytau2_2 = ytau2 * (
        6.0*lam**2 - (23.0/4.0)*(g2**2) + (1371.0/200.0)*(g1**2) + (27.0/20.0)*g2*g1
        + yt2_eff * (-(27.0/4.0)*yt2_eff - (27.0/4.0)*ytau2 + 20.0*g3 + (45.0/8.0)*g2 + (17.0/8.0)*g1)
        + ytau2 * (-3.0*ytau2 - 12.0*lam + (165.0/16.0)*g2 + (537.0/80.0)*g1)
    )
    dytau2 = k1*beta_ytau2_1 + k2*beta_ytau2_2

    return np.array([dg1, dg2, dg3, dyt2, dlam, dytau2], dtype=float)

def integrate_eta(mu_G, mu_EW, mu_low, gU2, Z, yt_G, lam_G, ytau_G):
    # initial conditions at mu_G
    g1_G = gU2 / Z[0]
    g2_G = gU2 / Z[1]
    g3_G = gU2 / Z[2]
    yt2_G = yt_G**2
    ytau2_G = ytau_G**2
    X0 = np.array([g1_G, g2_G, g3_G, yt2_G, lam_G, ytau2_G], dtype=float)

    u_G = math.log(mu_G**2)
    u_EW = math.log(mu_EW**2)
    u_low = math.log(mu_low**2)

    # Stage 1: full SM running from mu_G -> mu_EW
    sol1 = solve_ivp(lambda u, X: betas_two_loop(u, X, yt_decouple=False),
                     t_span=(u_G, u_EW), y0=X0, method="DOP853",
                     rtol=1e-9, atol=1e-12)
    if not sol1.success:
        raise RuntimeError(sol1.message)

    X_EW = sol1.y[:, -1].copy()

    # Stage 2: below mu_EW, decouple top Yukawa in the beta functions (scheme choice)
    X_EW[3] = 0.0  # set y_t^2 = 0 below mu_EW
    sol2 = solve_ivp(lambda u, X: betas_two_loop(u, X, yt_decouple=True),
                     t_span=(u_EW, u_low), y0=X_EW, method="DOP853",
                     rtol=1e-9, atol=1e-12)
    if not sol2.success:
        raise RuntimeError(sol2.message)

    ytau2_low = sol2.y[5, -1]
    eta_tau = math.sqrt(ytau2_low / ytau2_G)
    return eta_tau

def trunc(x, ndp=5):
    # Truncate (not round) to ndp decimal places (used for matching the lemma's quoted digits).
    s = 10.0**ndp
    return math.floor(x * s) / s

if __name__ == "__main__":
    mu_G = 1.51e15      # GeV
    m_tau = 1.77686     # GeV; chosen PDG 2022 central input for this diagnostic
    gU2 = math.pi/6.0
    # External tuple excluded from the literal-spectrum, gauge-trivial-A T0 specialization (Proposition T.17a.5).
    # Outputs below diagnose this external run; they are not predictions of that specialization.
    Z = (1 + 15.14/24.0, 1 + 20.94/24.0, 1 + 18.41/24.0)
    yt_G = 0.392
    lam_G = 0.0

    # A +/-5% variation about ytau_G=0.00896 changes eta_tau by about 5e-6 at the two matching-scale endpoints.
    ytau_G = 0.00896

    for mu_EW in (173.0, 252.0):
        eta = integrate_eta(mu_G, mu_EW, m_tau, gU2, Z, yt_G, lam_G, ytau_G)
        print(f"mu_EW = {mu_EW:7.1f} GeV  ->  eta_tau = {eta:.8f}  (rounded: {eta:.5f}, truncated: {trunc(eta):.5f})")

    eta173 = integrate_eta(mu_G, 173.0, m_tau, gU2, Z, yt_G, lam_G, ytau_G)
    eta252 = integrate_eta(mu_G, 252.0, m_tau, gU2, Z, yt_G, lam_G, ytau_G)
    eta_mid = 0.5*(eta173 + eta252)
    eta_half_range = 0.5*abs(eta252 - eta173)
    print(f"eta_tau(mid) = {eta_mid:.7f} ; half-range = {eta_half_range:.7f}")
~~~
A common $\mathcal{O}(1)$ threshold shift $\delta$ in standard unification-threshold notation, entering
$\alpha_i^{-1}(\mu_G)=Z_i\alpha_U^{-1}+\delta/(2\pi)$,
changes $\eta_\tau$ at the $\sim 10^{-4}$–$10^{-3}$ level (depending on sign/magnitude). This is subdominant to the $\mu_{\rm EW}$ matching band above, but should not be quoted more sharply without a full threshold analysis.

**Step 3 (Self-consistent extraction of $y_\tau(\mu_G)$).** For this calibration calculation, use the Particle Data Group (2022) central input $m_\tau^{\rm obs}=1776.86\ \text{MeV}$. The matching-scale Yukawa is then defined by inversion:
$$
 y_\tau(\mu_G)
 =\frac{m_\tau^{\rm obs}\sqrt{2}}{v_{\rm PU}\,\eta_\tau}
 =\frac{1776.86\times 10^{-3}\times\sqrt{2}}{252\times 1.1129251204\ldots}
 =0.00896\pm 0.00003,
$$
which *defines* the self-consistent $y_\tau(\mu_G)$ required to match $m_\tau^{\rm obs}$ for a given $(v_{\rm PU},\eta_\tau)$.

**Step 4 (Tau-anchored zero-remainder model candidates).** Theorem T.42.6
supplies model exponents, not physical mass ratios.  For the empirical-anchor
diagnostic obtained by setting both registered remainders to zero and anchoring
at $m_\tau^{\rm obs}=1776.86\,\mathrm{MeV}$, define
$$
m_\mu^{\rm model}:=m_\tau^{\rm obs}e^{-L_{\tau\mu}^{(0)}},
\qquad
m_e^{\rm model}:=m_\tau^{\rm obs}e^{-L_{\tau e}^{(0)}}.
$$
Direct evaluation gives
$$
m_\mu^{\rm model}=105.3123336\ldots\,\mathrm{MeV},
\qquad
m_e^{\rm model}=0.4609309395\ldots\,\mathrm{MeV}.\quad\square
$$

<a id="definition-t451b-absolute-lepton-normalization-correction-ledger"></a>**Definition T.45.1b (Absolute Lepton-Normalization Correction Ledger).** An absolute lepton-normalization correction ledger is a finite record
$$
\mathfrak N_\ell
=
(\Delta_{\mathrm{thr}},\Delta_{\mathrm{VVM}}^{\mathrm{abs}},\Delta_{\mathrm{aniso}},I_\ell,\chi_\ell,
\mathfrak C_{Y\to m})
\tag{T.45.1b.1}
$$
registered at the matching scale $\mu_G$, with $\Delta_{\mathrm{thr}}$, $\Delta_{\mathrm{VVM}}^{\mathrm{abs}}$, and $\Delta_{\mathrm{aniso}}$ finite and strictly positive, where:

1. $\Delta_{\mathrm{thr}}$ is the finite threshold-matching factor for the $\tau$ Yukawa normalization on the same SM running convention used in Lemma T.45.1a.
2. $\Delta_{\mathrm{VVM}}^{\mathrm{abs}}$ is the absolute-normalization Van Vleck-Morette determinant factor computed from a specified Bures heat-kernel or Jacobi-field determinant on the same $\mathrm{Gr}(2,8)$ branch as Theorem T.42.6, including the geodesic endpoints, determinant convention, and retained effective dimension.
3. $\Delta_{\mathrm{aniso}}$ is the finite PCE-anisotropy factor relating the isotropic normalization $1/(72\sqrt{12})$ to the retained lepton-sector block.
4. $I_\ell=[L_\ell^-,L_\ell^+]$ is a certified residual interval for omitted higher-order matching and curvature terms in logarithmic units.
5. $\chi_\ell=1$ records that no entry of the ledger is selected using $m_\tau$, $m_\mu$, or $m_e$.
6. $\mathfrak C_{Y\to m}$ is the accepted Theorem-T.39 certificate for the same normalization, matching scale, complex matrix assembly, diagonalization, ordered singular values, lepton labels, and residual intervals used by this ledger. Its $\tau$ interval must agree with $I_\ell$ under the declared matching map.

Write
$$
\Delta_\ell
:=
\Delta_{\mathrm{thr}}\Delta_{\mathrm{VVM}}^{\mathrm{abs}}\Delta_{\mathrm{aniso}}.
\tag{T.45.1b.2}
$$
A scalar Van Vleck-Morette multiplier is admissible in the absolute mass anchor only as the entry $\Delta_{\mathrm{VVM}}^{\mathrm{abs}}$ of such a ledger; the geodesic angle, retained dimension, and full determinant convention are part of the datum.

<a id="theorem-t451c-certificate-gated-absolute-charged-lepton-intervals"></a>**Theorem T.45.1c (Certificate-Gated Absolute Charged-Lepton Intervals).** If every entry of $\mathfrak N_\ell$, including $\mathfrak C_{Y\to m}$, is accepted, then the forward absolute charged-lepton anchor is
$$
y_{\tau,\mathrm{abs}}(\mu_G)
=
\mathcal N_{\rm PU}c_\ell\Delta_\ell,
\qquad
\mathcal N_{\rm PU}=\frac{1}{72\sqrt{12}},
\tag{T.45.1c.1}
$$
and the corresponding forward interval is
$$
\log m_\tau^{\mathrm{abs}}
\in
\log\left(\frac{v_{\rm PU}}{\sqrt2}\eta_\tau\mathcal N_{\rm PU}c_\ell\Delta_\ell\right)
+
[L_\ell^-,L_\ell^+].
\tag{T.45.1c.2}
$$
The muon and electron absolute intervals are obtained by interval subtraction using the residual-bearing exponents accepted inside the same $\mathfrak C_{Y\to m}$. If that full certificate is absent, (T.45.1c.1)--(T.45.1c.2) define only an absolute model-anchor interval; the displayed leading value $m_\tau^{(0)}\approx0.94\,\mathrm{GeV}$ and the corresponding muon/electron values are not physical mass intervals.

*Proof.* The scalar entries fix the multiplicative normalization and give (T.45.1c.1). The matching relation and $I_\ell$ give the model interval (T.45.1c.2). The accepted $\mathfrak C_{Y\to m}$ separately verifies that this normalization belongs to the same complex sector matrix, matching convention, ordered singular values, and labels, and that its residual intervals contain the $\tau$, muon, and electron logarithms. Only that conjunction promotes the model interval to physical mass intervals. If any scalar entry or the full-matrix certificate is absent, the corresponding promotion does not follow. ∎

1. The Leech lattice connection via $\sqrt{2}E_8$ and the Golay code aligns with the $M = 24$ interface mode structure.

# Part VI: Flavor Mixing

# Section T.22: CKM Matrix from $E_8$ Grassmannian Geometry

## T.22.1 Conditional CKM-Model Status

The CKM construction is a geometric flavor model whose triads, packet widths, sector weights, holonomies, threshold maps, phases, and remainder intervals must be specified before a forward comparison. Unitarity identities and arithmetic evaluation are exact after those inputs are supplied. A complete derivation of the observed matrix requires the flavor certificate of Theorem T.79, which remains open.

The Cabibbo-Kobayashi-Maskawa (CKM) matrix parametrizes quark flavor mixing in the Standard Model, encoding the mismatch between mass and weak interaction eigenstates (Cabibbo 1963; Kobayashi and Maskawa 1973). Its elements exhibit a striking hierarchical pattern: diagonal elements near unity, off-diagonal elements suppressed by powers of the Cabibbo angle $\lambda\approx 0.22$. This section computes the CKM matrix elements within the branch-qualified $E_8$ Grassmannian model of Section T.21, completing **Problem T.3** at the model layer.

The derivation proceeds through a unified framework with two limiting regimes:

1. **Heavy-generation mixing** ($3\leftrightarrow 1$, $3\leftrightarrow 2$): Gaussian overlap suppression on the generation manifold $\mathrm{Gr}(2,8)$
1. **Light-generation mixing** ($1\leftrightarrow 2$): Geometric frustration between incompatible lattice symmetries

The model uses the following prior branch entries:

- hierarchy coefficient $\alpha=3/2$ on the packet-width and Schur-normalization branch of Corollary T.41.3;
- registered $E_8$ triad distances from Section T.21.9.1;
- $N_g=3$ from the anomaly/CP minimality class of Theorem R.3.4 together with the additive-monotone selection branch of Proposition R.3.5.1a; and
- independently registered sector stiffness ratio $\kappa_d/\kappa_u=1.02$; Theorem T.38 determines a distinct prefactor ratio and does not derive this stiffness input.

Proposition R.4.2 records the triality/$E_8$/Leech compatibility of this family count.

## T.22.2 $E_8$ Triad Structure

### T.22.2.1 Root System Properties

The $E_8$ root system in $\mathbb{R}^8$ consists of 240 vectors with $\lVert r\rVert^{2}=2$. For any two roots $r_1,r_2$, the squared distance satisfies:

$$d^2 = ||r_1 - r_2||^2 = ||r_1||^2 + ||r_2||^2 - 2\langle r_1, r_2 \rangle = 4 - 2\langle r_1, r_2 \rangle$$

The allowed values are $d^{2}\in\{0,2,4,6,8\}$, corresponding to inner products $\langle r_1,r_2\rangle\in\{2,1,0,-1,-2\}$.

### T.22.2.2 Generation Triads

From Section T.21.9.1, the three fermion generations are represented by $E_8$ root triads with the following squared distances:

**Down-type quarks (d, s, b):**

|Pair|$d^{2}$ |Inner Product|Lattice Angle|
|:---|:-:|:-----------:|:-----------:|
|3↔2 |2 |+1 |60° |
|3↔1 |4 |0 |90° |
|2↔1 |6 |−1 |120° |

**Up-type quarks (u, c, t):**

|Pair|$d^{2}$ |Inner Product|Lattice Angle|
|:---|:-:|:-----------:|:-----------:|
|3↔2 |4 |0 |90° |
|3↔1 |8 |−2 |180° |
|2↔1 |4 |0 |90° |

These assignments yield hierarchy ratios $R=d^{2}_{31}/d^{2}_{32}$ consistent with observed mass hierarchies (Theorem T.37).

### T.22.2.3 Lattice Angles

<a id="lemma-t44a"></a>**Lemma T.44a** ($E_8$ Lattice Angles). *For two $E_8$ roots of squared norm $2$ and squared separation $d^2$, their angle $\theta$ satisfies*
$$
\cos\theta=\frac{4-d^2}{4}.
$$
*The registered up-sector pair with $d^2=4$ has angle $90^\circ$, and the down-sector pair with $d^2=6$ has angle $120^\circ$. Their rank-two reflection subsystems are $A_1\oplus A_1$ and $A_2$, respectively; a rank-four $D_4$ carrier is additional embedding data.*

*Proof.* The distance identity gives
$$
d^2=4-2\langle r_1,r_2\rangle,
\qquad
\cos\theta=\frac{\langle r_1,r_2\rangle}{2}
=\frac{4-d^2}{4}.
$$
For $d^2=4$, the roots are orthogonal. Reflections in them change their signs independently, so the generated roots are $\{\pm r_1,\pm r_2\}$, of type $A_1\oplus A_1$. For $d^2=6$, their inner product is $-1$, and the reflection formula
$$
s_{r_i}(v)=v-\langle v,r_i\rangle r_i
$$
gives the six-root subsystem
$$
\{\pm r_1,\pm r_2,\pm(r_1+r_2)\},
$$
of type $A_2$. Substitution in the angle formula gives $90^\circ$ and $120^\circ$. These pairwise results do not select a $D_4$ embedding or a physical mixing response. ∎

## T.22.3 Unified Framework for Flavor Mixing

### T.22.3.1 The Master Formula

<a id="theorem-t45"></a>**Theorem T.45** (Unified Mixing Kernel and Physical-Realization Gate). Fix a selected pair of generation labels $(i,j)$ carrying the finite embedding certificate $\mathfrak C_{B/E_8}$ of Lemma T.41.4. Let $q_{ij}=d_{E_8}(r_i,r_j)^2$, let $\mathcal P_{ij}\ge0$ be a registered geometric-response coefficient, and let $\Theta_{ij}$ be a registered orientation angle. Define the model kernel
$$
K_{ij}
:=
\mathcal P_{ij}\exp(-\alpha q_{ij})
\left|\sin\frac{\Theta_{ij}}2\right|,
\qquad
\alpha:=\frac{1}{16\sigma_B^2}.
\tag{T.45.1}
$$
On the unit-radius convention $\sigma_B^2=1/24$, one has $\alpha=3/2$. Equation (T.45.1) is a nonnegative response kernel; it is not, by itself, a CKM matrix element.

A finite unitary-realization witness requires a mixing certificate
$$
\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{mix}}
=
\bigl(M_u,M_d,U_u,U_d,W,b,\{K_{ij}^{(b_{ij})}\},
\varepsilon_U,\eta^{\max},\mathcal I\bigr),
\tag{T.45.2}
$$
where all objects are recorded at the same scale and in the same renormalization scheme, and the verifier checks:

1. $U_f^\dagger U_f=I_3$ and $U_f^\dagger M_fM_f^\dagger U_f$ equals the certified diagonal matrix of ordered squared singular values for $f\in\{u,d\}$, with outward-rounded residuals; the relevant singular values are pairwise distinct, or the certificate replaces entrywise claims inside a degenerate subspace by explicitly invariant subspace claims;
2. $W=U_u^\dagger U_d$, $\varepsilon_U\ge0$, and
   $\|W^\dagger W-I_3\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\varepsilon_U$;
3. the preregistered provenance map $b:(i,j)\mapsto b_{ij}$ names exactly
   one source branch for each modeled entry, records that branch's premise
   hash, and verifies that all selected branches use one family count, scale,
   scheme, row/column labeling, and phase convention; incompatible
   common-reference, sector-local, down-only, and two-channel prescriptions
   cannot be combined silently;
4. each modeled entry has a preregistered maximum tolerance
   $\eta_{ij}^{\max}$ and an outward-rounded interval $\mathcal I_{ij}$ for
   which the verifier proves
   $$
   |W_{ij}|,K_{ij}^{(b_{ij})}\in\mathcal I_{ij},
   \qquad
   \operatorname{diam}(\mathcal I_{ij})\le\eta_{ij}^{\max},
   \qquad
   \operatorname{dist}(|W_{ij}|,K_{ij}^{(b_{ij})})
   \le\eta_{ij}^{\max};
   $$
   an interval wider than its preregistered tolerance is rejected rather
   than used to certify unrelated values; and
5. $M_u,M_d$, the labels, provenance map, response data, tolerances, and
   every error interval were fixed independently of the CKM comparison.

If the certificate is accepted with $\varepsilon_U=0$ and singleton intervals,
then $|W_{ij}|=K_{ij}^{(b_{ij})}$ for the certified entries. With nonzero
intervals it yields only the corresponding interval statement.  The witness
must occur as the same CKM subrecord inside one accepted structurally independent global
flavor certificate $\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{fl}}$ of Definition T.79.4, accepted
by Algorithm T.79.5, before $W$ is promoted to the physical CKM matrix.
Without that global certificate, $K_{ij}^{(b_{ij})}$ and $W$ remain a model
kernel and a finite unitary-realization witness.

*Proof.* Lemma T.41.4 gives $d_{g_B}^2=q_{ij}/8$ exactly for the certified pair, so the intrinsic Gaussian probability-overlap exponent $d_{g_B}^2/(2\sigma_B^2)$ equals $q_{ij}/(16\sigma_B^2)$. The chordal distance $D_B$ is not used in this heat/Gaussian kernel. Multiplication by the two registered response factors proves (T.45.1). Item 1 verifies unitary left singular bases and removes basis ambiguity for distinct singular values; item 2 then constructs their relative unitary matrix. Items 3--5 make provenance, compatibility, and entrywise residuals finite acceptance tests. Definition T.79.4 and Algorithm T.79.5 supply the separate structural-independence, source-exhaustion, and cross-sector requirements needed for physical promotion. ∎

## T.22.4 Heavy-Generation Mixing: Tunneling Regime

### T.22.4.1 Mixing Amplitude Formula

<a id="theorem-t46-conditional-heavy-generation-sector-amplitudes"></a>**Theorem T.46 (Conditional Heavy-Generation Sector Amplitudes).** Assume the additive-monotone family-count branch of Proposition R.3.5.1a, the registered sector distances, the independently declared nonnegative response-weight convention

the Gaussian-overlap response branch with coefficient $\alpha$, and the common-reference prescription

=
\min(d_{3j,d}^2,d_{3j,u}^2).

and linearity gives

K^{\mathrm{mix}}_{3j}

Bures--$E_8$ certificates give the common exponential response at
$d_{\mathrm{ref}}^2$. Their product is the displayed sector magnitude.
Equation (T.46.1) and linearity give the coherent sum.

Under the common-reference prescription, the two retained sector amplitudes have identical exponential factors, so their exponential-factor ratio is $1$. ### T.22.4.2 Calculation of $\vert V_{cb}\vert$

<a id="theorem-t47"></a>**Theorem T.47** (Down-Only Heavy-Generation Model Kernel). Assume independently a down-only realization $T=T_d$, the selected-family value $N_g=3$, the registered down-sector distance $d_{32,d}^2=2$, the geometric-prefactor rule $\mathcal P_{32,d}=\sqrt{d_{32,d}^2/N_g}$, and the unit-radius Gaussian branch $\alpha=3/2$. *Proof.*

- $d^{2}_{32,u}=4$ (up-sector distance)

**Step 3 (Exponential suppression).**
$$e^{-\alpha d^2_{\mathrm{ref}}} = e^{-(3/2)(2)} = e^{-3} = 0.04979$$

**Step 4 (Model evaluation).**
$$
K_{cb}^{(d)}=0.81649658\ldots\times0.04978707\ldots
=0.0406509711\ldots .
$$
The PDG comparison is an empirical diagnostic of this down-only kernel. It becomes a CKM prediction only if one common-scale $\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{mix}}$ verifies the complete up/down mass matrices, their diagonalizers, unitarity, labels, and simultaneous entry intervals. ∎

### T.22.4.3 Calculation of $\vert V_{ub}\vert$

<a id="theorem-t48"></a>**Theorem T.48** (Two-Channel $K_{ub}$ Model on the Declared Interference-Phase Branch). Assume all hypotheses of Theorem T.46 for $j=1$ and independently register $\phi_u-\phi_d=\pi-\delta$. Then the two-channel model kernel satisfies

*where the sector amplitudes at common reference are:*
$$A_d = \sqrt{\frac{d^2_{31,d}}{N_g}} \times e^{-\alpha d^2_{\mathrm{ref}}} = \sqrt{\frac{4}{3}} \times e^{-6} = 0.00286$$
$$A_u = \sqrt{\frac{d^2_{31,u}}{N_g}} \times e^{-\alpha d^2_{\mathrm{ref}}} = \sqrt{\frac{8}{3}} \times e^{-6} = 0.00405$$

*Proof.*

**Steps 1--2 (Optional geometric realization obligation).**  A geometric

$$

$$
The existence or value of those data does not follow from the two distances.
The present theorem therefore uses only the independent interference-phase
hypothesis in Step 3; these geometric data are a separate promotion gate.

**Step 3 (Independent interference-phase hypothesis).** The half-surface relation would give $\Delta\gamma=\delta/2$ under the stated geometric partition; it does not imply $\pi-\delta$. The numerical branch therefore adopts $\phi_u-\phi_d=\pi-\delta$ as a separate interference-phase hypothesis.

**Step 4 (Interference formula).** The total amplitude is:
$$
K_{ub}^{\mathrm{mix}}
=A_d+A_ue^{i(\pi-\delta)}
=A_d-A_ue^{-i\delta}.
$$
Taking the modulus squared gives the theorem's interference identity. A CKM symbol is introduced only after $\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{mix}}$ is accepted.

**Step 5 (Numerical evaluation on the registered conventional-response branch).** Apply Theorem T.56's response map to Convention T.54's assigned lift:
$$

=66.6753023736826\ldots^\circ.

Using the unrounded amplitudes
$$

\qquad
A_u=\sqrt{8/3}\,e^{-6}=0.004047785354430481\ldots,

gives
$$
2A_dA_u\cos\delta^{\mathrm{conv}}
=9.174466622441\ldots\times10^{-6},
$$
$$
|K_{ub}^{\mathrm{mix}}|^2
=1.54023827908721\ldots\times10^{-5},

## T.22.5 Light-Generation Mixing: Frustration Regime

### T.22.5.1 The Geometric Frustration Mechanism

The corresponding heavy-channel response evaluated at $d^2=4$ is a model
kernel of order $e^{-6}$.  Its numerical difference from the empirical
$|V_{us}|$ motivates the separate light-generation
frustration-response model below.

<a id="theorem-t49"></a>**Theorem T.49** (Quadratic Frustration-Model Minimizer).  Work on the
unwrapped convex angular chart
$$
I:=\left[\frac\pi2,\frac{2\pi}3\right]\subset\mathbb R,
$$
with $\theta_u:=\pi/2$, $\theta_d:=2\pi/3$, and independently registered
stiffnesses $\kappa_u,\kappa_d>0$ in one common energy-per-radian-squared
normalization.  Define
$$
V_{\mathrm{fr}}(\theta)
:=\frac{\kappa_u}{2}(\theta-\theta_u)^2
+\frac{\kappa_d}{2}(\theta-\theta_d)^2.
\tag{T.49.1}
$$
Then $V_{\mathrm{fr}}$ has the unique global minimizer on $I$
$$
\theta_{\mathrm{vac}}
=\frac{\kappa_u\theta_u+\kappa_d\theta_d}
{\kappa_u+\kappa_d}.
\tag{T.49.2}
$$
On the independently registered branch $\kappa_d/\kappa_u=1.02=51/50$,
$$
\theta_{\mathrm{vac}}=\frac{59\pi}{101}
=105.148514851485\ldots^\circ.
\tag{T.49.3}
$$

*Proof.* Differentiating (T.49.1) gives
$V_{\mathrm{fr}}'(\theta)=\kappa_u(\theta-\theta_u)
+\kappa_d(\theta-\theta_d)$ and
$V_{\mathrm{fr}}''=\kappa_u+\kappa_d>0$.  Thus the stationary point
(T.49.2) is the unique global minimizer on the convex chart; positivity of
the weights places it between the two endpoints.  Substitution of $51/50$
gives (T.49.3).  Theorem T.38 separately gives
$c_d/c_u=1.024667673462575\ldots$ on its stated branch; it supplies no stiffness
law and does not imply $\kappa_d/\kappa_u=1.02$.  Equations (T.49.1)--(T.49.3)
are a stipulated model optimization, not a physical vacuum theorem. ∎

### T.22.5.3 The A₂ Projection Factor

The scalar-response hypothesis formalized in Theorem T.51 projects the
registered mismatch into an $A_2$ root--weight model.

<a id="theorem-t51"></a>**Theorem T.51** (Conditional Root-to-Weight Projection in $A_2$). *Assume that the retained mismatch response is directed along an $A_2$ root and that the physical mixing response is its Euclidean scalar component along the nearest weight direction in the union of the fundamental and antifundamental weight orbits. Then*

$$
\mathcal P
=
\cos(30^\circ)
=
\frac{\sqrt3}{2}.
$$

*Proof.* Choose normalized simple roots
$$
\alpha_1=\sqrt2(1,0),
\qquad
\alpha_2=\sqrt2\left(-\frac12,\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\right).
$$
They satisfy
$$
\lVert\alpha_1\rVert^2
=
\lVert\alpha_2\rVert^2
=
2,
\qquad
\alpha_1\cdot\alpha_2=-1.
$$
The fundamental weights are determined by
$$
\frac{2\langle\omega_i,\alpha_j\rangle}
{\langle\alpha_j,\alpha_j\rangle}
=
\delta_{ij},
$$
which gives
$$
\omega_1
=
\left(\frac1{\sqrt2},\frac1{\sqrt6}\right),
\qquad
\omega_2
=
\left(0,\sqrt{\frac23}\right).
$$
Thus $\omega_1$ and $\omega_2$ have directions $30^\circ$ and $90^\circ$. Their Weyl orbits, equivalently the union of the weight sets of $\mathbf3$ and $\overline{\mathbf3}$, have directions
$$
30^\circ,\ 90^\circ,\ 150^\circ,\ 210^\circ,\ 270^\circ,\ 330^\circ.
$$
The six roots have directions
$$
0^\circ,\ 60^\circ,\ 120^\circ,\ 180^\circ,\ 240^\circ,\ 300^\circ.
$$
Hence every root direction is separated from either nearest weight direction by $30^\circ$. Under the scalar-projection response hypothesis, the component of a unit root-direction response along the nearest weight direction is therefore
$$
\cos(30^\circ)=\frac{\sqrt3}{2}.
$$
The angular factor is determined after the scalar-projection response hypothesis is imposed; $A_2$ duality alone does not select that physical response rule. ∎

## T.22.6 CP Violation from Berry Holonomy

### T.22.6.1 Berry Connection on Gr(2,8)

<a id="lemma-t531"></a>**Lemma T.53.1** (Berry Connection on the Positive Determinant Line). *Let
$\mathcal S\to\operatorname{Gr}(2,8)$ be the tautological rank-two bundle and
fix, before any phase comparison, the positive Berry line*
$$
\mathcal L_+:=\det(\mathcal S)^*.
$$
*On a standard graph chart write $Z\in\operatorname{Hom}(\mathbb C^2,\mathbb C^6)$,
$h:=I_2+Z^\dagger Z$, and $K:=\log\det h$.  In the unitary frame induced from
the local holomorphic frame of $\mathcal L_+$, the real connection one-form is*
$$
\boxed{
\mathcal A
=\frac{i}{2}(\bar\partial K-\partial K)
=\frac{i}{2}\operatorname{Tr}\!\left[
h^{-1}(dZ^\dagger Z-Z^\dagger dZ)
\right].
}
\tag{T.53.1a}
$$
*Use the forward covariant derivative $D=d-i\mathcal A$ on components in a unitary frame $u_+$. Under $u_+'=e^{i\vartheta}u_+$, the component of a section changes by $f'=e^{-i\vartheta}f$ and*
$$
\mathcal A'=\mathcal A-d\vartheta.
$$
*Parallel transport therefore has holonomy $\exp(i\oint_\gamma\mathcal A)$, which is gauge invariant for every closed loop.*

*Proof.* Jacobi's identity gives
$$
\partial K=\operatorname{Tr}(h^{-1}Z^\dagger dZ),
\qquad
\bar\partial K=\operatorname{Tr}(h^{-1}dZ^\dagger Z),
$$
which proves (T.53.1a). The holomorphic frame $e_+$ of the dual determinant line has squared norm $e^{-K}$ and Chern connection form $-\partial K$. Its unitary frame $u_+=e^{K/2}e_+$ has connection form
$$
-\partial K+\frac12dK
=\frac12(\bar\partial K-\partial K)
=-i\mathcal A.
$$
The frame change adds $i\,d\vartheta$ to this form, yielding the displayed transformation of $\mathcal A$. The horizontal component equation $df-i\mathcal A f=0$ gives the stated forward holonomy. A closed-loop gauge change shifts the integral by an integer multiple of $2\pi$. Near $Z=0$,
$$
\mathcal A
=\frac{i}{2}\operatorname{Tr}(dZ^\dagger Z-Z^\dagger dZ)
+O(\lVert Z\rVert^3).
$$
Thus the linear expression is only the chart-origin expansion, not a global connection formula. ∎

<a id="lemma-t532"></a>**Lemma T.53.2** (Berry Curvature on $\operatorname{Gr}(2,8)$). *For the fixed
line $\mathcal L_+$ and connection of Lemma T.53.1,*
$$
\boxed{
\mathcal F:=d\mathcal A
=i\partial\bar\partial\log\det(I_2+Z^\dagger Z)
=-i\operatorname{Tr}\!\left[
h^{-1}dZ^\dagger\wedge(I_6+ZZ^\dagger)^{-1}dZ
\right]
=:\omega_{\mathrm{KE}}.
}
\tag{T.53.2a}
$$
*The last equality fixes the normalization of $\omega_{\mathrm{KE}}$ used in
the flavor-holonomy branch.  The tautological determinant line
$\det(\mathcal S)$ has the opposite curvature.*

*Proof.* Since $\partial^2=\bar\partial^2=0$ and
$\bar\partial\partial=-\partial\bar\partial$,
$$
d\mathcal A=i\partial\bar\partial K.
$$
Differentiating $h^{-1}$ and using the Woodbury identity gives the middle
matrix formula in (T.53.2a).  At the chart origin it reduces to
$$
\mathcal F
=i\sum_{\alpha,\beta}
dz_{\alpha\beta}\wedge d\bar z_{\alpha\beta}
+O(\lVert Z\rVert^2),
$$
which also checks the sign.  Dualizing a Hermitian line reverses its Chern
curvature, so the positive and negative determinant lines cannot be exchanged
after the phase convention is fixed. ∎

The conventional number becomes a geometric theorem only if the independently computed output of Theorem T.54b proves $A_\gamma=\delta_{\mathrm{flat}}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ in the registered lift; nonzero CP requires its certified interval to be disjoint from $\pi\mathbb Z$ modulo $2\pi$. ∎

<a id="definition-t54a"></a>**Definition T.54a** (Grassmannian Gauss-Bonnet CP-Area Certificate). A Grassmannian Gauss-Bonnet CP-area certificate for the loop $\gamma=(u_3,d_3,d_2,u_2,u_3)$ is a finite record
$$
\mathfrak G_{\mathrm{CP}}
=
(\Sigma_\gamma,g_\Sigma,q_\Sigma,\{\alpha_j\}_{j=1}^4,K_\Sigma,
\mathfrak N_\gamma),
\tag{T.54a.1}
$$
where the finite numerical ledger is
$$
\mathfrak N_\gamma
:=(I_A,I_{GB},E_A,E_{GB},
\varepsilon_A,\varepsilon_{GB},\mathcal M_A,\mathcal M_{GB},I_{\mathrm{lift}}).
\tag{T.54a.1a}
$$
Here $I_A$ and $I_{GB}$ are outward-rounded intervals for the Kähler area and
Gauss--Bonnet residual, $E_A$ and $E_{GB}$ are separately proved total
quadrature-and-truncation error bounds, $\varepsilon_A$ and
$\varepsilon_{GB}$ are preregistered tolerances, $\mathcal M_A$ and
$\mathcal M_{GB}$ specify the terminating quadrature or exact symbolic methods,
and $I_{\mathrm{lift}}$ is either a preregistered
interval of length less than $2\pi$ or the marker $\varnothing$ when only a
phase class is claimed.
The geometric entries satisfy:

1. $\Sigma_\gamma$ is an oriented piecewise-geodesic two-surface in $\mathrm{Gr}(2,8)$ with $\partial\Sigma_\gamma=\gamma$;

2. $g_\Sigma$ is induced from the Lemma-T.53.2 Kähler--Einstein
normalization.  If the calculation is performed with the Bures metric, the
ledger records the conversion $g_{\mathrm{KE}}=4g_B$ and the corresponding
conversion of $q_\Sigma$ and $dA_\Sigma$ before evaluating the Kähler area;

3. $q_\Sigma$ is the Kähler calibration density defined by
$$
\omega_{\mathrm{KE}}|_{\Sigma_\gamma}=q_\Sigma\,dA_\Sigma;
\tag{T.54a.2}
$$

4. $\alpha_j$ are the four interior angles of the geodesic corners;

5. $K_\Sigma$ is the Gaussian curvature of the induced two-metric;

6. the Gauss-Bonnet identity
$$
\int_{\Sigma_\gamma}K_\Sigma\,dA_\Sigma
+
\sum_{j=1}^{4}(\pi-\alpha_j)
=
2\pi
\tag{T.54a.3}
$$
holds for the disk topology of $\Sigma_\gamma$;

7. the ledger methods $\mathcal M_A$ and $\mathcal M_{GB}$ terminate and the
certificate verifies
$$
A_\gamma:=\int_{\Sigma_\gamma}q_\Sigma\,dA_\Sigma,
\qquad
R_{GB}:=\int_{\Sigma_\gamma}K_\Sigma\,dA_\Sigma
+\sum_{j=1}^4(\pi-\alpha_j)-2\pi,
\tag{T.54a.4}
$$
together with the interval containments and error tests
$$
A_\gamma\in I_A,
\qquad
R_{GB}\in I_{GB},
\qquad
0\in I_{GB},
$$
$$
\operatorname{rad}(I_A)\le E_A\le\varepsilon_A,
\qquad
\operatorname{rad}(I_{GB})\le E_{GB}\le\varepsilon_{GB}.
\tag{T.54a.5}
$$
An exact symbolic result is represented by a singleton interval and zero error.
Acceptance requires every displayed containment and inequality.

When a real representative rather than a class in $\mathbb R/(2\pi\mathbb Z)$ is claimed, the certificate additionally records a lift interval $I_{\mathrm{lift}}\subset\mathbb R$ of length less than $2\pi$. Acceptance then also requires the certified interval for $A_\gamma$ to lie in $I_{\mathrm{lift}}$. The Gauss--Bonnet residual checks the induced surface geometry and corner ledger; it does not determine $A_\gamma$ without an additional proved relation between $K_\Sigma$ and $q_\Sigma$.

The vertices, geodesic edges, induced curvature, corner angles, calibration density, orientation, tolerances, and numerical method must be specified independently of the CKM data being evaluated. The target value $2\arctan(d_{32,d}/d_{32,u})$ is not an input to the certificate.

$$
e^{i\delta_{\mathrm{flat}}}

*Proof.* Because $\Sigma_\gamma$ is a disk, the pullback of the complex line bundle to $\Sigma_\gamma$ is trivial. Choose a trivialization there. The holonomy--curvature identity gives
