       +(4m^2a^2+a^4)t^{-1}e^{-m^2t}\right]dt.
$$

Each summand is bounded by replacing $\int_T^\infty t^{-p}e^{-ct}\,dt$ with $e^{-cT}/(cT^p)$. These bounds are uniform on $|H|\le m$ and independent of a desired output.

##### 7. Finite box, spectral evaluation and quadrature

Use an equal-side Euclidean four-torus of side $L$, with spatial periodic and temporal antiperiodic fermionic boundary conditions. Let $\Theta_L(t,z)$ be its scalar Gaussian momentum sum per volume, shifted by real $z$. Poisson summation gives

$$
\begin{aligned}
|\Theta_L(t,z)-(4\pi t)^{-2}|&\le(4\pi t)^{-2}E_L(t),\\
\delta_L(t)&=\frac{2e^{-L^2/(4t)}}{1-e^{-L^2/(4t)}},\\
E_L(t)&=(1+\delta_L(t))^4-1.
\end{aligned}
\tag{T.78.14a.D12}
$$

The shift and the antiperiodic time boundary contribute phases of absolute value one, so the bound is uniform in $z$. A Euclidean-time Fourier cutoff stays separate from the source's physical clock.

The finite-torus version of (T.78.14a.D3) is a finite-part sum of the exact expression

$$
4Ny^2\left[
 \left(2m^2+\frac{q^2}{2}\right)
   \int_0^1dx\int dt\,t e^{-M_x^2t}\Theta_L(t,xq)
 -\int dt\,e^{-m^2t}\Theta_L(t,0)\right].
\tag{T.78.14a.D13}
$$

For its $\epsilon$-to-$T$ evaluation, the box-density error is at most

$$
\frac{Ny^2}{4\pi^2}E_L(T)
 \left[\left(2m^2+\frac{q^2}{2}\right)\log\frac{T}{\epsilon}
       +(\epsilon^{-1}-T^{-1})\right].
\tag{T.78.14a.D14}
$$

The kinetic secant uses two such evaluated quantities and divides their summed errors by $q^2$. After fixing a nonzero probe $q$, choose $L$ so this bound meets the assigned $q^2$-scaled allowance. Reciprocal-lattice admissibility is achieved by increasing $L$ through multiples of $2\pi/q$.

For constant-$H$ coefficient evaluations, convenient corresponding bounds are

$$
\begin{aligned}
E_{\mathrm{box},2}&\le\frac{Ny^2}{16\pi^2}E_L(T)
 \left[4(\epsilon^{-1}-T^{-1})+8m^2\log\frac{T}{\epsilon}\right],\\
E_{\mathrm{box},4}&\le\frac{Ny^4}{8\pi^2}E_L(T)
 \left[\log\frac{T}{\epsilon}+4m^2(T-\epsilon)
                      +\frac23m^4(T^2-\epsilon^2)\right].
\end{aligned}
\tag{T.78.14a.D15}
$$

These absolute bounds do not rely on cancellations of separately enclosed numbers. The counterterms are the same local ones on both sides and introduce no independent box constant.

For a Gaussian evaluation cutoff, suppose every omitted shifted momentum has length at least $p_{\mathrm{cut}}>0$. For $t\ge\epsilon$,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\Theta_{\mathrm{tail}}(t,z)
 &\le e^{-\epsilon p_{\mathrm{cut}}^2/2}\Theta_L(t/2,z)\\
 &\le4(4\pi t)^{-2}(1+\delta_L(T))^4
                  e^{-\epsilon p_{\mathrm{cut}}^2/2}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{T.78.14a.D16}
$$

In (T.78.14a.D14)–(T.78.14a.D15), replacing $E_L(T)$ by the final multiplier in (T.78.14a.D16) bounds the missing Gaussian evaluations. For a two-propagator finite Fourier calculation, retain the union of both shifted cutoff domains or add the two omission bounds. For $n\le4$ Born products, the union of the at-most-four shifted domains is finite and receives the sum of its four bounds. Identification with a finite canonical Hamiltonian cutoff uses the source/evaluation map in Parts B and E.

On the compact rectangle $[\epsilon,T]\times[0,1]$, all remaining functions are finite combinations of rational functions, $\exp$ and $\log$, with denominators bounded away from zero. Interval partition quadrature terminates by explicit derivative bounds, for example $|d\log x/dx|\le1/x_{\min}$. Rational alternating-series, logarithm and exponential routines produce any assigned arithmetic enclosure; the controls are deterministic.

Choose nonzero $q$ for (T.78.14a.D7), then $\epsilon,T$ for (T.78.14a.D9)–(T.78.14a.D11), a reciprocal-lattice $L$ for (T.78.14a.D14)–(T.78.14a.D15), $p_{\mathrm{cut}}$ for (T.78.14a.D16), and finally interval quadrature and coefficient words. Each bound tends to zero in this order. Finite physical pulse, preparation and current-meter errors remain separate source-owned entries of Part A §7.

##### 8. Uniform mixed gauge–Higgs remainder on a common analytic chart

For the noncommuting off-slice determinant, let $D_0=\gamma\cdot\partial+m$ and write $D=D_0+V$, with

$$
V=i\gamma\cdot A+y\Phi(H),
\qquad \|V\|\le b\le\theta m,\qquad \theta<1.
$$

For example, register $\sum_\mu\|A_\mu\|_\infty\le m/10$ and $\|H\|_\infty\le m$, so $\theta=1/5$. Fix a finite Fourier background alphabet with integer bandwidth $K$. The background is externally prescribed; its source/current work remains part of the complete physical source.

On the finite torus, $S=D_0^{-1}$ belongs to Schatten class $p$ for $p>4$. The Born remainder of order $n\ge5$ is absolutely convergent:

$$
\begin{aligned}
R_5(V)&=\sum_{n\ge5}\frac{(-1)^n}{n}\operatorname{Tr}[(SV)^n],\\
|R_5|&\le\frac{\|SV\|_5^5}{5(1-\theta)}
       \le\frac{b^5\operatorname{Tr}|S|^5}{5(1-\theta)}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{T.78.14a.D17}
$$

Indeed, Hölder's inequality gives $|\operatorname{Tr}A^n|\le\|A\|_5^5\|A\|^{n-5}$, and $\|SV\|\le\theta$. Summing the geometric majorant proves (T.78.14a.D17). The finite-torus constant is the convergent sum

$$
\operatorname{Tr}|S|^5=72\sum_p(p^2+m^2)^{-5/2}.
$$

In the translation-invariant volume limit its density is

$$
72\int\frac{d^4p}{(2\pi)^4}(p^2+m^2)^{-5/2}
 =\frac{72}{12\pi^2m},
$$

so $|R_5|/\operatorname{Vol}\le72b^5/[60\pi^2m(1-\theta)]$. At finite $L$, use the sum rather than this limiting integral.

This remainder belongs to the same $\zeta$ determinant. Its local UV counterterms arise from the first two nonconstant heat coefficients of $P$ and have degree at most four in $V$ and its source derivatives. Five variations annihilate them. The resulting resolvent products are trace class, so finite-mode differentiation and dominated convergence give the ordinary log-determinant Taylor coefficients. Integrating the fifth-and-higher derivatives from $V=0$ gives (T.78.14a.D17); the first four derivatives are reinstated with the $\zeta$ finite parts of §1. The local polynomial's gauge, scalar and mixed terms are therefore fixed by one prescription.

For mixed derivative bounds, complexify the finite real source coordinates. If $\|V\|\le b$ and the perturbation directions $W_j$ have norms $w_j$, choose positive radii $\rho_j$ with

$$
b+\sum_j\rho_jw_j\le\theta'm<m.
$$

The same absolutely convergent series is holomorphic on this polydisc. For every multi-index $\alpha$, Cauchy's formula gives

$$
|\partial^\alpha R_5(V)|
 \le\alpha!\,
    \frac{\theta'^5m^5\operatorname{Tr}|S|^5}{5(1-\theta')}
    \prod_j\rho_j^{-\alpha_j}.
\tag{T.78.14a.D18}
$$

This controls gauge, Higgs and mixed variations, including derivatives of physical source coefficients, uniformly on the registered smaller chart. The bound uses the first-order Dirac norm gap.

For the spectral tail, write $p=(2\pi/L)(n+\mathrm{spin\_shift})$. The infinity-norm shell $\|n\|_\infty=r$ has at most $64r^3+16r$ points, and $|n+\mathrm{spin\_shift}|\ge r-1/2$. Hence, for $N\ge1$,

$$
\sum_{\|n\|_\infty>N}(p^2+m^2)^{-5/2}
 \le\frac{80(L/\pi)^5}{N}.
\tag{T.78.14a.D19}
$$

The factor $72$ supplies spin/internal multiplicity. For a Fourier projector $P_N$ and finite background bandwidth $K$, the difference between $A=SV$ and its projected Born operator satisfies

$$
\|A-P_NAP_N\|_5\le2b\|(I-P_{N-K})S\|_5,
\qquad N>K.
$$

The second boundary term is shifted by at most $K$. A telescoping trace product and Hölder's inequality give

$$
|R_5(A)-R_5(P_NAP_N)|
 \le\frac{\|A-P_NAP_N\|_5
       \max(\|A\|_5,\|P_NAP_N\|_5)^4}{1-\theta}.
\tag{T.78.14a.D20}
$$

Equations (T.78.14a.D19)–(T.78.14a.D20), with Cauchy's formula on the same larger polydisc, yield explicit terminating finite-mode and mixed-derivative errors. Parts A–B distinguish the physical finite-current cutoff from this evaluation cutoff.

The coefficient outputs are derivatives of order at most four at $V=0$, so $R_5$ contributes exactly zero to them. It supplies the finite remainder and mixed-response control of the common source functional.

##### 8a. Complete first-four-variation algorithm and full mixed box limit

The entire degree-at-most-four Taylor polynomial is evaluated by the following finite rule. Register finitely many Fourier modes on a cell of side $\ell$, with their exact matrix coefficients. Using the squared operator in §1, expand

$$
P=P_0+P_1(V)+P_2(V,V),\qquad P_0=-\partial^2+m^2.
$$

For each derivative of total source degree at most four:

1. Enumerate all ordered Duhamel words of $P_1$ and $P_2$ with that total degree. There are at most four vertices. Use the simplex form of the derivative of $e^{-tP}$, retaining each word's sign and combinatorial multiplicity.
2. Enumerate the finite Fourier-mode labels and the zero-total-momentum words surviving the trace. Each intermediate momentum is $p+\kappa_j$, where $\kappa_j$ is a known partial sum of registered modes.
3. Complete the square in the weighted Gaussian exponent. Its variance is

$$
\begin{aligned}
C(\alpha)&=\sum_j\alpha_j|\kappa_j|^2
             -\left|\sum_j\alpha_j\kappa_j\right|^2\ge0,\\
\Delta(\alpha)&=m^2+C(\alpha)\ge m^2.
\end{aligned}
$$

   The numerator is a polynomial in $p$ of finite degree. Integrate it by the Gaussian Wick formula. Each result is a finite sum of $c_j(\alpha)t^je^{-\Delta(\alpha)t}/(4\pi t)^2$, with computable polynomial $c_j$ and integer $j$. The field-independent $j=0$ term cancels in the normalized source difference.
4. Apply exactly $J_{j-2}(\Delta)$, including $J_{-1}$ and $J_0$ of §1. This uses the same $\zeta$ finite part because the calculation starts with the heat derivative of $P$.
5. Integrate over the compact simplex by rational interval quadrature. The inequality $\Delta\ge m^2$ bounds every denominator; all numerators, simplex vertices and input Fourier coefficients are finite. Logarithms and exponentials use their fixed interval algorithms. The same procedure supplies interval bounds for every source derivative of the integrand.

This terminating finite sum/integral construction includes all gauge–Higgs mixed terms and their contact terms, without assuming that the mixed operators commute. The exact normalized functional is this complete polynomial plus $R_5$, bounded by (T.78.14a.D17). The coefficients in §§2–5 are closed-form evaluations of the relevant words.

For the large-box limit of $R_5$, take $L=k\ell$ with integer $k$. A background periodic on the $\ell$-cell leaves each of the $k^4$ Bloch residue classes invariant: writing each Fourier integer as $kn+j$, multiplication by a cell-periodic Fourier mode changes $n$ but not $j$. Thus the normalized large-box trace is the uniform grid average of the $\ell$-cell trace with boundary twist $\vartheta$, divided by $\ell^4$. Antiperiodic time shifts the grid without changing its mesh.

For the twisted free inverse $S_\vartheta$, one has $\|S_\vartheta\|\le1/m$ and

$$
\partial_{\vartheta_\mu}S_\vartheta
 =-S_\vartheta i\gamma_\mu S_\vartheta.
$$

The absolutely convergent series (T.78.14a.D17) therefore gives

$$
|\partial_{\vartheta_\mu}R_5|
 \le\frac{b^5\operatorname{Tr}|S_\vartheta|^5}{m(1-\theta)}.
$$

An explicit common bound over all real twists in the cell is

$$
\operatorname{Tr}|S_\vartheta|^5\le C_5,
\qquad C_5=72\left[81m^{-5}+80(\ell/\pi)^5\right].
$$

The $81$ integer modes with $\|n\|_\infty\le1$ are each bounded by $m^{-5}$; the shell argument (T.78.14a.D19) bounds the remaining sum uniformly for shifts of each component by at most one half.

The midpoint Riemann-sum inequality on the four-dimensional twist torus gives

$$
\left|\frac{R_{5,L}}{L^4}-R_{5,\mathrm{infinite\text{-}density}}\right|
 \le\frac{4\pi b^5C_5}{L\ell^4m(1-\theta)}.
\tag{T.78.14a.D21}
$$

Indeed, the mesh in each twist coordinate is $2\pi/L$. Integrating the coordinatewise Lipschitz bound over each centered grid cell and summing gives a factor $4\pi/L$, because every point is at most half a mesh away in each coordinate. Cauchy's formula on the larger source polydisc of (T.78.14a.D18) converts (T.78.14a.D21) into uniform mixed source-derivative bounds.

For the degree-at-most-four polynomial, the same Duhamel calculation before Gaussian integration gives the exact finite-box Gaussian momentum sum with polynomial moments. Poisson summation differentiates the Gaussian finitely many times, producing explicit Hermite polynomials. On $\epsilon\le t\le T$, the omitted winding sum is absolutely bounded by the corresponding polynomial times $e^{-L^2|n|^2/(4T)}$; the integer shell census bounds the remainder after any finite shell by a convergent geometric tail. Its UV contribution has the same exponentially small winding factor and no new local counterterm. All polynomials are known for every registered word. For the scalar target derivatives, (T.78.14a.D12)–(T.78.14a.D15) give simpler closed-form bounds.

##### 8b. Exact finite spatial-CAR to zeta interface by local counterterms

**Domain.** A sharp four-dimensional Fourier compression with spatially varying backgrounds produces intersections of shifted momentum domains. Subtracting a Taylor polynomial summed over only one unshifted domain does not then prove convergence: a two-vertex boundary loss can scale as $|k|\Lambda$. The following interface uses the canonical finite **spatial** CAR regulator with spatially homogeneous, time-dependent gauge and Higgs probes. Every physical spatial momentum is an invariant CAR block. Time/Matsubara frequencies evaluate its trace; they are not additional physical CAR states or a physical temporal cutoff. The separate constant-magnetic experiment uses its W.6a.7-style source map.

The continuum coefficient is the Lorentz-covariant coefficient of the same canonical action and $\zeta$ prescription. Its temporal response is physically accessible on this finite source; finite-cutoff Lorentz symmetry is not assumed. The fixed-domain argument below treats spatially homogeneous physical charts; a spatially inhomogeneous chart needs an additional regulator construction, such as a controlled gauge-covariant lattice.

Let the external Euclidean frequencies have magnitude at most $K$, and let $b_1$ be the sum of norms of the finitely many source Fourier matrices. Use the same chart $\|V\|\le\theta m$ for convergence of the full determinant; the sufficient condition $b_1\le\theta m$ may be imposed. For an ordered $n$-vertex loop with $n\le4$, define

$$
I_n(p;k)=\frac{(-1)^n}{n}
 \operatorname{Tr}\left[S(p+\kappa_1)V_1\cdots S(p+\kappa_n)V_n\right],
\qquad |\kappa_j|\le nK.
$$

The finite spatial-CAR determinant sums the same allowed spatial $p$ for every propagator because all $\kappa_j$ have zero spatial component. The trace includes all $72$ spin/internal coordinates; unaffected source complements factor before this calculation.

Let $d=4-n$, $r=d+1=5-n$, and let $t^d$ denote the multivariate Taylor polynomial in external frequencies at zero through total degree $d$. Equivalently, take the degree-$d$ Taylor polynomial of $I_n(p;tk)$ at $t=0$ and evaluate it at $t=1$. For every finite physical spatial cutoff $N$, define

$$
\mathrm{CT}_{N,n}
 =t^dA_{\zeta,n}-\mathop{\mathrm{Sum}}_{\mathrm{physical}\ p,N}t^dI_n.
$$

Here $A_{\zeta,n}$ is the $n$-field derivative of the common $\zeta$ functional, computed by §8a. In this physical counterterm definition, the sum includes the **vacuum continuous-$\omega$ integral**, not a $\beta$-dependent Matsubara sum: $\mathrm{CT}_{N,n}=\mathrm{CT}_{N,\mathrm{vac},n}$ is fixed once. A finite-$\beta$ Matsubara counterterm is only an intermediate evaluator table; §§10.5–10.6 restore its exact local difference from the fixed physical action. The Taylor operation acts on the analytic integrand before summation, not through changing physical Fourier spaces. Consequently $\mathrm{CT}_{N,n}$ is local in external time and polynomial in the same source fields and their derivatives, with no dependence on a fitted output. Part A §§2 and 7 retain its signed source work and normalization.

The renormalized finite determinant is exactly

$$
\Gamma_{N,\mathrm{ren}}
 =\Gamma_{N,\mathrm{raw}}+\sum_{n=1}^4\mathrm{CT}_{N,n}.
$$

Its $n\le4$ **vacuum** term is

$$
\mathop{\mathrm{Sum}}_{\mathrm{physical}\ p,N}(1-t^d)I_n+t^dA_{\zeta,n},
\tag{T.78.14a.D22}
$$

where the temporal operation is the vacuum integral. At finite $\beta$, the displayed form is an evaluator identity only with its temporary $\beta$-counterterm table; the unchanged physical action includes the thermal-jet polynomial in (T.78.14a.D44). For $n\ge5$, use the raw $\det_5$ remainder at the chosen vacuum or $\beta$ evaluation. In (T.78.14a.D22), the local regulator counterterms are explicit, while the nonlocal response remains the measured finite determinant.

To prove convergence to $\zeta$, apply $r$ frequency derivatives. They annihilate every allowed local degree-$d$ UV subtraction. The remaining product has $n+r=5$ resolvents and is absolutely integrable, so these derivatives commute with the limit and coincide with the $\zeta$ derivative. The difference is a polynomial of degree at most $d$; matching its prescribed zero-frequency jets to $t^dA_{\zeta,n}$ fixes it uniquely. This proves finite-part equivalence without an additional scalar or gauge finite constant.

###### Explicit high-momentum tail

For $|p|>2nK$, differentiation of the inverse gives

$$
\left\|\frac{d^j}{dt^j}S(p+t\kappa)\right\|
 \le j!\,|\kappa|^j\left(\frac2{|p|}\right)^{j+1}.
$$

The Leibniz sum over $n$ propagators has $\binom{n+r-1}{r}=\binom4r$ weak compositions. The integral Taylor remainder cancels the factor $r!$. After summing all ordered Fourier words,

$$
\begin{aligned}
|(1-t^d)I_n(p;k)|&\le C_n|p|^{-5},\\
C_n&=\frac{32\cdot72}{n}\binom4r(nK)^rb_1^n.
\end{aligned}
\tag{T.78.14a.D23}
$$

The loop factor $1/n$ is included. If that factor has already been distributed over cyclic representatives, retain the corresponding multiplicities once. The $n=1$ loop vanishes in this source by its traceless Higgs insertion and charge-symmetric gauge reference; (T.78.14a.D23) remains a valid bound.

A continuum spatial cutoff with omitted $|p_{\mathrm{spatial}}|>\Lambda>2nK$ has error at most

$$
\frac{C_n}{3\pi^3\Lambda},
\tag{T.78.14a.D24}
$$

because the integral of $(\omega^2+|p_{\mathrm{spatial}}|^2)^{-5/2}$ over $\omega$ is $4/(3|p_{\mathrm{spatial}}|^4)$. A cubical spatial cutoff has an omitted set contained in the radial omitted set used in (T.78.14a.D24), so the same bound applies.

For an equal-side length-$L$ torus with temporal antiperiodicity and physical spatial integer cutoff $N$, the omitted set is contained in the full four-dimensional integer tail. Once $\pi N/L>2nK$, the shell census in (T.78.14a.D19) gives

$$
E_{N,n}\le\frac{80C_nL}{\pi^5N}.
\tag{T.78.14a.D25}
$$

The temporal evaluation tail may independently use the same form with its temporal cutoff. It is an evaluator residual, not missing physical fermions.

###### Explicit finite-box bound

Set $c_\kappa=2[1+(nK/m)^2]$. For all $t\in[0,1]$,

$$
|p|^2+m^2\le c_\kappa\left(|p+t\kappa_j|^2+m^2\right).
$$

Six additional derivatives in any one momentum coordinate, followed by the same external-frequency Taylor remainder, give the $L^1$ bound

$$
\begin{aligned}
M_{6,n}&:=\max_i\int_{\mathbb R^4}
       |\partial_{p_i}^6(1-t^d)I_n|\,d^4p\\
&\le\frac{72}{n}\frac{(r+6)!}{r!}\binom{10}{r+6}
       (nK)^rb_1^nc_\kappa^{11/2}\frac{4\pi^2}{63m^7}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{T.78.14a.D26}
$$

The resolvent product has $n+r+6=11$ factors. Its integrated majorant uses

$$
\int d^4p\,(p^2+m^2)^{-11/2}=\frac{4\pi^2}{63m^7}.
$$

The factorial/composition factor in (T.78.14a.D26) safely overcounts mixed directional placements, without using cancellations of spin or internal traces.

For the Poisson estimate, integrate by parts six times in a coordinate attaining the largest winding index. The shell $\|\ell\|_\infty=s$ contains at most $80s^3$ points, while the sixth derivative contributes $s^{-6}$. Since $\sum_{s\ge1}s^{-3}<3/2$,

$$
\left|L^{-4}\sum_pR_n(p)
       -\int\frac{d^4p}{(2\pi)^4}R_n(p)\right|
 \le\frac{120M_{6,n}}{(2\pi)^4L^6},
\qquad R_n=(1-t^d)I_n.
\tag{T.78.14a.D27}
$$

Antiperiodic temporal phases have modulus one. Equations (T.78.14a.D25) and (T.78.14a.D27) control the finite spatial-CAR cutoff and finite-box interfaces for every first-four-variation term; (T.78.14a.D17)–(T.78.14a.D21) control the remaining $n\ge5$ determinant on the same compact source chart. All constants are finite functions of the upfront masses, norms and Fourier bandwidth.

##### 10. Rectangular time: $\beta$ may increase after the physical cutoff

Extend the equal-side estimates to spatial side $L$ and Euclidean-time length $\beta\ge L$, both integer multiples of the registered source period $\ell$. In the physical unit chart, $\beta$ is inverse energy, namely Euclidean duration divided by $\hbar$. The physical spatial-CAR mode count depends on $L,N$, not on $\beta$; all temporal frequencies below evaluate the same finite canonical Fock trace.

First fix the spatial box and physical cutoff using the deterministic bounds, then increase $\beta$ through period-compatible values until the finite-dimensional Gibbs-versus-vacuum/Lehmann error meets its tolerance. Increasing $\beta$ creates no new physical CAR modes, and the following analytic bounds are uniform in that increase.

###### 10.1 A $\beta$-uniform scalar Matsubara estimate

For $r>0$, let $f(\omega)=(\omega^2+r^2)^{-5/2}$. It is even and decreasing on the positive half-line. Comparing the half-shifted grid with its monotone integral gives

$$
\beta^{-1}\sum_{j\in\mathbb Z}f\left(\frac{2\pi(j+1/2)}{\beta}\right)
 \le\frac{2}{3\pi r^4}+\frac{2}{\beta r^5}.
\tag{T.78.14a.D28}
$$

One proof uses the bounded-variation Riemann-sum inequality

$$
h\sum_jf\bigl(h(j+1/2)\bigr)
 \le\int_{\mathbb R}f+2hf(0),
\qquad h=\frac{2\pi}{\beta},
$$

and $\int_{\mathbb R}f=4/(3r^4)$. The factor two also covers any real temporal twist, as needed for the Bloch estimate.

The three-dimensional spatial integer shell $\|n\|_\infty=s$ has $24s^2+2\le26s^2$ points, and its momentum length is at least $2\pi s/L$. Consequently, per spatial volume,

$$
\begin{aligned}
&L^{-3}\beta^{-1}\sum_{\substack{\|n\|_\infty>N\\j\in\mathbb Z}}
 \left[\left(\frac{2\pi(j+1/2)}{\beta}\right)^2
       +\left|\frac{2\pi n}{L}\right|^2+m^2\right]^{-5/2}\\
&\qquad\le\frac{13L}{12\pi^5N}
            +\frac{13L^2}{16\pi^5\beta N^2}\\
&\qquad\le\frac{91}{48}\frac{L}{\pi^5N}
          <\frac{2L}{\pi^5N},
\qquad \beta\ge L,\quad N\ge1.
\end{aligned}
\tag{T.78.14a.D29}
$$

The summations use $\sum_{s>N}s^{-2}\le1/N$ and $\sum_{s>N}s^{-3}\le1/(2N^2)$. Thus the bound $4L/(\pi^5N)$ is valid. Omitting $m^2$ only enlarges the tail.

For every first-four BPHZ remainder $R_n$ of §8b, once its high-momentum condition holds, the physical spatial-cutoff error satisfies

$$
E_{N,n}\le\frac{4C_nL}{\pi^5N},\qquad\beta\ge L.
\tag{T.78.14a.D30}
$$

This sharpens the equal-side bound without a growing $\beta$ factor.

###### 10.2 Uniform Schatten density and $\det_5$ cutoff error

For the $72$-dimensional spin/internal source, define

$$
\tau_5(L,\beta)=\frac{\operatorname{Tr}|S|^5}{L^3\beta}.
$$

For any fixed integer $N_0\ge1$, (T.78.14a.D28)–(T.78.14a.D29) give

$$
\tau_5(L,\beta)
 \le72\left\{\frac{(2N_0+1)^3}{L^3}
       \left[\frac{2}{3\pi m^4}+\frac{2}{Lm^5}\right]
             +\frac{4L}{\pi^5N_0}\right\},
\qquad\beta\ge L.
\tag{T.78.14a.D31}
$$

For a uniform constant over sufficiently large spatial boxes, choose $L\ge2\pi/m$ and $N_0=\lceil mL/(2\pi)\rceil$. Then

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{(2N_0+1)^3}{L^3}&\le\frac{125m^3}{8\pi^3},\\
\frac{2}{3\pi m^4}+\frac{2}{Lm^5}&\le\frac{5}{3\pi m^4},\\
\frac{4L}{\pi^5N_0}&\le\frac{8}{\pi^4m}.
\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore

$$
\tau_5(L,\beta)\le\frac{2451}{\pi^4m}=: \tau_{5,*},
\qquad\beta\ge L\ge\frac{2\pi}{m}.
\tag{T.78.14a.D32}
$$

This constant is independent of $\beta,L$ and the later physical cutoff. The omitted spatial Schatten density obeys

$$
\tau_{5,\mathrm{tail}}(N;L,\beta)\le\frac{288L}{\pi^5N},
\tag{T.78.14a.D33}
$$

including the spin/internal factor $72$.

On the spatially homogeneous physical probe class, the spatial projector commutes with $V$ and $S$. Thus $A=SV$ is block diagonal in spatial momentum, and

$$
\|A-P_NAP_N\|_5\le b\|(I-P_N)S\|_5.
$$

Using (T.78.14a.D20) and dividing by the full volume yields

$$
\frac{|R_5(A)-R_5(P_NAP_N)|}{L^3\beta}
 \le\frac{b^5\tau_{5,\mathrm{tail}}(N)^{1/5}\tau_{5,*}^{4/5}}
             {1-\theta}.
\tag{T.78.14a.D34}
$$

No factor two is needed because no spatial momentum is shifted. Also,

$$
\frac{|R_5|}{L^3\beta}
 \le\frac{b^5\tau_{5,*}}{5(1-\theta)}.
\tag{T.78.14a.D35}
$$

Both bounds are uniform under the later increase of $\beta$. Cauchy's argument (T.78.14a.D18), with $b$ replaced by the larger chart bound $\theta'm$, gives the corresponding uniform mixed source-derivative controls.

###### 10.3 Box and Bloch bounds on the rectangular torus

For the first-four BPHZ remainders, the Poisson winding vector is

(L\ell_1,L\ell_2,L\ell_3,\beta\ell_4).

A coordinate attaining $\|\ell\|_\infty$ has physical length at least $L\|\ell\|_\infty$ because $\beta\ge L$. The same six-integration-by-parts proof gives

For $R_5$, the exact cell-periodic Bloch decomposition has spatial meshes $2\pi/L$ and temporal mesh $2\pi/\beta$. The midpoint Lipschitz calculation in §8a becomes

\begin{aligned}
\left|\frac{R_{5,\mathrm{rect}}}{L^3\beta}

The twist-uniform $C_5$ is the one from §8a. Cauchy's formula supplies the mixed source-derivative versions. Choosing $\beta$ as an integer multiple of $\ell$ preserves source periodicity; antiperiodic fermionic time only shifts the twist grid.

**Terminating order.** Fix the physical nonzero response frequencies and source chart. Choose $L$, a period multiple with $L\ge2\pi/m$, for (T.78.14a.D36)–(T.78.14a.D37); choose $N$ for (T.78.14a.D30), (T.78.14a.D33)–(T.78.14a.D34); only then choose $\beta\ge L$, also a period multiple, for the finite Fock thermal/Lehmann error. This does not invalidate preceding bounds. Finally refine temporal summation, quadrature and source-word precision. Even a crude estimate containing the now-fixed Fock dimension becomes small with $\beta$, without simultaneous growth of that dimension.

###### 10.4 Stronger direct spatial $\det_5$ tail

On the homogeneous-spatial source, $[P_N,S]=[P_N,V]=0$. Hence the exact block decompositions are

###### 10.5 Fixed physical counterterms while lowering temperature

For the finite-spatial-CAR family, define and freeze $\mathrm{CT}_{N,\mathrm{vac}}$ using its zero-temperature continuous-frequency loop jets and the common $\zeta$ finite part. This source- and cutoff-dependent local prescription is fixed before the output and retained at every physical Gibbs $\beta$.

A finite-$\beta$ BPHZ evaluator table may temporarily use $\mathrm{CT}_{N,\beta}$. Its difference from the physical counterterm is the explicit local polynomial

$$
\mathrm{CT}_{N,\mathrm{vac}}-\mathrm{CT}_{N,\beta}
 =\sum_{n\le4}
   \left[\mathop{\mathrm{Sum}}_\beta
          -\mathop{\mathrm{Integral}}_\omega\right]t^{4-n}I_n.
$$

Restore this difference when evaluating the unchanged physical action. Equivalently, compare the physical $\beta$ source directly with its finite-$N$ vacuum source:

$$
[\Gamma_{\mathrm{raw},\beta}+\mathrm{CT}_{N,\mathrm{vac}}]
 -[\Gamma_{\mathrm{raw},\mathrm{vac}}+\mathrm{CT}_{N,\mathrm{vac}}]
 =\Gamma_{\mathrm{raw},\beta}-\Gamma_{\mathrm{raw},\mathrm{vac}}.
$$

The counterterms cancel exactly in the finite-Fock thermal/Lehmann comparison. Its local-jet and nonlocal thermal contributions form one shared thermal error, not separately tuned constants or duplicate error entries. The $\beta$-uniform bounds (T.78.14a.D29)–(T.78.14a.D38) permit the zero-temperature analytic limit followed by the finite physical $\beta$ approximation, without enlarging the physical mode count.

###### 10.6 Exact certificate for every finite-$\beta$ local thermal jet

The polynomial in §10.5 has a finite residue algorithm covering all gauge–Higgs mixed contacts. Fix the physical spatial box and cutoff, and write $E_p=\sqrt{|p|^2+m^2}$. For an $n$-vertex word with $n\le4$, expand at zero through external-frequency degree $j\le4-n$. Each coefficient is rational in $\omega$, with poles only at $\pm iE_p$ of order at most $n+j\le4$, since each frequency derivative adds one free resolvent. Pairing $\omega$ and $-\omega$ removes the odd part in both the symmetric fermionic Matsubara sum and the vacuum integral. The even proper rational part has the unique expansion

$$
J_{n,j,p}(\omega)
 =\sum_{s=1}^4\frac{c_{n,j,s}(p)}{(\omega^2+E_p^2)^s}.
\tag{T.78.14a.D39}
$$

Unused coefficients are zero. Polynomial division and partial fractions after the finite matrix trace produce the coefficients, including the loop factor, Fourier-word multiplicity and external-frequency monomial. The $n=1$ word vanishes in this source. In general, its odd leading term is paired before either evaluation. No even polynomial part remains because the even integrand decays at least as $\omega^{-2}$. Thus every term in (T.78.14a.D39) is absolutely temporally integrable. The physical spatial momenta and registered Fourier words form finite sets.

For fermionic frequencies $\omega_l=2\pi(l+1/2)/\beta$, define

$$
\Delta_s(E,\beta)
 =\left[\beta^{-1}\sum_l-\int_{\mathbb R}\frac{d\omega}{2\pi}\right]
        (\omega^2+E^2)^{-s}.
$$

A two-pole residue calculation, equivalently the partial-fraction expansion of $\tanh$, gives

$$
\Delta_1(E,\beta)=-\frac1{E(e^{\beta E}+1)},
\qquad \Delta_{s+1}=-\frac1{2sE}\partial_E\Delta_s,
\qquad s=1,2,3.
\tag{T.78.14a.D40}
$$

The derivative acts on the basis function, not on the already computed coefficients $c$. Put $z=e^{-\beta E}$ and

$$
f=\frac{z}{1+z},\qquad g=\frac{z}{(1+z)^2},
\qquad h=\frac{z(1-z)}{(1+z)^3},
\qquad k=\frac{z(1-4z+z^2)}{(1+z)^4}.
$$

Then

$$
\begin{aligned}
\Delta_1&=-\frac fE,\\
\Delta_2&=-\frac12\left(\frac f{E^3}+\frac{\beta g}{E^2}\right),\\
\Delta_3&=-\frac18\left(\frac{3f}{E^5}+
                   \frac{3\beta g}{E^4}+\frac{\beta^2h}{E^3}\right),\\
\Delta_4&=-\frac1{48}\left(\frac{15f}{E^7}+
                    \frac{15\beta g}{E^6}+
                    \frac{6\beta^2h}{E^5}+\frac{\beta^3k}{E^4}\right).
\end{aligned}
\tag{T.78.14a.D41}
$$

For $0\le z\le1$, all four functions have absolute value at most $z$; in particular, $|1-4z+z^2|\le(1+z)^2$. Since $E\ge m$, for every $\beta>0$,

$$
\begin{aligned}
|\Delta_s(E,\beta)|&\le e^{-\beta m}B_s(\beta,m),\\
B_1&=m^{-1},\\
B_2&=\frac{m^{-3}+\beta m^{-2}}2,\\
B_3&=\frac{3m^{-5}+3\beta m^{-4}+\beta^2m^{-3}}8,\\
B_4&=\frac{15m^{-7}+15\beta m^{-6}
                   +6\beta^2m^{-5}+\beta^3m^{-4}}{48}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{T.78.14a.D42}
$$

The exact local correction required by the fixed vacuum counterterm is therefore

$$
T_{N,\beta}=L^{-3}\sum_{p\in P_N}
             \sum_{\substack{\text{all }n\le4\text{ words},\,j,s}}
                 c_{n,j,s}(p)\Delta_s(E_p,\beta),
\tag{T.78.14a.D43}
$$

where $c$ includes the source amplitudes and external-frequency monomials. The physical $n\le4$ finite-$\beta$ density is exactly

$$
\mathop{\mathrm{Sum}}_\beta(1-t^{4-n})I_n
       +t^{4-n}A_{\zeta,n}+T_{N,\beta,n}.
\tag{T.78.14a.D44}
$$

For any mixed source derivative $\alpha$, differentiate the finite polynomial $c$ in (T.78.14a.D43). On the registered compact source chart, let $C_{\alpha,n,j,s}(p)$ be the sum of absolute monomial coefficients multiplied by their chart-radius powers and falling-factorial derivative factors, including the registered frequency powers. This is a finite arithmetic upper bound for $|\partial^\alpha c|$. Then

$$
|\partial^\alpha T_{N,\beta}|
 \le e^{-\beta m}L^{-3}\sum_{p,n,j,s}
                C_{\alpha,n,j,s}(p)B_s(\beta,m).
\tag{T.78.14a.D45}
$$

This covers every degree-at-most-four local thermal jet, including mixed gauge/Higgs and temporal-derivative contacts. The bound is a known polynomial of degree at most three in $\beta$ times $e^{-\beta m}$. For fixed physical $L,N$, it tends to zero and can be enclosed to any assigned tolerance through period-compatible $\beta$ values. No holomorphic interacting ground-state gap is assumed. Bare terms and frozen vacuum counterterms have no $\beta$ dependence. Equations (T.78.14a.D39)–(T.78.14a.D45) supply the local correction once; when a controlled full raw thermal difference is used instead, its local part is not counted again.

###### 10.7 Direct physical scalar-bubble cross-check

Write $N_f=3$ for flavor multiplicity, distinct from the physical cutoff. At each fixed spatial $p$, the continuous-$\omega$ integral obeys

$$
\int\frac{d\omega}{2\pi}
 \frac1{(\omega^2+E_p^2)((\omega+q)^2+E_p^2)}
 =\frac1{E_p(q^2+4E_p^2)}.
$$

Using

$$
\omega(\omega+q)
 =\frac{(\omega^2+E_p^2)+((\omega+q)^2+E_p^2)-q^2-2E_p^2}{2}
$$

in the Dirac numerator of §3 gives the raw vacuum scalar integrand

$$
-\frac{8N_fy^2|p|^2}{E_p(q^2+4E_p^2)}.
$$

Its remainder after subtracting the $q^0$ and $q^2$ jets is exactly

$$
-\frac{N_fy^2|p|^2q^4}{2E_p^5(q^2+4E_p^2)}.
\tag{T.78.14a.D46}
$$

This is summed over the physical spatial modes and is absolutely spatially integrable in the continuum. Its integral equals $\Pi(q^2)-\Pi(0)-q^2\Pi'(0)$ from §3. Combining denominators with one Feynman parameter, or differentiating twice in $q^2$ and performing the radial integral, gives the same $\Pi''$; both subtracted jets vanish at zero. The local counterterms therefore restore the common $\zeta$ mass and kinetic jets while retaining the measured nonlocal finite-mode response. Equation (T.78.14a.D46) checks the physical regulator without imposing another finite-part condition.

#### Part E. One local regulator-to-zeta matching for the physical source

##### 1. Physical cutoff and trace

The physical regulator has a finite three-dimensional spatial momentum set and continuous physical time. Its field trace is exactly $\det(I+U)$ by Part B. Euclidean-time/Matsubara cutoffs control evaluation accuracy; the physical CAR carrier remains fixed.

The physical mixed/kinetic chart is spatially homogeneous with finitely many external time frequencies. A source vertex therefore preserves each physical spatial momentum. The physical first-order determinant Taylor coefficients are loop sums over that fixed spatial set and all temporal frequencies, with the actual spin, flavor and gauge vertices and canonical current normalization.

The continuum coefficients use the covariant $\zeta$ prescription of Part D §1 at $\mu=Q$. The following local counterterm rule belongs to the source definition and matches its finite physical trace to that prescription.

##### 2. Exact local counterterm rule

For each ordered Born term $n=1,\ldots,4$, let $I_n(p;k)$ be the actual trace integrand, including its loop factor and every Fourier word. Let $t^{4-n}$ denote Taylor projection in the external frequencies at zero through degree $4-n$. Write $A_{\zeta,n}$ for the corresponding $n$-field variation of the common $\zeta$ functional, evaluated by the finite Duhamel/simplex algorithm in Part D §8a.

At each physical spatial regulator $r=(P,L)$, freeze the vacuum counterterm

$$
\operatorname{CT}_{r,\mathrm{vac},n}
=t^{4-n}A_{\zeta,n}
-\frac{1}{L^3}\sum_{\mathbf p\in P}
 \int_{\mathbb R}\frac{d\omega}{2\pi}\,
 t^{4-n}I_n(\mathbf p,\omega;k).
\tag{T.78.14a.R1}
$$

This is a density; its action contribution includes the physical spacetime volume. It is a finite polynomial in the source fields and their temporal derivatives. Its coefficients are fixed by $Q$, $y$, the representation, the spatial regulator and the common $\zeta$ rule. The continuous-frequency integrals converge at fixed finite spatial carrier; the $n=1$ term vanishes. Free-propagator residues or controlled quadrature evaluate these coefficients, including their source-force and work contributions.

The counterterm $\operatorname{CT}_{r,\mathrm{vac}}$ is independent of the later Gibbs duration $\beta$. The same finite Hamiltonian/source prescription is used at every temperature. Its $L$ dependence is part of the spatial-regulator family, while $\beta$ controls preparation and evaluation. Its signed work, source force, amplitude, precision and storage remain in the resource ledger. The independently fixed renormalized reference inputs are

$$
B_{\mathrm{ref}}=\frac6\pi,\qquad
z_0=1,\qquad \mu_0^2=Q^2,\qquad \lambda_0=1.
$$

Equation (T.78.14a.R1) supplies the additional finite bare/counterterm entries once. At finite $\beta$, the source is exactly

$$
\Gamma_{r,\beta,\mathrm{ren}}
=\Gamma_{r,\beta,\mathrm{raw}}
+\sum_{n=1}^{4}\operatorname{CT}_{r,\mathrm{vac},n}.
\tag{T.78.14a.R2}
$$

Let $\mathcal J_{r,\beta}$ denote the complete Matsubara loop sum, and $\mathcal J_{r,\mathrm{vac}}$ the spatial sum with continuous $\omega$. The contribution of order $n\le4$ is

$$
\mathcal J_{r,\beta}(1-t^{4-n})I_n
+t^{4-n}A_{\zeta,n}

$$

=\Gamma_{r,\beta,\mathrm{raw}}-\Gamma_{r,\mathrm{vac},\mathrm{raw}}.
$$

<a id="theorem-t79-conditional-closure-of-the-quantitative-parameter-sector"></a>**Theorem T.79 (Conditional Closure of the Quantitative Parameter Sector).** On a fixed PU structural branch with a fixed-loop-order SM RG system, suppose:
1. accepted $\mathfrak C_{A\to\mathrm{St}}$ and $\mathfrak S_{EW}$, together with a same-saddle determinant record for $A_{EW}$, are supplied whenever $v$ or a $v$-dependent quantity is requested;
2. a completed flag-lift spectral calculation provides a definite threshold triplet $\Delta$;
3. the flavor-geometric residual data $(\mathcal T_{E_8},\mathcal V)$ are fixed on the selected branch;
4. the CP-profile data $\mathcal B$ are fixed;
5. the accepted moment-map datum of Definition T.22a fixes $\gamma=1$ wherever the unit target-shift branch is used;
6. an accepted quartic matching record $\mathfrak M_\lambda$ fixes the map from $\lambda_{\mathrm{PU}}(\mathfrak A_{PU})$ to a renormalized SM boundary at a declared scale and scheme; and
7. every marginality, decoupling, pole/observable, unit, and remainder convention used in the requested rows is specified independently of the evaluated observables.
Then the requested quantitative vector $\Pi_T$ is uniquely determined up to the certified residual intervals on that fully specified branch.

*Proof.* Theorem T.5 fixes only $\kappa_{\mathrm{St}}$. The accepted action transport gives $\kappa_{EW}=\kappa_{\mathrm{St}}$, and $\mathfrak S_{EW}$ together with same-saddle $A_{EW}$ fixes the interval for $v$. Theorem T.78 fixes $\Delta$ once the spectral problem is completed; Theorem T.71 fixes the gauge/RG sector; Theorems T.72--T.73 fix the Yukawa ratios on the chosen flavor branch; and Theorems T.74--T.76 fix the CP sector. The target-shift, quartic-matching, criticality, RG, decoupling, and pole records fix the Higgs conversion. Every component is therefore a deterministic function of the complete declared input record. Omitting the action transport or scale record leaves $v$ open; omitting any output-specific record leaves that component open. ∎

<a id="corollary-t791-status-boundary-for-the-quantitative-appendix-t-sector"></a>**Corollary T.79.1 (Status Boundary for the Quantitative Appendix-T Sector).** The deterministic machinery closes only after every input consumed by the requested output is specified with its role and dependencies. In particular, a $v$ row requires accepted $\mathfrak C_{A\to\mathrm{St}}$, accepted $\mathfrak S_{EW}$, and a same-saddle forward determinant/remainder record for $A_{EW}$; threshold, flavor, target-shift, quartic, criticality, RG, decoupling, and pole rows retain their own named records. A completed flag-lift threshold tuple closes neither the action-transport/scale branch nor any independent Higgs or flavor gate. ∎

<a id="theorem-t792-appendix-t-deterministic-matching-functor"></a>**Theorem T.79.2 (Appendix-T Deterministic Matching Functor).** Fix an Appendix-T input record
$$
\mathfrak I_T
=
(A_{EW},\mathfrak C_{A\to\mathrm{St}},\mathfrak S_{EW},\mathfrak S_{\widetilde X},\delta^{\mathrm{heavy}},\mathcal T_{E_8},\mathcal V,\mathcal N_\nu,\mathcal B,\mathcal M_\gamma,\mathfrak M_\lambda,\mathcal C_{\mathrm{crit}},\mathcal R_{\mathrm{RG}},\mathcal C_{\mathrm{dec}},\mathcal C_{\mathrm{pole}}).
$$
Here $A_{EW}$ is a structurally independent same-saddle determinant-model prefactor when $v$ is requested; $\mathfrak C_{A\to\mathrm{St}}$ is the accepted action transport; and $\mathfrak S_{EW}$ fixes the unreduced Planck convention and units, common saddle, determinant/gauge-volume/matching normalization, no-double-counting audit, observable map, quantitative remainder, and structural independence. The remaining entries are respectively the completed flag-lift spectral tuple, residual threshold ledger, flavor normalization and Van Vleck data, neutrino/Majorana record, CP profile, target-shift datum, quartic match, criticality condition, RG system, decoupling map, and pole/observable map. Then there is a deterministic map
$$
\mathfrak F_T:\mathfrak I_T\longmapsto\Pi_T
$$
defined by:

1. for a $v$-dependent output, use $\mathfrak C_{A\to\mathrm{St}}$ to set $\kappa_{EW}=\kappa_{\mathrm{St}}=77/2$ and evaluate the interval $v=A_{EW}e^{-\kappa_{EW}}M_{Pl}(1+\epsilon_{EW})$ from $\mathfrak S_{EW}$;
2. evaluate the sector finite parts from $\mathfrak S_{\widetilde X}$ and set $\Delta=TF$ and $Z_i=1+\Delta_i/24$;
3. append exactly the registered residual heavy-threshold ledger;
4. form gauge and Higgs boundary data only from their declared threshold, target-shift, quartic, and criticality records;
5. form charged-fermion and neutrino Yukawa data from $(\mathcal T_{E_8},\mathcal V,\mathcal N_\nu)$;
6. form CKM and PMNS matrices from $\mathcal B$; and
7. evolve with $\mathcal R_{\mathrm{RG}}$, apply $\mathcal C_{\mathrm{dec}}$, and convert with $\mathcal C_{\mathrm{pole}}$.

The map is functorial only for isomorphisms preserving every component of $\mathfrak I_T$. Such an isomorphism may relabel equivalent flavor bases but cannot manufacture or retune a scalar input and leaves every basis-invariant component unchanged.

*Proof.* Step 1 is a function because the native action, its accepted transport, the scale record, the same-saddle prefactor, units, and remainder are all supplied. The completed spectral tuple determines $F$ and hence $\Delta$; the threshold rule then fixes Step 3. The explicit target-shift, quartic, and criticality tuple fixes the Higgs boundary. The flavor, neutrino, and CP records fix Steps 5 and 6. For Step 7, the full-interval perturbative-solution hypothesis of Theorem T.71 gives one RG trajectory, and the supplied decoupling and pole maps are functions. Composition proves determinacy and functoriality without any input beyond the complete record. ∎

<a id="proposition-t793-electroweak-higgs-flavor-neutrino-majorana-and-common-scale-dependency-ledger"></a>**Proposition T.79.3 (Electroweak, Higgs, Flavor, Neutrino, Majorana, and Common-Scale Dependency Ledger).** The dependency record for the Appendix-T matching, Higgs, flavor, and neutrino sectors is the following finite ledger.

| Input or convention | Role | Status at point of use | Uncertainty class carried forward | Affected outputs |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| Completed $\Delta$ from $\mathfrak S_{\widetilde X}$ | ThresholdData | branch theorem after Theorem T.78 data are fixed; validation target if not fixed | T2 until spectral branch is completed | $g_i$, $\sin^2\theta_W$, RG boundary data |

| $\mu_G$ and common-scale transport | SchemeScale | fixed gauge-matching convention on the adopted branch; not an identification with $\mathfrak A_{PU}$ or $\mu_\lambda$ | T2 for matching convention; T3 for empirical extraction comparisons | gauge, Yukawa, neutrino, and common-scale tables |
| $\mathcal M_\gamma$ | target-shift datum | branch-defining; unit value only after (T.22a.2)--(T.22a.3) are accepted | T2 | $\lambda_{\mathrm{elastic}}$, $\lambda_{\mathrm{PU}}$, and every downstream Higgs row |
| $\mathfrak M_\lambda$ and $\mathcal C_{\mathrm{crit}}$ | PU-to-SM quartic matching and marginality data | currently no accepted matching record; marginality is an additional branch input | T2 | SM quartic boundary, top criticality relation, and $m_H$ |
| $\mathcal R_{\mathrm{RG}},\mathcal C_{\mathrm{dec}},\mathcal C_{\mathrm{pole}}$ | RG scheme, decoupling, and running-to-pole conversion | declared branch-defining conventions; no accepted PU-internal pole record currently closes the Higgs row | T2, with T3 for experimental pole extraction | $m_H$ and every pole-level observable |
| $A_{EW}$ | determinant-model prefactor | model layer by Theorem T.29.2 | model allowance at the stated working order | $v$, quantities using $v/M_{Pl}$, and transferred prefactor rows |
| $(\mathcal T_{E_8},\mathcal V)$ | flavor-geometric ThresholdData / model profile | branch-fixed data for Theorems T.72-T.73 | T1 for geometric truncations; T2 for branch and normalization choices | charged-lepton and quark Yukawa ratios and normalizations |
| top-sector normalization $y_t(\mu_G)=1$ | boundary normalization | branch boundary condition | T2 | absolute Yukawa scale and seesaw normalization |
| Majorana $A_2$ geometry and anchored neutrino reading | branch geometry | branch/model layer as recorded in Proposition T.24.28 | T2 | neutrino mass hierarchy and PMNS geometry |
| type-I seesaw and $M_R=\mu_G$ identification | sector-linking identification | conditional branch input | T2 | absolute light-neutrino masses |
| CKM/PMNS CP-loop, response, and profile data $\mathcal B$ | PhenomenologicalKernel / ThresholdData | branch-fixed loop, response, orientation, and profile data | T2 for response/profile branches; T3 for phase-convention or extraction comparisons | CKM, PMNS, Jarlskog, baryogenesis CP factors |
| common-scale quark reductions | SchemeScale / EmpiricalInput for comparison | comparison convention, not derivation input | T3 | quark-ratio validation tables |
| baryogenesis washout and thermal factors | PhenomenologicalKernel | Appendix Y model layer unless separately derived | T2, with T3 only for observational extraction | $\eta_B$ comparison |

No empirical mass, mixing, or pole value is permitted to enter the derivation side of this ledger. Empirical quantities may appear only in the comparison columns governed by Convention P.14.1c.

*Proof.* The threshold rows follow from Theorem T.78, Definition T.19a, Proposition T.19c, and Corollary T.78.3. The target-shift row follows from Definition T.22a and Theorem T.22b; the quartic-matching and marginality row follows from Definition T.25.2 and Theorem T.26; and the RG, decoupling, and pole row is the explicit observable-conversion gate of Theorem T.79.2. The matching-scale and common-scale rows follow from the stated RG/matching conventions and Section T.25.5.3. The $A_{EW}$ row follows from Theorem T.29.2. The flavor-geometric rows follow from Theorems T.72–T.73 and Proposition R.3.5f; the Majorana, seesaw, and anchored-reading rows follow from Theorems T.24.11–T.24.15 and Proposition T.24.28. The CKM/PMNS row follows from Theorems T.74–T.76, and the baryogenesis row inherits the Appendix Y model inputs. ## 2. The volume-preserving physical calibration

Introduce a real symmetric traceless shape $S$. Its configuration space is the five-dimensional vector space $\operatorname{Sym}_0(3)$, with fixed Lebesgue measure and classical kinetic term $I_{s}\operatorname{Tr}(\dot{S}^{2})/2$, $I_s>0$. Its physical coupling matrix is

$$
B(S) = \exp(S/2)\,D\,\exp(S/2).
\tag{2.1}
$$

The constraint $\operatorname{Tr}S=0$ is built into the actuator coordinates, for example an orthonormal basis of $\operatorname{Sym}_0(3)$, before optimizing any output. It enforces $\det\exp(S/2)=1$ for every history. It does not set a target value for an eigenvalue.

Append three actual fermion calibration modes $c_{j}$, with Hamiltonian

$$
H_{\mathrm{cal}}(S) = \sum_{ij} c_i^{*}B(S)_{ij}c_j.
$$

Prepare the fixed $N_{\mathrm{cal}}=3$ sector. It is one dimensional: the filled state $|111\rangle$ is an exact eigenstate for every $S$, with energy

$$
V_{\mathrm{cal}}(S) = \operatorname{Tr}B(S) = \operatorname{Tr}(D\exp S).
\tag{2.2}
$$

Off-diagonal hopping annihilates the filled state. The state and its charge providers are therefore S-independent; no uncounted spectral-state preparation or Berry term is used as S changes. There is no normal-order subtraction of this energy. The calibration source directly measures the displayed native positive energy.

<a id="lemma-t795a1-filled-sector-calibration-and-local-stiffness"></a>**Lemma T.79.5a.1 (Filled-Sector Calibration and Local Stiffness).**

Over every real symmetric traceless S, $V_{\mathrm{cal}}$ has exactly one minimum:

$$
\begin{aligned}
B(S^{*}) &= rI,\quad r = (\det D)^{1/3},\\
S^{*} &= \log(rD^{-1}),\quad \min V_{\mathrm{cal}} = 3r.
\end{aligned}
\tag{2.3}
$$

Its sublevels are compact. At S*, for every symmetric traceless A,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{Hess}V_{\mathrm{cal}}[A,A] &= r\sum_{ij}\operatorname{sinhc}((s_i-s_j)/2)^{2}|A_{ij}|^{2}\\
&\ge r\lVert A\rVert_F^{2},
\end{aligned}
\tag{2.4}
$$

where $s_{i}$ are the eigenvalues of $S^{*}$, $\operatorname{sinhc}(x)=\sinh(x)/x$ and $\operatorname{sinhc}(0)=1$. The upper bound is $r\max_{ij}\operatorname{sinhc}((s_i-s_j)/2)^{2}\lVert A\rVert_F^{2}$.

Proof. $B$ is positive and $\det B=\det D$. AM–GM gives $\operatorname{Tr}B\ge 3(\det B)^{1/3}$, with equality only when $B=rI$. The positive solution $X=\exp(S/2)$ of $XDX=rI$ is uniquely $X=\sqrt{r}D^{-1/2}$, proving (2.3). For coercivity,

$$
\begin{aligned}
V_{\mathrm{cal}} &\ge d_{\min}\operatorname{Tr}\exp S \ge d_{\min}\exp(\lambda_{\max}(S)),\\
\lambda_{\max}(S) &\ge \lVert S\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}/2
\end{aligned}
$$

for traceless three-by-three $S$. Thus $V_{\mathrm{cal}}$ tends to infinity at infinity. At $S^{*}$ the derivative of $\exp(S/2)$, evaluated by divided differences in the diagonal frame, gives

$$
B'(0)_{ij} = r\operatorname{sinhc}((s_i-s_j)/2)\,A_{ij}.
$$

Since $\log\det B$ is constant, $\operatorname{Tr}B''=r^{-1}\operatorname{Tr}(B'^{2})$ at $B=rI$. This is (2.4). No global convexity assertion for a weighted matrix exponential is needed. ∎

There is no additional stationary point. In an eigenbasis of $S$, the gradient of $\operatorname{Tr}(D\exp S)$ has off-diagonal entries $D_{ij}\exp^{[1]}(s_i,s_j)$. The divided difference is strictly positive. A constrained critical point has a scalar gradient, hence $D$ commutes with $S$; its diagonal equation is $d_i\exp(s_i)=\text{constant}$. The trace constraint yields precisely $S^{*}$.

### Finite preparation and error

A constructive preparation may remain in the commuting plane $S=\sum_js_jP_j(D)$, $\sum_js_j=0$. This restriction contains the proved unique global minimum, rather than excluding a cheaper competitor. On a registered cube $|s_j|\le R$ containing $S^{*}$, $V(s)=\sum_jd_j\exp(s_j)$ has plane Hessian between $a=d_{\min}\exp(-R)$ and $L=d_{\max}\exp(R)$. Projected gradient steps with step $1/L$ contract distance to $s^{*}$ by at most $q=1-a/L$. Projection is Euclidean onto the fixed convex cube/trace plane. The bound follows by integrating the Hessian along the line segment and using nonexpansiveness of projection. A step implementation error at most $\eta$ gives

$$
\lVert s_n-s^{*}\rVert \le q^{n}\lVert s_0-s^{*}\rVert + \eta/(1-q).
\tag{2.5}
$$

For the actual Slater family $R=1$ contains $S^{*}$, since $\lVert S^{*}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}<\log(11/9)<0.201$. A finite number of steps and coefficient bits supplies every positive requested precision. The simple spectral gaps and finite interval functions are those already owned by N10; degenerate general $D$ can instead use any registered orthonormal basis in each repeated eigenspace, without changing $B$ or $r$.

Alternatively an energy tolerance gives a basis-independent estimate. If $V_{\mathrm{cal}}(B)-3r\le\delta$ and every eigenvalue is $r\exp(t_i)$, with $|t_i|\le M$, then $\sum t_{i}=0$ and

$$
\begin{aligned}
\sum t_i^{2} &\le 2\exp(M)\,\delta/r,\\
\lVert B-rI\rVert &\le \sqrt{2r\exp(3M)\,\delta}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{2.6}
$$

Indeed $\exp t\ge 1+t+\exp(-M)t^{2}/2$ on the interval; the second estimate uses $|\exp t-1|\le\exp(M)|t|$. A compact energy sublevel supplies $M$: each eigenvalue is at most $V_{\mathrm{cal}}$ and at least $r^{3}/V_{\mathrm{cal}}^{2}$. Thus the tolerance is an actual measured energy gap, not a declared mass-identity error.

The preparation objective is the filled calibration sector's energy. Matter, sterile vacuum baselines and actuator kinetic energy can exert additional $S$-dependent forces. They are not silently omitted from a claimed total autonomous minimum. Prepare the calibration with the downstream shape couplings gated off, move the actuator under a registered finite controller, clamp its value, and then enable the downstream couplings. At fixed $S$ the clamp absorbs those forces. A finite ultraviolet/mode and occupation budget makes their norms finite: for a variation $A$, $\lVert\delta B\rVert\le d_{\max}\exp(R)\lVert A\rVert$, and a fermionic second-quantized block with $n_{f}$ modes has derivative norm at most $n_{f}$ times its one-particle bound. The field baselines, controller force, loading providers, switching work and holding hardware remain owned. Zero displacement means no ideal clamp mechanical work; it does not mean zero apparatus cost. A full autonomous equilibrium claim is unnecessary and is not made.

A smooth interpolation of each actuator step over duration $T$ has kinetic action $I_{s}\int\lVert\dot{S}\rVert^{2}/2$ and finite acceleration/force. For a cubic endpoint-flat interpolant its kinetic action is $(3I_s/(5T))\lVert\Delta S\rVert^{2}$ and acceleration magnitude at most $6\lVert\Delta S\rVert/T^{2}$. The calibration energy remains bounded on the fixed program domain. All program memory, evaluation precision, steps and durations are finite at each requested accuracy; no uniformly bounded cost is claimed as accuracy tends to zero.

The fixed ordered Grassmann measure therefore proves the Pfaffian identity with no extra sign. This finite algebra precedes any frequency or continuum limit. At a kernel singularity the inverse/low-energy chart is not used; the full source is retained and the registered nonsingular domain is checked.

The calibration and threshold preserve different physical observables of the same source: trace energy under the shape control, and the signed gauge-current determinant of the unactuated D. They are not claimed to be equal effective actions or restrictions of one master-gradient one-form. Their common scalar r follows from the actual determinant-preserving control and the equal representation weights. Accordingly no T15/master-functional result is silently imported or exported.

<a id="proposition-t795a2-charge-preserving-calibration-energy-instrument"></a>**Proposition T.79.5a.2 (Charge-Preserving Calibration-Energy Instrument).**

The objective $\operatorname{Tr}B(S)$ is the actual energy of the three filled calibration modes. Its operational calibration does not require a coherence between different total charges.

Append three reference fermions of independently fixed energy $Q$ each. Denote $A=|111\rangle_{\mathrm{source}}|000\rangle_{\mathrm{ref}}$ and $B=|000\rangle_{\mathrm{source}}|111\rangle_{\mathrm{ref}}$. Both have total charge three and even relative parity. Their energies are $V_{\mathrm{cal}}(S)$ and $3Q$. Define $W$ to exchange $A$ and $B$ and to be identity on their orthogonal complement. All other sources evolve identically on both arms and their common phases cancel from this response, without removing their physical baseline energy from the resource record. Measuring both Ramsey quadratures identifies $V_{\mathrm{cal}}(S)$ in a preregistered bounded energy interval.

A finite gate independent of the unknown energy uses $A_{\mathrm{gate}}=(\pi/2)|1\rangle\langle 1|_{\mathrm{Ramsey}}\otimes(I-W)$ and $H_{\mathrm{control}}(t)=\hbar f_{T_g}(t)A_{\mathrm{gate}}$. Comparing its actual evolution under the bounded native $H_0$ with the ideal controlled-$W$ gives operator error $\le T_g\lVert H_0\rVert/\hbar$ by Duhamel in the control interaction picture. This does not cancel an unknown native phase. Two gates give at most twice that error, and the complete output-channel error is at most twice the resulting unitary bound. The relevant local bound is $H_{\max}=3d_{\max}\exp(R)+3Q$; other identically evolving sources factor out of this comparison without removing their resource baselines. This known prior makes every chosen gate error achievable with finite $T_g$, bandwidth and work. Source-aware drift tracking is an alternative only when its coefficients are actually supplied.

On $|S|\le R$ the source energy lies in $[3d_{\min}\exp(-R),3d_{\max}\exp(R)]$. Choose the Ramsey time so the entire prior interval for $(V_{\mathrm{cal}}-3Q)t/\hbar$ lies in a registered arc of width less than $\pi$. Both quadratures and that prior remove alias ambiguity. If the measured complex coherence is within $\eta<1/2$ of its unit-circle value, its phase error is at most $2\eta$; the corresponding energy error is at most $2\hbar\eta/t$, with independent $Q$, timing, gate and preparation errors added outward. Bernoulli quadrature sampling gives the usual finite Hoeffding bound. Inadequate precision retains the wider prior interval instead of claiming a smaller minimum gap.

Each gate has peak control norm $\le 2\pi\hbar/T_g$, integrated norm-action $\le\pi\hbar$, derivative peak $\le 2\pi^{2}\hbar/T_g^{2}$ and gross switching bound $\le 4\pi\hbar/T_g$. The initial three filled source fermions, empty reference modes, Ramsey preparation, six-mode exchange hardware, fresh copies and records are owned. Source/reference energy changes and the reference's physical energy $3Q$ are counted; a subsequent reset is not assumed free. All failures and both Ramsey outcomes remain in the instrument.

<a id="proposition-t795a3-complete-finite-weak-current-flavor-instrument"></a>**Proposition T.79.5a.3 (Complete Finite Weak-Current Flavor Instrument).**

This proof completes Theorem T.79.5a §7 on its declared finite homogeneous-probe domain. It is not an assertion that a matrix of weak generators is already a detector, or that a vectorlike gauge probe is a chiral weak representation.

## 1. Full source, ports and a physical current reference

Use the complete canonical chiral and heavy fields, mass couplings, Higgs preparation and shape from Theorem T.79.5a. In a finite periodic box retain a finite set of Fourier momenta containing zero and closed under $p\to -p$. Every homogeneous probe preserves momentum, and the Majorana mass preserves each paired $\{p,-p\}$ Nambu block. In particular the zero-momentum block is exactly invariant. At zero background gauge field the quadratic Hamiltonian $H_{F}$ is diagonalizable by a finite CAR/Bogoliubov transformation. Its exact ground reference, all filled-mode baseline terms, and positive excitation modes are retained. Charged masses and the six neutral masses are those of equations (5.1)–(5.3); there are no momentum/discretization errors for the normalized constant spatial mode in this finite box.

Let N be the number of complex fermion modes carrying the probe action. The three-generation chiral field list has 96 original two-component variables per momentum, including the neutral steriles, and W5 times three Dirac flavors has 60. Thus $N=156$ times the retained momentum count is a valid explicit upper bound. Gauge-neutral source complements and calibration modes remain present but add zero to this current norm bound.

The canonically normalized temporal weak currents are $J_a=d\Gamma(j_a)$, $a=1,2,3$, on the original Weyl/Dirac variables: $j_{a}$ is the weak fundamental generator on each actual left doublet, zero on the right singlets, and the appropriate vectorlike weak generator on the heavy W5 block. In four-component notation this is $P_{L}\otimes t_{a}$ on chiral doublets, not $I\otimes t_{a}$. Canonical variation of the kinetic action gives these currents. $\lVert j_a\rVert\le 1/2$, hence $\lVert J_a\rVert\le N/2$. The Majorana mass changes the free Bogoliubov basis, not this original current definition.

Append one spin-one current reference, with generators $T_a$, $\lVert T_a\rVert=1$, charge $Q_R=T_3$, and Hamiltonian $H_R=2\omega I+\omega T_3$, $\omega>0$. Its three physical energies are $\omega,2\omega,3\omega$. This splitting can be expressed covariantly using the already owned Higgs direction, $H_R=2\omega I-(2\omega/v^{2})(H^*\sigma_aH)T_a$ at $H_0$. The reference's Higgs coupling, loading and energy belong to the apparatus. It is an actual finite source of electric charge and a current orientation, not an undeclared classical phase reference.

The independently calibrated scalar probe coupling acts through

$$
\begin{aligned}
K &= \sum_{a=1}^{3} J_a\otimes T_a,\\
\lVert K\rVert &\le K_{\max} = 3N/2.
\end{aligned}
$$

This is a separately owned current-detector interaction: it contracts the canonical matter weak current with an adjoint reference. It does not substitute a noncommuting operator for a classical gauge potential and then omit the Higgs contact term. The Higgs action and its background current remain in the common source; a matter-species transition has zero matrix element of a Higgs-only identity term. It is invariant under simultaneous weak frame changes and hypercharge acts trivially on the reference. It commutes with total electric charge $Q_F+T_3$, because

$$
K = J_3T_3+(J_+T_-+J_-T_+)/2.
$$

The finite experiment therefore transfers charge to the reference and retains it; it does not apply a charge-changing unitary to matter alone.

## 2. Native-drift pulse and rigorous probability error

For $T>0$ choose $f_T(t)=2\sin^{2}(\pi t/T)/T$ on $[0,T]$. Its integral is one and both endpoint values vanish. The complete Hamiltonian is

$$
H(t) = H_F+H_R+\hbar\epsilon f_T(t)K,
$$

with dimensionless $\epsilon>0$ fixed before reading any flavor result. No drift cancellation is used. In the interaction picture,

$$
\begin{aligned}
U_I &= I-i\epsilon\int f_T(t)K_I(t)\,dt + R,\\
\lVert R\rVert &\le \rho := ((\epsilon K_{\max})^{2}/2)\exp(\epsilon K_{\max}).
\end{aligned}
\tag{2.1}
$$

The Dyson series and the ordered-simplex integral 1/k! prove this bound. It holds on the whole finite Fock/reference Hilbert space, including pair creation, the original filled sea and every spectator sector. It is not a rotating-wave or single-particle truncation.

Let $|a\rangle$ be a single positive charged matter excitation above the actual free ground, with one fixed spin at momentum zero. Let $|b\rangle$ be a positive excitation in the corresponding other member of the doublet, with the identical spin. Prepare the reference in $m=0$ and measure its $m=-1$ output together with the exclusive full matter port $|b\rangle$. All other Fock/reference outputs form the complementary failure effect. No success conditioning is used to renormalize the reported probability.

The matrix element of J+ between the two one-particle states is the one-body current matrix element. Its vacuum term vanishes because a and b are orthogonal species. At rest, the canonical positive-energy Dirac spinor has left-handed norm 1/sqrt(2), so

$$
\langle b|J_+|a\rangle = V_{ba}/2.
$$

For a Majorana active mass mode the same normalized left-handed component contributes its exact $c_{j}$ or $s_{j}$ and Takagi phase; thus $V$ is the appropriate full raising-current entry from Theorem T.79.5a §5: $V_{q}$ for down-to-up quarks, and $V_{\mathrm{light}}^*$ or $V_{\mathrm{heavy}}^*$ for charged-lepton-to-neutrino transitions (neutrino row, charged-lepton column). The e-row/neutrino-column matrices displayed there are the lowering-current coefficients. The spin-one matrix element $\langle m=-1|T_-|m=0\rangle=\sqrt{2}$, combined with the factor $1/2$ in $K$, gives

$$
\langle b,-1|K|a,0\rangle = V_{ba}/(2\sqrt{2}).
\tag{2.2}
$$

This factor is derived from the spinor and current-reference normalization; it is not absorbed into a fitted flavor coefficient.

Put $\Delta=E_b-E_a-\omega$ and

$$
F_\Delta = \int_0^T f_T(t)\exp(i\Delta t/\hbar)\,dt.
$$

The exact transition amplitude has leading term $-i\epsilon F_\Delta V_{ba}/(2\sqrt{2})$. Therefore

$$
\begin{aligned}
\bigl|p_{ba}-\epsilon^{2}|F_\Delta|^{2}|V_{ba}|^{2}/8\bigr|
&\le 2\epsilon K_{\max}\rho+\rho^{2}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{2.3}
$$

Native pair-production and other paths are bounded by this full-source remainder. The exclusive complementary outcome is retained, so no omitted-channel probability is relabeled as a successful weak event.

If all admitted port energies are $\le E_{\max}$, then $|\Delta|\le 2E_{\max}+\omega$. The elementary bound $|F_\Delta-1|\le T|\Delta|/\hbar$ shows that choosing

$$
T \le \hbar/[2(2E_{\max}+\omega)]
$$

gives $|F_\Delta|\ge 1/2$ for every registered port. Division by the known Fourier response is then stable. The systematic error in estimating $|V_{ba}|^{2}$ from $8p_{ba}/(\epsilon^{2}|F_\Delta|^{2})$ is explicitly at most

$$
8(2\epsilon K_{\max}\rho+\rho^{2})/(\epsilon^{2}|F_\Delta|^{2}).
$$

It tends to zero with $\epsilon$ on every fixed finite source budget. The small transition probability is not free: for $n$ fresh runs, a Bernoulli probability error $\eta_{p}$ has failure probability $\le 2\exp(-2n\eta_p^{2})$. Apply the displayed division and a union bound over all requested ports. There are finite $n$, pulse lengths and precision bits for every positive tolerance; their growth is part of the resource record.

## 3. Phases, current tomography and neutral leakage

Preparations $(|a_i\rangle+|a_j\rangle)/\sqrt{2}$ and $(|a_i\rangle+i|a_j\rangle)/\sqrt{2}$ use two initial ports of the same electric charge, with the same reference $m=0$. The corresponding leading amplitude is the sum of the two separately known $F_{\Delta}V$ entries. Subtracting the single-port probabilities yields their real and imaginary cross terms. All sums are probabilities of complete physical preparations, rather than interference between differently charged states without a reference. Division by the nonzero known Fourier factors recovers each current row up to its conventional common phase. Row and column rephasings act on the actual preparation/effects and leave the registered current invariants unchanged.

The neutral calculation uses all six Majorana modes. Both light and heavy output ports are measured. In particular the identity $V_{\mathrm{light}}V_{\mathrm{light}}^*+V_{\mathrm{heavy}}V_{\mathrm{heavy}}^*=I$ is tested on the full domain. A missing heavy port is not reported as a nonunitarity-free three-flavor model. The real source has the fixed Takagi phases and zero CP-odd invariant; this does not supply a nonzero baryogenesis CP record.

Full source-aware Fock ground/loading and spectral-port preparation are finite operations on the declared finite CAR carrier. They can use the inherited N10 even, charge-preserving loading constructors for charged modes, and the T09 parity-preserving Majorana apparatus for neutral modes, with explicit providers. Uniform free-mode mass and shape errors produce propagator error $\le T\delta_H/\hbar$, and full-channel probability error $\le 2T\delta_H/\hbar$. Projector errors require the actual gap or are reported as unresolved degenerate port subspaces. Degenerate blocks can be measured as their full spectral effect; no arbitrary splitting is claimed observable.

## 4. Resources and domain

The spin-one reference starts with energy 2omega. Every final charge/energy value is retained. Its raising/lowering charge is supplied physically, and resetting it is another charged preparation operation. The pulse satisfies

$$
\begin{aligned}
\text{peak }\lVert H_{\mathrm{control}}\rVert &\le 2\hbar\epsilon K_{\max}/T,\\
\int\lVert H_{\mathrm{control}}\rVert\,dt &\le \hbar\epsilon K_{\max},\\
\text{peak }\lVert\dot H_{\mathrm{control}}\rVert &\le 2\pi\hbar\epsilon K_{\max}/T^{2},\\
\int\lVert\dot H_{\mathrm{control}}\rVert\,dt &\le 4\hbar\epsilon K_{\max}/T.

The last expression bounds gross switching work; native matter/reference energy changes are not discarded. The full finite Fock baseline, calibration load, spatial volume, all retained modes, current reference, source-aware coefficient table, preparation duration, spectral-port resolution and n fresh-copy/output records are owned. The experiment is a controlled global current test in a finite periodic box. It does not prove local autonomous detector construction, bounded-resource zero-error limits, or a full continuum chiral gauge theory.

Within this domain it is a response-faithful physical flavor interface: the actual canonical weak current gives the predicted same-source masses, mixing/residue entries and retained update/readout maps, with a complete instrument and quantitative error. It supplies an observable overlap rather than simply naming three neutral matrix coordinates as weak flavors.

## 5. Explicit finite loading and readout controls

The preparation/effect statements above admit a bounded finite control realization; no exact finite-power instantaneous gate is needed. On the registered finite CAR space diagonalize the known charge-conserving quadratic $H_{F}$. Its CAR/Bogoliubov basis change is implemented by finitely many two-mode rotations: ordinary hopping between equal-charge modes, and pair rotations between opposite-charge modes (including neutral pairs). These commute with electric charge and preserve fermion parity. The usual elimination of a finite orthogonal Majorana transformation into plane rotations terminates in at most (2N)(2N-1)/2 rotations; in charge sectors the same elimination can be performed with the stated charge-preserving generators. A possible different reference ground parity is accommodated by an initially owned occupied provider, rather than implemented by a forbidden odd system-only unitary. A diagonal Fock occupation reference is prepared from empty modes and explicitly occupied provider modes of the same charge by hopping swaps. A swap is generated by the even bounded operator $f^\dagger b+b^\dagger f$ with integrated angle $\pi/2$, with its known phase corrected by a number rotation. Providers retain all transferred charge and energy. After the inverse Bogoliubov transformation this prepares the actual ground of $H_{F}$. To load one specified positive excitation, swap a fresh occupied provider into that normalized excitation mode. Neutral Majorana excitations use a neutral fermionic provider; parity is conserved on source plus provider. For every bounded ideal gate $\exp(-iA)$, use the finite pulse $H_{\mathrm{control}}=\hbar f_\tau A$ while retaining the native bounded finite-source Hamiltonian $H_{\mathrm{native}}$. The difference from the ideal gate is at most $\tau\lVert H_{\mathrm{native}}\rVert/\hbar$. Summing this bound over the finite gate list gives a prescribed positive preparation error using finite durations and finite peak controls. It consumes the full baseline bound of the involved source/provider block, not a subtraction of that physical baseline. As elsewhere, improved accuracy can cost increasing bandwidth and work. The resulting preparation trace-distance error adds to the complete output probability bound.

Finally the exclusive port effect $P_{b}$ is the product of the actual mode-occupation projectors specifying one $b$ excitation and the ground occupations of every other mode, together with the reference $m=-1$ projector. It is an even electric-charge-invariant projector. A neutral readout qubit, initialized in $|0\rangle$, can be coupled by the finite generator $(\pi/2)P_{b}\otimes(I-X)$. Its ideal unitary flips that qubit precisely on $P_{b}$; measuring the qubit gives the complete binary instrument $\{P_b,I-P_b\}$. The same native-drift bound supplies a finite implementation. A sequence of mode readouts followed by classical conjunction is an alternative, also retaining every failure record. The spectral basis, providers, coefficient bits, bounded pulse norms, duration and fresh qubits are explicit apparatus resources; no locality or autonomous compilation claim is used.

## 6. Explicit tomography normalization and projector errors

Write $A_i=F_iV_{bi}/(2\sqrt{2})$, so the single-port leading probability is $\epsilon^{2}|A_i|^{2}$. The normalized preparations $(|a_i\rangle+|a_j\rangle)/\sqrt{2}$ and $(|a_i\rangle+i|a_j\rangle)/\sqrt{2}$ have leading amplitudes $-i\epsilon(A_i+A_j)/\sqrt{2}$ and $-i\epsilon(A_i+iA_j)/\sqrt{2}$. Their leading probabilities obey

p_{i\mathrm{Phase}}-(p_i+p_j)/2 &= \epsilon^{2}\operatorname{Im}(A_i\overline{A_j}).
\end{aligned}
$$

The sign in the second identity follows by expanding $|A_i+iA_j|^{2}$. Every finite-pulse/sampling error adds with the displayed coefficients before division by $\epsilon^{2}$ and the known nonzero $F_i\overline{F_j}$. No unnormalized coherent input is assumed.

For port stability use the actual finite Hermitian one-particle/Nambu operator $H$ and a fixed Riesz contour $\Gamma$ enclosing the intended complete spectral cluster. Let $\operatorname{dist}(\Gamma,\operatorname{spec}H)\ge\delta>0$, contour length $\ell_\Gamma$, and $\lVert\tilde H-H\rVert\le\eta<\delta$. The resolvent identity and Neumann bound give

For an isolated eigenvalue with separation $g$ from every other eigenvalue, take the circle of radius $\rho=g/3$ around it, including its full exact spin multiplicity. Then $\delta\ge\rho$ and the bound is $\eta/(\rho-\eta)$. Mode-sign and physical-species projectors are retained, so an unrelated same numerical energy in a different exactly preserved field sector need not be artificially split. If a required contour cannot be certified, the effect is the larger unresolved cluster.

The new neutral domain has an explicit positive gap. Set $a=a_n$ and let $d_{\min},d_{\max},g_D$ be outward positive bounds on the selected $D$ and its adjacent gaps, with $r_{\min}\le r\le r_{\max}$. Since

dm/dd = 2a^{2}d/\sqrt{r^{2}+4a^{2}d^{2}},

adjacent light and adjacent heavy masses are separated by at least

Also $m_{\min}\ge a^{2}d_{\min}^{2}/[r_{\max}+a^{2}d_{\max}^{2}/r_{\min}]>0$, $m_{\max}\le a^{2}d_{\max}^{2}/r_{\min}$, and every heavy mass is at least $r_{\min}$. Thus a lower gap between light and heavy sets is $r_{\min}-m_{\max}$ whenever positive, and the signed positive/negative neutral gap is at least $2m_{\min}$. For the frozen $a=1/100$, $d\in(1/5,1/2)$, $r\in(1/8,1)$, $r_{\min}-m_{\max}>0$. The selected $D$ intervals in Theorem K.6.6d, Exact Mass Boxes and Full Labeled-Current Pullback, give $g_{D}>0$ by separated exact rational enclosures. These bounds, together with the accepted full-source complement gaps, supply the Riesz contours for the actual new ports.
