All finite coefficient approximants are compiled in exact total-electric-charge and total-parity blocks of source plus providers. If an initial matrix approximation does not have this property, apply the conditional expectation $X\to\sum_b P_bXP_{b}$ onto the registered joint blocks before implementation. It fixes every ideal gate generator above and is operator-norm contractive, so its approximation and integrated Duhamel error do not increase. Positive approximants and zero endpoints can be preserved blockwise. This enforces the stated charge/parity binding compilation condition on the supplied source rather than treating a small charge-violating term as an exact physical symmetry.

The full matter carrier and all preparation/compiler costs use $N_{\mathrm{full}}=(4d_E+144)|P|$ with $d_E=2\cdot 2^{72}-1$, as in Definition W.6a.1. The current-active bound $N=156|P|$ bounds only the new current. Its neutral complementary modes retain their baseline, native evolution, occupation preparation, memory and hardware costs. Calibration/reference modes, the original mediator archive/reserve, loading providers, current reference, controller, readout and records are additional resources. The source-defined coefficient tables are registered before the outputs; no selection theorem for another owner follows from this construction.

### T.79.5b Predictive Heat, Coherent Fibers and Common Packet

<a id="theorem-t795b-predictive-heat-coherent-fibers-and-common-packet"></a>**Theorem T.79.5b (Predictive Heat, Coherent Fibers and Common Packet).** The specified coherent source on $\mathrm{Gr}(2,8)$ has the complete Berezin spectrum, an actual proper-score Schur Hessian and a normalized same-clock finite collision approximation to the Bures scalar heat kernel. At the registered forward paths and thirteen marked triads, the actual coherent incidence and common packet have the certified derivatives, absolute normalization and nonzero residuals below. All derivative constants use the original $E_8$-distance parameter $s$, with Bures speed $1/\sqrt{8}$.

*Proof.*

**Proof component 1: Spectrum And Heat Limit.**

**1. Frame and normalized channel**

The span of \((q_1\wedge q_2)^{\otimes k}\) is the irreducible \(U(8)\) representation \(V_k\) of highest weight \((k,k,0,0,0,0,0,0)\). One way to see this is that \((e_1\wedge e_2)^{\otimes k}\) is a highest-weight vector in the tensor product; its group orbit spans precisely the generated irreducible highest-weight summand. The Weyl dimension product is

\[
 d_k=\prod_{i=1}^2\prod_{j=3}^8\frac{k+j-i}{j-i}
 =\frac{(k+7)!(k+6)!}{7!6!(k+1)!k!}.
\]

Schur's lemma and trace one imply

\[
 \int_M\Pi_{P,k}\,d\nu(P)=I_{V_k}/d_k.
\tag{T.79.5b.1.1}
\]

Thus \(d_k\Pi_{P,k}d\nu(P)\) is a normalized POVM. Its measure-and-prepare channel and its associated scalar response operator are

\[
 \Phi_k(A)=d_k\int_M\operatorname{Tr}(\Pi_{P,k}A)\Pi_{P,k}\,d\nu(P),
\qquad
 (B_k f)(P)=d_k\int_M K_k(P,Q)f(Q)\,d\nu(Q).
\tag{T.79.5b.1.2}
\]

The channel is completely positive and trace preserving. The scalar operator is positive self-adjoint, unital and positivity preserving; it has finite-dimensional image. In particular its eigenvalues lie in \([0,1]\). The derivation below determines all of them, including their multiplicities. The general orbit-POVM construction and Gelfand-pair convolution theorem are documented in Shmoish (2021). The specialization and constants here are derived directly.

**2. Radial measure and polynomial calculation**

Fix \(P_0\). Let \(x_1,x_2\in[0,1]\) be the eigenvalues of \(P_0QP_0\) on \(\operatorname{ran}P_0\); they equal \(\cos^2\theta_i\). The invariant radial measure, with both orders included, is

\[
 630(x_1-x_2)^2(1-x_1)^4(1-x_2)^4\,dx_1dx_2.
\tag{T.79.5b.1.3}
\]

For completeness its Jacobian follows by writing a full-rank frame as the QR normalization of an \(8\times2\) complex Gaussian matrix. Splitting its top 2 and bottom 6 rows yields independent complex Wishart matrices of ranks 2 and 6. The eigenvalues of \(A(A+B)^{-1}\) have Jacobian \(\prod x_i^{2-2}(1-x_i)^{6-2}\prod_{i<j}(x_i-x_j)^2\); the unitary angular integrals are constant. Normalization is checked without a probability convention: \(\int\Delta(x)^2\prod(1-x_i)^4 dx=2[B(3,5)B(1,5)-B(2,5)^2]=1/630\).

Set \(p_j(x)=P_j^{(4,0)}(2x-1)\). The Rodrigues formula is

\[
 p_j(x)=\frac{(-1)^j}{j!(1-x)^4}
 \frac{d^j}{dx^j}\big[x^j(1-x)^{j+4}\big].
\]

Repeated integration by parts gives, for integers \(t\ge0\),

\[
 I_j(t):=\int_0^1x^t(1-x)^4p_j(x)dx
 =\begin{cases}
 \displaystyle\frac{t!^2(j+4)!}{j!(t-j)!(t+j+5)!},&t\ge j,\\
 0,&t<j.
 \end{cases}
\]

No boundary term survives: before the last integration the factor at zero has sufficient order, and the order at one is at least five. Also
\(p_j(1)=\binom{j+4}{j}\) and
\(p'_j(1)/p_j(1)=j(j+5)/5\).

For integers \(m\ge n\ge0\), put \(a=m+1,b=n\) and

\[
 C_{ab}=\binom{a+4}{a}\binom{b+4}{b}\frac{(a-b)(a+b+5)}5,
\quad
 \varphi_{mn}(x_1,x_2)=
 \frac{p_a(x_1)p_b(x_2)-p_a(x_2)p_b(x_1)}{(x_1-x_2)C_{ab}}.
\]

These are symmetric polynomials, with \(\varphi_{mn}(1,1)=1\). Their removable diagonal is defined by the derivative formula. Orthogonality follows by expanding the determinant and using the one-variable Jacobi orthogonality. The partitions \((m,n)\) index a complete orthogonal basis of symmetric radial polynomials; density follows from symmetric polynomial approximation on the compact square.

Here is the representation identification needed for multiplicities, rather than merely a radial list. The compact spherical decomposition and its finite tensor cutoff are also given by Proposition 3.1 and Theorem 4.2 of Zhang (1998); the present descending partition order reverses his ascending order. The symmetric pair \(U(8)/(U(2)\times U(6))\) is multiplicity free: inversion fixes each double coset, because its principal angles are unchanged; the inversion anti-automorphism consequently makes convolution of bi-invariant functions commutative. The dominant highest weights having a stabilizer-fixed vector are

\[
 \lambda_{mn}=(m,n,0,0,0,0,-n,-m),\qquad m\ge n\ge0.
\]

They follow equivalently by the two-column invariant-tensor construction: contract all but \(m+n\) fundamental and \(m+n\) dual factors with the stabilizer, then remove traces. The surviving ordered row lengths are \((m,n)\); the traceless highest-weight vector has the displayed weight. The determinant polynomials above are its normalized stabilizer-fixed matrix coefficients: both have that leading partition, are orthogonal to lower partitions, and have value one at the identity. Thus the associated full representation has multiplicity

\[
 D_{mn}=\prod_{1\le i<j\le8}
 \frac{\lambda_i-\lambda_j+j-i}{j-i}.
\]

This also yields the finite tensor decomposition
\(\operatorname{End}V_k=\bigoplus_{0\le n\le m\le k}V_{\lambda_{mn}}\): the same two-column contraction construction in \(V_k\otimes V_k^*\) permits precisely those row lengths, each once. In particular \(\sum_{m\le k,n\le m}D_{mn}=d_k^2\).

Convolution by the bi-invariant kernel in (2) acts by a scalar on each such irreducible summand. Andreief's two-by-two determinant expansion gives its scalar as the ratio

\[
 b_{mn}(k)=
 \frac{[I_{m+1}(k+1)I_n(k)-I_{m+1}(k)I_n(k+1)]/C_{m+1,n}}
 {[I_1(k+1)I_0(k)-I_1(k)I_0(k+1)]/6}.
\]

Substitution and cancellation of factorials yield the complete answer

\[
 \boxed{b_{mn}(k)=
 \frac{k!(k+1)!(k+7)!(k+6)!}
 {(k-m)!(k+1-n)!(k+7+m)!(k+6+n)!}}
 \quad(0\le n\le m\le k),
\tag{T.79.5b.1.4}
\]

and zero for \(m>k\). Each positive eigenvalue is counted with its representation multiplicity \(D_{mn}\); accidental equal eigenvalues have summed multiplicity. Constants have eigenvalue one. For \(k=1\), the list is \((1,1),(1/9,63),(1/36,720)\), where each pair is (eigenvalue, multiplicity). Exact consistency identities are

\[
 \sum D_{mn}b_{mn}=d_k,\qquad
 \sum D_{mn}b_{mn}^2=d_k^2/d_{2k}.
\]

The second follows alternatively from \(K_k^2=K_{2k}\) and (1). The checker tests these identities in exact rational arithmetic over a nontrivial range; the preceding derivation proves them for every \(k\).

**3. The metric normalization and limiting eigenvalues**

The radial differential operator for the weight in (3) is

\[
 J=\sum_{i=1}^2\left[x_i(1-x_i)\partial_i^2+
 \left(1-6x_i+\frac{2x_i(1-x_i)}{x_i-x_j}\right)\partial_i\right],\quad j\ne i.
\]

Writing \(\Delta=x_1-x_2\) and
\(D_i=x_i(1-x_i)\partial_i^2+(1-6x_i)\partial_i\),
\(J=\Delta^{-1}(D_1+D_2)\Delta+6\). Since \(D_ip_j=-j(j+5)p_j\),

\[
 J\varphi_{mn}=-c_{mn}\varphi_{mn},\qquad
 c_{mn}=m(m+7)+n(n+5).
\]

In graph coordinates \(Z\in\operatorname{Hom}(\mathbb C^2,\mathbb C^6)\) at the base point, the retained Bures metric is \(g_B=\tfrac12\operatorname{Tr}(dZ^*dZ)\). Its real-coordinate Laplacian has coefficient 2 at that point. Comparing this principal symbol with the radial expression gives

\[
 \Delta_B=8J.
\]

An independent normalization check is \(f(Q)=\operatorname{Tr}(P_0Q)-1/2\): \(Jf=-8f\), while at \(Z=0\), \(f=3/2-\|Z\|^2+O(\|Z\|^4)\), so \(\Delta_Bf=-96=-64f\). Thus the first nonconstant eigenvalue of \(-\Delta_B\) is 64, not the Ricci constant 32.

On the finite image of \(B_k\), define
\(\Lambda_k=\nu_0I-8k\log B_k\) with \(\nu_0\ge0\). Its eigenvalues are \(\nu_0+\ell_{mn}(k)\), where \(\ell=-8k\log b\). The product form of (4) gives

\[
 \ell_{mn}(k)\longrightarrow8c_{mn}.
\tag{T.79.5b.1.5}
\]

This is a derived rate and metric scaling, not a fit to a desired eigenvalue.

**4. Explicit six-derivative fixed-time convergence**

For \(k\ge2(m+8)\), define the integer

\[
 A_{mn}=\sum_{i=0}^{m-1}[(8+i)^2+i^2]
       +\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}[(7+i)^2+(1-i)^2].
\]

The elementary estimate \(|\log(1+u)-u|\le u^2\) for \(|u|\le1/2\) gives

\[
 |\ell_{mn}(k)-8c_{mn}|\le8A_{mn}/k.
\tag{T.79.5b.1.6}
\]

For every \(m\le k\), without this size restriction, \(\log v\ge(v-1)/v\) applied to each factor gives

\[
 \ell_{mn}(k)\ge\frac{8k}{k+m+8}c_{mn}
 \ge\frac45c_{mn}.
\tag{T.79.5b.1.7}
\]

The normalized Haar heat kernels have expansions

\[
 H_{k,t}(P,Q)=e^{-\nu_0t}\sum_{m\le k,n\le m}
 D_{mn}e^{-t\ell_{mn}(k)}\varphi_{mn}(P,Q),
\]
\[
 H_t(P,Q)=e^{-\nu_0t}\sum_{m\ge0,n\le m}
 D_{mn}e^{-8tc_{mn}}\varphi_{mn}(P,Q).
\tag{T.79.5b.1.8}
\]

For a path whose defining fundamental generator has norm at most \(1/2\), the representation \(V_{\lambda_{mn}}\) is a subrepresentation of \((m+n)\) fundamental and \((m+n)\) dual factors. Its generator norm is at most \(m+n\le2m\). A normalized matrix coefficient therefore satisfies
\(|\partial_s^j\varphi_{mn}|\le(2m)^j\); also \(|\varphi|\le1\). These bounds hold for the original path normalization. Products of up to six such vector fields admit the same estimate, giving a fixed homogeneous-atlas \(C^6\) topology.

Fix \(0<t_0\le t\le T\), \(0\le j\le6\), \(R\ge1\), \(k\ge2(R+8)\). Let \(w_j(m)=(2m)^j\) for \(m\ge1\) and \(w_0(0)=1\), \(w_j(0)=0\) for \(j>0\). Then

\[
 \|\partial_s^j(H_{k,t}-H_t)\|_\infty
 \le \frac{8T}{k}\sum_{m\le R,n\le m}D_{mn}w_j(m)A_{mn}
 +4\,9^{28}2^j\sum_{m>R}m^{29+j}e^{-a m^2},
\quad a=4t_0/5.
\tag{T.79.5b.1.9}
\]

Indeed the finite prefix uses (6) and the Lipschitz bound for \(e^{-tx}\) on \(x\ge0\). For the tails, \(D_{mn}\le(2m+7)^{28}\le9^{28}m^{28}\), there are \(m+1\le2m\) labels, and both kernels obey (7). All bounds retain their source normalization; divide (9) by \(V_B\) for \(\mu\).

The remaining series has an explicit certificate. Put \(p=29+j\). If
\(r=\exp[p/(R+1)-a(2R+3)]<1\), successive terms beyond \(R\) have ratio at most \(r\), so

\[
 \sum_{m>R}m^pe^{-am^2}
 \le\frac{(R+1)^pe^{-a(R+1)^2}}{1-r}.
\tag{T.79.5b.1.10}
\]

Equations (9)–(10) give a finite algorithm for any requested absolute error: increase \(R\) until the tail is small, then increase \(k\) until the finite prefix is small. Outward rational bounds for exponentials make the algorithm fully certified. The bounds are deliberately conservative and do not assert economical resource scaling.

**Proof component 2: Predictive Source.**

**1. Fixed source and exact finite cubature**

Let \(M=\mathrm{Gr}(2,8)\), with normalized invariant measure \(\nu\), and let \(\Pi_{x,k}=|\Omega_{x,k}\rangle\langle\Omega_{x,k}|\), where \(\Omega_{x,k}=(q_1\wedge q_2)^{\otimes k}\). Its irreducible span has dimension

\[
d=d_k=\frac{(k+7)!(k+6)!}{7!6!(k+1)!k!}.
\]

The established coherent frame is \(d\int\Pi_xd\nu(x)=I\), and
\(B_k(x,y)=d\operatorname{Tr}(\Pi_x\Pi_y)\). All source modes, including the complement of that span in the underlying fixed-particle-number cells, remain present with the source's full-carrier identity completion.

There is an exact positive quadrature with \(S\le d^4+1\) nodes \(x_i\) and positive weights \(w_i\), \(\sum_iw_i=1\), satisfying

\[
\sum_iw_i\Pi_i\otimes\Pi_i=\int\Pi_x\otimes\Pi_xd\nu(x). \tag{T.79.5b.2.1}
\]

**Proof and constructor.** The integrand is a continuous map into the real vector space of Hermitian operators on a \(d^2\)-dimensional space, of real dimension \(d^4\). Its integral lies in the convex hull of its compact range: otherwise a separating real linear functional would be strictly smaller on the whole range than at its integral. The elementary convex-hull reduction removes one node whenever an affine dependence exists, leaving at most \(d^4+1\). Compactness makes this convex hull closed. Partial trace of (1) gives the first frame moment as well. Zero-weight nodes can be deleted.

For a terminating exact finite constructor, use orthonormal two-frames in \(\mathbb C^8\) as real polynomial variables and coherent coordinates in a fixed algebraic orthonormal basis of the irreducible span. Both sides of (1) have algebraic entries: invariant moments of polynomial unitary entries are the unique invariant tensor projection, found by finite linear algebra over algebraic numbers (equivalently integrate the finite tensor representation by its invariant orthogonal projector). Quantifier elimination over real closed fields finds a sample point of the nonempty compact semialgebraic moment system. This defines algebraic nodes and weights. It is a finite terminating constructor, not an assertion that its very large table has been computed. The table, its construction and desired coefficient precision are explicit resource coordinates. No unproved efficient cubature bound is used.

Set
\[
 B_{ij}=d\,w_j\operatorname{Tr}(\Pi_i\Pi_j). \tag{T.79.5b.2.2}
\]
Then \(B1=1\), \(w_iB_{ij}=w_jB_{ji}\), and \(B\) is a positive-semidefinite contraction on \(\ell^2(w)\). Positivity follows from the Gram representation. Its nonzero spectrum is exactly the coherent channel spectrum: the two products of the analysis and synthesis maps have the same nonzero eigenvalues, and (1) makes the finite quantum channel equal to the invariant channel on every matrix. Extra quadrature-label directions have eigenvalue zero. They remain in the physical register and in the predictive task.

The actual finite instrument on the coherent span is \(E_j=d w_j\Pi_j\). On the full operational carrier add the effect \(E_\perp=I-P_{V_k}\), archive its input and flag, and prepare a fixed reference output. This complement has exactly zero probability on the declared coherent inputs, but is part of the full channel and its capacity. Thus no identity on the irreducible code is silently treated as the identity on all \(28^k\) source levels. On input \(\Pi_i\), its probability is (2); after outcome \(j\), a fresh source block is prepared in \(\Pi_j\). Every outcome and the old block are archived. The binary terminal test is the full Lüders instrument with Kraus operators \(\Pi_y\) and \(I-\Pi_y\), using a retained binary-pointer completion. Its yes probability on \(\Pi_i\) is \(K(i,y)=\operatorname{Tr}(\Pi_i\Pi_y)\). Fine-graining the failure sector and forgetting its label is not substituted for this binary channel.

**2. An actual proper prediction task**

Draw \(I\sim w\), then prepare \(\Pi_I\) and obtain \(J\) using the instrument (2). Draw an independent fair bit \(Y\in\{0,1\}\). The predictor is told \((I,J)\) and predicts this bit with probability

\[
 p_{u,v}(Y=1\mid I=i,J=j)=\sigma(u_i-v_j),\quad \sigma(z)=(1+e^{-z})^{-1}. \tag{T.79.5b.2.3}
\]

The target and endpoint sampling do not depend on the boundary intervention. The intervention supplies finite real logits \(u,v\). Cross entropy is a strictly proper score. One event has loss \(\ell(z,Y)=\log(1+e^z)-Yz\). Averaging the fair bit and subtracting its fixed reference \(\log2\) gives \(\log\cosh(z/2)\). The physical score exposure is \(4a\) per unit physical time, where \(a=4k/t_c\). Its expected excess loss rate is

\[
\mathcal R(u,v)=4a\sum_{ij}w_iB_{ij}\log\cosh[(u_i-v_j)/2]. \tag{T.79.5b.2.4}
\]

Exposure means an owned event clock or repeated independent trials with the stated total duration. It is not a claim that the random number of trials is free. A dimensionless score can be converted to an independently registered work/stakes unit, if desired; that conversion does not change the Hessian's clock normalization and is not inferred from Landauer erasure.

At \((u,v)=0\), the Hessian in \(\ell^2(w)\oplus\ell^2(w)\) is

\[
D^2\mathcal R(0)=a\begin{pmatrix}I&-B\\-B&I\end{pmatrix}. \tag{T.79.5b.2.5}
\]

Indeed \(\log\cosh(z/2)=z^2/8+O(z^4)\), and reversibility gives \(\sum w_iB_{ij}(u_i-v_j)^2=\|u\|_w^2+\|v\|_w^2-2\langle u,Bv\rangle_w\). The internal Hessian is exactly \(aI>0\). Thus the visible/internal split and its internal invertibility arise from the specified proper prediction experiment.

**3. Boundary forcing, unique internal response and a finite-amplitude bound**

Impose \(u\). Adjust the internal logits to the unique minimum \(v_*(u)\) of (4). The internal equations are

\[
\sum_iB_{ji}\tanh[(u_i-v_j)/2]=0\quad\text{for each }j. \tag{T.79.5b.2.6}
\]

Each left-hand side is strictly decreasing in \(v_j\), with opposite signs at \(\pm\infty\); therefore each solution exists and is unique. It lies between \(\min_i u_i\) and \(\max_i u_i\). In particular \(\|u\|_\infty\le\eta\) implies \(\|v_*\|_\infty\le\eta\). Monotone bisection is an actual terminating finite-precision internal controller. On this interval the magnitude of the derivative of the left side is at least \(\tfrac12\operatorname{sech}^2\eta\), giving its explicit stopping/error criterion. The exact source model is its analytic limit; finite experiments retain their stated stopping tolerance.

Define the measured boundary flux to be the gradient of the expected proper-score loss with respect to the imposed boundary logit:

\[
 j_i(u)=2a\sum_jB_{ij}\tanh[(u_i-v_{*,j})/2]. \tag{T.79.5b.2.7}
\]

This is a measurable response: condition on input \(I=i\) and average the score-gradient sample \(4a[\sigma(u_i-v_J)-Y]\). Such samples have magnitude at most \(4a\); their clock, endpoint preparations and records are charged. Every boundary coordinate can be measured by a finite list of interventions. No inaccessible internal energy current is relabeled as this score-gradient flux.

Using \(|\tanh x-x|\le|x|^3/3\), equations (6)–(7) give

\[
\|v_*(u)-Bu\|_\infty\le\tfrac23\eta^3,
\qquad
\|j(u)-a(I-B^2)u\|_\infty\le\tfrac43a\eta^3. \tag{T.79.5b.2.8}
\]

Hence the actual linear boundary response is the Schur complement

\[
D j(0)=a(I-B^2),\qquad t_cD j(0)=\Lambda_k=4k(I-B^2). \tag{T.79.5b.2.9}
\]

There is no inverse on the constant zero mode: only the invertible internal block is eliminated. Constants are the common-logit gauge and give zero flux exactly. For the basis intervention \(u=\eta e_l\), the normalized measured column has deterministic finite-amplitude error at most \(4a\eta^2/3\). An internal logit error \(\delta_v\) adds at most \(a\delta_v\) to the flux because the derivative of \(2\tanh(z/2)\) is at most one. A fixed input \(i\) has bounded independent samples, so Hoeffding gives
\(\Pr(|\widehat j_i-j_i|>h)\le2\exp[-Nh^2/(32a^2)]\). This supplies finite trial, precision and duration reservations for every requested positive response error. The exact static operator is the derivative of the specified experiment, not a fitted mass matrix.

**Proof component 3: Physical Clock And Heat.**

**1. Generator and the physical terminal lift**

Write \(a=4k/t_c\) and \(0<\epsilon\le1/2\). On the two-layer classical register \(\{0,1\}\times\{1,\ldots,S\}\), let

\[
\mathcal L_\epsilon=a\begin{pmatrix}I&-B\\-B/\epsilon&I/\epsilon\end{pmatrix}. \tag{T.79.5b.3.1}
\]

The backward generator is \(-\mathcal L_\epsilon\). At layer0 jump to layer1 at rate \(a\), using transition B; at layer1 jump to layer0 at rate \(a/\epsilon\), again using B. The stationary probability is \((w,\epsilon w)/(1+\epsilon)\); detailed balance follows from \(w_iB_{ij}=w_jB_{ji}\). The layer variable is physical. No residence-time clock is substituted for the elapsed physical clock.

Prepare layer0 and apply the coherent POVM to \(\Pi_x\). Its register distribution is
\(p_i(x)=d w_i\operatorname{Tr}(\Pi_x\Pi_i)\). To read at time \(t_c\tau\):

* on layer0, prepare \(\Pi_i\) and perform the full binary projector instrument \(\{\Pi_y,I-\Pi_y\}\);
* on layer1, first perform one B transition using the same coherent instrument, prepare its output state and perform that identical binary test.

The layer, transition and failure records are retained. If the visible likelihood is \(f_i=\operatorname{Tr}(\Pi_i\Pi_y)\), the terminal observable is exactly \(Jf=(f,Bf)\). The starting state is only on layer0. Thus the positive unital lift is a terminal randomized measurement, not a special unnormalized initial density or discarded layer. Let P select the initial visible component. The intermediate visible response is

\[
S_{\epsilon}(t)=P e^{-t\mathcal L_\epsilon}J. \tag{T.79.5b.3.2}
\]

It is a Markov map for every \(t\ge0\), although generally not a semigroup. The exact measured probability and its continuous endpoint extension are

\[
 p_{k,\epsilon,\tau}(x,y)=\frac1d\,[B_k S_\epsilon(t_c\tau)B_k](x,y). \tag{T.79.5b.3.3}
\]

This follows by substituting the initial probability \(d w_iK(x,i)\) and the terminal likelihood \(K(j,y)\), with \(K=B_k/d\). Exact quadrature identifies the continuous endpoint features with the finite register's nonzero spectral space. Zero-eigenvalue quadrature surplus is suppressed by both endpoint factors but stays in the physical experiment and prediction task. In particular every yes/no distribution is normalized, with \(0\le p\le1\). The probability is not F. With Bures volume measure \(\mu_B=V_B\nu\), where \(V_B=(\pi/2)^{12}/(6!7!)\), the corresponding density kernel is \(F/V_B\), so the probability pullback is \((V_B/d)(F/V_B)\).

**2. The auxiliary estimate, checked independently**

For a spectral value \(b\in[0,1]\), put \(s=1-b^2\). The two dimensionless decay roots are

\[
r=\frac{1+\epsilon-\sqrt{(1-\epsilon)^2+4\epsilon b^2}}{2\epsilon},\quad
R=\frac{1+\epsilon+\sqrt{(1-\epsilon)^2+4\epsilon b^2}}{2\epsilon}. \tag{T.79.5b.3.4}
\]

Use the cancellation-free expression \(r=2s/[1+\epsilon+\sqrt{(1-\epsilon)^2+4\epsilon b^2}]\). Their polynomial is \(\epsilon z^2-(1+\epsilon)z+s\). Consequently

\[
 s-r=\epsilon r(1-r),\quad s/(1+\epsilon)\le r\le s\le1,\quad R\ge1/\epsilon. \tag{T.79.5b.3.5}
\]

The lifted scalar initial observable is \((1,b)\), so its visible component has initial derivative \(-as\). Therefore

\[
u_b(t)=(1-C)e^{-art}+Ce^{-aRt},\quad
 C=\frac{s-r}{R-r},\quad0\le C\le\frac{\epsilon^2}{4(1-\epsilon)}. \tag{T.79.5b.3.6}
\]

Both coefficients are nonnegative. The slow exponential differs from \(e^{-ast}\) by at most \(a t(s-r)e^{-art}\). For \(r>0\), its supremum is at most \((s-r)/(er)\le\epsilon/e\); for \(r=0\), \(s=0\) and it vanishes. Thus

\[
\sup_{t\ge0}\|S_\epsilon(t)-e^{-ta(I-B^2)}\|_{2\to2}
\le\epsilon/e+\epsilon^2/[4(1-\epsilon)]. \tag{T.79.5b.3.7}
\]

On \([0,T_{\mathrm{phys}}]\), replace \(\epsilon/e\) by \(aT_{\mathrm{phys}}\epsilon/4\). This confirms the parent lemma, including its zero mode and terminal-lift convention. For equal rates \(\epsilon=1\), the slow decay is \(a(1-b)\), which does not equal the static Schur rate \(a(1-b^2)\). That discrepancy is not removed by changing a normalization.

**3. Full spectrum of the measured kernel**

The established coherent spectrum is indexed by \(0\le n\le m\le k\):

 c_{mn}=m(m+7)+n(n+5),

**Proof component 4: Finite Implementation And Admission.**

**1. Finite implementation on one clock**

Fix a finite k, its exact algebraic quadrature, a finite positive observation time \(T_{\mathrm{phys}}=t_c\tau\), and a tolerance \(\zeta>0\). The ideal two-layer generator is implemented by a convergent sequence of finite, fresh-ancilla circuits. No infinite passive bath is hidden in a finite source.

Let \(r_*=a/\epsilon\) and choose an integer \(M\ge r_*T_{\mathrm{phys}}\). Set \(\delta=T_{\mathrm{phys}}/M\) and \(q=r_*\delta\le1\). The stochastic one-step matrix is

\[
 Q_\delta=I-\delta\mathcal L_\epsilon=(1-q)I+qT,
\quad
T=\begin{pmatrix}(1-\epsilon)I&\epsilon B\\ B&0\end{pmatrix}. \tag{T.79.5b.4.1}
\]

At a layer0 input, a fresh coin activates a B transition with probability \(\epsilon q\); at a layer1 input it does so with probability q. Otherwise it leaves the label and layer unchanged. Every activated transition is the coherent preparation, POVM and output preparation specified in Theorem T.79.5b, followed by the layer flip. The coin, outcome, original input and all unused branch registers are kept. This gives (1) from the actual source probabilities; no classical output multiplier is stipulated in place of a channel.

For a stochastic matrix T, the ideal continuous process is \(e^{-t\mathcal L_\epsilon}=e^{-r_*t}\sum_{n\ge0}(r_*t)^nT^n/n!\). The finite circuit is a mixture of \(T^n\) with \(n\sim\mathrm{Binomial}(M,q)\). Coupling these counts, or expanding their generating laws, gives the standard elementary bound \(\operatorname{TV}(\mathrm{Bin}(M,q),\mathrm{Pois}(Mq))\le Mq^2\). One proof couples each Bernoulli(q) to Poisson(q) with mismatch at most $q^{2}$, then uses the union bound. Therefore the induced classical distribution error in l1 is at most

\[

<a id="theorem-t796-certified-flavor-determinacy"></a>**Theorem T.79.6 (Certified Flavor Determinacy).** If $\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{fl}}$ is accepted, then the charged-lepton, quark, neutrino, CKM, PMNS, determinant-orientation, and $\bar\theta$ outputs assigned to that certificate are uniquely determined up to the certified interval $\mathcal R_{\mathrm{fl}}$. If no accepted $\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{fl}}$ exists, those outputs remain model-layer, validation-layer, or branch-classification statements.

*Proof.* Definition T.79.4 specifies the finite generation placement, flavor action, stationary actions, Hessian and Van Vleck data, normalization and determinant-line orientation, holonomy, electroweak matching, RG and pole conventions, and Majorana/seesaw entries needed by the declared output maps. Algorithm T.79.5 checks these entries and their structural independence. An accepted tuple therefore determines the assigned observables with the certified residuals. If no certificate is accepted, this route establishes no certified output interval; absence of a record does not alone prove that two admissible completions give different outputs. Such a non-identifiability conclusion requires the witnesses of Theorem P.14.1f. ∎

<a id="corollary-t797-no-flavor-back-fitting"></a>**Corollary T.79.7 (No Flavor Back-Fitting).** A flavor output may be promoted by Appendix T only through an accepted $\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{fl}}$. Changing generation placement, normalization, holonomy path, threshold input, or residual width defines a revised flavor branch. If the comparison data select the change, the revised comparison is calibration.

*Proof.* Each listed quantity is an input of $\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{fl}}$. The condition $\chi_{\mathrm{fl}}$ verifies acyclic dependencies under Definition 2.4.1d, including independence from the evaluated flavor data. Selecting a revised input to match those data makes the comparison calibration on the revised branch. ∎

<a id="corollary-t798-conditional-flavor-non-identifiability"></a>**Corollary T.79.8 (Conditional Flavor Non-Identifiability).** The certificate route in Theorem T.79.6 supplies no theorem-level numerical output without an accepted $\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{fl}}$. Suppose additionally that two completions satisfy all prior branch constraints, agree on the SM gauge algebra and $N_g=3$, and give different masses, mixing invariants, or CP observables. Then those prior data do not identify the differing output.

Theorem P.14.1f gives the stated non-identifiability. An omitted datum or a change in an intermediate entry alone is insufficient: the change must preserve every prior constraint and survive the physical response map. ∎

<a id="theorem-t798f-exact-neutral-response-and-its-aggregate-germ-obstruction"></a>**Theorem T.79.8f (Exact Neutral Response and Its Aggregate-Germ Obstruction).** On the explicitly registered real six-Weyl source with common positive Majorana block, canonical field/clock normalization, known compact-momentum preparation and parity-preserving instantaneous Ramsey apparatus below, the complete active response is classified by $(G,M)$, where $G=DD^{\mathsf T}$, except that $M$ is invisible to the active process when $G=0$. **2. Two exact even moments and the full response quotient.**

<a id="lemma-t798f1-two-even-moments"></a>**Lemma T.79.8f.1 (Two Even Moments).** On (1)–(5),

$$

<a id="lemma-t798f2-complete-retained-process-fibers"></a>**Lemma T.79.8f.2 (Complete Retained-Process Fibers).** Fix the clock, wavepacket and registered active probes. Two sources with $M,M'>0$ give the same $R(t)$ for all real $t$ if and only if either:

For exact real-algebraic inputs this is a terminating finite decision procedure: symmetry and equalities are algebraic equalities, positive semidefiniteness is equivalent to nonnegativity of all principal minors, and the sign and square-root choices have exact real-root isolation. **4. Sharp finite label tomography and its errors.**

Use the six normalized vectors

The vector `v_ab` is normalized; no additional division of its scalar response is taken. Thus every complex symmetric response is recovered. The same formulas apply to its real part and even moments.

Six is sharp for unrestricted linear second-moment tomography: the real symmetric three-by-three matrices have dimension six. Fewer fixed scalar quadratic probes have a nonzero symmetric matrix in their linear kernel. Adding sufficiently small positive and negative multiples of that matrix to any positive-definite `G` gives distinct positive-definite admissible Grams with equal probe data. For $t>0$, use only the real Ramsey quadrature and define

Spectral functional calculus gives

For the first inequality, Taylor's integral remainder gives $|2(\cos x-1)+x^2|\le x^4/12$. For the second, the stencil is $16\sin^4(x/2)$. Substituting $y=|x|/2$ proves $|16\sin^4(x/2)-x^4|\le|x|^6/6$. Integrating a positive operator-valued measure of total mass $I$ preserves these operator-norm bounds, including every collision and zero mode.

If each scalar real-part estimate in (8) at each of `t,2t` has absolute error at most `epsilon`, (9) gives diagonal errors at most `epsilon` and off-diagonal errors at most `2epsilon`. **4a. All even moments and a terminating rational response calculation.**

S_K(t) = \sum_{k=0}^{K}(-1)^{k}J_{2k}t^{2k}/(2k)!

is rational. Taylor's theorem for the scalar cosine, compressed and integrated as in (5), gives the rigorous operator bound

$$
\begin{aligned}
&\lVert\operatorname{Re}R(t)-S_K(t)\rVert\\
&\quad \le E_{\max}^{2K+2}|t|^{2K+2}/(2K+2)!.
\end{aligned}
\tag{14c}
$$

An independently known rational upper bound for $E_{\max}^2$ makes this an entirely rational enclosure. At any fixed rational time its remainder tends to zero, so increasing $K$ terminates for every positive rational tolerance. This computes actual normalizable readout enclosures, not only their derivatives. It also avoids radical eigenvector evaluation and splitting-field assumptions. The executable packet checks this recurrence against direct block powers and uses (14c) for the populated finite-time contrast.

**5. Full-germ aggregate obstruction on this actual source.**

<a id="lemma-t798f5-exact-real-quadrature-reconstruction-norm"></a>**Lemma T.79.8f.5 (Exact Real-Quadrature Reconstruction Norm).** The following separate refinement improves the conservative valid noise bounds above without changing their source domain.

**1. Complete fixed-map theorem.**

Let the six measured scalar errors be $e_1,e_2,e_3$ for the coordinate probes, and $f_{12},f_{13},f_{23}$ for the normalized pair probes. Suppose each belongs to $[-\epsilon,\epsilon]$. Their exact reconstructed real symmetric matrix error is

$$
\begin{aligned}
E_{ii} &= e_i,\\
E_{ij} &= f_{ij}-(e_i+e_j)/2.
\end{aligned}
$$

Then $\lVert E\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\le c_*\epsilon$, and no smaller constant works on this error cube.

Proof. Homogeneity reduces to $\epsilon=1$. The matrix norm is convex in the six input coordinates, so its maximum on the cube is attained at a vertex. At a vertex every $e_{i}$ and $f_{ij}$ equals +1 or -1. Global sign and coordinate permutation preserve the norm and reduce the diagonal patterns to the following two cases.

First all diagonal errors equal $+1$. Then $E=I-2A$, where $A$ is the adjacency matrix of a simple undirected graph on three vertices: an edge marks $f_{ij}=-1$. Up to permutation the graphs have zero, one, two or three edges. Their adjacency spectra are respectively $(0,0,0)$, $(1,-1,0)$, $(\sqrt{2},-\sqrt{2},0)$, and $(2,-1,-1)$. The resulting operator norms are $1$, $3$, $1+2\sqrt{2}$, and $3$.

Second the diagonal pattern is (-1,1,1). Write

$$
E = \begin{bmatrix} -1 & a & b\\ a & 1 & c\\ b & c & 1 \end{bmatrix},
$$

where $a,b$ belong to $\{-1,1\}$ and $c$ belongs to $\{0,-2\}$. Conjugating by the diagonal orthogonal matrix $\operatorname{diag}(1,a,b)$ makes $a=b=1$ and changes $c$ to one of $0,2,-2$. The vector $(0,1,-1)$ is an eigenvector with eigenvalue $1-c$. Its orthogonal complement has matrix $\begin{bmatrix} -1 & \sqrt{2} \\ \sqrt{2} & 1+c \end{bmatrix}$. Thus:

- $c=0$ gives eigenvalues 1,sqrt(3),-sqrt(3);
- $c=2$ gives -1,1+sqrt(6),1-sqrt(6);
- $c=-2$ gives 3,-1+sqrt(2),-1-sqrt(2).

All have operator norm smaller than $1+2\sqrt{2}$. These cases exhaust the cube vertices, proving the upper bound. The legitimate simultaneous errors $e_1=e_2=e_3=1$, $f_{12}=f_{13}=-1$, $f_{23}=1$ give the two-edge graph and attain $c_*$. In particular, the unattainable relaxed-entry matrix used by the earlier checker to illustrate norm 5 is unnecessary. Every maximizing error here is an actual vertex of the six-scalar error model. End proof.

The model is the deterministic set of scalar error bounds used by the original Hoeffding argument. The inputs are estimates from separate source preparations, so the six error coordinates are not required to be entries of one positive density matrix. No assertion is made that a particular finite-sample empirical error equals an irrational endpoint. On a nondegenerate Bernoulli output family, empirical estimates can approach the displayed cube vertex while retaining the specified inequalities; exact deterministic-map sharpness itself does not require a statistical attainment theorem.

**2. Consequence for the actual response estimator.**

Let $R_R(t)$ denote the real symmetric part measured by Pauli $X$. The T15 source, normalizable momentum packet and detector conventions are retained. Six scalar estimates at $t$, each with error at most $\epsilon$, reconstruct $R_R(t)$ with norm error at most $c_*\epsilon$. A separate set at $2t$ gives the same bound.

The existing second and fourth stencils therefore have the sharpened errors

$$
\begin{aligned}
\eta_G &\le E_{\max}^{4}t^{2}/12 + 2c_{*}\epsilon/t^{2},\\
\eta_{J_4} &\le E_{\max}^{6}t^{2}/6 + 10c_{*}\epsilon/t^{4}.
\end{aligned}
$$

The coefficients 2c_* and 10c_* are exact induced norms of their independent additive-noise maps: align the maximizing vertex at t, and for the fourth stencil choose the opposite vertex at 2t. The Taylor remainder constants are inherited valid bounds and are not asserted sharp. The original nonlinear Gram-square and positive-margin trace-ratio estimates apply unchanged after substituting these smaller $\eta$ values. The same twelve-setting Hoeffding union bound, source-work/copy accounting, known preparation moments and response domain remain required.

No additional physical parameter was learned from this norm improvement. It only supplies the exact finite-probe error propagation constant on the already specified real-response inverse.

The retained response is not thereby a candidate coordinate of the master determinant gradient. Along the isospectral rotation its actual determinant derivative is zero; the nonzero label response remains an independently retained observable. The common RHG/flavor/Higgs gradient, all global periods, determinant constant and complete overlaps remain separate original obligations.

<a id="theorem-t799-common-carrier-flavor-complement-theorem"></a>**Theorem T.79.9 (Common-Carrier Flavor Complement Theorem).** Let $V_u,V_d:\mathbb C^3\to\mathcal H_{\mathrm{int}}$ be isometries for the retained up- and down-type flavor triples, let $P_u=V_uV_u^\dagger$, $P_d=V_dV_d^\dagger$, and define the overlap matrix
$$
C=V_u^\dagger V_d.
\tag{T.79.9.1}
$$
Then
$$
\mathbf1-C^\dagger C
=V_d^\dagger(\mathbf1-P_u)V_d\succeq0,
\qquad
\mathbf1-CC^\dagger
=V_u^\dagger(\mathbf1-P_d)V_u\succeq0.
\tag{T.79.9.2}
$$
Consequently every singular value of $C$ lies in $[0,1]$ and equals the cosine of a principal angle between $\operatorname{ran}V_u$ and $\operatorname{ran}V_d$. Moreover,
$$
\operatorname{rank}(\mathbf1-C^\dagger C)
=\operatorname{rank}\bigl((\mathbf1-P_u)V_d\bigr),
\tag{T.79.9.3}
$$
with the analogous up/down identity, and
$$
C\text{ is unitary}
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\operatorname{ran}V_u=\operatorname{ran}V_d.
\tag{T.79.9.4}
$$

*Proof.* Equation (T.79.9.2) follows by inserting the projectors and using $V_f^\dagger V_f=\mathbf1$. Each right-hand side is a Gram matrix $X^\dagger X$, which proves positivity and the rank identity. Principal-angle theory identifies the singular values of the overlap of two orthonormal frames. If the ranges coincide, the two frames differ by a unitary. Conversely, if $C$ is unitary then (T.79.9.2) vanishes, so $(\mathbf1-P_u)V_d=0$ and the two three-dimensional ranges coincide. ∎

<a id="corollary-t7910-flavor-leakage-falsifier"></a>**Corollary T.79.10 (Flavor-Leakage Falsifier).** Within an accepted isometric common-carrier model, a computed nonzero $\mathbf1-C^\dagger C$, or a measured value outside its registered uncertainty set, is the retained Gram matrix of the down-type component outside the up-type carrier rather than a unitary three-family matrix. Its rank counts the independent leaking directions and its nonzero eigenvalues are the squared sines of the corresponding principal angles. Without the accepted embedding and uncertainty certificate, apparent nonunitarity may instead be model failure or measurement/systematic error. A unitary CKM identification is theorem-level only on the common-range branch (T.79.9.4) or after the complement is explicitly included in the response certificate.

<a id="corollary-t7911-log-hierarchyjarlskog-determinant-identity"></a>**Corollary T.79.11 (Log-Hierarchy/Jarlskog Determinant Identity).** On the common-range branch, take $C$ unitary and strictly positive Yukawa eigenvalues. Define
$$
\ell_{u,i}=\log\frac{y_{u,\max}}{y_{u,i}},
\qquad
\ell_{d,i}=\log\frac{y_{d,\max}}{y_{d,i}},
$$
$$
A_u=\operatorname{diag}(\ell_{u,1},\ell_{u,2},\ell_{u,3}),
\qquad
A_d=C\operatorname{diag}(\ell_{d,1},\ell_{d,2},\ell_{d,3})C^\dagger.
\tag{T.79.11.1}
$$
Then
$$
\left|\det[A_u,A_d]\right|
=2|J(C)|
\prod_{i<j}|\ell_{u,i}-\ell_{u,j}|
\prod_{i<j}|\ell_{d,i}-\ell_{d,j}|,
\tag{T.79.11.2}
$$
where $J(C)=\operatorname{Im}(C_{11}C_{22}C_{12}^*C_{21}^*)$ up to the common row/column orientation convention. Thus the determinant vanishes exactly when $J(C)=0$ or either logarithmic spectrum is degenerate.

*Proof.* The matrices $A_u$ and $A_d$ are Hermitian $3\times3$ matrices: $A_u$ is real diagonal and $A_d=C\operatorname{diag}(\ell_{d,1},\ell_{d,2},\ell_{d,3})C^\dagger$ is Hermitian because $C$ is unitary and the $\ell_{d,i}$ are real. The Jarlskog commutator-determinant identity (Jarlskog 1985) therefore applies and gives, for a specified common ordering of rows and columns,
$$
\det[A_u,A_d]
=2iJ(C)
\prod_{i<j}(\ell_{u,i}-\ell_{u,j})
\prod_{i<j}(\ell_{d,i}-\ell_{d,j}).
$$
The cited identity requires precisely two Hermitian $3\times3$ matrices related to their eigenbases by a unitary matrix; those hypotheses are the definitions of $A_u$, $A_d$, and $C$ in the theorem. Reversing an eigenvalue ordering changes the signs of one Vandermonde product and the orientation convention for $J(C)$, but not the absolute value. Hence
$$
\left|\det[A_u,A_d]\right|
=2|J(C)|
\prod_{i<j}|\ell_{u,i}-\ell_{u,j}|
\prod_{i<j}|\ell_{d,i}-\ell_{d,j}|.
$$
This product vanishes exactly when $J(C)=0$ or at least one pair of eigenvalues in either spectrum is equal. ∎

Equations (T.79.11.1)--(T.79.11.2) are asserted only when all three Yukawa eigenvalues in each sector are strictly positive. At a zero eigenvalue, the finite $3\times3$ identity is undefined; one may prove the positive-regulator identity at $y_i=\epsilon>0$ and report any $\epsilon\downarrow0$ limit under a separate regulator and normalization certificate. Equation (T.79.11.2) is not asserted for a nonunitary contraction $C$; in that case the complement data of Theorem T.79.9 are response-active.

<a id="theorem-t7912-measured-flavor-frame-fiber-on-the-common-source"></a>**Theorem T.79.12 (Measured Flavor-Frame Fiber on the Common Source).** In the physical chamber of Theorem T.79.8g fix $m=Q_*$, $D=m\operatorname{diag}(1,2,3)$, the four Yukawa normalizations, $H=H_0$, $O_n$, and every non-frame source control. Retain the 12-plane part of its admitted down-frame control:
$$
O_d(\theta)=R_{12}(\theta)O_{d0},\qquad
R_{12}(\theta)=
\begin{pmatrix}\cos\theta&-\sin\theta&0\\\sin\theta&\cos\theta&0\\0&0&1\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
O_{d0}=
\begin{pmatrix}3/5&-4/5&0\\4/5&3/5&0\\0&0&1\end{pmatrix},
\qquad |\theta|<1/100.
\tag{T.79.12.1}
$$
Every point has the same charged masses, six neutral masses, RHG threshold inputs, Higgs background and filled calibration energy. Its actual charged-current matrix in the mass ports is $V_q(\theta)=O_d(\theta)$, and
$$
b(\theta):=|(V_q(\theta))_{12}|^2
=\frac{(4\cos\theta+3\sin\theta)^2}{25}.
\tag{T.79.12.2}
$$
The two admitted values $\theta=0$ and $\theta=\delta=1/1000$ satisfy
$$
b(\delta)-b(0)>d,\qquad d=9/10000.
\tag{T.79.12.3}
$$
The complete weak-current instrument of Proposition T.79.5a.3 separates these sources at finite pulse strength, duration, precision and sample count. Consequently the common fixed data listed above do not identify this current probability on the declared chamber.

*Proof.* Theorem T.79.8g installs $M_u=a_uD$ and $M_d=a_dO_dDO_d^T$ in the actual chiral action. Orthogonal conjugation preserves the down singular masses; the neutral matrices and all other listed source inputs are unchanged. Since $D$ is diagonal with distinct entries, Theorem T.79.5a's current identity gives $V_q=O_d$. Multiplication gives (T.79.12.2).

For $0\le\theta\le\delta$,
$$
b'(\theta)=\frac2{25}
(4\cos\theta+3\sin\theta)(3\cos\theta-4\sin\theta)
$$
and $\sin\theta\le\delta$, $\cos\theta\ge1-\delta^2/2$. Both factors are positive, so integration gives
$$
b(\delta)-b(0)\ge
\frac{8\delta}{25}(1-\delta^2/2)
\bigl[3(1-\delta^2/2)-4\delta\bigr]>9/10000.
$$
The last inequality is exact rational arithmetic.

The two ports have identical masses and reference energy, hence the same Fourier pulse factor $F_\Delta$. Use Proposition T.79.5a.3's duration bound to obtain $|F_\Delta|\ge1/2$. With its fixed finite $K_{\max}\ge1$, choose
$$
0<\epsilon\le\min\{K_{\max}^{-1},d/(768K_{\max}^3)\}.
$$
Write $x=\epsilon K_{\max}\le1$. The proposition's amplitude remainder is $\rho=x^2e^x/2$, and its probability error is bounded by $2x\rho+\rho^2\le6x^3$, using $e<3$. The difference of leading probabilities is at least $\epsilon^2d/32$, while the two remainders together are at most $12\epsilon^3K_{\max}^3\le\epsilon^2d/64$. Therefore the exact complete-event probabilities satisfy
$$
p_\delta-p_0\ge\epsilon^2d/64>0.
\tag{T.79.12.4}
$$
Source preparation and pulse approximants with error at most $\epsilon^2d/256$ per setting retain a gap at least $\epsilon^2d/128$. Their finite existence and resource records are supplied by Theorem T.79.5a §8 and Proposition T.79.5a.3. For any fixed confidence $1-\eta$, choose per-setting Bernoulli error $e_p=\epsilon^2d/512$ and $n\ge\log(4/\eta)/(2e_p^2)$ fresh trials. Hoeffding's inequality and a union bound give a finite separating experiment. Both complete output branches and every charged reference remain in the source record. ∎

<a id="proposition-t7913-hierarchy-fiber-at-a-fixed-calibrated-matching-scale"></a>**Proposition T.79.13 (Hierarchy Fiber at a Fixed Calibrated Matching Scale).** On the general-positive canonical-source alternative of Theorem T.79.5a, fix an energy $Q>0$, the source field representations, all positive $a_f$, the two program frames and the independently owned Higgs amplitude.
