The calibrated sterile coefficient, matching root and minimized calibration energy are independent of $t$:
$$
r=(\det D(t))^{1/3}=6^{1/3}Q,\qquad
B(S_*(t))=rI,\qquad
V_{\mathrm{cal}}(S_*(t))=3r.
\tag{T.79.13.2}
$$
The charged hierarchy varies; for example
$$
\frac{m_{u,1}(t)}{m_{u,2}(t)}=\frac{e^{2t}}2.
\tag{T.79.13.3}
$$
Thus a selector depending on this minimized calibration energy and the other fixed data is constant on this family and cannot uniquely select its hierarchy.

*Proof.* The product of the three entries of $D(t)$ is $6Q^3$. Lemma T.79.5a.1 gives the unique shape minimum $S_*(t)=\log(rD(t)^{-1})$ and (T.79.13.2). The matching-scale equality is the common-source result of Theorem T.79.5a. Its actual charged mass map is $M_u=a_uD(t)$, which gives (T.79.13.3). The eigenvalues remain positive, distinct and in their fixed order throughout the displayed compact interval. Every member is therefore admitted to the theorem's general-positive finite source alternative with its corresponding declared source-aware controls. The final selector assertion follows because all its listed inputs are constant. ∎

These source-owned fibers instantiate Corollary T.79.8 for the specified reduced data. Definition T.79.4 includes the frame and source matrices in the full flavor record, and Theorem T.79.6 determines the outputs when that full record is fixed.

<a id="theorem-t79a-nuclear-extension-determinacy-boundary"></a>**Theorem T.79a (Nuclear Extension Determinacy Boundary).** A finite nuclear operator-package branch specifies a nonempty aggregate Hilbert space and self-adjoint Hamiltonian $H_A^{\mathrm{PU}}(Z,N)$ for each retained proton-neutron sector, together with the daughter-sector, spin-current, transition, decay, preparation, and exterior-channel data needed by each claimed observable.

(i) Non-identifiability from the elementary vector $\Pi_T$ requires two admissible packages agreeing on $\Pi_T$ and differing in a claimed nuclear response. Absence of a nuclear entry alone does not construct those witnesses.

(ii) An accepted complete package determines its spectra, energetic decay thresholds, shell gaps, and declared transition or decay responses. In a degenerate energy subspace, the package must supply the initial density operator or the prescribed average over that subspace. A rate additionally requires its normalization, time-evolution or scattering prescription, and admitted final channels.

(iii) These are conditional operator-package conclusions. A PU nuclear prediction requires the accepted effective-action or response-completeness bridge of Corollary T.79a.1.

*Proof.* For (i), the two-witness hypothesis makes the nuclear response map nonconstant on the admissible completion class, which is the criterion of Theorem P.14.1f. In the broader class of finite many-body Hamiltonians constrained only by their elementary one-particle data and symmetries, the two-body perturbation $Q_A=\binom A2 I$ vanishes for $A=1$ and shifts every $A\ge2$ eigenvalue in $H_A+\eta Q_A$ by $\eta\binom A2$. This gives an explicit response-active example in that class; it is a PU witness only if all additional PU constraints admit both packages.

For (ii), the finite spectral theorem determines
$$
E_0(Z,N)=\min\operatorname{spec}H_A^{\mathrm{PU}}(Z,N),
\qquad
\Delta_N^2E_0=E_0(Z,N+1)-2E_0(Z,N)+E_0(Z,N-1).
$$
For specified daughter sectors and emitted particles,
$$
\Delta E=\sum_iE_0(Z_i,N_i)-E_0(Z,N)
$$
determines the energetic threshold. An energetically allowed channel need not have a nonzero decay rate. For a supplied initial density operator $\rho_i$, final projector $P_f$, and transition operator $\mathcal O$, the inclusive transition strength
$$
\operatorname{Tr}(P_f\mathcal O\rho_i\mathcal O^\dagger)
$$
is basis independent and determined by the package. The declared dynamical and exterior-channel prescription converts the relevant amplitudes or strengths into the claimed rates. A Hamiltonian alone does not choose $\rho_i$ within a degenerate eigenspace. These statements give determinacy precisely for the completed response data, proving (ii) and (iii). ∎

<a id="corollary-t79a1-conditional-boundary-impedance-closure-of-nuclear-data"></a>**Corollary T.79a.1 (Conditional Boundary-Impedance Closure of Nuclear Data).** For a proton-neutron sector $A=(Z,N)$, the boundary response required by a declared nuclear protocol is determined by an accepted finite impedance map $\Lambda_A^{\mathrm{PU}}(E)$ satisfying Definition X.8k.5 and Theorem X.8k.6. To determine the full aggregate spectrum and the spin, transition, and decay quantities of Theorem T.79a, also supply an accepted operator package $\mathfrak B_A^{\mathrm{nuc}}$ of Definition X.8k.6a, or an equivalent certificate proving that every claimed quantity is determined by the retained boundary and operator data.

For $E\notin\operatorname{spec}H_{II}^{A}$, the Schur identity gives the retained bound-state equation
$$
\det\Lambda_A^{\mathrm{PU}}(E)=0.
\tag{T.79a.1}
$$
This equation does not by itself account for boundary-invisible interior states at poles of the Schur map. Those states require the full operator or an additional completeness certificate.

On the registered exterior sheet and away from the interior poles, the resonance equation is
$$
\det\left(\Lambda_A^{\mathrm{PU}}(E)-\Lambda_{\mathrm{out}}(E)\right)=0.
\tag{T.79a.2}
$$
The accepted package must contain the transition, spin-current, decay, daughter-sector, and exterior-channel data needed by each claimed observable, with residuals propagated through its uncertainty ledger.

*Proof.* Theorems X.8k.6 and X.8k.6b give the Schur formulas, including the exclusion of interior poles and the limitation to retained boundary response. Equation (T.79a.1) uses (X.8k.18) on that domain; (T.79a.2) uses (X.8k.19) with the declared exterior continuation. A PCE-selected representative exists under the nonempty compact admissible-set and lower-semicontinuity hypotheses of Theorem X.8k.6b; unique response additionally requires its strictness hypothesis, and unitary equivalence of full operators requires a separate completeness certificate. Once an accepted full operator and all claimed observable operators are supplied on the same retained Hilbert space, their spectra and prescribed matrix elements determine the stated quantities. ∎

**Theorem T.79a.2 (Elementary/Nuclear Separation and Nuclear Completion Criterion).** Let $\Pi_T$ be an accepted Appendix T elementary parameter vector on a fixed electroweak/flavor branch. The nuclear observable vector
$$
\mathcal O_A^{\mathrm{nuc}}
=
\left(
\operatorname{spec}H_A,
\Delta_{\mathrm{shell}},
\mathcal M_A^{\mathrm{spin}},
\mathcal M_A^{\mathrm{tr}},
\Gamma_A^{\mathrm{dec}},
\mathcal R_A^{\mathrm{open}}
\right)
\tag{T.79a.3}
$$
is certified by this operator-package route when every proton-neutron sector and every daughter or exterior channel entering a claimed row carries an accepted $\mathfrak B_A^{\mathrm{nuc}}$ of Definition X.8k.6a, transported by $\Pi_{A\leftarrow T}$ with dependencies independent of the data used to compare the claimed component. Each claimed component must be determined by the full operator and associated response data, with the selection or response-completeness gates of Corollary T.79a.1 where needed. The elementary vector alone does not supply the following nuclear effective-action or boundary-response entries:

1. retained many-body measure and Hilbert-space truncation;
2. finite two-body, three-body, exchange, contact, spin-orbit, and finite-size operators;
3. colorless boundary impedance record $\Lambda_A^{\mathrm{PU}}(E)$;
4. exterior open-channel impedance $\Lambda_{A,\mathrm{out}}(E)$;
5. spin-current operators;
6. transition operators;
7. decay operators;
8. resonance sheet, width, and tail prescription;
9. nuclear uncertainty and covariance ledger.

Consequently, Appendix T elementary closure fixes the elementary currents, charges, masses, mixings, and coupling normalizations that may enter $\Pi_{A\leftarrow T}$, but it does not by itself close isotope stability, magic-number gaps, spin-dependent anomalies, transition rates, or nuclear decay rows.

*Proof.* An accepted package supplies the elementary-to-nuclear overlap map, retained aggregate operator, observable operators, channels, and uncertainty ledger. Under Theorem X.8k.6b's existence and response-uniqueness hypotheses, every claimed component is a spectral or prescribed matrix-element image of those data. For a converse non-identifiability claim, require two completions that satisfy every prior constraint, agree on $\Pi_T$, and differ in a claimed nuclear output. Theorem X.8k.6c is conditional on such an admissible response-active variation; it does not construct one from the absence of an entry. With the two witnesses, Theorem P.14.1f proves that elementary data alone do not identify the differing nuclear row. ∎

### T.79b Finite Two-Cell Nuclear Source

Construction T.79b specifies one finite nuclear source for the ten proton–neutron sectors with $Z+N\le3$. Lemma T.79b.1 and Theorems T.79b.2–T.79b.6 prove its elementary-input, spectral, channel, selection, protocol and input statements, and Proposition T.79b.7 identifies its entries with the eighteen components of Definition X.8k.6a.

<a id="construction-t79b-finite-two-cell-nuclear-source"></a>**Construction T.79b (Finite Two-Cell Nuclear Source).** Fix the energy unit $Q>0$ of the elementary source in item 1. Where no $\hbar$ or $c$ is displayed, formulas use $\hbar=c=1$ in this unit.

1. *Elementary factor.* Each cell of item 3 carries one copy of the $p=0$ field program of the $B-L$ Dirac source of Theorem T.79.5d, built on the supplied legacy triad $(2,4,2)$ of Construction T.79.5b.9 with coefficient $T_Q$: lepton mass matrices $M_\nu=QT_Qh$ and $M_e=QT_QD^\dagger hD$, quark mass matrices $3/\sqrt{43}$ times these, all heavy, complement, calibration and reference factors of that source, its neutral dressing $W_F$, ready projector $p_0$ and holding penalty $B_{\mathrm{ref}}(I-p_0)$ with $B_{\mathrm{ref}}>2\|H_{\mathrm{field}}\|+Q$. Put
$$
H_T=W_F\bigl(H_{\mathrm{field}}\otimes I+I\otimes B_{\mathrm{ref}}(I-p_0)\bigr)W_F^\dagger,\qquad
J_a=W_F(j_a\otimes I)W_F^\dagger,\qquad
\iota_T\psi=W_F(\psi\otimes r_{\mathrm{ready}}),
$$
where $j_-=\sum_{\mathrm{generation,\,spin}}c^\dagger_{e,L}c_{\nu,L}$, $j_+=j_-^\dagger$, $j_\pm=j_x\pm ij_y$ and $j_z=\tfrac12(N_{\nu,L}-N_{e,L})$ is the canonical left-handed lepton current on the 24 lepton modes at $p=0$. The code of a copy is the range of $\Pi_T=\iota_T\iota_T^\dagger$ with its quark, heavy and complement modes in their vacuum; the nuclear source couples to the lepton current only. If $r_{\mathrm{ready}}$ has odd fermion parity, each copy carries a second identical neutral ready reference, so that its ready state is even.

2. *Electromagnetic coefficient.* $e>0$ is the coupling of Theorem W.6a.10, with $e^2\in[0.1166503385721042297833693,\,0.1166503385721042297833694]$.

3. *Carrier.* There are four banks $j\in\{0,1,2,3\}$, each with two cells $\kappa\in\{0,1\}$. Each cell carries four fermionic modes $b_{j,\kappa,f}$, $f\in\{p{\uparrow},p{\downarrow},n{\uparrow},n{\downarrow}\}$, which are effective colorless nucleon fields; the retained nucleon space is the Fock space of these 32 modes with total baryon number $B\le3$, of dimension $\sum_{k=0}^{3}\binom{32}{k}=5489$. Each of the eight cells $(j,\kappa)$ also carries one elementary factor (item 1) and one spin-one mediator with matrices $S_{a;j,\kappa}$, $a\in\{x,y,z\}$, whose states $S_z=\pm1$ carry electric charge $\pm1$. Write $n_{j,\kappa}$ for the nucleon number of a cell, $n_{j,\kappa,f}$ for the occupation of a mode, $B_j$ for the nucleon number of a bank, $Q_{j,\kappa}$ for the electric charge of a cell in units of $e$ (its protons, the normal-ordered charge $6-N_e$ of the charged leptons of its elementary copy, and $S_{z;j,\kappa}$), $Q_{\mathrm m}=\sum_{j,\kappa}Q_{j,\kappa}$, and $T_{a;j,\kappa}$ for the isospin generators of a cell, with $T_+=\sum_{\mathrm{spin}}b^\dagger_pb_n$. One common return island carries a charge register $q_R\in\{-68,\dots,68\}$ with energy $H_R=Q|q_R|$; its neutral code is $q_R=-Q_{\mathrm m}$.

4. *Parameters.* Put
$$
\mu=\frac Q2,\quad \Delta=\mu,\quad u=\frac{\mu}{100}=\frac{Q}{200},\quad \varepsilon=\frac{u}{64}=\frac{Q}{12800},\quad m=10\mu=5Q,\quad t_1=\frac{\varepsilon}{96}=\frac{Q}{1228800},
$$
$$
g=\frac{\varepsilon}{384\sqrt2},\qquad C_g=C_c=\frac{64\cdot17^2}{\varepsilon},\qquad h_\ell=\mu,\qquad v=\frac{\varepsilon}{128},
$$
the Pauli-port amplitudes $b=\Omega=\varepsilon/96$ of the spin protocol of item 11(b), and no static spin field. The named nuclear inputs are the three-body ratio $3/2$ in (T.79b.1); spin–orbit coefficient $0$; the finite-size observable $R^2=\ell_n^2\,n_{j,0}n_{j,1}/B_j^2$ for $B_j>0$ and $R^2=0$ for $B_j=0$, which is the mean-square distance of the nucleons of a bank from their centre of mass on the two-node graph of length $\ell_n=\hbar c/Q$, with added action coefficient $0$; the Pauli form factors $F_1^p(0)=1$, $F_2^p(0)=0$, $F_1^n(0)=0$, $F_2^n(0)=1$ at the common nucleon mass $m$, which give both nucleons the magnetic coefficient $e/(2m)$ in the $\sigma$ convention with zero neutron charge; and the axial coefficient $g_A=0$.

5. *Bank Hamiltonian.* With binomial polynomials of the number operators,
$$
H_{\mathrm{nuc}}^{(j)}=mB_j-u\sum_\kappa\binom{n_{j,\kappa}}{2}+\frac{3u}{2}\sum_\kappa\binom{n_{j,\kappa}}{3},
\tag{T.79b.1}
$$
$$
L^{(j)}=\sum_f\bigl(n_{j,0,f}+n_{j,1,f}-b^\dagger_{j,1,f}b_{j,0,f}-b^\dagger_{j,0,f}b_{j,1,f}\bigr),
\tag{T.79b.2}
$$
$$
H_C^{(j)}=e^2\Bigl[\frac{(Q_{j,0}+Q_{j,1})^2}{4C_g}+\frac{(Q_{j,0}-Q_{j,1})^2}{4(C_g+2C_c)}\Bigr],
\tag{T.79b.3}
$$
$$
V^{(j)}=\sqrt2\sum_\kappa\sum_{a}S_{a;j,\kappa}K_{a;j,\kappa}
=\sum_\kappa\Bigl[\tfrac1{\sqrt2}\bigl(S_+K_-+S_-K_+\bigr)+\sqrt2\,S_zK_z\Bigr]_{j,\kappa},
\qquad K_a=g\,(T_a+J_a),
\tag{T.79b.4}
$$
with the common raising convention $[Q_{\mathrm m},T_+]=T_+$, $[Q_{\mathrm m},J_+]=J_+$, $[S_z,S_+]=S_+$. Write $\Sigma^z_{p;j,\kappa}=n_{j,\kappa,p\uparrow}-n_{j,\kappa,p\downarrow}$, and similarly $\Sigma^z_{n;j,\kappa}$, for the nucleon spin densities and $S_N$ for the total nucleon spin. At hopping amplitude $t$ the bank Hamiltonian is
$$
H_j(t)=\sum_\kappa H_{T;j,\kappa}+\Delta\sum_\kappa S_{z;j,\kappa}^2+H_{\mathrm{nuc}}^{(j)}+tL^{(j)}+H_C^{(j)}+V^{(j)},
$$
and the decoupled source is $H_{\mathrm{dec}}=\sum_jH_j+H_R$. Write $V_j=tL^{(j)}+H_C^{(j)}+V^{(j)}$ for the perturbation of bank $j$. Every term of $H_{\mathrm{dec}}$ commutes with the three components of $S_N$: the hopping and (T.79b.1) do not depend on spin, (T.79b.3) and $H_R$ depend on charges only, $T_a$ is a sum over spin of proton–neutron bilinears, and the elementary and mediator factors carry no nucleon modes. The charge-unit current from cell $0$ to cell $1$ of a bank is $I_{0\to1}=(i/\hbar)[tL^{(j)},Q_{j,1}]$ and the electric current is $eI_{0\to1}$.

6. *Programs.* Four neutral two-level flags have projectors $P_1,\dots,P_4$ onto their on states and start off; one coupling-enable control is retained. The hopping term of the source is $t_1\bigl(\sum_iP_i\bigr)\otimes\sum_jL^{(j)}$. The program sector $n\in\{2,3,4\}$ is the range of the projector onto "flags $1,\dots,n$ on, the others off"; on it the hopping amplitude is $t=nt_1$. The admissible family is $\mathcal H^{\mathrm{adm}}=\{H(n):n=2,3,4\}$, the compressions of the source to the three program sectors, and $t_0=3t_1$. Flag populations change only under local $\pi$ pulses on single flags, each of action $\pi\hbar/2$; every other primitive of the source commutes with each $P_i$.

7. *Sectors.* The joint cell swap $\mathsf T$ exchanges the two cells of every bank, $\mathsf Tb_{j,0,f}\mathsf T^{-1}=b_{j,1,f}$ as an automorphism of the canonical anticommutation relations, together with the elementary copies and mediators of the two cells: on the field modes of the two copies $\mathsf T$ is the automorphism of the canonical anticommutation relations that exchanges corresponding modes (the graded swap), and on the mediators it exchanges the two spin-one factors; $P_+=(I+\mathsf T)/2$. The code ground state of an elementary copy has even fermion parity, because every filled negative-energy level at $p=0$ is filled with both spin occupations and the ready state is even (item 1); hence the product of the ground states of the two copies of a bank is $\mathsf T$-even. A sector $A=(Z,N)$, $Z+N\le3$, of the four banks is the joint range of total baryon number $Z+N$, matter charge $Q_{\mathrm m}=Z$, one program sector, the code of every elementary copy, the neutral return code and $P_+$. It is closed when its nucleons lie in bank $0$. The sector $A$ of one bank is defined in the same way with the other banks omitted and $H_R=QZ$. Because $V^{(j)}$ exchanges proton and neutron number with lepton and mediator charge, $A$ labels the dressed sector of total charge $Z$.

8. *Fragmentation channels and exterior leads.* On the bank index let $v_{\mathrm{out}}=(0,1,1,1)/\sqrt3$, $w=(e_0-v_{\mathrm{out}})/\sqrt2$ and $U=I-2|w\rangle\langle w|$, acting identically on cell, spin and species, so that $Ue_0=v_{\mathrm{out}}$; $\Gamma(U)$ is its second quantization on the nucleon modes and the identity on every other factor. Let $P_c$ project onto the states whose nucleons lie in bank $0$, and for $b=(b_1,b_2,b_3)$ with $b_1+b_2+b_3=B\ge1$ let $P_b$ project onto bank $0$ empty and $b_i$ nucleons in bank $i$. Put
$$
R_b=P_b\,\Gamma(U)\,P_c,\qquad C_b=vR_b,\qquad A_b=P_bH_{\mathrm{dec}}P_b,\qquad H_{\mathrm{core}}=P_cH_{\mathrm{dec}}P_c.
\tag{T.79b.5}
$$
Channel $b$ carries the exterior lead $\ell^2(\mathbb N)\otimes\operatorname{ran}P_b$ with onsite operator $A_b+2h_\ell I$ and nearest-neighbour hopping $-h_\ell I$, coupled to the core through $C_b$ at its first site. Bank $0$ in its nucleon vacuum has no exterior.

9. *Boundary and interior.* A nucleon configuration of bank $0$ is split when both cells are occupied and coincident otherwise (all nucleons in one cell, including the empty configuration). In a sector, $\mathcal H_\partial$ is spanned by the split configurations and $\mathcal H_I$ by the coincident ones, each tensored with all other factors, and $\Lambda_A(E)$ is the Schur map (X.8k.7) of the core Hamiltonian of the sector on $\mathcal H_I\oplus\mathcal H_\partial$. For $B\le1$, $\mathcal H_\partial=\{0\}$ and the sector is described by its full Hamiltonian. The portal (T.79b.5) couples coincident and split configurations alike to the leads, so the exterior matching uses the decomposition whose boundary is the whole core, with Schur map $H_{\mathrm{core}}-E$.

10. *Preparations.* For each composition with $B=k\le3$ let $\mathsf m$ be the lexicographically first occupation of that composition in bank $0$, in the mode order $(p{\uparrow}_0,p{\downarrow}_0,n{\uparrow}_0,n{\downarrow}_0,p{\uparrow}_1,p{\downarrow}_1,n{\uparrow}_1,n{\downarrow}_1)$, with $P_+|\mathsf m\rangle\ne0$. When $\mathsf T|\mathsf m\rangle\ne|\mathsf m\rangle$, a neutral two-state reference starts in $|+\rangle$, and the logical swap of the pair $\{|\mathsf m\rangle,\mathsf T|\mathsf m\rangle\}$ with the reference (item 2 of Theorem T.79b.5) maps $|\mathsf m\rangle\otimes|+\rangle$ to $\sqrt2P_+|\mathsf m\rangle\otimes|0\rangle$; the reference is kept. When $\mathsf T|\mathsf m\rangle=|\mathsf m\rangle$, $|\mathsf m\rangle$ lies in the range of $P_+$. Elementary copies start in $r_{\mathrm{ready}}$ with leptons in their vacuum, mediators in $S_z=0$, flags in the program sector, and the return register in $q_R=-Z$, loaded from a countercharge stock that is kept.

11. *Protocols.*
   (a) *Split protocol* on the closed sector $(1,1)$. The initial state is $c\otimes\Omega$, with
   $$
   c=\tfrac1{\sqrt2}\bigl(|p{\uparrow}_0n{\uparrow}_0\rangle+|p{\uparrow}_1n{\uparrow}_1\rangle\bigr),\qquad
   s=\tfrac1{\sqrt2}\bigl(|p{\uparrow}_0n{\uparrow}_1\rangle-|n{\uparrow}_0p{\uparrow}_1\rangle\bigr)
   $$
   in bank $0$ (canonical mode order, creation operators applied in increasing mode index), $\Omega$ any normalized state of the other factors of bank $0$ in their codes, banks $1$–$3$ in prepared states and no exterior coupling. The hopping is switched with $f(s')=\sin^2(\pi s'/T)$ on $[0,T]$ and zero outside, $T\in[\tfrac{31}{32},\tfrac{33}{32}]\,\hbar/Q$. Afterwards two neutral record qubits, initially $|00\rangle$, evolve under $H_{\mathrm{read}}(s')=\lambda_0(s')\,n_{0,0}\otimes X_0+\lambda_1(s')\,n_{0,1}\otimes X_1$ with $\theta_\kappa=\hbar^{-1}\int\lambda_\kappa\in[\tfrac\pi2-\tfrac1{16},\tfrac\pi2+\tfrac1{16}]$. The outcome is "split" when both records read $1$.
   (b) *Spin protocol* on the closed sectors with $B=1$. During $[0,T_{\mathrm{spin}}]$ the nuclear Pauli port of item 4 adds exactly $H_{\mathrm{spin}}(s')=f_{\mathrm{spin}}(s')\bigl(b\,S_{N,z}+\Omega S_{N,x}\bigr)$ to the source, with $b=\Omega=\varepsilon/96$, $f_{\mathrm{spin}}(s')=\sin^2(\pi s'/T_{\mathrm{spin}})$ and $T_{\mathrm{spin}}=2\pi\hbar/(\sqrt2\,\Omega)$, and nothing outside this interval; then the total nucleon spin is measured.

12. *Cost.* $V(n)=C_{\mathrm{common}}+n\,p_{\mathrm{gate}}$, where $p_{\mathrm{gate}}>0$ prices the action $\pi\hbar/2$ of one flag pulse and $C_{\mathrm{common}}<\infty$ is the cost of every register, stock, clock, control and record shared by the three programs.

<a id="lemma-t79b1-elementary-inputs"></a>**Lemma T.79b.1 (Elementary Inputs).**

1. Every eigenvalue of $M_\nu$ and $M_e$ lies in $(1.12\,Q,1.49\,Q)$ and every eigenvalue of the quark mass matrices in $(0.51\,Q,0.68\,Q)$. At $p=0$ the lepton field Hamiltonian, after subtraction of its filled negative-energy sea, is $\sum_im_i(a_i^\dagger a_i+\bar a_i^\dagger\bar a_i)$ with every $m_i>Q$, so its ground state is unique and every excitation exceeds $Q$.
2. $\|j_a\|=3$ on the 24-mode lepton Fock space for $a=x,y,z$; hence $\|J_a\|=3$.
3. $\iota_T^\dagger H_T\iota_T=H_{\mathrm{field}}$, $\iota_T^\dagger J_a\iota_T=j_a$ and $[\Pi_T,H_T]=[\Pi_T,J_a]=0$.
4. On the code the charged-lepton charge of one copy is $6-N_e$, of modulus at most $6$, and every matter charge of the carrier satisfies $|Q_{\mathrm m}|\le48+3+8=59<68$.
5. $e^2<1$.

*Proof.* Item 1. The matrix $h$ has unit diagonal and off-diagonal entries $h_{12}=h_{23}=h(2)$, $h_{13}=h(4)$ with the intervals of Construction T.79.5b.9, so $h(2)\in(0.0985556269,0.0985556270)$ and $h(4)\in(0.0102621248,0.0102621249)$. Its eigenvalues are $1-h(4)$, with eigenvector $(1,0,-1)$, and $1+\tfrac12h(4)\pm\tfrac12\sqrt{h(4)^2+8h(2)^2}$; they lie in $(0.86565,0.86566)$, $(0.98973,0.98974)$ and $(1.14460,1.14461)$. The matrix $D$ is diagonal and unitary, so $D^\dagger hD$ has the spectrum of $h$. With $1.29671851278686773986\le T_Q\le1.29671851278686773989$ (proof of Theorem Y.8a, proof component 3), the lepton eigenvalues lie in $(1.1225\,Q,1.1226\,Q)$, $(1.2834\,Q,1.2835\,Q)$ and $(1.4842\,Q,1.4843\,Q)$, and since $3/\sqrt{43}\in(0.45749,0.45750)$ the quark eigenvalues lie in $(0.5135\,Q,0.5136\,Q)$, $(0.5871\,Q,0.5872\,Q)$ and $(0.6790\,Q,0.6791\,Q)$. At $p=0$ every species and spin block of the Dirac Hamiltonian is $\bigl(\begin{smallmatrix}0&M\\M&0\end{smallmatrix}\bigr)$ with $M$ Hermitian and positive; for a normalized eigenvector $\varphi$ of $M$ with eigenvalue $m_i$ the vectors $(\varphi,\pm\varphi)/\sqrt2$ are eigenvectors with energies $\pm m_i$. Filling the negative-energy modes and subtracting their energy gives the displayed normal form, whose least excitation is $\min_im_i>Q$.

Item 2. On the twelve left-handed lepton modes $j_a=d\Gamma(\tfrac12\sigma_a\otimes I_6)$. The second quantization of a Hermitian one-body operator has norm equal to the larger of the sum of its positive eigenvalues and the modulus of the sum of its negative eigenvalues, here $6\cdot\tfrac12=3$; conjugation by $W_F$ preserves the norm.

Item 3. $W_F$ is unitary, and $H_{\mathrm{field}}\otimes I+I\otimes B_{\mathrm{ref}}(I-p_0)$ and $j_a\otimes I$ commute with $I\otimes p_0$; conjugation gives the identities.

Item 4. At $p=0$ each copy has twelve charged-lepton modes (three generations, two spins, two energy signs), six of them filled in the vacuum, so the normal-ordered charge is $6-N_e\in[-6,6]$. Eight copies give at most $48$ in modulus, the nucleons at most $3$ and the eight mediators at most $8$.

Item 5 is the interval of item 2 of Construction T.79b. ∎

<a id="theorem-t79b2-closed-core-spectra-binding-and-thresholds"></a>**Theorem T.79b.2 (Closed-Core Spectra, Binding and Thresholds).** For a sector $A$ of one bank in a fixed program let $F_A$ be the least eigenvalue of $H_0+QZ$ on it, $F_A^0$ the least eigenvalue of $H_0-V_0+QZ$ on it, $E_A=F_A-F_{(0,0)}$ and $E_A^0=F_A^0-F^0_{(0,0)}$.

1. $E_A^0$ is the minimum of (T.79b.1) over the even nucleon states of $A$, plus $QZ$. In particular
$$
E_p^0=m+Q,\qquad E_n^0=m,\qquad E_{pn}^0=2m-u+Q,\qquad E_{pnn}^0=3m-\tfrac32u+Q,
\tag{T.79b.6}
$$
attained by onsite clusters, and on the nucleon factor of one bank the even part of the cell swap is nonzero in each of the ten compositions with $B\le3$.
2. $\|tL^{(0)}\|\le6t\le\varepsilon/4$, $\|V^{(0)}\|\le\varepsilon/16$ and $\|H_C^{(0)}\|<\varepsilon/192$; hence $\|V_0\|<\varepsilon$ and $\sum_j\|V_j\|<4\varepsilon$.
3. For every input in the intervals of items 1–2 of Construction T.79b and every program,
$$
\bigl|E_p+E_n-E_{pn}-u\bigr|\le4\varepsilon,\qquad
\bigl|E_{pn}+E_n-E_{pnn}-\tfrac u2\bigr|\le4\varepsilon,\qquad
\bigl|E_{pnn}-2E_{pn}+E_p-\tfrac u2\bigr|\le4\varepsilon .
\tag{T.79b.7}
$$
Since $4\varepsilon=u/16$, the two-nucleon binding, the separation energy of the second neutron and the shell second difference $\Delta_N^2E_0(1,1)$ of Theorem T.79a are positive.
4. The least eigenvalue of a closed four-bank sector $A$ is $F_A+3F_{(0,0)}$, and the least eigenvalue of the sector $(0,0)$ of one bank is simple.
5. For a closed parent $A$ and a channel whose $k$ occupied daughter banks carry compositions $d$ with bank charges equal to their proton numbers, the least eigenvalue of $A_b$ on that subsector minus $F_A+3F_{(0,0)}$ is at least $\sum_dE_d^0-E_A^0-2k\varepsilon$. For $A=(1,2)$ and three single-nucleon daughters it is at least $\tfrac32u-6\varepsilon>0$.

*Proof.* Item 1. With $V_0=0$ the bank Hamiltonian is a sum of commuting terms: (T.79b.1), which is diagonal in occupations and commutes with $\mathsf T$, the elementary copies, the mediator gaps and $QZ$. By items 1 and 3 of Lemma T.79b.1 the code ground state of each copy is unique with excitations above $Q$, and the mediator ground state $S_z=0$ has gap $\Delta=\mu$. A state of the sector with an excitation of an elementary copy or a mediator costs at least $\mu$ in those factors, and its nucleons, whatever their composition at the same $B$, have a value of (T.79b.1) at least the minimum for $A$ minus $\tfrac32u$, because $m$ is common and the binomial terms take values in $[-\tfrac32u,0]$ for $B\le3$; so its energy is at least $F^0_A+\mu-\tfrac32u$. The least energy is therefore attained with all copies and mediators in their ground states, and $E_A^0$ is the stated nucleon minimum plus $QZ$. The binomial terms are minimized by placing as many nucleons as possible in one cell: a cell holds at most two protons and two neutrons, an onsite pair contributes $-u$ and an onsite triple $-3u+\tfrac32u=-\tfrac32u$, which gives (T.79b.6). An occupation and its swap are distinct and $\mathsf T$ commutes with (T.79b.1), so $P_+|\mathsf m\rangle$ is a nonzero vector of the same energy. On the nucleon factor of one bank the even subspaces of the compositions $(0,0),(0,1),(0,2),(0,3),(1,0),(1,1),(1,2),(2,0),(2,1),(3,0)$ have dimensions $1,2,2,2,2,8,12,2,12,2$.

Item 2. For each species, $n_0+n_1-b_1^\dagger b_0-b_0^\dagger b_1$ is the second quantization of $\bigl(\begin{smallmatrix}1&-1\\-1&1\end{smallmatrix}\bigr)$, with eigenvalues $0$ and $2$; with at most three nucleons $\|L^{(0)}\|=6$, and $6t\le24t_1=\varepsilon/4$. In each cell $T_z=\tfrac12(N_p-N_n)$ with $N_p,N_n\le2$ and the three isospin components are unitarily equivalent, so $\|T_a\|=1$; with $\|J_a\|=3$ and $\|S_a\|=1$, $\|V^{(0)}\|\le\sqrt2\cdot2\cdot3\cdot g(1+3)=24\sqrt2\,g=\varepsilon/16$. On the code $|Q_{0,0}\pm Q_{0,1}|\le3+12+2=17$, so $\|H_C^{(0)}\|\le e^2\cdot17^2\bigl(\tfrac1{4C_g}+\tfrac1{12C_g}\bigr)=e^2\varepsilon/192<\varepsilon/192$ by item 5 of Lemma T.79b.1. The sum is below $0.32\,\varepsilon$.

Item 3. $V_0$ preserves baryon number, matter charge, the program, the codes (item 3 of Lemma T.79b.1) and $\mathsf T$, so each sector is invariant under $H_0$ and under $H_0-V_0$, and Weyl's inequality gives $|F_X-F^0_X|\le\|V_0\|<\varepsilon$ for every sector $X$ of one bank. Each combination in (T.79b.7) is a signed sum of four least eigenvalues: $E_p+E_n-E_{pn}=F_p+F_n-F_{pn}-F_{(0,0)}$, $E_{pn}+E_n-E_{pnn}=F_{pn}+F_n-F_{pnn}-F_{(0,0)}$ and $E_{pnn}-2E_{pn}+E_p=F_{pnn}-2F_{pn}+F_p$. Their unperturbed values are $u$, $\tfrac u2$ and $\tfrac u2$ by (T.79b.6), so each error is at most $4\varepsilon$. The proof uses only $e^2<1$ and the lepton gap above $Q$, which hold on the whole input intervals.

Item 4. $H_{\mathrm{dec}}$ conserves the charge of every bank, since the banks interact only through $H_R$, which depends on $Q_{\mathrm m}$ alone. The closed sector splits into subsectors with fixed bank charges. The swap of each bank commutes with $H_{\mathrm{dec}}$, so every subsector splits further by the swap characters of the four banks, whose product is $+1$. On the subsector with all charge in bank $0$, $H_R=QZ$ and $H_{\mathrm{dec}}$ is the sum of $H_0+QZ$ and three copies of the empty bank. If banks $1$–$3$ are swap-even, bank $0$ is swap-even and the least eigenvalue is $F_A+3F_{(0,0)}$. The unperturbed ground state of a bank without nucleons is simple and swap-even, so a swap-odd bank without nucleons carries an excitation of an elementary copy or a mediator, of energy at least $\mu$, while a swap-odd bank $0$ with $B\ge1$ has the same unperturbed minimum as a swap-even one, because onsite clusters come in swap pairs; these states therefore have unperturbed energy at least $F^0_A+3F^0_{(0,0)}+\mu$ and energy at least $F_A+3F_{(0,0)}+\mu-8\varepsilon$. Every other subsector carries charge on an empty bank, which is a lepton or mediator excitation of energy at least $\mu$, while the value of (T.79b.1) in bank $0$ is at least the minimum for $A$ minus $\tfrac32u$ as in item 1; so its unperturbed least energy is at least $F^0_A+3F^0_{(0,0)}+\mu-\tfrac32u$ and its least energy at least $F_A+3F_{(0,0)}+\mu-\tfrac32u-8\varepsilon>F_A+3F_{(0,0)}$. The sector $(0,0)$ of one bank has no nucleons, so its unperturbed least eigenvalue is simple with gap at least $\mu$, and a perturbation of norm below $\varepsilon<\mu/2$ keeps it simple.

Item 5. On the subsector the charges of the banks are fixed and nonnegative, so $H_R$ is the sum of the bank values $QZ_j$ and $A_b$ is a sum over banks. For $B\ge1$ the unperturbed nucleon minimum of a composition is the same for both $\mathsf T$-characters, since (T.79b.1) is diagonal, commutes with $\mathsf T$ and is minimized by onsite clusters, which come in swap pairs. Hence every state of the subsector, whatever its joint character, has energy at least $\sum_d(F_d^0-\varepsilon)+(4-k)F_{(0,0)}$, while the parent energy is $F_A+3F_{(0,0)}\le F_A^0+\varepsilon+3F_{(0,0)}$ by item 4. Writing $F^0_X=F^0_{(0,0)}+E^0_X$ and using $|F_{(0,0)}-F^0_{(0,0)}|<\varepsilon$, the difference is at least $\sum_dE_d^0-E_A^0-(k+1)\varepsilon-(k-1)\varepsilon$. For $(1,2)\to p+n+n$ the unperturbed difference is $(m+Q)+2m-(3m-\tfrac32u+Q)=\tfrac32u$, and $\tfrac32u-6\varepsilon=90\varepsilon>0$. ∎

<a id="theorem-t79b3-fragmentation-channels-exterior-sheets-and-resonance-map"></a>**Theorem T.79b.3 (Fragmentation Channels, Exterior Sheets and Resonance Map).**

1. For every $B\in\{1,2,3\}$ and every $b$ with $b_1+b_2+b_3=B$,
$$
R_b^\dagger R_b=\frac{B!}{b_1!\,b_2!\,b_3!\,3^B}\,P_c^{(B)},
\qquad\sum_bR_b^\dagger R_b=P_c^{(B)},
\tag{T.79b.8}
$$
where $P_c^{(B)}$ is $P_c$ at baryon number $B$. Every one of the $3$, $6$ and $10$ ordered channels for $B=1,2,3$ is nonzero, and the stacked coupling $(C_b)_b$ has norm $v$.
2. The lead of channel $b$ has first-site Green function
$$
G_b(z)=f\bigl(z-A_b-2h_\ell I\bigr),\qquad f(w)=\frac{w-\sqrt{w^2-4h_\ell^2}}{2h_\ell^2},
\tag{T.79b.9}
$$
by functional calculus, with the branch for which $f(w)\sim w^{-1}$ at infinity; an eigenvalue $\lambda$ of $A_b$ contributes the band $[\lambda,\lambda+4h_\ell]$. The Schur complement of the core in $z-H$ is $z-H_{\mathrm{core}}-\sum_bC_b^\dagger G_b(z)C_b$, and the exterior impedance is $\Lambda_{\mathrm{out}}(E)=-\sum_bC_b^\dagger G_b(E)C_b$.
3. With $\rho_b(E)=\sqrt{\bigl[4h_\ell^2-(E-A_b-2h_\ell I)^2\bigr]_+}\,/(2\pi h_\ell^2)=-\pi^{-1}\operatorname{Im}G_b(E+i0)$ and $\Phi_b(E)=2\pi C_b^\dagger\rho_b(E)C_b\ge0$, the stationary outgoing probability flux of a unit core amplitude $\psi$ into channel $b$ is
$$
-\frac2\hbar\operatorname{Im}\bigl\langle\psi,C_b^\dagger G_b(E+i0)C_b\psi\bigr\rangle=\frac1\hbar\langle\psi,\Phi_b(E)\psi\rangle .
\tag{T.79b.10}
$$
There are a channel $b$ and an eigenvalue $\lambda$ of $A_b$ with $\Phi_b(E)\ne0$ for every $E\in(\lambda,\lambda+4h_\ell)$. On a lead truncated after $N$ sites the channel current is $J_b=(i/\hbar)[H,P_{b,\mathrm{lead}}]$ and the survival probability is $\operatorname{Tr}(P_{\mathrm{core}}U(t)\rho U(t)^\dagger)$; if $M$ bounds the norms of the full and the truncated generators, $\|(U_\infty(T)-U_N(T))P_{\mathrm{core}}\|\le2\sum_{k\ge N+1}(M|T|/\hbar)^k/k!$.
4. Fix a closed parent sector $A$ with $B\ge1$ nucleons and put $e_*=4F^0_{(0,0)}+mB+QZ$. On the corresponding sector every $A_b$ has its spectrum in $(e_*-\tfrac32u-4\varepsilon,\,e_*+4\varepsilon)\cup(e_*+\mu-\tfrac32u-4\varepsilon,\infty)$; let $\mathsf P_b$ be its spectral projector onto the first part. The interval
$$
I_A=\bigl(e_*+4\varepsilon,\ e_*+\mu-\tfrac32u-4\varepsilon\bigr)
$$
has a closure that contains no eigenvalue of any $A_b$ or $A_b+4h_\ell I$; every band of the first part is open on $I_A$, every band of the second part is closed, and $\sum_bC_b^\dagger\rho_b(E)C_b\ne0$ for $E\in I_A$. On $\operatorname{Im}z<0$,
$$
G_{b,\mathrm{out}}(z)=(I-\mathsf P_b)\,G_b(z)+\mathsf P_b\Bigl[\frac{z-A_b-2h_\ell I}{h_\ell^2}-G_b(z)\Bigr]
\tag{T.79b.11}
$$
is the analytic continuation of $G_b$ from $\operatorname{Im}z>0$ across $I_A$, and $K_{\mathrm{out}}(z)=H_{\mathrm{core}}-z+\sum_bC_b^\dagger G_{b,\mathrm{out}}(z)C_b$ is analytic on $\operatorname{Im}z<0$ with
$$
\lim_{|z|\to\infty}\frac{K_{\mathrm{out}}(z)}{z}=-I+h_\ell^{-2}\sum_bC_b^\dagger\mathsf P_bC_b,
\tag{T.79b.12}
$$
an invertible limit because the second term has norm at most $v^2/h_\ell^2<1$. Hence $\det K_{\mathrm{out}}$ is not identically zero and has finitely many zeros, counted with multiplicity, in the rectangle $\operatorname{Re}z\in\bar I_A$, $\operatorname{Im}z\in[-R,-\eta]$ with $R=\mu+\|H_{\mathrm{dec}}\|+4h_\ell+v$ and $\eta=v^2/(1024h_\ell)$. The resonance map of a sector is $z\mapsto\det K_{\mathrm{out}}(z)$ on this sheet; it is the matched determinant $\det(\Lambda-\Lambda_{\mathrm{out}})$ of (X.8k.15a) for the matching decomposition of item 9 of Construction T.79b, continued to the sheet, with residual $\sigma_{\min}(K_{\mathrm{out}}(z))$, energy width $\Gamma_{\mathrm{res}}=-2\operatorname{Im}z$ and rate $\Gamma_{\mathrm{res}}/\hbar$.

*Proof.* Item 1. $\Gamma(U)$ maps $b^\dagger_{0,\kappa,f}$ to $3^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^3b^\dagger_{i,\kappa,f}$ and fixes the vacuum. For an occupation $\mathsf m$ of bank $0$ with $B$ modes, $\Gamma(U)|\mathsf m\rangle$ is $3^{-B/2}$ times the signed sum over the $3^B$ assignments of its modes to banks $1$–$3$; distinct assignments, and distinct $\mathsf m$, give orthogonal occupations, the signs do not affect norms, and $P_b$ keeps the $B!/(b_1!b_2!b_3!)$ assignments with counts $b$. This gives (T.79b.8); the multinomial coefficients sum to $3^B$. Equivalently, $V_3^\dagger\operatorname{diag}(z_1,z_2,z_3)V_3=\tfrac13(z_1+z_2+z_3)$ for $V_3=(1,1,1)^{\mathsf T}/\sqrt3$, and the coefficients of the $B$-th exterior power of this identity are (T.79b.8). Then $\sum_bC_b^\dagger C_b=v^2P_c$ on $B\ge1$.

Item 2. On $\ell^2(\mathbb N)$ with onsite $\lambda+2h_\ell$ and hopping $-h_\ell$, the first-site Green function $g$ satisfies $g=(z-\lambda-2h_\ell-h_\ell^2g)^{-1}$, whose root with $g\sim z^{-1}$ is $f(z-\lambda-2h_\ell)$, and the spectrum is $[\lambda,\lambda+4h_\ell]$. The lead of channel $b$ is $A_b$ tensored with this chain, so functional calculus in $A_b$ gives (T.79b.9) and keeps degenerate eigenspaces whole. The Schur complement formula for the block operator with off-diagonal blocks $C_b$ and $C_b^\dagger$ gives the stated complement.

Item 3. For $|w|<2h_\ell$, $f(w+i0)=(w-i\sqrt{4h_\ell^2-w^2})/(2h_\ell^2)$, so $-\pi^{-1}\operatorname{Im}f(w+i0)=\sqrt{4h_\ell^2-w^2}/(2\pi h_\ell^2)$, and (T.79b.10) follows by functional calculus. Because $\sum_bC_b^\dagger C_b=v^2P_c\ne0$ and the spectral projectors of each $A_b$ sum to the identity, some $b$ and some eigenvalue $\lambda$ have $C_b^\dagger\mathbf 1_{\{\lambda\}}(A_b)C_b\ne0$, and $\rho_b(E)\ge\sqrt{4h_\ell^2-(E-\lambda-2h_\ell)^2}\,\mathbf 1_{\{\lambda\}}(A_b)/(2\pi h_\ell^2)$ is nonzero on the interior of that band. The current formula is the Heisenberg derivative of $P_{b,\mathrm{lead}}$. For the truncation bound, $H^kP_{\mathrm{core}}$ and $H_N^kP_{\mathrm{core}}$ coincide for $k\le N$ because $k$ applications reach at most $k$ lead sites, so the difference of the exponential series starts at order $N+1$, and each term has norm at most $2(M|T|/\hbar)^k/k!$.

Item 4. Without the perturbations $V_j$, $A_b$ on the sector is a sum of commuting terms whose eigenvalues are $4F^0_{(0,0)}+QZ$ plus a value of (T.79b.1) summed over the banks, which lies in $[mB-\tfrac32u,mB]$ for $B\le3$, plus excitation energies of elementary copies and mediators, each at least $\mu$ (on the codes only leptons and mediators can be excited, by Lemma T.79b.1). The perturbations of the four banks have total norm below $4\varepsilon$ (item 2 of Theorem T.79b.2, which also holds for an empty bank), so every eigenvalue moves by less than $4\varepsilon$, which gives the two spectral parts. An eigenvalue $\lambda$ of the first part satisfies $\lambda<E<\lambda+4h_\ell$ for $E\in I_A$, because $E-\lambda<\mu<4\mu=4h_\ell$, while every eigenvalue of the second part exceeds $E$; neither $\lambda$ nor $\lambda+4h_\ell$ lies in $\bar I_A$. For the density, take $\psi$ in the core sector with all nucleons in an onsite cluster of bank $0$ and all other factors in their unperturbed ground states. Then $R_b\psi$ is nonzero by (T.79b.8) and lies in the range of the unperturbed projector $\mathsf P_b^0$ onto the first part, and the Davis–Kahan theorem gives $\|\mathsf P_b-\mathsf P_b^0\|\le4\varepsilon/(\mu-\tfrac32u-4\varepsilon)<10^{-3}$, so $\langle R_b\psi,\mathsf P_bR_b\psi\rangle>0$. Since $\rho_b(E)\ge c_E\mathsf P_b$ with $c_E>0$ the least density of the open bands at $E$, $\langle\psi,\sum_bC_b^\dagger\rho_b(E)C_b\psi\rangle>0$. The second root of $h_\ell^2g^2-wg+1=0$ is $w/h_\ell^2-f(w)$; across the interior of a band the boundary value of $f$ from above equals the boundary value of $w/h_\ell^2-f$ from below, while outside the band $f$ is analytic across the real axis. Since no edge lies in $\bar I_A$, the bands open on $I_A$ are exactly the eigenvalues selected by $\mathsf P_b$, which proves (T.79b.11). As $|z|\to\infty$ in the lower half-plane, $G_b(z)=O(z^{-1})$ and $(z-A_b-2h_\ell I)/h_\ell^2=z/h_\ell^2+O(1)$, which gives (T.79b.12). The limit is $-I$ plus a positive semidefinite operator of norm at most $\|\sum_bC_b^\dagger C_b\|/h_\ell^2=v^2/h_\ell^2<1$, hence invertible, so $\det K_{\mathrm{out}}(z)\ne0$ for large $|z|$. An analytic function on the connected open lower half-plane that is not identically zero has finitely many zeros in every compact subset. Finally, on the matching decomposition the interior is empty and the Schur map is $\Lambda=H_{\mathrm{core}}-z$, so $\det(\Lambda-\Lambda_{\mathrm{out}})=\det\bigl(H_{\mathrm{core}}-z+\sum_bC_b^\dagger G_b(z)C_b\bigr)$, which becomes $\det K_{\mathrm{out}}(z)$ on the sheet. For an exterior coupled only to $\mathcal H_\partial$, the Schur determinant formula gives $\det K=\det(H_{II}-z)\det(\Lambda_A-\Lambda_{\mathrm{out}})$ on the split decomposition; the portal (T.79b.5) couples to $\mathcal H_I$ as well, so the matching space is the whole core, and the determinant has no interior Schur poles. ∎

<a id="theorem-t79b4-boundary-datum-joint-selection-and-equivalence-certificate"></a>**Theorem T.79b.4 (Boundary Datum, Joint Selection and Equivalence Certificate).**

1. $\langle s,L^{(0)}c\rangle=-2$, and the component of $L^{(0)}c$ on split configurations is $-2s$. In the core Hamiltonian of the closed sector $(1,1)$ the only term that connects $\mathcal H_I$ and $\mathcal H_\partial$ is the hopping term, so the off-diagonal block is $tB_0$ with $B_0$ independent of $t$; on the even nucleon states with all other factors in their ground states, $B_0B_0^\dagger=4I$ on the four split spin states.
2. As $|z|\to\infty$,
$$
\Lambda_{(1,1)}(z)=-z+H_{\partial\partial}+z^{-1}\,t^2B_0B_0^\dagger+O(z^{-2}),
\tag{T.79b.13}
$$
so the boundary response of the sector $(1,1)$ determines $t^2$ and hence $t>0$.
3. Let the boundary datum $Z_A^{\mathrm{PU}}$ be the Schur map $\Lambda_A$ of every sector $A$ at $t_0=3t_1$, fixed together with the exterior map of item 8 of Construction T.79b. The joint completion set $\{n\in\{2,3,4\}:\Lambda_A^{(n)}=Z_A^{\mathrm{PU}}\text{ for every }A\}$ is $\{3\}$. Its $V$-minimizer is $n=3$, and on it PPI equivalence and boundary-preserving unitary equivalence are both the identity relation, so the equivalence certificate of Theorem X.8k.6b holds with the identity intertwiner.
4. $V(2)<V(3)<V(4)$: preparing program $n$ from the all-off flags needs at least $n$ flag pulses, and $n$ pulses suffice.

*Proof.* Item 1. In the occupation basis of the canonical mode order, hopping the proton or the neutron of $c$ to the other cell produces $|p{\uparrow}_0n{\uparrow}_1\rangle$ and $|n{\uparrow}_0p{\uparrow}_1\rangle$ with the anticommutation signs that give $-2s$, and the diagonal part of $L^{(0)}$ adds $2c$; so $\langle s,L^{(0)}c\rangle=-2$. The terms (T.79b.1), (T.79b.3) and the elementary terms are diagonal in the cell occupations, and $V^{(0)}$ changes isospin and charge inside one cell, so all of them preserve $\mathcal H_I$ and $\mathcal H_\partial$. The block $B_0$ is the restriction of $L^{(0)}$; on the even states of the composition $(1,1)$ the four coincident and the four split spin states give $B_0B_0^\dagger=4I$ by direct computation.

Item 2. Expand $(H_{II}-z)^{-1}=-\sum_{k\ge0}H_{II}^kz^{-k-1}$ in (X.8k.7).

Item 3. By item 2 the three programs give the $z^{-1}$ coefficients $4t_1^2$, $9t_1^2$ and $16t_1^2$ times the nonzero operator $B_0B_0^\dagger$ in the sector $(1,1)$, so only $n=3$ matches $Z_{(1,1)}^{\mathrm{PU}}$, and $n=3$ matches every $Z_A^{\mathrm{PU}}$ by definition. A one-point set is finite and nonempty, so its argmin exists and is that point; any two of its members are equal and are intertwined by the identity, which preserves the boundary.

Item 4. Every primitive other than a flag pulse commutes with each $P_i$, so the number of flags that are on changes only through flag pulses, by one per pulse; program $n$ has $n$ flags on and all flags start off. ∎

<a id="theorem-t79b5-separating-split-protocol-preparations-and-spin-response"></a>**Theorem T.79b.5 (Separating Split Protocol, Preparations and Spin Response).**

1. In the split protocol of item 11(a) of Construction T.79b with $t=nt_1$ and $x=T/\hbar$, the probability $p_t$ of a split configuration after the hopping pulse satisfies
$$
\beta^2t^2x^2-e_t\le p_t\le t^2x^2+e_t,\qquad e_t=t\varepsilon^2x^3+\tfrac14\varepsilon^4x^4,\qquad\beta=\tfrac{31}{32}.
\tag{T.79b.14}
$$
The record effect of the outcome "split" is $\vartheta\,P_{\mathrm{split}}$ with $\vartheta=\sin^2\theta_0\sin^2\theta_1\in[\beta,1]$; an unsplit configuration with $B=2$ gives the outcome "split" with probability $0$. For every admitted timing and angle in the three programs the outcome probabilities of adjacent programs differ by at least
$$
\gamma=\frac{3t_1^2}{Q^2},
\tag{T.79b.15}
$$
and $N_{\mathrm{trial}}$ independent replicas with $2\exp\bigl(-2N_{\mathrm{trial}}(\gamma/8)^2\bigr)\le\delta_{\mathrm{fail}}$, with effect and preparation errors below $\gamma/8$, identify the program with failure probability at most $\delta_{\mathrm{fail}}$.
2. For an occupation $\mathsf m$ with $B=k$, the normal-ordered monomial that annihilates the $k$ modes of $\mathsf m$ and creates the $k$ modes of $\mathsf T\mathsf m$ equals $\pm|\mathsf T\mathsf m\rangle\langle\mathsf m|$ on the sector $B=k$, with the sign fixed by the anticommutation relations. The preparations of item 10 of Construction T.79b produce a state in the range of $P_+$ for each of the ten compositions.
3. In the spin protocol, for nucleon spin up and any state of the other factors,
$$
P_{\downarrow}(T)=\frac{\Omega^2}{b^2+\Omega^2}\sin^2\Bigl[\frac{\sqrt{b^2+\Omega^2}}{2\hbar}\int_0^Tf_{\mathrm{spin}}(s')\,ds'\Bigr],
\tag{T.79b.16}
$$
and $P_\downarrow(T_{\mathrm{spin}})=\tfrac12$ at $b=\Omega$. At $b=\Omega$ and $|T/T_{\mathrm{spin}}-1|\le\delta$, $|P_\downarrow(T)-\tfrac12|\le\tfrac12\sin^2(\pi\delta/2)\le\pi^2\delta^2/8$. The probability refers to the spin of the nucleon, proton or neutron.

*Proof.* Item 1. Put the hopping, $H_C^{(0)}$ and $V^{(0)}$ into the interaction $V(s')$ and the remaining terms into $H_D$. On $c\otimes\mathcal K$ and $s\otimes\mathcal K$, with $\mathcal K$ the other factors, $H_D$ acts by one operator on $\mathcal K$ plus the nucleon energies, which differ by $u$ (one onsite pair), and the hopping acts as the identity on $\mathcal K$. By item 1 of Theorem T.79b.4 the first-order interaction-picture amplitude from $c\otimes\Omega$ into split configurations is $-i\hbar^{-1}\int f(s')e^{ius'/\hbar}(-2t)\,ds'\,s\otimes\Omega$ for every $\Omega$ in the code. The other terms of $V$ preserve the cell occupations. With no exterior coupling the banks evolve independently, so only bank $0$ enters, with $\|V(s')\|\le\varepsilon$ by item 2 of Theorem T.79b.2. The first-order amplitude has norm $2t|F(x)|$ with $F(x)=\int_0^xf(\hbar r)e^{iur}dr$; since $\int_0^xf(\hbar r)\,dr=x/2$ and $\cos(ux)\ge\cos(\tfrac{33}{32}\cdot\tfrac1{200})>\beta$ on the registered interval, $\beta x/2\le|F(x)|\le x/2$. The interaction-picture unitary differs from its first-order part by at most $\varepsilon^2x^2/2$, so $(|A_1|-r)^2\le p_t\le(|A_1|+r)^2$ with $|A_1|\in[\beta tx,tx]$ and $r\le\varepsilon^2x^2/2$, which gives (T.79b.14). After the pulse every remaining term preserves $n_{0,0}$ and $n_{0,1}$ and commutes with $H_{\mathrm{read}}$; the factor $\exp(-i\theta_\kappa n_{0,\kappa}\otimes X_\kappa)$ flips the record of an occupied cell with one nucleon with probability $\sin^2\theta_\kappa$. An unsplit configuration with $B=2$ leaves one cell empty, so one record never flips. For $|\theta_\kappa-\tfrac\pi2|\le\tfrac1{16}$, $\vartheta\ge\cos^4\tfrac1{16}>\beta$. With $x\in[\beta,\beta_+]/Q$, $\beta_+=\tfrac{33}{32}$, the outcome probability of program $n$ lies in $[\beta^5n^2t_1^2/Q^2-e,\ \beta_+^2n^2t_1^2/Q^2+e]$ with $e$ the bound of (T.79b.14). For $r_*=\varepsilon^2/(t_1Q)=\tfrac3{400}$ the sum of the two error bounds of programs $3$ and $4$, divided by $t_1^2/Q^2$, is at most $7r_*\beta_+^3+\tfrac12r_*^2\beta_+^4<0.06$, that of programs $2$ and $3$ is smaller, and the leading gaps are $9\beta^5-4\beta_+^2>3.42$ and $16\beta^5-9\beta_+^2>4.08$; this gives (T.79b.15). The identification statement is Hoeffding's inequality for the empirical frequency against thresholds at the midpoints of the separating gaps: with probability at least $1-\delta_{\mathrm{fail}}$ the frequency lies within $\gamma/8$ of its mean, which lies within $\gamma/8$ of the interval of the true program.

Item 2. On the sector $B=k$ an occupation other than $\mathsf m$ lacks at least one mode of $\mathsf m$, so the annihilators give zero; on $|\mathsf m\rangle$ they give the vacuum up to sign, and the creators give $\pm|\mathsf T\mathsf m\rangle$. When $\mathsf T|\mathsf m\rangle\ne|\mathsf m\rangle$, the two vectors $|\mathsf m\rangle$ and $\mathsf T|\mathsf m\rangle$ span a two-level space on which $\mathsf T$ is a logical flip, realized on $B=k$ by the monomial, its adjoint and their signs; three controlled flips, alternately controlled by the reference and by the pair, implement the logical swap, which maps $|\mathsf m\rangle\otimes|+\rangle$ to $\tfrac1{\sqrt2}(|\mathsf m\rangle+\mathsf T|\mathsf m\rangle)\otimes|0\rangle=\sqrt2P_+|\mathsf m\rangle\otimes|0\rangle$. An occupation with $P_+|\mathsf m\rangle\ne0$ exists in every composition by item 1 of Theorem T.79b.2.

Item 3. On $B=1$ the nucleon space is $\mathbb C^2_{\mathrm{cell}}\otimes\mathbb C^2_{\mathrm{isospin}}\otimes\mathbb C^2_{\mathrm{spin}}$, with $S_N=\tfrac12\sigma$ on the last factor. Every term of the source commutes with the components of $S_N$ (item 5 of Construction T.79b), so by Schur's lemma for the spin-$\tfrac12$ representation it acts as the identity on the spin factor, and so do the charge, program and swap projectors; the source has no static spin field (item 4), and during the protocol the Pauli port adds exactly $H_{\mathrm{spin}}$ (item 11(b)). Hence the Hamiltonian during the protocol is $f_{\mathrm{spin}}(s')(b\sigma_z+\Omega\sigma_x)/2\otimes I+I\otimes H_{\mathrm{rest}}(s')$, with $H_{\mathrm{rest}}(s')$ the whole source on the other factors. The spin part commutes with itself at different times and is the rotation by the angle $\hbar^{-1}\sqrt{b^2+\Omega^2}\int f_{\mathrm{spin}}$ about the axis $(\Omega,0,b)/\sqrt{b^2+\Omega^2}$, which gives (T.79b.16) for any state of the rest. At $b=\Omega$ the factor in front is $\tfrac12$ and, since $\int_0^Tf_{\mathrm{spin}}=T/2$ for the envelope on $[0,T]$, the sine is $\sin\bigl(\pi T/(2T_{\mathrm{spin}})\bigr)$, which equals $1$ at $T=T_{\mathrm{spin}}$ and equals $\cos(\pi\delta'/2)$ at $T=(1+\delta')T_{\mathrm{spin}}$; hence $P_\downarrow=\tfrac12\cos^2(\pi\delta'/2)$ and the tolerance bound. ∎

<a id="theorem-t79b6-additional-nuclear-input"></a>**Theorem T.79b.6 (Additional Nuclear Input).** Keep the elementary factor and the values of $\varepsilon$, $t_1$, $g$, $C_g$, $C_c$, $m$, $\Delta$, $h_\ell$ and $v$ of Construction T.79b fixed, and let $u\in[0.99u_0,1.01u_0]$ with $u_0=Q/200$. The bounds of Theorems T.79b.2–T.79b.5 hold on the whole interval. On the closed sector $(1,1)$ in a fixed program, $\partial H/\partial u=-\sum_\kappa\binom{n_{0,\kappa}}{2}\le0$ with strictly negative trace on the sector. Hence $u$ is an independent nuclear input: two sources with the same elementary factor and different $u$ are not unitarily equivalent by any unitary that maps the sector $(1,1)$ onto itself.

*Proof.* The bounds of Theorems T.79b.2–T.79b.5 use $u-4\varepsilon>0$, $\tfrac u2-4\varepsilon>0$, $\tfrac32u-6\varepsilon>0$ and $\mu-\tfrac32u-8\varepsilon>0$ together with the fixed values listed; on the interval $63.36\,\varepsilon\le u\le64.64\,\varepsilon$ and $\mu=6400\,\varepsilon$, so all of them hold. With at most two nucleons the three-body term of (T.79b.1) vanishes, so $\partial H/\partial u$ is the displayed operator: it is $-1$ on coincident configurations with two nucleons and $0$ on split ones, and the coincident states of $c$ lie in the sector, so its trace on the sector is negative. The sector is fixed and finite-dimensional, so the trace of the Hamiltonian on it is strictly decreasing in $u$, and a unitary equivalence mapping the sector onto itself preserves that trace. ∎

<a id="proposition-t79b7-package-entries-and-uncertainty-ledger"></a>**Proposition T.79b.7 (Package Entries and Uncertainty Ledger).** For every sector $A=(Z,N)$ with $Z+N\le3$, Construction T.79b and Theorems T.79b.2–T.79b.6 supply the eighteen entries of Definition X.8k.6a as follows, and the package is accepted.

| Entry of Definition X.8k.6a | Supplied by |
|:--|:--|
| 1. $\mathcal H_A^{\mathrm{adm}}$ | the three program compressions $H(n)$, $n=2,3,4$, of item 6: finite, self-adjoint, colorless and antisymmetric, built on the elementary factor and coupling of items 1–2; the banks are decoupled except through $H_R$, which is additive on the consumed compositions |
| 2. $\mathcal H_A^{\mathrm{ret}}$ | the sector of item 7: 32 nucleon modes with $B\le3$, elementary copies on their codes, mediators, flags, return register, joint swap quotient |
| 3. $\mu_A^{\mathrm{ret}}$ | the canonical Fock inner product and counting trace, with the density matrices of items 10–11 |
| 4. $\mathcal S_A^{\mathrm{mb}}$ | one-body $mB$; two-body contact $-u\binom n2$; three-body $\tfrac32u\binom n3$; exchange by the anticommutation relations; spin–orbit coefficient $0$; Coulomb (T.79b.3) with $H_R$; weak (T.79b.4); finite size $R^2$ with action coefficient $0$; resolution: two cells per bank, $B\le3$ |
| 5. $\mathcal B_A^\partial$ | split boundary and coincident interior of item 9; channel basis $b$ and coupling $C_b$ of item 8; exterior matching on the whole core (item 9) |
| 6. $\mathcal P_A^\partial$ | the split protocol, the spin protocol and the preparations of items 10–11 |
| 7. $Z_A^{\mathrm{PU}}$ | $\Lambda_A$ at $t_0=3t_1$ (item 3 of Theorem T.79b.4) |
| 8. $\Lambda_A^{\mathrm{PU}}$ | the Schur map of item 9, with Theorem X.8k.6 |
| 9. $\Lambda_{A,\mathrm{out}}$ | $-\sum_bC_b^\dagger G_bC_b$ with the bands, widths and outgoing sheet of Theorem T.79b.3 |
| 10. $H_A^{\mathrm{PU}}$ | the compression of $H(3)$ to $A$ |
| 11. $J_A^{\mathrm{spin}}$ | $\Sigma^z$ and $S_N$, with the Pauli port of item 4 and $g_A=0$ |
| 12. $\mathcal T_A$ | the hopping, readout, spin and weak transition operators, with (T.79b.14)–(T.79b.16) and outputs $\operatorname{Tr}(E\,U\rho U^\dagger)$ |
| 13. $\mathcal D_A$ | the channels $b$ of (T.79b.5) with thresholds $A_b$, fluxes (T.79b.10), currents $J_b$ and survival probabilities |
| 14. $\mathcal R_A^{\mathrm{open}}$ | $\det K_{\mathrm{out}}$, the determinant (X.8k.15a) of the matching decomposition on the sheet (T.79b.11), with the rectangle and residual of item 4 of Theorem T.79b.3 |
| 15. $\mathcal U_A$ | the ledger below |
| 16. $\Pi_{A\leftarrow T}$ | $Q$, the lepton current $J_a$ and the lepton spectrum (Lemma T.79b.1) and $e$ (Theorem W.6a.10) enter the source; $u$ is independent of them by Theorem T.79b.6, and the other named inputs of item 4 are model entries |
| 17. $V_A^{\mathrm{PCE}}$ | $V(n)$ of item 12, strict by item 4 of Theorem T.79b.4 |
| 18. $\chi_A^{\mathrm{nuc}}$ | $1$: every entry, including the Pauli-port amplitudes and the timing and angle intervals of the protocols, is fixed by Construction T.79b, which uses no isotope, spin, transition-rate or decay datum; a change of any entry defines a new source |

The uncertainty ledger $\mathcal U_A$ has the following separated rows, each entering once.

| Row | Content |
|:--|:--|
| Elementary inputs | $T_Q$ and $h$ with the intervals of Lemma T.79b.1; the bounds of Theorems T.79b.2–T.79b.5 hold for every value in them |
| Electromagnetic input | $e^2$ with the interval of Theorem W.6a.10, one value shared by all cells; it enters through (T.79b.3) and the bound $e^2<1$ |
| Named nuclear inputs | the values of item 4 of Construction T.79b, exact; the source has no static spin field |
| Isotope outputs | (T.79b.6)–(T.79b.7) and the threshold bounds of Theorem T.79b.2, valid jointly for all inputs |
| Spin output | (T.79b.16), with the port field of item 11(b) as the only spin-dependent term; $\lvert P_\downarrow-\tfrac12\rvert\le\pi^2\delta^2/8$ for a relative timing tolerance $\delta$ |
| Rates and probabilities | (T.79b.10) and (T.79b.14)–(T.79b.15) on the timing and angle intervals of item 11 |
| Finite evaluation | the truncation bound of Theorem T.79b.3; for an $r$-step product formula of $H=\sum_kh_k$ over time $T$, the error $T^2(2r\hbar^2)^{-1}\sum_{k<l}\Vert[h_k,h_l]\Vert$ |
| Resonance extraction | the outgoing sheet, rectangle and residual of Theorem T.79b.3, separate from the truncation row |

*Proof.* Each row of the first table restates the cited item. The acceptance conditions of Definition X.8k.6a hold: every entry is finite or, for the leads, given by the finite matrix functions (T.79b.9) and (T.79b.11); $H(3)$ and its compressions are self-adjoint; the Schur map equals $Z_A^{\mathrm{PU}}$ at $t_0$; the exterior map is derived from the item 8 source data; all transition and decay operators act on the one carrier of item 3; the ledger rows are separated; and $\chi_A^{\mathrm{nuc}}=1$. The admissible completion set (X.8k.16) of the joint source is $\{H(3)\}$ by Theorem T.79b.4, so Theorem X.8k.6b applies with a unique representative and the identity certificate, and every listed output is a spectral or matrix-element image of the package. ∎
